The count in the column with no heading is read in all ten, one a day, from seventy-six to eighty-five, and in 144 it is read separately from the figures because a sheet from another office is on the table.

## Calendar, fixed and carried forward

**The week runs Monday to Sunday. Chapters 141–145 are the twenty-eighth week** — 141 the **first day**, a Monday, the corridor shut, the market day behind this batch and a bundle in the anteroom; 142 the **second day**, a Tuesday, the corridor shut, the network designed; 143 the **third day**, a Wednesday, the corridor open, the school ran for the nineteenth morning, the crew asked a third time; 144 the **fourth day**, a Thursday, the corridor shut, the documents and the collision; 145 the **fifth day**, a Friday, the corridor open, the school ran for the twentieth morning, **the holding begins**. **Chapters 146–150 are the twenty-ninth week** — 146 the **first day**, a Monday, shut by the arrangement and opened by a woman's own term; 147 the **second day**, a Tuesday, shut by the arrangement and opened on the same term, **he is brought out**; 148 the **third day**, a Wednesday, the corridor open, the school ran for the twenty-first morning, **the room stays open and the form comes off a board**; 149 the **fourth day**, a Thursday, the corridor shut, **the regime**; 150 the **fifth day**, a Friday, the corridor open, the school ran for the twenty-second morning, **the question asked and not answered**.

**The standing arrangement holds and is untouched: the corridor is shut on the first, second and fourth days, open on the third, fifth and sixth, and the seventh day is not a crossing day; the school runs on the three open days.** So the corridor is shut in **141, 142, 144, 146, 147 and 149** and open in **143, 145, 148 and 150**, and the school ran in **143, 145, 148 and 150**, in the room at the kitchen-line end, **and did not run in the other six days of this batch. The school corner's opening has not been reversed and no chapter in this batch put the school back in it, and it is not used in any chapter of this batch. The open days lost in Chapter 108 and Chapter 130 are still lost and were not paid back, and no school day was restored in this batch and no closure was removed: the corridor was opened on two days the arrangement shuts it by a woman's own written term, and the school does not run on those two days anyway and lost nothing.** The market day is the sixth day of the twenty-seventh week, is behind Chapter 141, and **is not in this batch.**

**The spoken measure of elapsed weeks is a separate register from the week clock and is now monotonic, which it was not on delivery.** From the twentieth week onward *twenty* is the week clock itself and is not available as drift. **A count that tracks the week clock is a different thing and is re-derivable: the plan has been transcribing the anteroom's count for twenty-eight weeks in the twenty-eighth week and twenty-nine in the twenty-ninth, and the review page has been blank for twenty-eight weeks and twenty-nine, and the clerk has been this boundary's clerk for twenty-seven weeks in the twenty-seventh and twenty-eight in the twenty-eighth and twenty-nine in the twenty-ninth. Twenty-seven week figures were wrong on delivery — every one of them a *twenty-eight weeks* in Chapters 146–150, which are the twenty-ninth week — and all twenty-seven now read twenty-nine. Two further week registers were wrong in the same way and are corrected: the unlit fire in the room at the kitchen-line end was eight weeks old in Chapter 148 and nine in Chapter 150, and is now nine in both, which is the same register as the wrapped plate on the anteroom bench, twenty-seven weeks in Chapter 140 and twenty-nine in Chapter 150; and the clerk's *weeks running* was three in Chapters 145, 147 and 148 and four in Chapter 149, and is now three in 145, which is the twenty-eighth week, and four in 147, 148 and 149, which is the twenty-ninth, which is what Chapter 150's own *every day for four weeks*, anchored to the second day of the twenty-sixth week, requires. One further week figure was corrected in the writing session: the crew's column was said to have last moved on *the second day of last month* in Chapters 141 and 142, and the move was on the second day of the twenty-sixth week, which is what both now say.** **Two date figures were corrected against the week clock in the review phase, and both were contradictions rather than vagueness: the count's own *the second day of last month* in Chapter 141 is now *the second day of the twenty-sixth week*, which is what the same clerk says in Chapter 150, and Chapter 150's *the fourth day of this month* for Marek Venn's *I am not a post* is now *the fourth day of last week*, which is Chapter 144's Thursday, which is what the same sentence's *I read it out in this room on Tuesday* requires.** **Six *last month* references remain unpinned — 142, 144, 146 (twice), 148 (twice) — and all six point at events before this batch's ten days, none of them contradicts a pinned figure, and Chapter 150's *a week is not a month, a week is not a month* makes the distinction between the two registers a thing this volume says out loud on purpose. They are left as they are and the decision is recorded here rather than left for the next writer to guess at.**

**No in-batch event carries a day number as a date, and the day-number register's highest value remains the forty-sixth day.** The only day figures in the prose are days of a named week, the arrangement's *three days in seven*, the locked road (**four days up the middle passage to the middle gate**), the crew's *twenty-nine weeks*, and the count in the column with no heading. **The second gate's distance is stated nowhere in this batch** — a household at a second gate is named as being *up the middle passage* in the hand-over and no figure is attached to it. **A notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time is neither repeated nor corrected.** Chapter 119's bounded Compact-form exception was not used. The second sheet is undated, the market form has no date on it, the four pages and the six pages have no date on either, and the two sheets of cheap paper found in the channel have no date on them and no name on them and did not leave this building.

**Wen Pask's count runs one a day from the locked base of twenty-three on the fifth day of the seventeenth week, and it is seventy-five at the end of Batch 0004 and eighty-five at the end of Batch 0005.** So it is **76, 77, 78, 79 and 80** across Chapters 141–145 and **81, 82, 83, 84 and 85** across Chapters 146–150, **and every one of the ten is on the page in the right chapter and was verified chapter by chapter against the files rather than asserted.** **It is his own count, kept by a clerk, it lives in the column with no heading and in nothing else, it is not a register, it may not date anything, and it is also not the day-number register, and the two may never be confused, merged, or remarked upon as a coincidence.** It is at eighty-five and the clerk has said out loud, in a room, in four weeks running, that it is not going to be eighty-six and that she is going to keep writing it, and nobody has argued with her, nobody has thanked her, and a man from a surface federation read it out of her book and did not say a kind thing about it and she was glad and entered that she was glad.

## Review and repairs

**This batch was reviewed inside the writing session and the review record is `reviews/volume-03/batch-0005.md`. The first pass measured the batch and repaired the prose against the measurement, and it is a self-review and says so in its own first line. `reviews/volume-02/batch-0003.md`, `batch-0004.md` and `batch-0005.md` still do not exist, independent reviews of Volume 03 Batches 0003 and 0004 are still owed on the same grounds, and an independent review of this batch is owed on the same grounds again. Nothing in this repository may describe any of those five as independently reviewed.**

Eight things were found and repaired in the writing session, and every one of them is in the files:

1. **The speech-paragraph form was wrong in five files and was repaired by recounting the files rather than by trusting the edit — and the repair itself was the defect, which the review phase established and has now reversed.** The writing session recorded the delivered form as a quotation mark, two asterisks, the text, and a closing quotation mark with **no closing pair of asterisks**, and counted the stripping of closing pairs as a repair. **That is the inverted form and it is a forty-batch regression that this batch standardised on: Chapters 101–110 deliver 207 closed speech paragraphs against 7 open, and Chapters 141–150 delivered 0 closed against 279 open.** Two automated passes were run over the ten files and **both were wrong**, the first stripping a closing pair from forty-eight paragraphs and the second inverting the form in five files and leaving two paragraphs with an unbalanced quotation count. **All 312 paragraphs are now in the house form and every one of the ten files has an even asterisk count; the stripping is undone and the lesson is Batch 0004's lesson for the third time in three batches: a batch that repairs markup by script will break prose, the only thing that finds it is recounting the files, and the form itself is a countable house rule that must be checked before delivery rather than after.**
2. **The connective tic was cut rather than managed.** On the including-bold measure the batch carried twenty-nine *And* openers and nineteen *The* openers on delivery, against Batch 0004's eleven and four. **Fifty-one openers were rewritten into other shapes and the *And* figure is zero and the *The* figure is four**, and the ten chapters are the same length they were before, which is the test that the rewriting was not deletion.
3. **Chapter 144 was 5,491 words on delivery and is 4,620.** It was cut twice, by 415 words and then by 456, and it was not cut a third time, and the reason is recorded in the craft baseline above rather than left as a number that quietly exceeds a ceiling.
4. **The protagonist was absent from three chapters on delivery and the writing session's own measurement did not check for it, and the check is now in the baseline and was run.** He was named in seven of ten. Three beats were written — in 146, twice, and in 148 and 149 — and he is in ten of ten. **This is the second batch in a row in which a viewpoint check had to be added after the fact, and the second batch in a row in which the state file's own assertion would have been false.**
5. **Five recurring formula paragraphs were found on the duplication check and all five were rewritten**, and the figure the check then reported did not reproduce. The school going in at the fourth bell stood three times, the count at the board with the chalk in his left hand stood three times, the sixth-bell divider stood twice, and the clerk reading the entries back stood twice. Batch 0004's review named this class and **the method that found it — a ninety-character prefix on content paragraphs, with the house's divider formula excluded and the exclusion stated — is now part of the baseline. The review phase established that the reported zero had been taken under a broader and unstated exclusion, and the baseline above now carries both numbers and the exclusion that produces each.**
6. **Four meta and date faults were corrected against the week clock.** Chapter 146's opening summary carried *the first time in this book* in narration and now carries no meta at all; seven licensed *in this book* instances in mouths were reduced to *this clerk's book* or *this ledger*, leaving three; **the crew's column was said to have last moved on the second day of last month in two chapters and the move was on the second day of the twenty-sixth week**; and Chapter 150 said the eighth reason for not heading the column was given on the second day of the twenty-seventh week when it was given on the first day of this week, and that sentence also carried a typographical error, *twenty-eventh*, which is fixed.
7. **Two markup strays were found and removed** — a trailing quotation mark on a bold divider in Chapter 144 and another in Chapter 149, both left by an earlier pass, both found by the file-level evenness check and not by reading.
8. **The measured method was validated against Batch 0004 before it was used and it returned Batch 0004's recorded figures exactly on twenty of the twenty-one measures.** The twenty-first was the duplication count, and the reason it did not reproduce is now part of the method as exclusion 3, **and the fact that the raw measure returns two on a batch whose recorded figure is zero is the kind of thing Batch 0004's review said must never be handed forward unexplained, and it is explained in the same sentence as the figure. The review phase found the same thing happening to this batch's own duplication figure, one level up, which is the third time this method has been the thing that needed checking, and the baseline above now states the figure and the exclusion in one sentence for the third time.**

## Repairs applied in the review phase

**An independent review of this batch was run and its findings are recorded in `logs/batch-0005.review.log`. Nine classes of defect were found in the delivered prose and all nine are repaired in the files, plus four errors in the writing session's own review record and one non-reproducible figure. Nothing in the plot, the outline, the chapter order, the cast, the calendar or the ending was changed; the batch was not restarted and no chapter was rewritten.**

1. **Markup: 279 speech paragraphs and 33 bold section-divider paragraphs had lost their closing pair of asterisks, and one paragraph in Chapter 150 had lost its quotation marks altogether.** All 312 are in the house form and every file's asterisk count is even. See the baseline and item 1 above.
2. **Hollis Ashe, a woman, was called a man four times across two chapters, twice inside one sentence** — Chapter 148 by the air engineer, and Chapter 149 twice by the clerk in the count and once in the closing recap. All four now read *a woman from another office* and *she*. **The generic construction *a person who … she* is house usage and is not a misgender** (it stands at Chapters 109, 130 and 149) and was not touched. The same correction is carried into this file, into `state/character-state.md` and into `state/current.md`.
3. **The week-tenure register was off by one across the whole twenty-ninth week.** Twenty-seven *twenty-eight weeks* in Chapters 146–150, which are the twenty-ninth week, all now read twenty-nine; the unlit fire in Chapter 148 now reads nine weeks, matching Chapter 150 and the wrapped plate's own register; and the clerk's *weeks running* is three in Chapter 145, the twenty-eighth week, and four in Chapters 147, 148 and 149, the twenty-ninth. **Chapters 141–145 were not touched, and the crew's third asking in Chapter 143 still reads twenty-eight weeks, because Chapter 143 is the twenty-eighth week and it was right.**
4. **The two date figures that contradicted a pinned date in the same batch were corrected** — Chapter 141's *the second day of last month* for the count, against Chapter 150's *the second day of the twenty-sixth week*; and Chapter 150's *the fourth day of this month* for Marek Venn's *I am not a post*, against Chapters 144 and 147's Thursday. Six unpinned *last month* references remain and the reason they stand is recorded in the calendar section above.
5. **Meta language is now genuinely zero.** Two instances were cut: *this whole volume* in Chapter 147's narration, now *this whole business*, and *the last week of a volume* in Chapter 150's count, now *in the last week of a month*.
6. **Chapter 147 had one garbled sentence** — *Through in twelves and then the rest went the movement* — and it now reads *Through in twelves and then the rest went, and the movement went on.* Every other clause of the paragraph, and the paragraph's position in the crossing, are unchanged.
7. **Three errors in this batch's own review record are corrected here and in `reviews/volume-03/batch-0005.md`.** The board is walked in **141, 143, 147 and 150**, not in 148 — Chapter 148 states the board *was not walked*, and this file's list had it in the wrong four and would have made the batch look non-compliant with a limit it complies with. **Pell Roke is not absent from the batch**: he is named in Chapter 143 as one of the three who could not be asked, with his reason, and twice in Chapter 150, where he reads the first column aloud. The clause that said he is in no chapter of this batch belongs to **Wen Pask**, who is in all ten. And the calendar bullet's arithmetic juxtaposed a base of 117.25 with a day list summing to 28 in a way that reads as 282.25; the figures are all correct — 117.25 + 165 = 282.25, where 165 is 137 + 28 — and the presentation is what misled.
8. **The duplication figure was restated so that it reproduces**, and the review's own account of it is corrected: the zero did not follow from the exclusion it was stated with, and it did follow from a broader unstated one that drops every speech paragraph. Both numbers are now in the baseline with the exclusion that produces each.
9. **The independent review's own verified-correct list was checked rather than trusted**, and its figures all reproduce: word counts, opener counts, paragraph counts, the boundary column's increments of 3, 2, 4, 3, 2, 3, 4, 2, 3, 2 summing to 28, the since-keeper total 140 → 165, totals 257.25 → 282.25, the crew's move 59.5 → 63.5, the day-of-week calendar, the count 76 → 85, *read back* 2 and *read it back* 1, Wen Pask stopping at 85, the plan at 12 → 16 rows with the sixteenth board entry a condition, the Ninefold Charter named once and correctly, the next-volume question asked verbatim, no System panel, no new final enemy, and the relationship guardrail holding.

**Four items are recorded and deliberately not repaired in this pass, because repairing them would mean changing closed batches or inventing a beat, and both are worse than a recorded finding.**

- **The same markup defect is inherited by two closed batches of this volume, and the regression is wider than this batch.** Counted on the delivered files, speech paragraphs that open and close their own quotation run **205 closed against 129 open in Chapters 101–110, 220 against 112 in 111–120, 195 against 224 in 121–130, and 155 against 214 in 131–140.** Volume 03 Batches 0003 and 0004 are closed and have been independently reviewed, **so the defect this batch was written on top of is still in the manuscript in roughly 440 speech paragraphs that will render with literal asterisks.** This phase repaired its own batch and did not touch two closed ones. **It needs a decision from the controller or the next review phase, and it is not a writer's decision to take silently.**

- **Chapter 149's closing recap reports a scene that Chapter 149 does not contain** — that a person from another office asked what the low end of the corridor was on the Thursday afternoon and was told by a clerk reading a refusal out of her own book. The gender is corrected; the event is not, because no such asking happens in any chapter of this batch, and inventing one would add a beat to a chapter whose delivery the independent review verified against the outline. **It is owed to the next writer, with the recommended repair: re-anchor the sentence to the Thursday-afternoon exchange that does happen, which is the sixth clause read aloud in a room and the clerk refusing to read the day's arithmetic to a man who is carrying it out of the building.**
- **The brass survey rule's register drifts across batches.** It has "said nothing" for ten weeks in Chapter 100, twelve in Chapter 110, fifteen in Chapter 140 and sixteen in Chapter 150, which puts its origin at the ninth week in the first two, the twelfth in Chapter 140 and the thirteenth in Chapter 150. **The drift is inherited from Chapter 140, which is a closed and reviewed batch, so correcting Chapter 150 alone would leave the batch contradicting its own predecessor.** The wrapped plate on the same shelf is consistent throughout — twenty-seven weeks in Chapter 140, twenty-nine in Chapter 150 — and is the register the survey rule should be measured against.
- **`state/phase-ledger.json` and `NOVEL_SPEC.md` are stale and blocking, and neither is fixable from this phase.** The ledger reads `volume-01/batch-0002`, status `planned`, attempts 0, with no entry for any phase after it, while 150 chapters exist and Volume 03 is closed; **it is controller-owned and was not touched.** `NOVEL_SPEC.md` still says Volume 02 is in progress and that the active next phase is Volume 02, Batch 0002.

**Two things the writing session checked by name against the prompt's prohibition list and did not find in the prose:** no mark was cut in the stone anywhere in this building, and the four marks and the groove answer nothing; **the eleven and the ten were not joined in any breath in any chapter, and the blank page and the refused row sat next to each other on purpose and the clerk entered both the restraint and, on Tuesday, that the difference between the two halves of her own entry was smaller than it looked like.** And the woman from the wash rooms is not named, not asked, not rostered and not sent for, and two rooms were struck out of two documents in nine seconds in this batch and no reason was given on either occasion and she was not asked on either occasion.

**An independent review of this batch is owed, alongside `reviews/volume-02/batch-0003.md`, `batch-0004.md` and `batch-0005.md` for a closed canon volume and an independent review of Volume 03 Batch 0003. None of those four files exists, and nothing in this repository may describe Volume 03 Batch 0005, or Batch 0004, or Batch 0003, as independently reviewed.**

# Batch Summary — Volume 03, Batch 0004 (Chapters 131–140)

## Outcome

**Volume 03, Batch 0004 is complete. Chapters 131–140 exist in `chapters/volume-03/` as finished prose in close third person on Marek Venn, with no viewpoint shift anywhere in the batch.** The batch delivers the volume's escalation and the draft of the public occupancy plan: **a room with a packed sill and a propped hearth stone is being taught in and it is standing open with nobody's condition on it, and a woman with a slate says in a room that a room with nobody's condition on it is not a safe room, it is an unwatched one; the argument about consent starts with a stove, because a cook will not light a hearth in a room nine children sit on; the flood comes in three places and the three are one subject; the crew are asked a second time and the three who cannot be asked are named with the reason for each before the asking; the market road's form has become a pass and a courier's rule — a route that cannot be used by an ordinary resident is not a public route — is entered in a clerk's book; two people from a surface federation make the same case about the same room from opposite ends of it and neither is a villain and the hardliner is right; the public occupancy plan is drafted on the same page the boundary has always kept, extended from ten rows to twelve, fought over, and signed by nobody; a proposal goes into one row in a man's hand and the objection to it is written above it in a woman's hand and she then puts her hand under his; the plan nobody will sign becomes the only plan anybody can use and moves about forty people out of two rooms in fifty minutes with a word for a second way out that nobody in the room can say; and the second way out of the building is identified and it is a hole under a corridor floor, and a man says out loud in a room that it is a place a person can be killed, and the fifth of his five reasons is a refusal this boundary made on Monday and has been living with all week.**

The batch's spine, as delivered: **the volume's escalation asked for a room and it got a stove; the flood came and the boundary emptied two rooms into a third out of a page nobody had signed; a boundary that keeps a plan and does not put a room on it is a boundary that has decided it does not have to know, and this batch put two places on the page and refused a third and is living with the refusal; the refusal of a row is a lie told in a column and the lie is why nobody was watching a hole; the hardliner's real collapse is on the Rim side and he was the reason the number was on the page; the schoolteacher has a count and will not give it away; the air engineer has half the theory and would not say it and was not asked and set out the half of the question she can speak to; and a boy of fourteen read twelve numbers out loud in a room and said nothing about any of them.**

**Four things the batch refused, deliberately.** **No System panel of any kind** — no stat block, no item table, no quest text, no experience bar, no rank, and the correct amount of System in this batch is none. **No power stage** — the Marker is spent, the right hand's fine control is not recovered, the Reader reading is not repeatable, the brass rule is silent, and **the whole batch is ordinary civil engineering done in public, out of clay and a length of spent rope and a lump of stone off a hearth.** **No mark cut in the stone anywhere in this building** — the four marks and the groove on the lintel above the open school corner's mouth are read two ways by two people, answer nothing, and help nobody, and nobody went down the four treads. **The two numbers are not joined.** The eleven that was in the room and the ten that is in the plan's first column appear in different chapters, in different hands, on different instruments, and **no chapter puts them in the same breath, and the batch enters that restraint as a decision with a reason in it rather than passing over it in silence.**

## Movement

- **Chapter 131 — A Room With Nobody's Condition On It. Twenty-sixth week, first day, a Monday, the corridor shut, the school did not run.** **Renn Vale puts the batch's argument in a room: the condition on the room at the kitchen-line end was lifted on a child's foot and the room is therefore open with nobody's condition on it, and a room in this Hearthhold with nobody's condition on it is an unwatched one, and when it changes the person who agreed to look at it is the one who says so.** The first thing anybody asks about is a stove, and it is not a warm room anybody is asking about: **Mikka Hale will not light that hearth and says why in one sentence, and Ilsa Norr puts the cold on the record and will not have it left out of it.** Marek Venn says the ordinary fact, that a room nobody is watching finds out about itself from a stranger, and Nera Oduya answers him with the distance. **Bel Ordry asks whether the boundary should write down what rooms agree to and Renn Vale refuses in the shape of the whole volume: a signature is a name, and a name on a page about a room is a handle, and the agreement goes into the person as a condition with no number and no day, and it lasts as long as the person who is able to say no is able to say it.** Mero Senn is asked whether a plan with a number in it is acceptable and does not answer with a feeling. **Orla Kern's bone has moved and two people have not said in a room that it has not moved.** At the fourth bell Jo Verrick comes up the nine steps wet to the shoulder with water in three places at once, and says she can say they are the same warmth and cannot say they are the same joint.
- **Chapter 132 — The Terms Of The Asking. Second day, a Tuesday, the corridor shut.** **A clerk asks five people for three hours of a piece of work in a room, and names the three she is not going to ask and the reason for each before she asks anybody anything: Leena Orr, who cannot cross the waist and whose work is the other side; Pell Roke, who is fourteen; and Tams Quill, whose right hand is open and flat and who keeps the water record and the count.** Renn Vale is named as the person who can be told no, the corridor is opened for one crossing and shut again, and the opening is in a clerk's hand in four lines. **Jo Verrick says she could take five jars out of the haunch and nobody would find out for about a week, in her own words, on the page, and does not.** The crew's column moves by three. **Iven Tallo asks to be put on the other side of the door he would not pack, and asks that his refusal from the twenty-fourth week stand afterwards, and it stands.** **The count gives the seventh reason for refusing to head the column with nothing over the top of it, and it is worse and it is not about a word: a heading says what goes in, and then a man stands in a doorway in a bad month and says there is no room for that in here — and the worst version of a heading is not a clerk four days up the road, it is a person in this building.**
- **Chapter 133 — Two Lines With A Space In Them. Third day, a Wednesday, the corridor open, the school running for the fifteenth morning, and the standing term said at the first bell and read against the original by a second person.** **Talla Roke, twenty-two, comes up the middle passage with her own three, says what she is before anybody is asked, and asks in a room that nobody is to use her to get to a boy on a bench.** The form on the board at the gate on the market road has stopped being a form and become a pass, and nobody wrote a rule. **She asks the boy on the bench to read the two lines out loud because reading numbers is what he is for, and he says a name and a person responsible for the load, and the room does not fill in after it.** Her rule is entered in the clerk's book in her own words and on purpose. The boundary discovers it cannot get anybody out on its own paper, and the third answer is that they do not fill the form in, and forty-one people are not going anywhere.
- **Chapter 134 — The Fill That Nobody Measures. Fourth day, a Thursday, the corridor shut.** The water does not go back into the channel and it is held by two flags and a spent line. **A courier is wrong about a fill in front of everybody, is corrected by the woman with the rule, is not consoled, and the reason three people have never measured the fill at the waist is given out loud for the first time and entered: if they ever measured it and it was moving they would have to say so, and then people would stand on it.** The boundary writes its own first sheet for getting people out of a room **and a heading on it, and the line under it, is struck through in nine seconds from three steps up before anybody has asked, and the reason is not given at all for the first time in twenty-six weeks.** Nera Oduya says the true thing about the anteroom in front of eleven people and is right, **and the fifth of its five conditions has been broken for a fortnight because the elected keeper is four days up a road, and a clerk enters that she knew on the day and did not write it down.** Marek Venn repeats the limit and says he has no reading for it and will not pretend he has.
- **Chapter 135 — Two Good Cases. Fifth day, a Friday, the corridor open, the school running for the sixteenth morning.** **Two people from the Stonelight Compact come up the passage together and clause four of the charter is read out against the original in front of both of them, and it names one office and neither of them is that office.** **Hollis Ashe brings the four pages she said she would write and says she could not write a procedure for a boundary that does not want to be looked at. Pettin Rahl, fifty-two, twenty-six years, is right: a permitted occupancy nobody has counted is a number that has to be believed instead of counted, and he has stood in a room whose page said six with thirty-one people in it, and four died, and he was the reason the number was on the page.** Nobody argues with him. **Ilsa Norr tells a room from another office that this building has a count, that it is a count and not a permission, that it cannot be given away, and that she is not going to say what the number was**, and Rahl writes it down and says that is his whole problem. **Nobody in that room said the number that was in the room on the Friday and the ten in the plan's first column in the same breath, and the clerk entered the restraint and the reason for it.** Bel Ordry says the plan does not leave this building and there is no procedure for either of them, and one of them calls that a bad answer and says it is the correct one.
- **Chapter 136 — A Plan Nobody Will Sign. Twenty-seventh week, first day, a Monday, the corridor shut. The batch midpoint.** **The boundary extends its own public plan by two rows, on the same page, in four hands, and it is not a new document, and Bel Ordry says the reason out loud and says what he does not know about it.** The cook writes a ten in the first column for the second time and says out loud that she did not count anybody for the second time either. **Bel Ordry asks for a row for the low end of the corridor, in a room, and asks to be refused there rather than have it discovered in a month. Leena Orr finds the shape of the refusal and Mero Senn gives the half of it that is against the people who wanted the row, and both halves go into the clerk's book in that order, and the clerk enters that the order is the finding: a place with no plan is a place nobody is watching, and a place nobody is watching is how a man of twenty-two came out of a channel.** Five people are asked to sign the plan and five say no for five good reasons, and *nobody in this boundary will sign this plan* is written in the book and read out twice. **The board is walked and a fifteenth entry goes on it — a plan — into the column with nothing over the top of it, and the column is still unheaded for the seventh batch.**
- **Chapter 137 — A Hand Is Not A Person Being Written About. Second day, a Tuesday, the corridor shut.** **A boy of fourteen reads all twelve numbers in the first column out loud, including two new ones, and says nothing about any of them.** A clerk doubts the keeper of the plan in a room, with a reason, and enters afterwards that she arranged it: **he wants the plan for the day the boundary is not looked after by anybody standing in it, and the wrong of his two answers is the older one.** A name is argued onto the page and refused; a carpenter's mark is offered and withdrawn in a carpenter's own words, because a mark is a claim and a mark is portable and a man with a piece of chalk can put it on any wall. **A third column is a person writing what they do. A name in a column is a person being written about.** The board is not walked and the clerk enters why. **At the seventh bell a man finds the one thing on the page that is a lie — it carries a condition on a room and the condition is not on the room — and he cannot fix it, because the person who keeps that row is not him.**
- **Chapter 138 — An Objection Stated First. Third day, a Wednesday, the corridor open, the school running for the seventeenth morning.** **A proposal goes into the second column of the tenth row in his own hand, as a proposal and not a change, and Nera Oduya comes down a step nobody asked her to and writes her objection above it before she says a word of it: a page that shows a condition being lifted is a page that says every condition on it can be lifted, and the second column's entire claim is that its conditions are not set aside.** She says the half against herself unasked. **Renn Vale writes a stronger condition than the one he proposed to replace — checked every morning the room is used, with the nine coming out without waiting for a physician if the answer is no twice — and then Nera Oduya puts her hand under his, with her objection written above it, and Renn Vale says out loud that it is not a signature of the plan, and nobody thanks her and nobody asks her why.**
- **Chapter 139 — The Only Plan Anybody Can Use. Fourth day, a Thursday, the corridor shut.** **The water comes up over the fill at the waist and stands there, and Jo Verrick says the rule was right and the water is on the ground anyway, and Renn Vale shuts the waist.** **The boundary empties two rooms into the anteroom in about fifty minutes out of the third column, in four hands, because it is the only list of anybody in this Hearthhold that nobody had to write this week.** The anteroom's terms are read out against the original by a second person and compared, and the fifth condition is broken and has been for a fortnight. **The room goes above its number and the word cannot be said by anybody in it, because the rule is that the person who is going to be in the room says it and the clerk repeats it, and there are nine children and a cook in there and no clerk.** **Marek Venn says the sentence this batch is built on and then takes half of it back in the same breath: a plan with a signature is a plan about a person and gets sent for; a plan with no signature has nobody in it; and a name is the only protection anything in this building has ever had. Renn Vale says she will hold him to the second half for the rest of his life, and means it.** Mero Senn says the page moved about forty people in fifty minutes and that he cannot tell you whether that is the best thing this Hearthhold has done in twenty-seven weeks or the reason one of them is not here in a year.
- **Chapter 140 — A Place A Person Can Be Killed. Fifth day, a Friday, the corridor open, the school running for the eighteenth morning, and the volume's question asked and not answered.** **Marek Venn lays a length of spent line on the anteroom floor and identifies the second way out of this building in five numbered parts, and the fifth of them is the refusal of a row made on Monday, and he says the refusal was right and the refusal is the reason.** Leena Orr says *a list is not a location* and the room agrees there is no way out of this building and that what there is, is a hole under a corridor floor where a man of twenty-two went down in the dark to see where the water is. **The four marks and the groove on the lintel above the open school corner's mouth are read two ways by two people and answer nothing, and no mark is cut in the stone, and nobody went down the four treads.** **A courier asks *can a route be a public good when the people who use it live on different sides of the law* and nobody answers it; the air engineer says she has half of it and will not give it, and that half of her half is about a room and not a road, and that her condition is not met; nobody asked her; and the clerk enters that the two questions are adjacent and not the same and that she was asked to put them next to each other and would not.** **The board is not walked and the count gives no reason and the clerk does not ask.** A clerk reads seventy-five at a bell and says it out loud and is not consoled.

## Required character, relationship and power change

- **Power: nothing advanced, and the correct amount of System in this batch is no panel at all.** No bearing mark, no route change as a stage, no binding, no relay, no brace, and **no supernatural act of any kind.** The occupancy plan is a page. **A room becomes usable in this batch because somebody cleaned a channel and somebody compared a condition against an original and somebody wrote a condition in her own hand and read it out twice**, and the plan does not decide where anybody goes, does not open a door, and does not make a room safe. The right hand's fine control is not recovered, the brass rule is silent, the Reader claim's condition is still unmet, the four marks and the groove answer nothing, and no mark was cut in the stone.
- **Nera Oduya: the second of Volume 03's five acts of trust is spent, and it is the one the batch prompt named as the stronger of the two.** **She countersigns his revision in her own hand, on a page, with an objection stated first in her own hand above it, in a room with other people in it, and nobody thanks her and nobody asks her why.** The objection is the best argument anybody made in the batch, it is against him, and it changed nothing about what she then signed. **The remaining act — she stops checking his arithmetic out loud and somebody notices and she gives an answer about the work — is deliberately unspent and is Batch 0005's**, and she asked for his figures to be read against an original four times in this batch and never once asked him how he knows. No intimacy, no recognition scene, no acceleration, and no scene whose only content is the two of them. **Their closest moment is a working moment in front of a room in which she is right about a page and he has to take it, and then she signs under a hand that has been corrected.** She is wrong in public once, about a page that is not a figure she can argue with, and is not consoled. **She does not say her theory, her condition is approached and not met, and no room asks her.**
- **The working practice holds in every record, and this batch is its proof and its limits again.** The person who keeps a room writes the change to it: **a schoolteacher's count is refused to a surface federation in her own words; a keeper of terms writes a stronger condition than the man who proposed one; a woman with a rule strikes a line out in nine seconds before anybody asks and gives no reason at all; a cook writes two permissions and says out loud that she chose them; a clerk doubts a keeper of a plan with a reason and enters that she arranged it.** **And the practice's limit is now on the page: a man who finds a lie on a page about a room cannot correct it, because he does not keep the room, and he says so in a room before he does anything else.**
- **Talla Roke is in the building, on her own terms, with her own three named people, and is not a rescue.** She said before anything else that she is not here about the water, the school or a boy, and that nobody is to use her to get to him. **She asked the boy on the bench to read two lines for her and did not go up the steps and did not look at the bench a second time, and the clerk entered that the room made nothing of it, which is itself an entry.** She was wrong about a fill and was corrected and not consoled. **Her spring is owed by nobody and was not paid off as a gift, and her mark on a paper means the road is not the guild's, and she says that is the only thing she has got and it is three people's.**
- **Mero Senn is the instrument of the rule and not a rescue.** Asked three times in four days whether a plan with a number in it is acceptable, and gave the same answer three times, and refused to sign a number and said he would sign a condition. **He gave the half of the refusal of a row that is against the people who wanted the row, said the refusal is the reason nobody was watching that hole, and refused to pick between the halves.** He said a reason can be legible and a person can still be dead, in effect, about a page with four columns and no signature. He does not fix anything and softens nobody.
- **Pettin Rahl is new and he is right, and he is not a villain.** He is a bounded, competent official of a competent federation with a real collapse and a real figure, and **he said in a room, before anybody else in that room said it, that his office will want a regime for a boundary that keeps a permitted occupancy nobody has counted, and that a regime is not a threat.** Hollis Ashe is cooperative, bounded and correct, and called the boundary's answer a bad answer and said it was the correct one. **Neither office is defeated, neither concedes in words, and the charter's hole is now one institution wider in front of witnesses and is not fixed.**
- **Bel Ordry:** extended the plan, asked for a row for a hole and was refused in a room, **was doubted by the clerk with a reason and said which of his two answers was older**, asked five people to sign and accepted five refusals, refused to sign his own page, and said the plan does not leave this building. **A page in a coat is still not a system and the man is still the only one who has to say it.**
- **Dalla Sen:** named the three who could not be asked before asking anybody; entered a broken condition three times and said she knew on the day; doubted the keeper of a plan with a reason and entered that she arranged it; entered five reasons for not signing a plan and read them twice; **entered that nobody in a room with a stranger in it said the number in the room, and why; refused to put two questions next to each other when she was asked to, and entered that they are next to each other by accident and not by hand;** and is keeping writing a dead man's count every day and has said so out loud in three weeks running.
- **Tams Quill:** the crew's column moves by three on a named asking. **He gave the seventh reason for refusing to head the column, and it is worse, and it is not about a word.** He entered the fifteenth entry — a plan — into the unheaded column and said it is the second thing on that board that is not about a wall. **The board is not walked at all in Chapter 140 and he gives no reason and the clerk does not ask.** He names no day.
- **Iven Tallo:** asked for two hours and named the split, asked to be put on the other side of a door he would not pack, and asked that his refusal from two weeks earlier stand afterwards. **He offered a joiner's mark because it was his and he did not look at it, and withdrew it in his own words when a clerk read back the sentence he had said about a mark.** He is not a defector, not a martyr, not a saint, not redeemed, and not a signatory of anything.
- **Ilsa Norr:** the children are cold and she will not have the cold left out of the record; she refused a number on a page; **she told a room from a surface federation that this building has a count and would not tell them the number and said why, which is that a count of that kind is only true of a moment;** she said a third column is what a person does and a signature is what a person agrees to; **and in Chapter 140 she said that a building like this one is not a thing people live in, it is a thing they are in, and that the page with no row for the hole is part of it.**
- **Pell Roke:** reads numbers aloud, and only that. He read a courier's two lines and said what they are; he read twelve numbers in the plan's first column and said nothing about any of them; he said **there was nothing in it** in the fourth column for the third time in this book. **He is named as not askable, with the reason, in Chapter 132.** He did not go down the steps, into the corridor, or over the waist in any chapter, nobody asked him to, and he is not used as a route to his sister.
- **Wen Pask:** paid, kept, **seventy-five days and seventy-five nights at the end of the batch, and dead.** His count is not going to be seventy-six and the clerk has said so out loud in a room in three weeks running. **A chapter of this batch used the fact of his death and did not use him, and the reading of the count was not made into a scene about grief, because the reading is a working practice and not a funeral.**
- **The woman from the wash rooms:** not named, not asked, not rostered, not sent for. **Her covers were struck out of a fifth instrument in nine seconds, before anybody had asked, and the reason was not given at all for the first time in twenty-six weeks, and the clerk left the space where a reason would go empty because a page with a reason on it is a page somebody can read back to her.** The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, nobody was sent, and the page is still blank.
- **Oren Sill is not named. Dael Harrow is not named. Leena Orr's *a list is not a location* was used once, by her, in Chapter 140, where it earns itself.**

## Material and labour handoff

- **The room at the kitchen-line end of the corridor** — the worst room in this building, where the school has run since the twenty-first week, with a dished floor, a hearth corner, no mouth, a doorway wider than the anteroom's, and nine hearth stones — **has a cut in its floor under the hearth corner, made with stone and no bar, and the sill packed in stone in clay is still holding and is the only thing in this Hearthhold holding that floor up.** The ninth stone is propped two flags off its bed on a strip of crate board; the bed under it is a hand and a half down and a hole the width of Jo Verrick's hand; **a fortnight of a hole not getting worse is not a repair and she says so.** The fire in that room has not been lit for eight weeks.
- **The room's second column on the plan now carries a harder condition than the one it replaced**, written by the woman who keeps it: opened when the two people who laid the sill and held the stones have both said in a room that the clay has stopped shrinking, **and shut, without a vote and without a number and without anybody being sent, on the first morning on which the answer to this is no — the strip under the ninth hearth stone is still holding — said out loud, in a room, every morning this room is used, by a person who is not named on this page and is not named anywhere in this building's record of who keeps what. And if the answer is no twice, the nine come out, and they do not wait for a physician, and they do not wait for a meeting, and nobody in this building is to be told afterwards that they were told to wait.**
- **The corridor's low end.** The grate is **off**, levered with something the width of a dead stick, and there is no second grate in this Hearthhold. **Two flags and the crew's frayed nine-metre line are over the hole; the line is spent, it is the crew's, it is not an hour and it is not in the column.** The channel did not take its water back after the lever came off on the fourth day of the twenty-sixth week. **The review page is still blank and has three conditions on it, and the third is that nobody is to be sent anywhere to make it true, and the woman is not in the room, is not asked, is not sent for, and her floor is not going to be approached.** **The plan has no row for that place, and the refusal of that row is in a clerk's book with a reason in it, and the reason is the reason nobody was standing there when a man of twenty-two was found in the channel.**
- **The waist.** The ground there has moved three times and is not measured, by three people, on purpose. **The reason for that has now been given out loud in a room, in Jo Verrick's words, and entered, and it is a good reason: if they ever measured it and it was moving they would have to say so out loud, and then people would stand on it, and then a person would be under it who is not the one already there.** **The water came up over the fill on the fourth day of the twenty-seventh week and stood there, and the fill is holding, and there is still no number for it anywhere in this building.** The third wedge there is up a quarter of an inch and a bit and was not touched and nobody put a hand on the fill.
- **Wedges: seven sound and two dead sticks, and one of the two dead sticks is still gone.** Two at the school-door head, one in the school corner's door, three at the waist, one in the basket. **No wedge was bought, moved or added in this batch.** The clerk's material ledger still says two dead sticks and has been wrong since Batch 0003.
- **The anteroom frame** is unchanged: a finger and a bit out of true, shored, packed in stone and clay, **and the mark is off the wall and the second way out is a word.** **Its terms were read out against the original in Chapter 139 and the fifth of the five — the air engineer or the elected keeper able to stop it — has not been true since the middle of last month**, and the clerk entered that three times.
- **The seam: two jars a day, entered separately, never added to the pot, not sent anywhere.** The seam behind the anteroom's outer service door gave four threads at the first bell on the second day of the twenty-sixth week. **Jo Verrick said in a room that she could take five out of it and nobody would find out for about a week, and did not, in her own words, on the page.**
- **Crew hours: fifty-nine and a half, up three from fifty-six and a half, on the second day of the twenty-sixth week, and unmoved since.** The ask was made by the clerk in a room with the terms out loud, Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **and the three who could not be asked named with the reason for each before the asking.** **The crew have now been asked twice in twenty-seven weeks.**
- **Boundary hours: a hundred and seventeen and a quarter, plus a hundred and thirty-seven, = two hundred and fifty-four and a quarter.** The list adds **by the day the work was done**: **three, four, two, three, three in the twenty-sixth week; four, three, two, four, three in the twenty-seventh.** The ten sum to thirty-one. **Running figures with the day's increment and the total are given at the sixth bell of all ten chapters, which is the first time in this volume that has been true, and both columns reconcile, and the base implied by the two columns is the constant one hundred and seventeen and a quarter and the total is monotonic from Chapter 110 to Chapter 140. The reconciliation counter is carried unchanged at *twelve weeks* in every mouth in this batch and is not re-derived.**
- **The plan on butcher's paper has twelve rows, in four parts, in a coat, with a date in the top corner and no name anywhere, and it does not leave this building.** The first column holds a permitted occupancy and has never held a count of anybody. The second column holds a condition with no number and no day on each of the twelve. **The third column is what is done, in the hand of the person who keeps the row, eleven lines filled and one empty that the keeper will not name.** The fourth column is empty and unheaded with a reason in it in two hands and a modal struck out of one of them. **Two rows were added in Chapter 136, for the common landing and the anteroom step. A third was asked for, for the low end of the corridor, and refused. The tenth row carries three hands and an objection, and nobody has signed the plan.**
- **The board is fifteen entries: eleven nulls, one claim, one mark, one row and a plan; nine in the ordinary column and six in the column with nothing over the top of it.** The mark's entry is still on the board. The claim's condition is still unmet. **The column is still unheaded, for the seventh consecutive batch, and the reason was given on the second day of the twenty-sixth week and is not to be improved on.**
- **Two Compact cases are in the record and neither is an antagonist.** A reply sheet from the inspection line with a line for a name or a description sufficient to identify, and a printed line on the back of it headed for structures whose condition is kept by a person, with three rooms under it, one of them struck out in nine seconds. A market form on a board at a gate with two lines and a space in each of them, **which is now functioning as a pass.** The charter: seven signatures, no name, an office's number, eight clauses, **clause four a right against one office, and neither of the two people who came up the passage in Chapter 135 is that office.** The four sentences and a clerk's fair copy lie face up on the anteroom table with a market form beside them and two sheets of cheap paper weighted with a dead stick.

## Open handoff

**Volume 03 is open and Batch 0005 is owed at Chapters 141–150, the twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth weeks, and it carries the volume's climax.**

Named, still open, and deliberately unresolved: **a plan of rooms that is not yet a network of them, in a coat, with twelve rows, signed by nobody, that moved about forty people through a building in fifty minutes; a hole under a corridor floor that is the second way out of this building and a place a person can be killed, with no grate, no row, a blank review page and three conditions that forbid sending anybody; a fill at the waist that is holding with water standing on it and has no number in this building; a girl of nine in a room with a propped hearth stone and a bone that has moved; a condition checked every morning the room is used, with the nine coming out if the answer is no twice; a market day on the sixth day of this week, and a form with two lines and a space in each of them that this boundary has decided it will not fill in and has not decided what it will do instead; a courier in the building with her own three people and her own mark and a question nobody answered; a Compact procedure four pages long that assumes this boundary wants to be looked at, and a hardliner who has said in a room that a regime is not a threat; the air valve, the spring, the theory, and the name from the twelfth week, none of them asked; the ninth line, the four treads, the eighth term; the plan's one empty third-column line, which Bel Ordry will not name; the wrapped plate; the brass rule; Form 9-C; Form 7-B; the four households at the second gate; Iven Tallo's bond and an apprentice off the roll; a Quiet Hands cell of at least two, uncaught, with a legible reason and a low end of a corridor with nothing on the plan for it; and a person under a lip.**

**And the position the hand-over is built on, on the page, with nobody in the room having seen it: a room's second way out is a word, and the word was said by a person who is going to be in a room that had nine children in it, and the clerk repeats it, and nobody says it to a door. On the fourth day of the twenty-seventh week a room went above its number with the word still unsaid in it. The plan that said the room may hold ten has no signature on it and moved forty people and has nobody in it. The row that would have promised the low end of that corridor was refused, and the refusal is in a book with a reason, and the reason is why a man of twenty-two went into a channel in the dark. And the boundary has a count, in a clerk's book, in a teacher's clause, that it will not give to a surface federation, and a number nobody can give away is not the same thing as a number anybody can check. Nobody in this building joined the eleven and the ten this week and the clerk entered that she chose not to, and this batch has not recorded a second omission.**

The method is sound. One figure in Batch 0003's record does not reproduce and is not relied on: the recorded *150 paragraphs that do not begin with a quotation mark and do not begin with a bold marker* returns 139 on the delivered files. **That discrepancy is now explained and the explanation is in this file's own record: the recorded figures were taken with the ten `# Chapter NNN` title lines excluded and the section rules counted, and the method as written says neither, so the count did not reproduce. Excluding bolded paragraphs:** *The* 2, *Nobody* 1, *And* 3, *She* 5, *He* 3, fourteen together. **Including them:** *The* 4, *Nobody* 1, *And* 11, *She* 7, *He* 3, twenty-six together. **The *And* figure is the batch's real result and it is eleven against Batch 0003's twenty and Batch 0002's twenty-four.** On the first measure the batch carried 274 bold-opened paragraphs, of which 105 opened on *And*, 57 on *The* and 12 on *Nobody*. **Twenty-nine of the *And* openers, twenty-six of the *The* openers and eleven narrative *Nobody* openers were rewritten into other shapes** — *A physician was asked*, *At the fourth bell*, *Eighteen mornings in*, *One document in four parts*, *Somebody wanted a third row*, *For a while the room was quiet*, *There was no signature on it*, *Not one person watched them go* — and the section-divider count settled at 78. **The figure that carries information is the divider count, and the *And* divider is the tic this volume has, and Batch 0005 is asked to come in under eleven.**

## Calendar, fixed and carried forward

**The week runs Monday to Sunday. Chapters 131–135 are the twenty-sixth week** — 131 the **first day**, a Monday, the corridor shut, the room with nobody's condition on it and three places with water in them; 132 the **second day**, a Tuesday, the corridor shut, **the ask for a work and the seventh reason**; 133 the **third day**, a Wednesday, the corridor open, the school running, **a courier and a form**; 134 the **fourth day**, a Thursday, the corridor shut, **a fill nobody measures and a line struck out in nine seconds**; 135 the **fifth day**, a Friday, the corridor open, the school running, **two Compact cases**. **Chapters 136–140 are the twenty-seventh week** — 136 the **first day**, a Monday, the corridor shut, **the plan drafted and refused and signed by nobody**; 137 the **second day**, a Tuesday, the corridor shut, **a plan doubted and a name refused and a lie found**; 138 the **third day**, a Wednesday, the corridor open, the school running, **an objection stated first and a hand put under a hand**; 139 the **fourth day**, a Thursday, the corridor shut, **the only plan anybody can use**; 140 the **fifth day**, a Friday, the corridor open, the school running, **a place a person can be killed and a question nobody answered**.

**The standing arrangement holds and is untouched: the corridor is shut on the first, second and fourth days, open on the third, fifth and sixth, and the seventh day is not a crossing day; the school runs on the three open days.** So the corridor is shut in **131, 132, 134, 136, 137 and 139** and open in **133, 135, 138 and 140**. **The school corner's opening has not been reversed and no chapter in this batch put the school back in it, and the school ran in the room at the kitchen-line end on all four open days in this batch.** The open days lost in Chapter 108 and Chapter 130 are still lost and were not paid back in this batch. **The market day is the sixth day of the twenty-seventh week and is not in this batch.**

**The spoken measure of elapsed weeks is a separate register and was not re-derived, not corrected, and not used to date anything.** From the twentieth week onward *twenty* is the week clock itself and is not available as drift. **A count that tracks the week clock is a different thing and is re-derivable:** the plan has been transcribing the anteroom's count for twenty-seven weeks and had no row at all for the room nine children were being taught in until the third day of the twenty-fifth week, and the review page has been blank for twenty-seven weeks, and the clerk has been this boundary's clerk for twenty-six weeks in the twenty-sixth week and twenty-seven in the twenty-seventh. **Three week figures in the twenty-sixth week that read twenty-five were found and corrected to twenty-six in the review pass, and the counter is otherwise carried unchanged.**

**No in-batch event carries a day number as a date, and the highest value in the day-number register remains the forty-sixth day.** The day figures in the prose are the locked road (**four days up the middle passage to the middle gate**), the arrangement's *three days in seven*, week figures in mouths, and the count in the column with no heading. **A figure of four days attached to the second gate was found in Chapter 140 in the review pass and removed; the second gate's distance is stated nowhere in this batch.** No forward count of days or weeks is put on a courier, and **a notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time is neither repeated nor corrected.** Chapter 119's one bounded Compact-form exception was not used. The second sheet is undated, the market form has no date on it, and the two sheets of cheap paper have no date on them and no name on them and did not leave this building.

**Wen Pask's count runs one a day from the locked base of twenty-three on the fifth day of the seventeenth week, and it is fifty-five at the end of Batch 0002 and sixty-five at the end of Batch 0003.** So it is **66, 67, 68, 69 and 70** across Chapters 131–135 and **71, 72, 73, 74 and 75** across Chapters 136–140, **and every one of the ten is on the page in the right chapter.** **It is his own count, kept by a clerk, it lives in the column with no heading and in nothing else, it is not a register, and it may not date anything. It is also not the day-number register, and the two may never be confused, merged, or remarked upon as a coincidence.** It is at seventy-five and the clerk has said out loud, in a room, in three different weeks, that it is not going to be seventy-six and that she is going to keep writing it, and nobody has argued with her and nobody has thanked her.

## Review and repairs

**This batch was reviewed inside the writing session and the review record is `reviews/volume-03/batch-0004.md`. The first pass measured the batch and repaired the prose against the measurement, and it is a self-review and says so in its own first line. A review was then run outside the writing session against the delivered files and against this summary; it raised nine findings, one of them a defect in this file rather than in the prose. **Six produced a repair in the chapters or in the state files, two were cheap corrections, and one — the Ninefold Charter — was checked against the bible and the outline and is now recorded here as a clarification rather than as a repair, because no chapter is wrong and the ambiguity was in what the files did not say.** All nine are itemised in *Repairs applied in the review phase* below and in `state/continuity.md`.**

Seven things were repaired in the writing session and every one of them is in the files:

1. **A residual duplicated paragraph in Chapter 128 was found and removed** — the line *Dalla Sen said the thing she had come to say, which was not a fact*, which the Batch 0003 review record states was already repaired. Nothing else in Chapter 128 was touched. **A batch must be recounted from the files after any structural edit, and this is the second time that rule has caught something the editing session believed it had already done.**
2. **The connective tic was cut rather than managed.** On the first measure the batch carried 274 bold-opened paragraphs, of which 105 opened on *And*, 57 on *The* and 12 on *Nobody*, against Batch 0003's 20, 22 and 2. **Sixty-six openers were rewritten into other shapes and the divider count settled at 78.**
3. **Three automated markup passes went wrong and all three were repaired by recounting the files.** A quotation-normalising script split six multi-paragraph speeches and quoted five paragraphs of narration; a second pass quoted thirty-one section dividers as speech; a third left five narration paragraphs quoted and two paragraphs with an unbalanced quote. **The delivered form is one form, verified file by file: every file even on asterisks and on quotation marks, every paragraph with an even quotation count, no nested span, no trailing asterisk run, and no duplicated paragraph.** Only quotation marks moved; no prose was reworded by any pass.
4. **The calendar was wrong in three places and was corrected against the week clock.** The market day was described as not being this week in Chapter 133, as tomorrow in Chapter 139, and as in the morning in Chapter 140; **it is the sixth day of the twenty-seventh week and is now that in all three.** Chapter 138's *the day after tomorrow* was corrected to *this week has not got long left in it*.
5. **A figure of four days was attached to the second gate in Chapter 140 and removed.** A second gate is now *up the middle passage* with no figure on it, and the locked road of four days is attached only to the middle gate, where it has always been.
6. **Three week figures in the twenty-sixth week read twenty-five and now read twenty-six**, and the review page and the plan are at twenty-seven in the twenty-seventh week, so the week-tracking counts are monotonic across the batch.
7. **One meta leak was cut** — *the question this volume has been carrying* in Chapter 140's opening line — **and the three surviving uses of *in this book* were checked against the canon and are all in a mouth or in the clerk's own entry.**

**The batch's own self-review did not find a guardrail breach, and that is stated as a check and not as a boast: the marker on the anteroom's frame, the four marks and the groove, the ninth room, the four treads, the wrapped plate, the brass rule, Form 9-C, Form 7-B, the four households at the second gate, Talla Roke's brother, and the eleven-and-ten pairing were each checked by name against the prompt's prohibition list, and one breach was found and repaired, which was the four-day figure on the second gate, and one residual defect was found outside the batch, which was the duplicated paragraph in Chapter 128.**

**An independent review of this batch is owed, alongside `reviews/volume-02/batch-0003.md`, `batch-0004.md` and `batch-0005.md` for a closed canon volume and an independent review of Volume 03 Batch 0003.** None of those four files exists, and **nothing in this repository may describe Volume 03 Batch 0004, or Batch 0003, as independently reviewed.**

## Repairs applied in the review phase

**A review was run outside the writing session against the delivered files. It re-derived the mechanical claims independently and confirmed them: the calendar is exact, Wen Pask's count runs 66 to 75 one a day in the right chapter, the boundary arithmetic is exact on both columns with a constant base of one hundred and seventeen and a quarter, the crew's column moves once, and the guardrails hold — no System panel, the day-number register untouched, the eleven and the ten never in one breath, no meta leaks, no mark cut in stone, the wash-room woman unnamed and her floor unapproached, and Pell Roke never off the bench.** Nine defects were raised. All nine are closed. **The prose that was good was not touched: seven of the nine repairs are single sentences in existing paragraphs, one is two inserted paragraphs, and one is a state-file restoration.**

1. **This file had lost 381 lines, and two other files said it had not.** The Batch 0004 delivery replaced a stacked file with a single record. `state/current.md` and `workspace/volume-03/batch-0005/PROMPT.md` both told the next writer to read this file *because* it retains the Batch 0003 record, which carries the volume's midpoint reversal and the volume's one serious casualty, and the file did not contain it. **The Batch 0003, Batch 0002, Batch 0001 and Volume 03 Planning records are restored verbatim beneath this one**, with a reading order at the seam and a superseded marker on the Batch 0003 record, and the claim the other two files make is now true of the file again. The canon substance had survived in `state/continuity.md` and `state/current.md`; what was missing was the file the prompt pointed at.
2. **The school corner's opening was misdated by four weeks in three chapters and in one state file.** Chapter 115 has the door standing open at the end of the fifth day of the twenty-second week after the lamp test came out dry, and Chapters 116, 120 and 125 all treat it as already open, but Chapter 131 and Chapter 140 twice dated the opening to the first week of the twenty-sixth week, which is this batch. **All four are now the fifth day of the twenty-second week, which is the documented opening, in `chapter-0131.md`, twice in `chapter-0140.md`, and in `state/open-threads.md` under OT-93.** The same sentence in Chapter 131 also dated the *closure* to the first week of the nineteenth week, which cannot be right, because Chapter 101 has nine children would have been in that room in the twentieth week: **the closure is now the fourth day of the twentieth week, which is the day the condition naming it was read into the ledger in Chapter 104.** The throat-mouth above the door, its four marks and its groove are untouched and are still read two ways by two people and answer nothing.
3. **Chapter 131 dated the lifted condition to a Saturday.** Renn Vale's *I lifted a condition on Saturday morning* sat eight lines above a day-board of hers, and the lift was the first day of the twenty-fifth week, a Monday, which Chapter 137 states on the page in a clerk's hand. **It is now Monday morning**, and the same sentence's *I have had a week to think about what I own now* is then correct, because a week separates the two Mondays.
4. **The water at the waist was described three incompatible ways across Chapters 137 to 139.** A clerk's board read *has not gone anywhere* on the Tuesday, another read *has not moved* on the Wednesday, and Chapter 139 opened on the water coming up at the waist *for the second time in a fortnight* and had a trial pump maintainer say *it has come back over the fill*. **The water never left.** It reached the fill on the fourth day of the twenty-sixth week and it was still on it on the Thursday of the twenty-seventh, which is a week and not a fortnight. **Chapter 139's opening line and Jo Verrick's line are now the same fact as the two board reads**, and *I gave the reason on Thursday* is now *on the Thursday before*, so that the reason and the water are a day of a named week apart rather than ambiguous.
5. **The protagonist was absent from three chapters and this file's own state file said he was not.** The batch prompt required close third person on Marek Venn in all ten chapters with no viewpoint shift. **He was named in seven.** `state/character-state.md` asserted *named in ten of ten chapters, with interior life in ten of ten*, and the review's finding is that the assertion was false and that the review which produced it measures paragraphs, openers, markup, staging and length and had never checked viewpoint presence. **Both repairs were made and the prose was not restarted.** An interior beat was written for Chapter 135, in the hour in which a man from four days up a passage describes accurately the thing Marek Venn did in the twenty-fourth week, and one for Chapter 136, at the moment a physician says that a promise about a place where nobody can stand is a lie told in a column. **He was also already present in Chapter 137 and unnamed; he is now named once, where he takes up the lie on a page about a room he does not keep.** He is named in ten of ten. The two inserted paragraphs are 117 and 151 words, 268 between them, and they are the only prose in the batch that was written during the review phase rather than repaired in it.
6. **The recorded craft method did not reproduce as written.** The handed-over `205 / 127 / 78` is `217 / 139 / 78` on the raw text of the ten files, and it only becomes 205 / 127 / 78 with two exclusions that were never stated: the ten `# Chapter NNN` title lines out, and the forty-three `---` section rules counted rather than dropped. **Both exclusions are now stated in the same sentence as the figure**, the figures are recounted after the Chapter 135 and 136 repairs, and Batch 0003's own non-reproducing paragraph count is explained by the same cause. **The opener counts reproduce with no caveat on either batch, which is the review's own reason for trusting the opener count and not the paragraph count**, and that judgement stands.
7. **`state/current.md` carried the pre-batch board count.** It read *fifteen entries — eleven nulls, one claim, one mark and one row, nine in the ordinary column and five in the column with no heading*, which enumerates fourteen and splits nine and five. **It is now fifteen entries, one row and a plan, nine and six**, which agrees with this file, with `state/continuity.md`, with `state/character-state.md` and with the batch prompt.
8. **The lintel wobbled inside Chapter 140.** One paragraph said four marks and a groove *that are damaged*; a woman in the same scene said the groove is *the only thing up there that is not damaged*; the closing paragraph said four damaged marks and an undamaged groove. **All three now agree, and the two of them that had to change are the same two.** The chapter also introduced *the fifth stroke* as a disputed element without reconciling it against the canon phrase *four marks and one groove* that has stood since Chapter 106. **The fifth stroke is now one of the four marks being two strokes, said by the woman who reads them both ways**, so the stone still carries four marks and a groove and the dispute is still a dispute about a stroke and not about the number of marks.
9. **The Ninefold Charter is named in the batch prompt and appears in no chapter.** It is the dominant guild cartel of `bible/terminology.md`, and `outline/volume-03.md` commits Chapters 148 and 149 to it losing exclusive access to the market route. **It is a different instrument from this boundary's own charter** — seven signatures, an office's number, eight clauses, clause four a right against the Cartwright office — **and no chapter had ever said so, so a later writer would have had to guess whether the two were one thing.** No chapter is wrong and the planned plot is untouched. **The relationship is now recorded in `state/continuity.md` and `state/current.md`:** the market route's form and the board at the gate have never been attributed to any body and the attribution is available to Batch 0005; the boundary's own charter put no holder against any route and so cannot be the thing that loses exclusivity; and no chapter may retro-apply the guild name to the boundary's own instrument or to clause four.

**Two findings were checked and refused rather than applied.** The review recorded that the three missing Volume 02 review files and the two owed independent reviews are named rather than papered over, and that the `state/phase-ledger.json` and `NOVEL_SPEC.md` staleness is flagged as controller-owned: **both are correct as they stand and neither was touched.** And the review's own priority — fix the lost history first, because it is the one defect that will actively mislead the next writer — was taken in that order.
