# Volume 03, Batch 0002 — delivered, Chapters 111–120

**Ten chapters in `chapters/volume-03/`, close third person on Marek Venn, with one marked viewpoint shift, in Chapter 114.** The batch's delivery record is at the head of `state/batch-summary.md`; this section records only what a later phase must not contradict.

## What the batch established, in canon

- **The anteroom was emptied at the second bell in the pump's window for the first time in twenty-two weeks, and the word *door* was not said, because a room with nobody in it does not need a second way out.** The clerk entered that she did not say the word and did not repeat it. **Renn Vale put the sentence on it out loud — *a room nobody is in does not need a second way out, that is the reason it does not have one, do not let anybody in here find that out before the rest of us has* — and the clerk wrote it once.** This is a standing condition of the book and later batches may not treat it as a solution.
- **Nine people went out and the plan's first column says ten, and the page is right and the room is empty.** The clerk's finding is entered: **the number did not go anywhere when the people did.** Nobody joined it to anything.
- **The crew's column moved for the first time since the fifth day of the nineteenth week, from fifty-two and a half to fifty-three and a half, by one hour**, on an asking made in a room by Dalla Sen with the terms out loud and Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no. The hour's work is Iven Tallo looking at the head of the anteroom frame and giving four findings in the clerk's book.
- **The Marker stage was placed at Chapter 112, out of the anteroom's outer service door frame.** It is **chalk and gland grease on the dressed face of the jamb at the height of a hand, where anybody coming through that door can see it, and it is not cut**, because Renn Vale's objection is that a mark cut in a stone is a claim that outlasts the person who agreed to it. It has one direction (holding a head that is carrying nothing) and one stated limit (it carries the head of the frame and the clay in it and nothing else, and if the head takes a real weight it is not holding and everything said about it is out of date). Its condition is in Renn Vale's hand with no number and no day on it: *on while the head of this frame is out of true; off when the head has not been further out of true than the line on this jamb through a night and a morning, and I take it off and nobody argues with me about it.* **Nera Oduya is the second person who can stop it**, because the anteroom's air comes in at the service door and leaves at it, and the two of them can be stopped by each other.
- **All four costs are on the page and none is soft.** A road hand saw it in a doorway for four seconds and wrote it in a field book. The left hand burned, did not close that night, closed on the second morning, and was serviceable on the fourth. The anteroom's count arrived as a sound again, he knew what it was, and knowing did not stop it — **and the sound stayed after the mark came off.** Nera Oduya wrote the limit in her own mouth and gave the sentence to Marek Venn to say, on purpose, and said so out loud, and the clerk entered that she did it on purpose and why.
- **It saves nobody by itself, and the batch says so in Chapter 112 before it happens.** Nothing in the building is safer than it was the morning before; the shoring is still stone and lime and one wedge out of seven; the packing is still clay.
- **The mark's condition was met on the third day of the twenty-third week, a Wednesday, and Renn Vale took it off a jamb with a cloth in front of eleven people. Marek Venn was not allowed to touch it, and the reason she gave out loud is that if the man who puts a thing on a wall is the one who takes it off, then in a year there is a man in that room who can put things on walls and take them off and there is nothing on the wall to stop him.** The anteroom's frame is a finger and a bit out of true again and the anteroom's second way out is a word said to a page.
- **The school corner's floor is dry at the low corner, tested under a lamp through a night and a morning at two places and not the middle, and the room is open.** **The school is not in it and does not go back into it.** Renn Vale opened the room anyway so that no condition of hers is left on a page looking met while it is not. The closure, the opening and the un-restored school day are on the page together with a reason beside them and nothing between them. **No school day was restored and no closure was removed, and no chapter in this batch put the school back in the school corner.**
- **The school corner's mouth is now set by the woman who keeps the room.** Nera Oduya left a strip of dyed cloth in it at a width she would not have chosen and said why, and Renn Vale went down and set it to what she would have set, and Nera said *Good* and nothing else, and nobody was thanked.
- **The keeper's promise was kept, in person, at the second gate's counter, on the first of the month, and nobody in the batch says which day of the week that is.** Four doors were walked because nothing at that gate can summon anybody. **The true sentence was said and it is not good, and it fixed nothing, and the fourth household asked *will it be open again* and the answer was *I do not know*.** Nobody in this building knows when he arrives and the room has decided not to write down how long he has been gone. Wenna Dray stated that nobody is going to be cruel about the lock, nobody is going to hurry, and at the end of it the water is still a step away and down a slope, exactly as it was before anybody surveyed it, and that nobody did anything wrong.
- **The sealed archive answered one question, asked in a room by a person, and the answer is a fact about a room and not a cause.** Room eleven of the lower row of Hearthhold Middle is entered in the inventory as a records room, and under the entry, on the same sheet, in a hand nobody can date, there is one more line: **the bench is to be kept clear.** There is no bench in room eleven and there never has been in any inventory, and the Middle's route keeper has stood in the room himself and has refused **in writing** to say what it means. **The resemblance to the dowel and to the plan is not a resolution and nobody joined it to the charter, the mouth, the four treads, the air engineer's theory or the plate.**
- **The market route's first form arrived and the first toll on it is not money.** Seven lines: business stated at the gate, a name, a number of persons, what is carried, the person responsible, a signature, and a countersignature by a person of that office. **Five of seven were objected to in a room and nothing was marked until it had been argued.** The word in the form for not doing it is **attended** — the same word the second gate's water-lock notice used and the same word this boundary reads four hundred times a day — and it is not compulsory, it costs nothing, and four gates in a month have printed it and none of them has asked anybody what this boundary means by it.
- **The boundary's answer to the market form is two sentences with no name and no signature**, and it went out **on a market day** and not on a carrying day, **because a market day is not a delivery and the charter's protection runs to a road that is not shut for a delivery and may not be charged for.** The clerk said that out loud before the sheet left anybody's hand. Bel Ordry did not put his ring on it. It went with a man going that way anyway and by nobody else, and the boundary has not sent anybody.
- **A guild survey worked this boundary's sector under a clearance the charter does not mention and found it stable, and the survey is right.** Three wedge holes at the waist, dated, none the same date, total movement between a finger and a hand, seasonal, **not a fault** — which is the answer to twenty-two weeks of three people deciding on purpose never to measure it. The frame is **a bad repair on a sound wall.** The school corner's floor is **a use**, and the surveyor told the room that in a building this old the difference between a use and a fault is a matter of whose floor it is. **And the finding and the fact that a sound sector gets no crew put in it again are in the same sheet on purpose, and the man who put them there said so and said he would do it again.** The timber the halfpenny sheet promised is in the survey camp's store.
- **The mark's visibility cost is not the mark; it is the record of the mark.** A Compact inspector came up the passage with a form of five lines, filled in three of them — an inscription, a condition and a limit, **and no name** — and told the room that the worst of it is the fifth, because her clerk has already filled that line once with a **title**, *the person who keeps the anteroom's terms*, and **a title is worse than a name, because a title is a post and a post can be asked for by a body that has never met the person who holds it.** Renn Vale's answer is that there is nothing here to be sent for, that she would rather be named and refused than titled and found, and that she does not know which of the two she would survive.
- **The rule that can be read off a page cost what it cost.** The market form lay face up on the anteroom table by the clerk's own choice, and **a woman from another office read all seven lines off it in about eleven seconds and nobody in that room stopped her**, and Bel Ordry's four sentences came out of the coat and were read out loud with a stranger standing at the end of them. **The clerk entered that she chose to put the form there and is not putting it away, because this boundary is going to be read from outside whether it is on a table or in a drawer, and the only thing it gets to choose is whether a stranger finds it in a room with people in it.**
- **The charter's hole is one institution wider than it was and is not fixed.** The charter names the Cartwright office. Three bodies have now come to this boundary that the four sentences do not name: the Compact inspection line, the guild survey camp, and the market gate. The boundary has four instruments and one procedure, has used that procedure for a body it does not name, and **has refused to write one for a third, on the standing reason: a document that gets amended every time it is inconvenient is the guild's counter-draft with better manners.**
- **The board on surfaces is thirteen entries: eleven nulls, one claim, and one mark, nine in the ordinary column and four in the column with no heading.** The mark is entered on its own terms, is **not a null and not a claim and not a reading**, and **was not taken off the board when it was stopped**, on the count's reason that the mark stopping is a fact about the mark and not about the entry.
- **The position the volume's midpoint reversal will exploit is on the page and nobody saw it coming.** The anteroom's second way out is a word said to a page; the word is written down in a stranger's hand; a boundary surveyed and found sound will not be inspected again when it changes; a room with nobody in it does not need a second way out; a room with nine children in it has no row on the plan at all. **At the seventh bell of Chapter 118 the clerk had the chalk in her hand and did not put those facts side by side, and has never given a reason.**

## Numbers a later batch must not re-derive

- **The week runs Monday to Sunday. Volume 03 opened in the twentieth week. 101–105 the twentieth, 106–110 the twenty-first, 111–115 the twenty-second, 116–120 the twenty-third, 121–125 the twenty-fourth, 126–130 the twenty-fifth, and so on to 146–150 the twenty-ninth.** Each chapter sits on the matching day of its week. **The corridor is shut on the first, second and fourth days, open on the third, fifth and sixth, and the seventh day is not a crossing day; the school runs on the three open days.** So in Batch 0002 the corridor is shut in **111, 112, 114, 116, 117 and 119** and open in **113, 115, 118 and 120**.
- **The school corner is now open rather than shut, and the opening changed no corridor day and restored no school day.** The school is in the worst room in this building on the three open days exactly as it was. **No chapter may put the school back in the school corner and no chapter may treat the opening as a restored school day.**
- **One of the three open days is still lost from Chapter 0108 against a closure added on a day the arrangement had open. Nothing is paid back. Ilsa Norr has not been told which of the two facts is the independent one and has not asked, and no later batch may tell her.**
- **Wen Pask's count is 46 in Chapter 111 and 55 in Chapter 120, one a day, on the locked base of twenty-three on the fifth day of the seventeenth week, and all ten are on the page in the right chapter.** It is his own count, kept by a clerk, in the column with no heading and in nothing else, and **it is not a register and may not date anything. It is also not the day-number register, and the two may never be confused, merged, or remarked upon as a coincidence.**
- **No day number may be attached to any in-batch event. The day-number register's highest value remains the forty-sixth day.** The only date on any object is the date in the top corner of the plan. **One bounded new exception exists: a Compact form has a line for the date observed, and the inspector says she is required to fill it, would fill it, and that it is the only lie on the form. That is a fact about a form and is not available to any other instrument.** The second sheet remains undated and the archive's answer came back undated and the market form has no date on it.
- **The spoken measure of elapsed weeks is a separate register**, is not re-derived, is not corrected, and may not be used to date anything. **From the twentieth week onward *twenty* is the week clock itself and is not available as drift.** A count that tracks the week clock is a different thing and is re-derivable: the school corner's mouth has been shut for twenty-two weeks in the twenty-second week and is opened on the fifth day of it, and the plan has been transcribing the anteroom's count for twenty-two weeks.
- **No forward count of days or weeks is put on a courier.** The road is four days up the middle passage to the middle gate and then on, **and the second gate's distance is stated nowhere in Batch 0002.** Bel Ordry **refused in a room to put a figure on how long the archive's answer would take.** **The batch's standing discovery about a notice with no date on it was neither repeated nor corrected.**
- **Crew hours: fifty-three and a half, up one from fifty-two and a half, and unmoved since the first day of the twenty-second week.** The hour was Iven Tallo's, asked for in a room with the terms out loud. **The reason is in Renn Vale's words and in the clerk's hand and in the book, and the count declined to give it because a clerk gave it better.**
- **Boundary hours: a hundred and seventeen and a quarter, plus thirty-five, = a hundred and eighty-eight and a quarter, and seventy-one since the keeper signed.** The list adds **by the day the work was done**: four, three, five, four, three in the twenty-second week; four, three, four, three, two in the twenty-third. Running figures are given at the sixth bells of 111, 112, 115, 117, 118, 119 and 120, and both columns reconcile and have reconciled for ten weeks.
- **The column with no heading holds a leg, a bundle, a man's count, a half hinge, a line refused, a page gone out of sight, a wage, and a mark — and it is still unheaded, for the fifth consecutive batch.** The count **said out loud, for the first time in five batches, that he has run out of reasons**, and the clerk entered the omission and entered that she noticed it and did nothing about it. **It was referred to and not itemised, and the clerk also stopped reading it out in full**, on the entered reason that a thing read in full four times is a thing with a shape.
- **Wedges: seven sound and two dead sticks, unchanged in number, none bought, none added.** The third wedge at the waist is up a quarter of an inch and a bit and **the ground there has now been measured for the first time by a third party**, which found three wedge holes, none the same date, between a finger and a hand in total, seasonal, and not a fault. **The three people who decided on purpose never to measure it have not been asked to comment and have not been.**
- **The pot is at ten days, has been ten days for twenty-six days, and has not gone up and did not go up in Batch 0002.**
- **The brass survey rule has now said nothing for longer than twelve weeks**, and nobody looked at it in this batch.
- **The right hand's fine control is not recovered. The left hand burned at the Marker, did not close that night, closed on the second morning, was serviceable on the fourth, and is not what it was.** The load echo in the body **stayed after the mark was stopped**, and he says he does not know what it is and has had since the second day of the twenty-second week to guess and has not guessed.
- **The Reader stage is not repeatable and was not used.** The Chapter 99 claim is still a claim and its condition is still not met. **No route change, no binding, no relay, no brace, and no mark cut in the stone anywhere in this building.**

## Repairs applied to Batch 0002

**This batch was reviewed twice. The first review was a self-review run in the writing session, which rewrote the prose and then certified it. The second was independent, found a whole class of defect the first had certified as clean, and the repairs below are the result of both. The independent review's findings are in items 10 to 16.**

A self-review was run against the delivered prose in the writing session and **the findings were repaired in the chapters, not recorded and deferred.** The repairs that changed a fact or a count:

1. **The boundary's hours did not add, and one running figure was wrong.** Chapter 120 said *thirty-five since the keeper signed* where the arithmetic gives seventy-one. **It now gives both figures: thirty-five in these ten chapters and seventy-one since the keeper signed.** Every other running figure was checked against the day list and is exact.
2. **Wen Pask's count was on the page in only five of the ten chapters.** 47, 49, 50, 52 and 53 were missing. **All ten are now on the page in the right chapter**, and 114's is in the narrator's note under the scene, because the boundary's book is four days back down the passage and the counter scene is not in this building.
3. **Marek Venn was named in only five of the ten chapters.** The prompt requires seven with interior life and both of the last two. **He is now named in nine — 111, 112, 113, 115, 116, 117, 118, 119 and 120 — with interior life in all nine, and 114 is the one chapter he is not in and is carried entirely by Sefu Aran.** Four interior beats were added: what he cannot say in Chapter 115 when the school corner opens without the school, putting a question down in Chapter 116 because the air engineer has said *nobody asked me anything* in the tone of a woman who has been counting, wanting to take the market form in Chapter 117 and not being able to be useful at the end of the road, and a stranger saying out loud in Chapter 119 a thing about himself that he had not worked out.
4. **Chapter 112 came out of the writing session at 4,416 words**, above the 4,000 ceiling. **It was cut by 421 words to 3,995 without losing a beat** — the trimming was of repeated restatements in the consent argument, the limit handoff, the act itself, and the board, and the four costs of the stage are all intact.
5. **Nine instances of meta language were cut**: *this chapter does not say which*, *and this chapter is about that*, *the whole of this chapter turns on*, *because the volume has a habit of making these things larger*, *the twenty-second chapter of Volume 02*, *and this is why the next four months*, *and that is where the chapter's oldest piece of business is*, *the night of the reader*, and *when the reader is a market gate*.
6. **Six markup defects were repaired**: two unclosed bold spans, one trailing over-close, two nested spans where a bold span closed inside an italic one, and one triple-asterisk run. **Every file is now even, every file's paragraph-level balance is zero, there is no nested span, and there is no run of three or more asterisks at the end of any paragraph.**
7. **A doubled attribution was repaired in Chapter 119** — *it had been filled in, Hollis Ashe's clerk had filled it in* — and three identical short paragraphs were rewritten so that the batch's duplicated-paragraph count is **one, and that one is deliberate**: Renn Vale's condition, read out word for word when it is met and again when it is acted on, because the room checks a condition by reading it out again against the original.
8. **The chapter's craft figures were re-measured rather than estimated, and the batch was reworded against them.** Sixteen narrative *The* openers were moved to the book's own bolded-clause convention, sixteen *Nobody* and *not one person* openers were rewritten into other shapes, **and sixteen bold `**And …**` section dividers were cut or rewritten outright**, which took the bold-stripped *And* count from 40 in the first pass to **24 against Batch 0001's 41** — the one place this batch is genuinely better than the last, and the one the Batch 0001 reviewer named as the real lever.
9. **The staging debt Batch 0001 left is paid.** Batch 0001 had seven of ten chapters unambiguously staged away from the anteroom bench and named Chapter 106 as the one that still needed it. **All ten of this batch's chapters are staged elsewhere**, and **Chapter 114 is in a different building four days up a road with a body in every scene.**

**Then the independent review, and what it found that the self-review had certified as clean:**

10. **Twelve day numbers were attached to in-batch events and every one of them was wrong.** The mark goes on in Chapter 112, the second day of the twenty-second week, and comes off in Chapter 118, the third day of the twenty-third — **a span of eight days, not the nine the batch said.** Eight instances of *nine days* and *nine days ago* in Chapters 118 and 120; four of *ten days* and *ten days before* in Chapter 112, which points back at the refusal in Chapter 109 and is five days; *eight days later* in Chapter 115, which is three days; *six days ago* in Chapter 119, which is a fortnight; and *three weeks ago* in Chapter 120, dating the same speech in the same room that Chapter 112 dates five days back. **Every one has been removed rather than corrected, because a count of days between two in-batch events is a day number on an in-batch event whatever its arithmetic and the prompt forbids it. They are now given as a day of the week or a day of a named week, and the two ends of the mark are the second day of the twenty-second week and the third day of the twenty-third.**
11. **Chapter 116 put a forward count of weeks on a courier** — the archive's answer came up the passage *some weeks later* — which breaks the guardrail against forward counts on a courier and contradicts its own scene, since the question is asked and the answer read out in the same chapter. **The count is gone.** The three instances at item 10 that this review did not find — *eight days later* in 115, *six days ago* in 119 and *some weeks later* in 116 — were turned up while verifying its findings rather than by it.
12. **Chapter 117 named a day the scene had not reached**, saying *a mark that was off a wall by Thursday* when the mark comes off on the Wednesday. **The clause now states something true on the Tuesday it is written** — a mark on a doorframe that a man has already stood in a doorway in front of for four seconds and not stopped at, which is what Chapter 113 puts in the clerk's book.
13. **Three state files misdated the batch's climax by three days**, saying the mark was stopped on the *sixth* day of the twenty-third week where Chapter 118 and the batch's own calendar section both say the *third*. **All three are corrected, in this file, in `state/current.md` and in `state/batch-summary.md`.**
14. **Two pre-existing markup defects in Chapter 120** that the self-review's own method could not see: an orphaned trailing `**` closing a bold span that had already closed eight clauses earlier, and a bold span in a quoted speech that closed early and left an orphan close at the end of the paragraph. **The claim that every file's paragraph-level balance was zero was therefore false — Chapter 120 was at 2. It is at 0 now.**
15. **Three figures in the self-review did not reproduce** and are corrected in `reviews/volume-03/batch-0002.md` and in `state/batch-summary.md`: *read back* is **5**, not 3, and Batch 0001's is **4**, not 3, so the batch went up by one and the *held exactly* claim rested on an unreproducible number; **the batch total is 29,893 words**, not 32,896, which is not reproducible at any point in the batch's history; and **the duplicated-prefix count is 0** under the stated method, not 1, because **the two deliberate verbatim repeats both open inside dialogue** — Renn Vale's condition in Chapters 112 and 118, not 115 and 118, and the boundary's hours read out as a bare list of figures in Chapters 110 and 115.
16. **Two things were deliberately not changed.** **The *read it back* count stays at 5** rather than being cut to a target, because the beat is the clerk's working practice and cutting good prose to satisfy a counting rule is the wrong trade. **And the spoken week register — *a fortnight*, *three weeks*, *five months*, *in a month*, *about three weeks* — is untouched**, because the prompt establishes it as a separate register that is not re-derived and not corrected, and because it is load-bearing in the two places where a character is imprecise on purpose. **The rule for Batch 0003: a day number is a date and is load-bearing; a week figure in a mouth is a register and is not.**

**Nothing else moved.** No scene was rewritten, no beat was cut, no character was relocated, and nothing was added to or removed from the plan. **The mark's four costs, both acts of trust, the board's arithmetic, the hours, the calendar, Wen Pask's ten counts, the staging of all ten chapters away from the anteroom bench, and the omission the volume's midpoint reversal depends on are all intact and were re-read after the pass.**

## Two things Batch 0002 leaves for Batch 0003

1. **The board is a beat in four chapters, not ten — 112, 115, 118 and 120 — and in Chapter 119 it is deliberately not walked at all**, for the first time in twenty-two weeks, because there is a woman in the anteroom from another office. The other five chapters close on something else. **Batch 0003 should keep the board off the closing beat in most chapters and not repeat the Chapter 119 omission without a reason that is as good.**
2. **The position the reversal needs is on the page and the room does not see it.** This is not a summary of the batch; it is the exact ground Batch 0003 stands on, and the prompt for that batch lists it as a non-negotiable. **What must not happen is a character noticing it. The clerk's omission in Chapter 118 is the mechanism, and it must not be undone, explained or noticed.**

## How this batch was written

**Ten chapters were written in one session in chapter order, then measured, then repaired against the measurement, and the repairs were made in the chapters.** Two problems were structural rather than cosmetic and both were fixed by the same lever the Batch 0001 reviewer had identified: **the first pass carried Batch 0001's density of bold section dividers and its density of *Nobody* and *The* openers, and both were cut rather than managed.** The Marker chapter was over the length ceiling and was cut by 421 words. **There was no checkpoint draft for this batch, so none of the batch was replaced, and the chapter voices are continuous with 101–110.**

# Volume 03, Batch 0003 — delivered, Chapters 121–130

**Ten chapters in `chapters/volume-03/`, close third person on Marek Venn, no viewpoint shift.** The batch's delivery record is at the head of `state/batch-summary.md`; this section records only what a later phase must not contradict.

## What the batch established, in canon

- **The volume's midpoint reversal is delivered, and it is `bible/power-system.md`'s own worked failure case.** The room at the kitchen-line end of the corridor — the worst room in the building, where the school has run since the twenty-first week, with a dished floor, a hearth corner, no mouth, a doorway wider than the anteroom's, and nine hearth stones — is leaking. The only ordinary repair this Hearthhold owns is **stone in clay in its sill**, which is the bedding that sill already had nine hundred years ago by a tool that is not a mason's. **Marek Venn recommends that the room be shut, says the alternative out loud, and names the numbers: eleven behind the door, fourteen at the kitchen line, and the higher number is on the other side of the door.** He says each number twice on purpose and the clerk enters that she did not know it was on purpose when she wrote the first one. **He does not decide in a hurry and nobody accuses him of hurrying.**
- **He does not have the power to do it alone and is not asked to, and the door is closed by the person who keeps the room, on his recommendation.** The person who keeps it is **the schoolteacher, Ilsa Norr**, and the working practice is that any change to a room people use is written by the person who will keep it. *Shut* is struck in her hand and *closed* written over it. **The condition has no number and no day on it**: the room is opened when the clay under that sill has stopped shrinking, and the person who decides that is the man who held the stones and the man who beat the clay, and they have to be in a room together and both of them have to say it. Renn Vale and Nera Oduya can stop it and can be stopped by each other.
- **The door is not wedged, on a stated reason**: a wedged door is a door a person can open with a shoulder, and a schoolteacher wants the only way out of a room with nine children in it to be a decision. **The system works exactly as designed and produces a trapped room.** The room holds; the structure is saved; **the corridor's low end is saved**, because the water that had been reaching a low point in the corridor is stopped at a packed sill. **The ventilation and the only exit are gone.**
- **The second way out of that room is a word, and it was said in a corridor by the eleven people who were going to be in it, one at a time, and the clerk repeated it eleven times, and nine of them did not know what it was for and the teacher said *in case*.** It opened nothing. **On the next morning the clerk said it at a shut door into an empty room and repeated it, and there was nobody in the room to say it, and the rule could not be kept and was not kept.**
- **The cost is people and it is counted honestly.** **The count is read out at both ends of a corridor in the number eleven, and the number is said before the name, and the name is Orla Kern, nine, the fourth of the nine.** The ninth hearth stone has gone over a hand's width at its low side and down at the front, and there is a hole under it the width of Jo Verrick's hand, and **she says the lime that let go was not the water's — the water went away — and that it was nine children on a warm stone for five weeks, and that she said on the Monday that she would not put a cat on that bed and nobody went back to it.** The condition was not met and the door was opened anyway on a child's foot, **because a slate is a thing a room agrees to in a room and that morning the room was full of one person.**
- **His first public failure is read out in a room, in his own words, with the number in it**, out of a book of his own that nobody else has read, which the clerk says out loud before she reads it. **The boundary does not forgive him and does not blame him, and the two are said in that order by the cook, by the teacher and by the nine words of the man himself.** **Renn Vale says out loud what the working practice is actually worth, which is that she is not the one a doctor looks at, and that the rule does not say the person who keeps it gets to be comfortable.**
- **Mero Senn appears, in Chapter 127, as the aftermath and not a rescue.** Forty-five, twenty-two years, came down the last of the middle passage from the second gate, says what he is before anybody asks and says the thing that is against him before he looks at the child, and **was not in the room when the door was opened and was not sent for.** **His rule is the volume's instrument — *a plan without a named injured person is not a plan; a plan with an acceptable casualty is not automatically acceptable* — and a schoolteacher said it in a corridor the day before he arrived and did not know whose it was, and four people in this building have been doing his work for twenty-five weeks without knowing it.** He sets the foot and says the set is correct and bad and that both are true. **He is wrong in public about the room, is told so by Jo Verrick, and says so first.** He does not fix anything, does not soften anybody, and is not a saint and is not a rebuke.
- **The plan on butcher's paper has a tenth row, and the number in its first column is a permission.** Bel Ordry says the reason out loud before the page is opened. **The row was written at the sixth bell of the third day of the twenty-fifth week on the back of a day-board. First column: a ten, in the cook's hand, and it is a permitted occupancy and not a count of people, and the cook says out loud that she did not use eleven and why. Second column: a condition with no number and no day on it, in Renn Vale's hand. Third column: Ilsa Norr's own hand, and she stood up and said yes to it. Fourth column: still empty, with its reason in two hands, read out with the strike.** The plan is in four parts in a coat and does not leave the building.
- **A boy of fourteen read the first column aloud in a room and the new number was in it and he said ten.** **The number is a permission and not a count of people, and the number in the room was eleven, and nobody in the building joins the two numbers and the book does not join them either.** The clerk, who has spent twenty-five weeks putting facts next to each other on purpose, **did not put the two numbers next to each other, and this batch does not record a second omission.** **The chapter's omission of Chapter 118 is not undone, explained, or noticed anywhere in Chapters 121–130.**
- **A Quiet Hands cell is found after a sabotage, its reason is legible, and its dead are dead in the same chapter.** Two sheets of cheap paper in one hand, folded twice, pressed with a thumb, **weighted with one of this building's two dead sticks**, found under a flag in the covered channel at the low end of the corridor. **Their argument is that two offices have printed a line with a space in it for a person in this boundary, that a line with a space in it is a post being cut, and that a title is not a name because a name can be refused and a title is a box a letter goes into.** Their fourth line is about the survey's finding that the sector is stable and is true. Their second sheet **is a column of the rooms of this building.** **Three people say out loud that they understand why, and nobody is recruited, and the clerk enters the difference between understanding a reason and agreeing with it.** **Mero Senn says that a reason can be legible and a person can still be dead, and says the good half of the plan's empty fourth column, which he had not read.** The cell is not named, not caught and not spoken to. **The volume's one serious casualty is Wen Pask, twenty-two, apprentice carpenter, three years, out of the middle gate's store, no bond, paid, sixty-four days and sixty-four nights into a count that was his own at the finding, found in the channel at the low end of the corridor under where the grate is. Nobody sent him.**
- **The grate at the low end is off and there is no second one.** Two flags and the crew's frayed nine-metre line, which is spent and is the crew's, are over the hole, and the line **went to a hole on a Friday and is not counted as an hour** and the crew's column does not move. **The review page is still blank.** The woman's two sentences on it are read out of the page by the clerk, and she is not in the room, is not asked, is not sent for, and her three conditions stand in a clerk's hand without a name against them.
- **The board is fourteen entries: eleven nulls, one claim, one mark and one row; nine in the ordinary column and five in the column with nothing over the top of it.** The mark's entry is still on the board. **The claim's condition is still unmet.** The row is the first entry on that board that is not about a wall. **The column is still unheaded, for the sixth consecutive batch, on a new reason and it is worse: a heading would put a room under a word, and a word is portable and rooms are not, and the only protection a wage has ever had in this Hearthhold came out of a hearth stone.**
- **Nera Oduya spent one of Volume 03's five acts of trust, and it is the one the batch prompt named**: she opposes Marek Venn in public, in a room with twelve people in it, on a matter that matters, and she is right, and nobody consoled her, and she says out loud that she knows who is going to lose and that it is not she. **The other two acts are Batches 0004 and 0005.** She also put herself into a condition in a room without being asked, struck the woman's covers out of a fourth instrument in nine seconds without a reason, and did not say her theory.
- **The charter's hole is one institution deeper as well as wider.** A reply sheet came up the passage from the same inspection line with a line for a name or a description sufficient to identify, and a printed line on the back of it headed for structures in the boundary whose condition is kept by a person, with three rooms under it. **One of the three was the wash rooms and the air engineer struck the heading and the three entries in nine seconds without coming down the steps and gave no reason for the fourth time in this book, and nobody asked her.** **The clerk enters that somebody four days up the middle passage has put a keeper against a row on a page that has never left this building, and that she is not going to write the rest of that sentence.**

## Numbers a later batch must not re-derive

- **The week runs Monday to Sunday. 101–105 the twentieth, 106–110 the twenty-first, 111–115 the twenty-second, 116–120 the twenty-third, 121–125 the twenty-fourth, 126–130 the twenty-fifth, 131–135 the twenty-sixth, 136–140 the twenty-seventh, 141–145 the twenty-eighth, 146–150 the twenty-ninth.** Each chapter sits on the matching day of its week. **The corridor is shut on the first, second and fourth days, open on the third, fifth and sixth, and the seventh day is not a crossing day; the school runs on the three open days.** So in Batch 0003 the corridor is shut in **121, 122, 124, 126, 127 and 129** and open in **123, 125, 128 and 130**.
- **The school corner is still open and is still not used, and no chapter in Batch 0003 put the school back in it.** The school ran in the room at the kitchen-line end on the third and fifth days of the twenty-fourth week and on the third day of the twenty-fifth week, **and did not run on the fifth day of the twenty-fifth week, and that loss is entered in a schoolteacher's own words and is not paid back.** The open day lost in Chapter 108 is still lost. **Two open days have now been lost since the school was moved, in two different weeks, for two different reasons, and neither is paid back, and Ilsa Norr has still not been told which of the two facts is independent and has not asked.**
- **Wen Pask's count is 56 in Chapter 121 and 65 in Chapter 130, one a day, on the locked base of twenty-three on the fifth day of the seventeenth week, and all ten are on the page in the right chapter.** **It is at sixty-five and the clerk has said out loud, in a room, that it is not going to be sixty-six and that she is going to keep writing it anyway. It is his own count, kept by a clerk, in the column with no heading and in nothing else, it is not a register, it may not date anything, and it may not be confused, merged or remarked upon as a coincidence with the day-number register.**
- **No day number may be attached to any in-batch event. The day-number register's highest value remains the forty-sixth day.** The only date on any object is the date in the top corner of the plan, and **Chapter 119's one bounded exception — a Compact form's line for *the date observed*, which the inspector says is the only lie on it — stands and was not used in this batch.** The second sheet is undated, the market form has no date on it, and **the two sheets of cheap paper found in the channel have no date on them and no name on them.**
- **The spoken measure of elapsed weeks is a separate register**, is not re-derived, is not corrected, and is not used to date anything. **From the twentieth week onward *twenty* is the week clock itself and is not available as drift.** A count that tracks the week clock is a different thing and is re-derivable: **the plan has been transcribing the anteroom's count for twenty-five weeks.**
- **No forward count of days or weeks is put on a courier.** The road is four days up the middle passage to the middle gate and forty days on from the top of it to the guild file, **and the second gate's distance is stated nowhere in Batch 0003.** **The batch's standing discovery about a notice with no date on it is neither repeated nor corrected.**
- **Crew hours: fifty-six and a half, up three from fifty-three and a half, and unmoved since the fourth day of the twenty-fourth week.** The three hours were two of Iven Tallo's and one of Marek Venn's, on an asking made in a room with the terms out loud by the clerk with Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **and with the three who could not be asked named with the reason for each.** A piece of the crew's frayed line went to a hole in Chapter 130 and **is not an hour and is not in the column.**
- **Boundary hours: a hundred and seventeen and a quarter, plus thirty-one, = two hundred and twenty-three and a quarter, and a hundred and six since the keeper signed.** The list adds **by the day the work was done**: **four, three, two, three, three in the twenty-fourth week; four, three, four, three, two in the twenty-fifth.** Running figures are given at the sixth bells of **121, 123, 124, 125, 126, 127, 128, 129 and 130**, both columns reconcile, and they have reconciled for twelve weeks. **The base implied by the two columns is a constant one hundred and seventeen and a quarter at every chapter that states both, and the running total is monotonic from 110 to 130. Do not re-derive either figure; carry both.** *(Corrected in the Batch 0003 review phase. The total was short by exactly one hundred from Chapter 124 to Chapter 130 and the day list for 124 was overstated; see `reviews/volume-03/batch-0003.md`, repairs 1 and 2.)*
- **The column with nothing over the top of it gains a row and stays unheaded for the sixth consecutive batch**, and the refusal now has a stated reason.
- **Wedges: seven sound and two dead sticks, and one of the two dead sticks is gone.** Two at the school-door head, one in the school corner's door, three at the waist (the third up a quarter of an inch and a bit), one in the basket. **No wedge was bought, moved or added in this batch. The clerk's material ledger still says two dead sticks and she has entered that it is wrong and that she never looked in the basket.**
- **The pot is at ten days, has not gone up since the fifth day of the nineteenth week, and did not move on the night a man died in the low end of this corridor.**
- **The brass survey rule has now said nothing for longer than fifteen weeks**, and nobody looked at it in this batch.
- **The right hand's fine control is not recovered. The left hand burned at the Marker and is not what it was. The Reader stage is not repeatable and was not used, and the Chapter 99 claim's condition is still unmet. No route change as a stage, no binding, no relay, no brace, and no mark cut in the stone anywhere in this building.**

## Repairs applied in Batch 0003

**This batch was reviewed twice in the writing session. The first pass measured the batch and repaired the prose against the measurement. The second pass was a structural check run against the files after the length cuts, and it found real damage, and the damage was in the chapters.**

1. **Six chapters were over the length ceiling and were cut in the chapters.** Chapters 128 and 130 came out of the writing session at 4,236 and 4,246 words and were cut to 3,895 and 3,981. The cut was of repeated restatement, not of beats: the row-writing, the physician's speeches, the cook's reasons, the board, and the closing catalogue.
2. **The connective tic was cut rather than managed.** The first pass carried **thirty-seven** bold `**And …**` section-divider openers against Batch 0002's twenty-four, and seventeen were rewritten into other shapes, which also took eleven plain `**The …**` openers out of the count. **The primary *And* count is zero and the bold-stripped *And* count is twenty, both the best figures in the volume.**
3. **A paragraph-index edit during the length pass introduced six duplicated paragraphs — two in Chapter 128 and four in Chapter 130 — and dropped one paragraph and one speaker's line.** All six duplicates and both losses were found by recounting the files after the cuts and were repaired in the chapters, **and the figures in `state/batch-summary.md` are the counted ones from the files, not the ones the editing session believed it had produced.** **This is the defect class the Batch 0002 independent review found in a self-review, and the rule for Batch 0004 is that a batch must be recounted from the files after any structural edit, because a repair made by paragraph index will duplicate paragraphs.**
4. **Eleven elapsed-day figures were removed or re-registered.** A count of days between two in-batch events is a date on an in-batch event whatever its arithmetic. The first pass had *three days and been not keeping it three days*, *looked for two days*, *thought about a number for two days*, *did not act on it for four days*, *spent four days since then*, *a room four days before it moved*, *a day late*, *the whole of this took four days*, *four days of work* by the survey, and *I was four days down this road at the second gate*. **Every one was replaced with a day of the week, a day of a named week, or the locked road.** The second gate's distance is stated nowhere in the batch.
5. **Nine further instances of meta language were cut**, and the surviving uses of *in this book* were checked against the canon, which uses the phrase in Renn Vale's mouth in Chapter 117 and in the clerk's own entry in Chapter 118. **Three licensed uses of *in this book* survive, at 123, 124 and 129, all in a mouth or in the clerk's own entry, and a fourth at 121 in third-person narration was cut in the review phase.** *In this Hearthhold* is now used for the batch's own new instance.
6. **Marek Venn was named in six of ten chapters on first measure, including neither of the last two, and is now named in ten of ten.** Four interior beats were written: the millimetre in a private book given to a woman and not to a room (128); the week in which being right about five walls stopped being the same fact as being right about a floor (128); the statement that being right about a series cost a boy his life (129); and the admission that the sound in the room is not the anteroom and that he has no standing to say what a sound in a house is (130).
7. **Two things were deliberately not done.** **Leena Orr's *a list is not a location* was not used again** — the new row's problem is that a number is a permission, not that a list is not a location, and repeating the sentence would have been a tic. **And Nera Oduya's two remaining acts of trust were not attempted**; the batch spends the third and holds the first and the second for Batches 0004 and 0005.
8. **The measured craft figures were recounted from the delivered files after every structural edit**, and the method was validated against Batch 0002's recorded figures before it was used, where it returned them exactly: 216 paragraphs not opening in dialogue, *The* 4, *Nobody* 3, *And* 2, *She* 10, *He* 20, thirty together, and on the bold-stripped measure *The* 36, *Nobody* 3, *And* 24, *She* 12, *He* 23.

## Repairs applied in the external review of Batch 0003

**A review run outside the writing session, against the delivered files and against the state files, is recorded in full at `reviews/volume-03/batch-0003.md` under *Repairs applied in the review phase*. Six of its eight findings produced a change and two did not. The ones that touch canon are these.**

1. **The boundary's running total was short by exactly one hundred from Chapter 124 to Chapter 130, and the error had been copied into this file, into `state/batch-summary.md` and into the Batch 0004 prompt as fact.** The two columns of the board imply a base of **one hundred and seventeen and a quarter**, and that base is the one implied at 110, at 120 and at 121; from 124 the implied base was seventeen and a quarter. **The word *hundred* had been dropped. It is restored**, and the total is now **two hundred and four and a quarter** at 124, **two hundred and seven** at 125, **two hundred and eleven** at 126, **two hundred and fourteen** at 127, **two hundred and eighteen** at 128, **two hundred and twenty-one** at 129 and **two hundred and twenty-three** at 130.
2. **The external review restored the total and stopped, and that left the same sentence still contradicting itself.** Chapter 124's day list read *four, three, five, four* = sixteen, against a rise of twelve in the companion column. **It is now *four, three, two, three* = twelve.** 121 fixes day one at four, 125 fixes day five at three, and 121's seventy-five with 125's ninety require days two to four to sum to eight. **The ten daily figures across the batch sum to thirty-one, not thirty-five.**
3. **The reconciliation counter broke mid-week.** *They have reconciled for thirteen weeks* at 129 and 130, where 128 — the third day of the same week — says twelve. **Both are now twelve, and the chain is non-decreasing through the whole batch.**
4. **A meta leak in narration at 121:149** — *stood where he has stood every evening of this book*, third person, about Marek Venn. **Cut to *every evening since the first week*.** This was the only real meta violation; the three licensed survivors are untouched and are not to be removed.
5. **The two opener measures were transposed in both this repository's summary and the review record, and the headline *And* figure was an artifact.** The measure that excludes bolded paragraphs returns *And 0* **by construction, because all twenty of the batch's *And* paragraphs are bold section dividers.** The figure that carries information is the divider count: **thirty-seven in the first pass, twenty as delivered.** Both labels are now correct and the *And* 0 is published with its limitation attached.
6. **Count errors in records that state their figures are counted, not estimated.** The closure clause repeats at **124 and 125**, not 124 and 126. The length figures are now raw `wc -w` — **2,937 to 3,987, 34,421 in all** — replacing a different measurement that was printed as if it were the same one. **Chapter 130 clears the ceiling by thirteen words.**

**Two findings were checked and refused, and the reasons are recorded so the next reviewer does not re-break a correct figure.**

- ***read back* 4 / *read it back* 5.* Reported as inverted at 6 and 3. **Recounted per occurrence and not per line, the file says 4 and 5, and the record was already right.** The two phrases are not overlapping substrings, so the total of nine proves nothing on its own; the split was checked directly. **Not changed.**
- **The review gate.** `reviews/volume-03/batch-0003.md` was produced inside the writer's commit and disclaims independence in its own first line. **That is true and no edit to prose can repair it.** The consequence has been made honest rather than papered over: nothing in this repository now describes Batch 0003 as independently reviewed, and the outstanding debt is named — **an independent review of Volume 03 Batch 0003, and `reviews/volume-02/batch-0003.md`, `batch-0004.md` and `batch-0005.md` for a closed canon volume.** Producing those from inside a writer phase was not done and must not be.

**One instance of the same defect class was found outside this batch and deliberately not edited.** Chapter 112 says the columns *have reconciled for eight weeks* where Chapter 115, four chapters later and in the same week, says seven. **Chapter 112 is in Batch 0002, which is closed, reviewed and repaired, so the figure is recorded here for the next reviewer rather than changed here.** The in-mouth week register is otherwise not re-derived, per the standing rule.

## What Batch 0003 leaves for Batch 0004

1. **The volume's escalation, made explicit.** The reversal's aftermath has produced an argument this boundary has never had with anybody — **that public consent may be a luxury in an emergency, and who decides, and for how long the answer lasts** — and Batch 0004 is that argument, with the flood coming and both Compact cases good and the market route the only way out and it going through a rule.
2. **The position on the page that a later batch may not resolve cheaply.** **A room with a packed sill and a propped hearth stone is being taught in nine children. A grate is off a channel at the low end and the review page is blank and a man is dead under where the grate was. A count in a column with nothing over the top of it is not going to stop. Two sheets with a legible argument are on an anteroom table face up. A title is in a field book and a reply line with a space in it is coming up a road.** **The plan's first column has a ten in a new row and the room had eleven, and nobody has joined the two numbers, and nobody in a later batch may join them either.**
3. **The boundary's two unspent relationship acts are Nera Oduya's first and second** — she stops checking his arithmetic out loud and somebody notices and she gives an answer about the work, and she countersigns his revision in her own hand on a page with an objection stated first — **and one of them is owed in Batch 0004.**
4. **The engine is a room, and the room is the one that was sealed.** The public occupancy plan is the reversal's own answer to itself, and the sealed room is kept open under it.

## Repairs applied in a review-fix phase, after Batch 0004's independent review

**Recorded separately from the batch record above because every item here changed the delivered files of Chapters 176–180 and a later phase must inherit the repaired state, not the delivered one. No plot fact in the section above was altered: no beat moved, no figure changed, no date shifted, no guardrail traded, and `outline/volume-04.md` and the planned ending untouched.**

1. **A device was removed.** Forty-three fully-bold epigraph and recap paragraphs deleted — three from the top of each chapter and four to six from the bottom. **The only bold left in the batch is a person speaking; narration is not bold anywhere in 176–180.** Chapters 171–175 still carry 36 of these blocks and were not touched; the divergence is recorded in `reviews/volume-04/batch-0004.md` and in the Batch 0005 prompt.
2. **A shape was changed.** Fifty-two spoken paragraphs that opened by demanding speech, and twenty-six clerk recitations that opened *Entered, in his words, and entered that*, resolved into about twenty request shapes and mostly into plain narration. **Zero request-to-speak openers and one surviving clerk recitation remain in five chapters, with three bare *Say* imperatives in three mouths.** The half against is canon and is in all five chapters; what was retired is asking for it in the same four words.
3. **A calendar error was corrected, and this one changes a fact a later phase would otherwise inherit.** Chapter 179's deleted epigraph said *at the third bell* while the scene had Jo Verrick finding the gap at the first bell, and this file's own Chapter 179 summary had inherited the block. **The scene stands: the lime let go in the night before the first bell, Jo reads the wall at the first bell, and the air engineer comes down the four steps at the fourth bell with the word she will not say twice.** `state/chapter-summaries.md` is corrected and marks the correction. **A batch that reads this file must not reintroduce the third bell.**
4. **An arithmetic gap was closed.** Chapter 180 said the clerk read the total out loud and never stated it, so **+1 / 243 / 360.25** existed only in the state layer. **Both figures are on the page now, and the batch reconciles from the prose alone: 2, 3, 2, 3, 1; running 234, 237, 239, 242, 243; boundary 351.25, 354.25, 356.25, 359.25, 360.25; counts 111–115.**
5. **Two turns were re-staged without changing their events.** A courier still arrives in 176 and a repair still lets go in 179, because both are canon. **176 now opens three days into Marek's hunt for a lie and takes the leaf as an interruption; 179 opens on Jo's thumb coming out of the string wrong.** The rule this produced for 181–185 is in the Batch 0005 prompt: at least three of the five must turn on somebody deciding something.
6. **The 4000-word ceiling is retired.** It was never canon, it appears first in Batch 0003's own review record, and 179 and 180 were delivered at 4303 and 4142 and cut to 3999 and 3997. **Lengths are measurements now, and the trimmed prose stands rather than being padded back out.** Delivered lengths are 3200, 3499, 3052, 3511 and 3582.
7. **Repetition reduced.** *Wrote* 12 to 6, every one of the six a document being written. *Counted* left at 8 as domain vocabulary with the reason stated. Two weak instances of *held* reworded.
8. **One new duplicate was introduced by repair 2 and caught by recount**: the crew line had converged on the same opening in 176 and 177 once the clerk's recitation became narration. Varied. **Duplication across 151–180 is 3 groups and none of them is on the new side; 151–175 gives the same 3.**

## What Batch 0004 leaves for Batch 0005 (Chapters 176–180 delivered)

**The reversal delivered, and it is a document.** A waxed leaf from the ninth district of a guild cleared-risk insurance office arrives by a road hand: *occupied rooms, compiled from clearance records, no surveyor of this office has entered any room shown, every figure is the last certified permitted occupancy of that room, this office certifies permissions, this office does not count.* **Every figure is true and no surveyor lied; the word *falsified* is a clerk's word and she enters it against her own professional instinct and enters the objection to her own entry in her own hand.** The word at the top is *independent* and means independent of the rooms, not of the office. Two of the six district rooms name this boundary's and both figures are a ten, **the same figure as this boundary's own first column for the same two rooms, entered as an agreement and not joined to anything — and the Volume 03 guardrail that the first column may never be joined to the number of people in that room is held in both 176 and 177.** The exposure itself is **not made**: the two documents go on one table side by side under a chalk line with nothing written under it, a comparison is entered as owed, and Renn Vale says the room which can hear it does not exist yet. **The sentence that ends the comparison belongs to Chapter 197 and is not said anywhere in 176–180.**

**Sabotage by a correct form, about a different road.** A carrier comes down the middle passage with the fact that a new board has been nailed over an old one at the middle gate, four days up, with a form on it and **both of the two lines filled in** — a route-holder's name and the person responsible for a load, the same cleared-risk post-holder in both lines, a real seal number, an ordinary pen, an ordinary day, **in the hand of the clerk who took this boundary's form off its board in the twenty-ninth week.** Nobody refused anything and nothing is untrue. The section named is the ground between the end of the middle passage and the middle gate, so **ordinary residents crossing to a market road are now on a working road with a named person responsible for a load, and a person with a survey lamp, a line and a note-book is a person carrying a load.** The alternative Marek needed — a survey of a void — is closed, because a room nobody has surveyed cannot have a row and a room with no row has no keeper and no condition, and nobody is admitting a survey party into a room on a printed leaf. **The chapter says out loud that nobody refusing anything is worse than a refusal, and that a sheet saying an office is not in there is harder to argue with than a door.**

**The faultform is in the party wall, in the wrong place, and is not killed.** On the seventh day, a shut day with the school not running and **nine children therefore not in the building**, a lime repair comes away along the line where bad work meets sound stone, in the anteroom's party wall, and a gap opens about two fingers wide with air coming out of it four times in the time it takes to say a sentence and stopping for a count. **Jo Verrick's eleven readings were read out against the original and against the clerk's book and all eleven were the same, and the wall this morning is not one of the eleven. Nobody cut anything and there is no tool mark in the join, and no mark was cut in the stone anywhere in this building.** The room named the *shape* of what the void was doing and **could not say what it was doing it about**, which is the honest position and the one the batch required. Sefu Aran heard it second and did not find it out and declined to guess. **The load reason for not killing it is on the page in Marek's own mouth: the void is the only thing in that wall doing anything with the force coming through that wall, and the force is coming through that wall whether the void is there or not, so a bar in the gap is a removal and not a repair.** Iven Tallo does not believe the reason and will not put a bar in there anyway, entered as his trade and not a virtue. **Nobody went through it, nobody put a tool or a hand or a tape into it, it is not a route change as a stage, and nobody joined it to the dowel, the charter, the mouth, the four treads, the ninth room, the low end, Nera Oduya's theory, her twelfth-week name or the plate.**

**Cassian Rook intervened for the first time, and it is a sheet, six people and six shores.** A Warden-General's instruction came down the middle passage under a seal with a number on it, brought by **Warden-Officer Ansel Karr** and six people. Three numbered things (kitchen-line room emptied on the next open morning and the four rooms held as one space; the count taken by the arriving crew into the district book with **no competing figure from this boundary**; the party wall shored from the common landing side, timber charged to the district) and one sentence not numbered, in Rook's own hand, which is his rule and the reason the other three were written: **a decision without a responsible operator becomes an accident.** Rook is **not in the room**. The work took nineteen minutes, six shores went on the common landing side, **Marek's only instruction was that no shore goes on the kitchen-line side of the wall, his left hand held a shore and did not close, nobody watched and he was not thanked**, and the cost was recorded without one word against the man, including the clerk's entry that this is **the first post this boundary has ever had and it arrived in somebody else's handwriting and was not asked for**. The boundary did not refuse. **He is not a new final enemy, the One-Seat is not named, Morrowlight is not named, he survives this batch and stays boundable, and no chapter says otherwise.**

**A condition, unasked, and a going, unanswered.** **Nera Oduya raised her own condition in a working morning, unasked by anybody, and said that this boundary has said no to nothing this week and that she does not trust herself with her own sentence this month; nobody consoled her and nobody asked her.** **Bel Ordry raised the going by other people — a person who certifies air for a district a Warden's instruction has been written about is a person who will be asked to sit at a table with a seal on it — said plainly that it is not leaving, and she answered one word, gave no reason, and nobody asked her for one and nobody asked her whether she is going anywhere.** Her first condition and her second both remain unmet, her theory and her twelfth-week name remain unasked, and she is not leaving and no chapter stages it. Her sixth act was already spent in Batch 0002 and no seventh was taken; her closest moment in this batch is a cloth out of a doorway and four numbers and not a fifth.

**Renn Vale's sixth-day answer was owed from 175 and was given in 178, and it is a sentence and not a door.** The anteroom's second way out is a word, and **a word is a way out of a room and not a way out of a building**, and she has known it since the first week and did not say it out loud because a room holding a sentence it does not say out loud has a way out it can use without asking anybody. She entered that she let a man spend two days finding it out in a room because it was kinder at a kitchen table. **The carpenter's unanswered question about the word is still on the page, and the elected keeper's refusal to answer it as first-week decisiveness still stands and is not re-argued.**

**Numbers, delivered, not re-derived.** Week runs Monday–Sunday. **176–179 the thirty-fourth week, 180 the thirty-fifth; 176 fourth day Thursday, 177 fifth day Friday, 178 sixth day Saturday, 179 seventh day Sunday, 180 first day Monday.** Corridor **shut in 176 and 179 (179 by the standing arrangement alone) and open in 177 and 178, and shut in 180. The school ran in 177 only**, the thirty-second morning, in the room at the kitchen-line end; **fire asked and refused for the eleventh time in 177 and the refusals were asked to be counted.** 178 is the batch's one market day and **no chapter puts a market inside or dates an event to one.** No day number on any in-batch event; the register's highest is the forty-sixth; the only date is the plan's top corner and the Compact *date observed* exception was not used. **Wen Pask is 111, 112, 113, 114 and 115 across the five chapters, one a day, all on the page in the right chapter, read at the sixth bell, with the weeks-running clause at twenty, twenty-one, twenty-two, twenty-three and twenty-four continuing the nineteen in 175. Nothing is made of any figure by anybody.** Crew **seventy-one, unmoved, no sixth asking**, with a distinct morning-specific reason in all five chapters and walking paper in named as not asking in 177 and 178. Boundary day list **two, three, two, three, one = 11**; running **234, 237, 239, 242, 243**; totals on the constant base of **117.25** of **351.25, 354.25, 356.25, 359.25, 360.25**; both columns reconcile; **counter carried at seventeen.** Board **eighteen, 9 + 9**, walked in 177 and 180, refused a nineteenth in 177 and in 180 for two different stated reasons, and passed over with a reason in 176, 178 and 179. **The unheaded column's batch ordinal is deliberately not restated anywhere in 176–180** — see the record in `state/batch-summary.md`; no later phase may put an ordinal on it from a prompt. **Brass rule twenty-five weeks silent and plate thirty-four unopened in 176–179, twenty-six and thirty-five in 180, on the ninth-week origin, and neither in a room in any chapter.** Pot **nine in 176, 177 and 178, and eight in 180**, with the seam giving one on Friday and two on Sunday and the cook entering that those are not the same quantity; four households at a second gate have nothing and no figure is attached to that gate. Capacity **ten including one litter, unchanged, said in 180 with six strangers in the room.**

**What the next batch inherits that it may not spend cheaply.** The comparison is owed and is not made. The void is open, unnamed, unwatched and unmeasured, and the kitchen-line room is not to be used and is not shut. **A Warden's count of four rooms stands in a district book and this boundary may not enter a competing figure, and the crew that took it is going back up a road, and six shores on the common landing side are a new failure point on a wall nobody has a row for.** A brace and a shore are now both pushing on walls and one of them is the wall nine children lean against. Iven's post in the stiff cover is unresolved, his second line is empty, **and in 180 he said the correct answer about foot plates out loud and would not say the rest of what he is thinking, which is a thing a later batch may pull on.** Marek's hole is drawn and not cut, and a survey is closed, and a man who drew a hole for three days so that he would have something to be wrong about has said that out loud twice in two chapters. Bel Ordry's question about a page in a coat against a printed page is on the page and unanswered. Bel Ordry's suspicion of a man with a store is unchanged and untouched. The four words about who owns a wall are still unanswered. The brace's watching, the shim, the school door at the far end of nine steps, the low end of the corridor, the ninth room, the four treads, the market form, the wrapped plate and the brass rule are all where Batch 0003 left them, and **the volume's one serious injury remains unspent and available.**
