# Volume 03, Batch 0004 — delivered, Chapters 131–140

**Ten chapters in `chapters/volume-03/`, close third person on Marek Venn, no viewpoint shift anywhere in the batch.** The batch's delivery record is at the head of `state/batch-summary.md`; this section records only what a later phase must not contradict.

## What the batch established, in canon

- **The batch's argument, argued in rooms: public consent may be a luxury in an emergency, who decides, and for how long the answer lasts.** It starts with a stove, because a cook will not light a hearth in a room nine children sit on, and it ends with a document nobody will sign. **Renn Vale's answer to *for how long* is the volume's: the agreement goes into the person, as a condition with no number and no day on it, and it lasts as long as the person who is able to say no is able to say it.** A signature is a name, and a name on a page about a room is a handle, and this boundary has no procedure for a body it has not written one for.
- **A room standing open with nobody's condition on it is not a safe room.** Renn Vale lifted a condition on a child's foot in the twenty-fifth week and owns the consequence: a watched room is a room somebody has agreed to look at, and when it changes the person who agreed to look at it is the one who says so. **A room nobody is watching is a room that finds out about itself from a stranger.**
- **The flood came, in three places, and the three are one subject.** Water in the bed joint under the open school corner, water between the hearth stones of the room at the kitchen-line end, and water in the channel at the low end. **Jo Verrick says she can say they are the same warmth and cannot say they are the same joint, and the clerk enters three findings and one reason and not one conclusion.** Four threads at the seam behind the anteroom's outer service door; **two jars a day, entered separately and never added to the pot.**
- **The crew were asked a second time, and the asking is the practice.** In Chapter 132, in a room, with the terms out loud, the three who could not be asked named with the reason for each **before** the asking — **Leena Orr, who cannot cross the waist and whose work is the other side; Pell Roke, who is fourteen; and Tams Quill, whose right hand is open and flat and who keeps the water record and the count.** Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no. **The crew's column moved by three, from fifty-six and a half to fifty-nine and a half, and has not moved since the second day of the twenty-sixth week.** The corridor was opened for one crossing, shut again after, and the opening is in a clerk's hand in four lines.
- **The market route's form has become a pass.** A gate four days up the middle passage has a printed sheet on a board with seven lines and two of them are for a name and for the person responsible for the load, and a clerk there has begun to require them of anybody who wants to go along that road with more than what they are carrying. **Nobody wrote a rule and there is no order and no notice and nothing with a date on it.** Talla Roke's rule is entered in a clerk's book in her own words: *a route that cannot be used by an ordinary resident is not a public route.* **The boundary's answer, in Marek Venn's words, is that it will not fill the form in, and the road is not a public route, and forty-one people are not going anywhere.** The market day is the sixth day of the twenty-seventh week and nothing in this batch is dated.
- **Talla Roke is in the building, on her own terms, with her own three named people, and is not a rescue.** She said so in a room before she said anything else, including that she is not here about a boy and that nobody in the building is to use her to get to him. **Pell Roke read the form's two lines out loud for her at her request, because reading numbers is what he is for, and she said thank you at the same volume she said everything else and did not go up the steps and did not look at the bench a second time, and the clerk entered that the room made nothing of it, which is itself an entry, and entered that she entered it on purpose.** She was wrong about a fill in front of everybody, was corrected by Jo Verrick, and was not consoled.
- **Two Compact cases, both good.** **Hollis Ashe**, forty-one, sixteen years, has written the four pages she said she would write, and a page that shows a condition being lifted is a page that says every condition on it can be lifted. **Pettin Rahl**, fifty-two, twenty-six years, continuity, is right about a number nobody has counted: a permitted occupancy that has to be believed instead of counted is how a room fills, and he has stood in a room on the Rim side whose page said six with thirty-one people in it, and four died, and he was the reason the number was on the page. **Neither is a villain and the hardliner is right.** **Clause four of the charter was read out against the original in front of both of them and names one office, and neither of them is that office, and this boundary has no procedure for either of them and has refused to write one.**
- **Nobody joined the two numbers, and the book did not join them either.** **Nobody in that anteroom said the number that was in the room on the Friday and the ten that is in the plan's first column in the same breath.** Ilsa Norr told a room from another office that this building has a count, that it is a count and not a permission, that it is in a clerk's book, that it cannot be given to anybody, and that **she was not going to say what the number was, because a count of that kind is only true of a moment and the moment is the only thing about a room that is worth a number.** Pettin Rahl wrote it down and said that is his whole problem: a boundary with no count. **The clerk entered that nobody in the room said it and entered the reason, which is that a clerk who has spent twenty-seven weeks putting a reason beside two facts on purpose is not going to be the one who does it in a room with a stranger in it.**
- **The public occupancy plan is drafted, fought over, and not signed by anybody.** It is **the plan on butcher's paper, extended, and it is not a new document**: one document in four parts, in a coat, a date in the top corner, no name anywhere, **twelve rows.** The first column holds a permitted occupancy and has never held a count of anybody; the second column holds a condition with no number and no day on each of the twelve; the third column is what is done, in the hand of the person who keeps the row, eleven lines filled and one empty that the keeper will not name; the fourth column is empty and unheaded with a reason in it in two hands and a modal struck out of one of them. **Two rows were added, for the common landing and the anteroom step, and the first column took a ten in the cook's hand for the second time and she said out loud that she did not count anybody for the second time either.**
- **A third row was asked for and refused, and the refusal is the reason nobody was watching the hole.** Bel Ordry asked for a row for the low end of the corridor. **Leena Orr found the shape of the refusal — every row on that page is a place somebody is going to be, and the low end of that corridor is the only place in this building nobody is ever going to be in — and Mero Senn gave the other half and said he would not support the refusal for that reason: a promise about a place where nobody can stand is a lie told in a column.** Both halves went into the clerk's book in that order and the clerk entered that the order is the finding. **A refusal to put a row there means there is no plan for it, and a place with no plan is a place nobody is watching, and a place nobody is watching is how a man of twenty-two came out of a channel. The refusal is correct and the refusal is the reason.**
- **Five people were asked to sign the plan and five said no, for five good reasons.** Renn Vale will not be the one a clerk looks at; Mikka Hale is the worst person in the room and has written two thirds of the numbers on it and been in neither room; Ilsa Norr writes the third column and says a third column is what a person does and a signature is what a person agrees to; Mero Senn will sign a condition and not a number and said so on Friday and was not moved by a better reason; and Bel Ordry will not, because a signed instrument is a thing a person four days up the passage can hold up. **The clerk wrote *nobody in this boundary will sign this plan* in the book and read it out twice.**
- **A revision, an objection stated first, and a countersignature.** In Chapter 138 a proposal went into the second column of the tenth row in Marek Venn's own hand — **a proposal, and not a change, because the person who keeps that row is not him.** **Nera Oduya came down a step nobody asked her to and wrote her objection above it in her own hand before she said a word of it: a page that shows a condition being lifted is a page that says every condition on it can be lifted, and the second column's entire claim is that its conditions are not set aside.** She said the half against herself: a condition that has never been lifted is a sentence, and this boundary had a page of sentences for twenty-seven weeks and shut a room with eleven people in it while every sentence on it was true. **Renn Vale then wrote a stronger condition in her own hand than the one it replaced, checked every morning the room is used, with the nine coming out without waiting for a physician if the answer is no twice.** And **Nera Oduya put her hand under his, with her objection written above it. Renn Vale said out loud that it is not a signature of the plan and that five people refused to sign the plan on Monday. Nobody thanked her and nobody asked her why and one woman who might have said one did not.** This is the **second** of Volume 03's five acts of trust. **The third — she stops checking his arithmetic out loud and somebody notices and she answers about the work — is unspent and is Batch 0005's.**
- **The plan nobody will sign became the only plan anybody can use, and it is a civic consequence and not a triumph.** **In Chapter 139 about forty people were moved out of two rooms into the anteroom in fifty minutes out of the third column, in four hands**, and the anteroom went above its number and **its second way out is a word and the word could not be said by anybody in the room, because the rule is that the person who is going to be in the room says it and the clerk repeats it, and there were nine children and a cook in there and no clerk.** **Marek Venn said the sentence and then took half of it back in the same breath: a plan with a signature is a plan about a person and gets sent for; a plan with no signature has nobody in it; and a name is the only protection anything in this building has ever had.** Renn Vale said she would rather be argued with than sent for and that she has looked for a better answer. Mero Senn said the page moved about forty people through a building in fifty minutes and that he cannot tell you whether that is the best thing this Hearthhold has done in twenty-seven weeks or the reason one of them is not here in a year, and that neither of those two things is a thing he can tell you about before it happens.
- **A condition of the anteroom's rating has been broken for a fortnight and the clerk entered that she knew and did not write it down.** Ten including one litter, no more than two hours, the outer service door, the pump attended, **and the air engineer or the elected keeper able to stop it** — and **Sefu Aran is four days up a road and has been since before the first of the month, and the room decided not to write down how long he has been gone.** Dalla Sen entered it three times and entered that a condition you have broken and written down is a condition you have agreed to keep.
- **The secondary route is identified and it is a place a person can be killed, and it is the channel at the low end.** In five parts, said out loud: the water comes up the channel before it comes up the corridor, so anybody in it is a foot and a half lower than the floor; there is no grate in that frame, so nothing on the floor says where the channel is; a person holding that opening stands at the lowest point of a corridor that fills, under two flags and a spent line, with no second grate and a wall in lime four days up the passage; the review page that says somebody stands there has been blank for twenty-seven weeks and the woman who wrote the two sentences on it has three conditions and the third is that nobody is to be sent anywhere to make it true, and she has never been asked and nobody is going near her floor to find out whether the conditions are met; and the refusal of a row for that place in Chapter 136. **Leena Orr said *a list is not a location*, and the room agreed that there is no second way out of this building and that what there is, is a hole under a corridor floor.**
- **The volume's question is asked in a room and not answered.** Talla Roke asked *can a route be a public good when the people who use it live on different sides of the law?* **Nera Oduya said she has had half of it since the fourth day of the eleventh week, did not give it, said that half of what she knows is about a room and what was asked is about a road, and that her condition is not met and that a plan with twelve rows in it and a river at the waist is not the thing that meets it. Nobody asked her. The clerk entered that the two questions are adjacent and not the same and that she has been asked to put two questions next to each other and is not going to, and that they are next to each other in the book by accident and not by hand.**
- **The four marks and the groove on the lintel above the open school corner's mouth are read two ways by two people and answer nothing.** The stone carries four marks and one groove and has carried them since Chapter 106. **Renn Vale read one of the four as two strokes and said the fifth stroke is a stroke and not a stop; Marek Venn read that stroke as a stop, or as the middle of a letter with no letter.** The four marks are damaged and the groove under them is not, and Chapter 140 now says so the same way in all three places it says it. **No mark was cut in the stone anywhere in this building and nobody went down the four treads.**
- **The board is fifteen entries: eleven nulls, one claim, one mark, one row and a plan; nine in the ordinary column and six in the column with nothing over the top of it.** **The plan is the fifteenth entry and it is the first thing on that board a person in this building wrote and then refused to sign, and it is the second thing on it that is not about a wall.** It goes in the unheaded column because a plan in the ordinary column is a plan somebody can point at, and this one cannot be pointed at, and that is not a flaw in the plan. **The column is still unheaded, for the seventh consecutive batch, and the reason for it was given on the second day of the twenty-sixth week and is not to be improved on.** The mark's entry is still on the board and the claim's condition is still unmet.
- **The wash-room condition is untouched and the protection is now five times.** In Chapter 134 a heading on the boundary's own evacuation sheet, and a line under it for who keeps a room while it is emptied, **was struck through in nine seconds by a woman three steps up, before anybody had asked, and the reason was not given at all for the first time in twenty-six weeks.** The clerk entered the time, the absence, and that there is no reason in the space where a reason would go, **because a page with a reason on it is a page somebody can read back to her.** Nobody asked. The floor was not approached. Nobody went near it. Nobody was sent.
- **A Quiet Hands cell is unchanged and uncaught.** Nothing in this batch recruits anybody, nothing turns their reason into a riddle or a voice, and **the only sentence this batch gave them is a sentence of a woman with a rule about why three people have never measured the fill at the waist, which is a different argument and is entered beside theirs and not joined to it.** Mero Senn's second rule was said again in a room and did not get softer.

## Numbers a later batch must not re-derive

- **The week runs Monday to Sunday. 131–135 the twenty-sixth, 136–140 the twenty-seventh.** Each chapter sits on the matching day of its week: 131 the first, a Monday; 132 the second, a Tuesday; 133 the third, a Wednesday; 134 the fourth, a Thursday; 135 the fifth, a Friday; 136 the first of the twenty-seventh, a Monday; 137 the second; 138 the third, a Wednesday; 139 the fourth, a Thursday; 140 the fifth, a Friday. **The corridor is shut on the first, second and fourth days and open on the third, fifth and sixth, and the seventh day is not a crossing day; the school runs on the three open days.** So the corridor is shut in **131, 132, 134, 136, 137 and 139** and open in **133, 135, 138 and 140**, and the school ran in **133, 135, 138 and 140.** **The school corner was shut as a room on the fourth day of the twentieth week and opened as a room on the fifth day of the twenty-second week, and those are the two dates and no chapter may restate them as anything else** — the lamp test on the floor at the low corner was read at the first bell on the fifth day of the twenty-second week, it came out dry, and the door was standing open at the end of that day. **The school corner is open and is not used, and no chapter in this batch put the school back in it.** **The market day is the sixth day of the twenty-seventh week** and is not in this batch.
- **The water at the waist reached the fill on the fourth day of the twenty-sixth week and was still on it on the fourth day of the twenty-seventh, and it did not go away in between.** It is on the ground, not in the channel, about the height of a knee, and it is not moving. The third wedge at the waist is up a quarter of an inch and a bit and was not touched. **Any chapter that says the water came back, came up again, or came up for a second time is wrong, and the span between the two Thursdays is one week and is written as a day of a named week and never as a count of days.**
- **Wen Pask's count is 66 in Chapter 131 and 75 in Chapter 140, one a day, on the locked base of twenty-three on the fifth day of the seventeenth week, and all ten are on the page in the right chapter.** **It is his own count, kept by a clerk, in the column with no heading and in nothing else. It is not a register, it dates nothing, and it may not be confused, merged or remarked upon as a coincidence with the day-number register.** The clerk has said out loud, in a room, in three weeks running, that she is going to keep writing it, and nobody has argued with her and nobody has thanked her.
- **No day number is attached to any in-batch event and the day-number register's highest value remains the forty-sixth day.** The only day figures in the prose are the locked road (**four days up the middle passage to the middle gate**), the arrangement's *three days in seven*, week figures in mouths, the review page's **twenty-seven weeks** and the plan's **twenty-seven weeks**, and the count in the column with no heading. **The second gate's distance is stated nowhere in this batch** — a household at a second gate is named as being *up the middle passage* and no figure is attached to it. **A notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time is neither repeated nor corrected.** Chapter 119's bounded Compact-form exception was not used.
- **Crew hours: fifty-nine and a half**, up three from fifty-six and a half on the second day of the twenty-sixth week, on a named asking made in a room with the terms out loud and Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **with the three who could not be asked named with the reason for each before the asking.** The three are **Leena Orr, Pell Roke and Tams Quill.** **A piece of the crew's spent frayed line is still over the hole at the low end and is still not an hour and is not in the column.**
- **Boundary hours: a hundred and seventeen and a quarter, plus a hundred and thirty-seven, = two hundred and fifty-four and a quarter.** The list adds **by the day the work was done**: **three, four, two, three, three in the twenty-sixth week; four, three, two, four, three in the twenty-seventh.** The ten sum to thirty-one. Running figures with the day's increment and the total are given at the sixth bells of **131, 132, 133, 134, 135, 136, 137, 138, 139 and 140** — in all ten, which is the first time that has been true in this volume. **The base implied by the two columns is a constant one hundred and seventeen and a quarter at every chapter that states both, the total is monotonic from 110 to 140, and both columns reconcile. The reconciliation counter is carried unchanged at *twelve weeks* in every mouth in this batch and is not re-derived.**
- **Wedges: seven sound and two dead sticks, and one of the two dead sticks is still gone.** Two at the school-door head, one in the school corner's door, three at the waist (the third up a quarter of an inch and a bit), one in the basket. **No wedge was bought, moved or added in this batch, and the third wedge at the waist was not touched and nobody put a hand on the fill.** The clerk's material ledger still says two dead sticks and has been wrong since Batch 0003.
- **The pot is at ten days and has not gone up since the fifth day of the nineteenth week.** The jars are **two a day, entered separately and never added to the pot**, and the seam gave four threads at the first bell on the second day of the twenty-sixth week.
- **The brass survey rule has now said nothing for longer than fifteen weeks** and was not put on a table. **The right hand's fine control is not recovered, the left hand burned at the Marker and is not what it was, the Reader reading is not repeatable and was not used, and the Chapter 99 claim's condition is still unmet. No route change as a stage, no binding, no relay, no brace, no panel of any kind, and no mark cut in the stone anywhere in this building.**

## What Batch 0004 leaves for Batch 0005

1. **The network, the crews, the counts and the month after next.** The plan is a plan of rooms, not a network of them. **The multi-room evacuation network is Batch 0005's design and it has not been drawn.** Nothing in this batch connects two rooms to each other; Chapter 139 moved people out of rooms and into a room, which is the opposite of the network the volume ends on.
2. **The secondary route is identified and is a place a person can be killed, and the conditions under which it would be opened have not been stated.** **A person holding that opening is a person who is not visible, cannot be reached, and is in a place with no row, no grate, a blank review page and three conditions that forbid sending anybody.** **The word for the second way out of a room in this building is still a word, and the anteroom is over its rating on a condition that was broken a fortnight ago and entered by a clerk who knew on the day.**
3. **The market day is the sixth day of the twenty-seventh week and the form has two lines and a space in each of them, and this boundary has decided it will not fill them in and has not decided what it will do instead.** Talla Roke is in the building with her own three people and her own mark, and Batch 0005's climax moves people on her route and not on a guild's. **The form has become a pass without a rule, and the body that put the form on the board has never been named in any chapter — see the charter note below, which Batch 0005 must read before it writes Chapters 148 and 149.**
4. **A Compact instrument exists that this boundary has never read, written by an office that does not cover it, and two people from that office said in a room that it is a bad answer and the correct one.** **A page in a coat that cannot be carried, and a keeper who said out loud that he is the only person who has to say that it is not a system.** Batch 0005 inherits the inspection-regime threat without its having been made yet.
5. **Nera Oduya's remaining act is the one Batch 0003 set up and this batch deliberately did not spend: she stops checking his arithmetic out loud and somebody notices and she gives an answer about the work.** She made him say how he knows in a corridor in the twenty-fourth week, she read a limit out of her own hand over his in the twenty-seventh, and in this batch she asked for his figures to be read against an original four times and never once asked him how he knew. **Nobody has noticed that yet.**
6. **The Ninefold Charter, and the fact that it is not this boundary's charter.** `outline/volume-03.md` commits Chapters 148 and 149 to **the Ninefold Charter losing exclusive access to one essential route, and the route it loses is the market route** — decided at a counter, by a person, with a form withdrawn and no concession in words. **The name has never appeared in a delivered chapter, and the ambiguity that created is closed here.**
   - **The Ninefold Charter is a guild cartel** — `bible/terminology.md`: the dominant guild cartel that controls recognized clearance seals and route insurance. `bible/world.md` puts it inside the Cartwright Guilds, and `bible/characters.md` lists it as the second rung of the opposition: an institution that turns private expertise into exclusive access and can starve a Hearthhold of materials without declaring war.
   - **This boundary's own charter is a different instrument and is not it.** Butcher's paper, an office's number at the top, no name anywhere, eight clauses argued out loud, seven signatures, and **clause four a right against one office, the Cartwright office.** It is a local instrument kept by the people who live behind it. **No chapter may retro-apply the guild name to it, and the Cartwright office named in clause four is a guild office and is not the Ninefold Charter either.**
   - **The boundary's own charter cannot be the thing that loses exclusivity, because it puts no holder against any route** — not the stair and not the way up the middle passage. That is the whole of what it was for. **So the exclusivity lost in Chapter 149 comes from the guild side of the road and not from this building, and the two must not be collapsed into one instrument when the chapter is written.**
   - **The market form and the board at the gate have never been attributed to any body at all.** They arrived as a fact in Chapter 133 — a printed sheet on a board, seven lines, two of them for a name and for the person responsible for the load, and a clerk at that gate who began requiring them of anybody going along the road with more than they carry, with no order and no notice and nothing with a date on it. **Naming the body behind that form is available to Batch 0005 and is not a change of plot, because `outline/volume-03.md` already commits the chapter to a person at a counter deciding that a thing a stranger's mark can be used on is not exclusive.** If the writer names it, it is the guild side; if the writer does not, **the chapter still resolves, and a form withdrawn by a person at a counter does not require the counter's owner to be named first.**
   - **The guardrail stands: this is not a new final enemy.** The Ninefold Charter is already on the opposition ladder and is a guild cartel, not a person. **Cassian Rook and the One-Seat protocol remain the destination, per `outline/ending.md`, and Volume 03 does not name the One-Seat.**
## Repairs applied in Batch 0004

1. **A residual duplicated paragraph was found in Chapter 128 and repaired before this batch was written.** The Batch 0003 review record states that all six paragraph-index duplicates were repaired; **one of them — the line *Dalla Sen said the thing she had come to say, which was not a fact*, immediately above her own entry about the fourth column's reason — was in the delivered file twice and has been removed.** Chapter 128 is otherwise untouched, no prose of it was changed, and the defect is recorded here rather than in the Batch 0003 record because the repair was made in the Batch 0004 writing session. **This is the defect class the Batch 0003 review named, and it is the second time it has survived a recorded repair.**
2. **A markup pass over the ten delivered files went wrong three times and was repaired.** A script written to normalise quotation marks across the batch split six multi-paragraph speeches, wrapped five paragraphs of narration, and then a second and a third pass over-corrected thirty-one section dividers into quoted speech and left five narration paragraphs quoted. **All ten files were put back to a single consistent form — every speech paragraph opens and closes its own quotation — and then verified file by file: every file is even on asterisks and on quotation marks, every paragraph has an even quotation count, there is no duplicated paragraph on a ninety-character prefix, and there is no run of asterisks at the end of any paragraph.** The prose was not reworded by any of the passes; only quotation marks moved.
3. **Thirty-one section-divider openers and twenty-six narrative openers were rewritten into other shapes** after the measured count showed a bold *And* divider figure of one hundred and two and a bold *The* figure of forty-nine against Batch 0003's twenty and twenty-two. **The delivered figures are in the delivery record and they are counted from the files after every structural edit, which is the rule Batch 0003's review set for this batch.**
4. **Four continuity faults were found and repaired in the prose.** The market day was dated wrongly in three chapters against the week clock and is now the sixth day of the twenty-seventh week in all of them. A figure of four days was attached to the second gate in Chapter 140 and is removed. Three week figures in the twenty-sixth week read twenty-five and now read twenty-six, and the review page and the plan are at twenty-seven in the twenty-seventh week.
5. **One meta leak was cut.** Chapter 140's opening line read *the question this volume has been carrying*; it is now *a question this boundary has been carrying since the first week of the twentieth week*. **The three surviving uses of *in this book* are all in Dalla Sen's mouth or in the clerk's own entry, which is the use the canon licenses at Chapters 117 and 118.**
6. **Leena Orr's *a list is not a location* was used once, in Chapter 140, and it is hers.** It was attributed to the wrong mouth in the first pass of that chapter and was moved to her, where it belongs, and where it earns itself: she uses it to stop a man who has laid a length of rope on a floor and called it a way out.

The itemised list, with the reasoning, is in `state/batch-summary.md` under *Repairs applied in the review phase*. What a later phase must not undo is this:**

# Volume 03, Batch 0005 — delivered, Chapters 141–150, and with it Volume 03

**Ten chapters in `chapters/volume-03/`, close third person on Marek Venn, no viewpoint shift anywhere in the batch, and the protagonist named in ten of ten.** The batch's delivery record is at the head of `state/batch-summary.md`; this section records only what a later phase must not contradict.

## What the batch established, in canon

- **The volume's immediate promise is answered and the volume's larger question is open.** The room that was shut in the twenty-fourth week is open, and it is open under a public occupancy plan that is the same page it has always been, extended by four rows, **made public by being read out loud in a room to a person from another office with no copy given, under the Compact's own first and third clauses.** The plan names, in a room and not on a page, a person who may stop it. The volume's question is asked out loud at the third bell of Chapter 150 and is not answered.
- **A plan of rooms became a network of four rooms and a door.** Multi-room by construction: the kitchen, the room at the kitchen-line end, the common landing, the anteroom; each emptied into the next; each with its own count and its own keeper, and **each keeper wrote their own condition.** The first column took the same number four times and not four numbers. **There is no order on it: the last one out of a room decides when that room is empty.** The network's second way out is a word, and it is the same word it was in the twenty-fourth week, and it opened nothing.
- **The first thing missing from a network was not a design.** It was a pair of hands and a crew that is not on a rota. The crew were asked a third time in twenty-nine weeks, in a room, with the terms out loud, Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **and the three who could not be asked named with the reason for each before the asking, and the reasons are not the reasons of Batch 0004.** The crew's column moved by four, from fifty-nine and a half to sixty-three and a half.
- **A condition with a hole in it, found by the woman who wrote it.** A room used three days in seven has its condition checked three mornings in seven. The answer is four sentences a week in an empty room, and it costs nothing, and the woman who proposed it said out loud that it is stupid and cheap and that a condition which costs nothing is a condition a person in a bad month will decide is not worth saying. **The schoolteacher agreed and put the cost in the book as a preference and not as a noble position.**
- **The secondary route is the channel at the low end of the corridor, and a man held it open with a lamp and his hands for two and a half days.** The limit on the holding has no number and no day on it: **the opening is held while there is water standing on the fill at the waist.** The person who may stop it is the air engineer. **The limit was never met and the holding was stopped anyway**, by a woman turning a wheel she had not turned in twenty-nine weeks, because a person in a channel cannot be told anything and cannot be known to be in one.
- **He is brought out by a route that is not the one he was holding.** He got himself out of the channel, and then he walked the corridor and down nine steps and out of the anteroom's door in daylight in front of everybody, and the anteroom's second way out was a word he said himself and the clerk repeated, **and it opened nothing and he opened the door.** Nobody carried him and nobody thanked him and it is not a rescue.
- **The central collision is staged as a collision in a room and not as a technicality.** The network cannot be used on any day of the week, because the waist will not open on a day anybody is at the low end, and the only way the low end is watched is if somebody is there, and the page that says somebody stands there is blank, and the third of its three conditions says that nobody is to be sent anywhere to make it true. **Nobody is sent. He is not sent. And the clerk entered that nobody sent him as two entries and not as one, and entered on Tuesday that the difference between that and the man of twenty-two was the smallest thing in her book, and that she is entering the difference as a difference and will not be asked whether it is a large one.** The condition was broken. The page is still blank. Nobody was asked and nobody went near that floor.
- **The refusal of a row for the low end stands and was not re-argued.** Both halves of it were restated in one sentence each in a room and the order they were given in is the finding. **The plan has sixteen rows and none of them is the low end of the corridor.**
- **The Ninefold Charter is named for the first time in this book, and it is a guild cartel and not this boundary's charter.** It controls the recognized clearance seals and the route insurance, and the form on the board at the market gate is its instrument: a road a person carries a load along is not a recognized road unless there is a named person responsible for the load. **This boundary's own charter puts no holder against any route and therefore could not be the instrument that lost anything, and no chapter may retro-apply the guild name to it.** On the second day of the twenty-ninth week a woman at a counter read a courier's mark, found that it is three people's and cannot be entered in a register, and took the form off the board, and said four other things: the board is a courtesy, the road is unchanged, the seal stands, and a sheet comes back on a board in a month by a clerk who does not know about Tuesday. **Nobody was defeated and the office conceded nothing in a word.**
- **The Stonelight Compact threatened intervention and the threat is an inspection regime and a good argument.** Six pages, of which the fifth clause says a room whose condition is not being checked at the time the room is in use may be entered, and the boundary may not refuse, and the refusal of the person who keeps the room is not a ground. **A teacher argued that a network with four numbers in it is a queue with a signpost on it. A boundary's route inspector said out loud, against her own office, that the instrument which made this boundary arguable is hers and that she knew the price of it when she wrote it and is still glad she wrote it. The hardliner said the belief he has in this boundary is worth nothing, because a competent and tired man in a cell on a Tuesday will look at the first column and see a building with a number in it.** Nobody was defeated and nobody conceded in a word.
- **A reply sheet with a title in it was answered by leaving it wrong.** The title *the person who keeps the anteroom's terms* is in a field book four days up the middle passage and the person it describes was standing in the room. **She picked the half where the title stays wrong on purpose, and said the third and best thing is available and she is not going to ask for it, because a woman who has spent four weeks being a handle does not get to choose the shape of the handle.**
- **Nera Oduya's third act of trust is spent and it is the one Batch 0003 set up and Batch 0004 held.** She stops checking his arithmetic out loud, a clerk notices out loud in a room with a stranger in it, **and she answers about the work and not about him: there are two handholds on that page now, one a man's and one a room's, and a schoolteacher's hand in a column cannot be adjusted by anybody who finds it inconvenient.** Nobody thanked her and a woman who might have said a kind thing did not, and it is not a recognition scene and there is no scene between them.
- **The air gate was shut for the first time in twenty-nine weeks, and an uncertified mouth was opened as a vent for two hours, and both were professional acts and neither was a favour to anybody.** She said out loud, before anybody could say it after her, that she was not doing it for him.
- **Talla Roke is in the building, on her own terms, with her own three, and is not a rescue.** She brought the market day and a bundle that cannot leave this building. **She set the test the evacuation had to pass — ordinary residents, no order, nobody at the front — and it passed, and thirty-one people went up a market road and her three and she were four people out of thirty-five.** Her rule is in a clerk's book in her own words. **She said out loud in an anteroom that the withdrawal of the form was not a win, and the clerk wrote *a week is not a month* twice in the book so that the second one is the one a person reads.** **Her brother is named in two chapters of this batch, as one of the three who could not be asked and reading the first column aloud, she is in neither of those two, no chapter in this batch puts the two of them in the same room, and he is not used as a route to her.**
- **The board is sixteen entries: eleven nulls, one claim, one mark, one row, a plan and a condition; nine in the ordinary column and seven in the column with nothing over the top of it.** The sixteenth is a condition, entered by the clerk herself, the first thing anybody in this building has put on that board that is a sentence somebody can stop. **The column is still unheaded, for the eighth consecutive batch, and the eighth reason is new and worse and is not about a word: a heading is a place to keep the person who works under it.**
- **The woman from the wash rooms is not named, not asked, not rostered and not sent for.** A room was struck out of a clerk's list of rooms in nine seconds in Chapter 142 and a room was struck out of a printed schedule in nine seconds in Chapter 149, and no reason was given on either occasion and she was not asked on either occasion. The floor was not approached. The page is still blank.

## Numbers a later batch must not re-derive

- **The week runs Monday to Sunday. 141–145 the twenty-eighth, 146–150 the twenty-ninth.** Each chapter sits on the matching day of its week. The corridor is shut in **141, 142, 144, 146, 147 and 149** and open in **143, 145, 148 and 150**, and the school ran in **143, 145, 148 and 150**, for the nineteenth, twentieth, twenty-first and twenty-second mornings, **all four in the room at the kitchen-line end. The school corner is open and is not used and no chapter in this batch put the school back in it. The market day is the sixth day of the twenty-seventh week and is behind Chapter 141 and is not in this batch.**
- **The corridor was opened on the first and second days of the twenty-ninth week by Renn Vale's own written term**, with a condition and no number and no day on it. **No closure was removed and no school day was restored: the school does not run on those two days and lost nothing, and the open days lost in Chapter 108 and Chapter 130 are still lost.**
- **The water at the waist was on the fill for the whole batch and never came back and never came up again.** It went off the fill for about an hour on the Friday afternoon of the twenty-eighth week and came back on it before the pump came off, and that is entered. **It is on the ground, not in the channel, about the height of a knee, and it is not moving, and the third wedge at the waist is up a quarter of an inch and a bit and was not touched, and there is no number for that fill in this building and there is not going to be one.**
- **Wen Pask's count is 76 in Chapter 141 and 85 in Chapter 150, one a day, and all ten are on the page in the right chapter, verified file by file.** It is his own count, kept by a clerk, in the column with no heading and in nothing else. It is not a register, it dates nothing, and it may not be confused, merged or remarked upon as a coincidence with the day-number register. **It is at eighty-five and the clerk has said out loud in a room, in four weeks running, that it is not going to be eighty-six and that she is going to keep writing it, and nobody has thanked her, and a man from a surface federation read it out of her book and did not say a kind thing about it.**
- **No day number is attached to any in-batch event and the day-number register's highest value remains the forty-sixth day.** **The second gate's distance is stated nowhere in this batch.** **A notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time is neither repeated nor corrected.** Chapter 119's bounded Compact-form exception was not used.
- **Crew hours: sixty-three and a half**, up four from fifty-nine and a half on the third day of the twenty-eighth week, on a named asking made in a room with the terms out loud, Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **and the three who could not be asked named with the reason for each before the asking.** **A man's two and a half days at the low end are in the boundary's column and not the crew's, and a spent line is not an hour and never was.**
- **Boundary hours: a hundred and seventeen and a quarter, plus a hundred and sixty-five, = two hundred and eighty-two and a quarter.** The list adds **by the day the work was done**: **three, two, four, three, two in the twenty-eighth week; three, four, two, three, two in the twenty-ninth**, summing to twenty-eight, and the weekly list is given at the fifth chapter of each week. Running figures with the day's increment and the total are given at the sixth bells of **141, 142, 143, 145, 147, 148 and 150**, and are entered and not read in **144, 146 and 149** with a reason in a clerk's hand in each. **The base is the constant one hundred and seventeen and a quarter, the total is monotonic from 110 to 150, both columns reconcile, and the reconciliation counter is carried unchanged at *twelve weeks* in every mouth in this batch and is not re-derived.**
- **Wedges: seven sound and two dead sticks, and one of the two dead sticks is still gone.** Two at the school-door head, one in the school corner's door, three at the waist (the third up a quarter of an inch and a bit), one in the basket. **No wedge was bought, moved or added, and nobody put a hand on the fill.**
- **The pot is at ten days and has not gone up since the fifth day of the nineteenth week**, and the jars are two a day, entered separately and never added to the pot.
- **The brass survey rule has now said nothing for longer than sixteen weeks** and was not put on a table. **The right hand's fine control is not recovered, the left hand did not close after the holding, the Reader reading is not repeatable and was not used, the Chapter 99 claim's condition is still unmet, no route change as a stage, no binding, no relay, no brace, no panel of any kind, and no mark cut in the stone anywhere in this building.**

## What Batch 0005 leaves for Volume 04

1. **The immediate promise is answered and the larger question is open, and the question is about routes and the law.** A public occupancy plan that a boundary keeps and a surface federation has asked to be able to see; a guild cartel that has lost exclusivity on one road at a counter and expects to have it back in a month; six Compact pages with a clause in them; and a question asked out loud twice and not answered either time.
2. **The crew have been asked three times in twenty-nine weeks, on a named asking, in a room, with the terms out loud.** Their column is **sixty-three and a half** and is a quantity of asking. **A fourth asking is owed nothing and is available**, and the three who cannot be asked now have a third set of reasons, and the reasons must be re-derived again from the state of those three people rather than carried.
3. **A network of four rooms and a door, public and bounded, on a page in four parts in a coat, with a person named in a room who may stop it and no name on the page.** Its second way out is a word. **Its bottleneck is a woman and an anteroom's ten for two hours, one of whose five conditions has been broken since the middle of the twenty-sixth week.**
4. **A room that was sealed and is open, under a condition in a keeper's own hand, checked every morning the room is used and four mornings a week in an empty room by a woman saying a sentence to a building.** A girl of nine with a foot, on the page, named once in the volume's last chapter.
5. **A grate off a channel, a review page that is still blank, a woman who was never asked, a condition that was broken by a man who was not sent, and a clerk's own entry that the difference between the two halves of it was the smallest thing in her book.**
6. **A dead man of twenty-two whose count is at eighty-five and is not going to be eighty-six, and a bundle in an anteroom that cannot leave this building because this boundary will not fill in two lines on somebody else's form.**
7. **A cell that is uncaught, unrecruited and unread, with a legible reason, and a grate that is still off and no second one.**
8. **A title in a field book that is wrong on purpose, a reply line with a space in it, four pages and six pages from a federation that assume this boundary wants to be looked at, and a clause that says a room whose condition is not being checked may be entered.**
9. **A board with sixteen entries and a column with nothing over the top of it, and a count read at a sixth bell that is not going to stop.**
10. **A man with a left hand that will not close, a mark on his forearm, a knee, and a statement made in a room that he cannot go down there again and does not know why — and a clerk's question at a seventh bell about what he is going to do when the weather turns, which he did not answer, and which is the volume's last open thread about him.**
11. **A person under a lip, packed and not held, with a post that has never been built, and an anteroom frame a finger and a bit out of true with the mark off the wall and declared stopped, and a second way out that is a word a woman on a landing has said in a room is not a way out and has not taken out of a room's terms.**
12. **A market route that a person at a counter decided is not exclusive, and a competent person at the same counter who expects it to be exclusive again in a month, and a plan on a page of sixteen rows that has no row for the one place in this building where a man is dead.**

## Repairs applied in Batch 0005

1. **The speech-paragraph markup form was wrong on delivery and the repair made it worse; the review phase has reversed the repair.** The house form is a quotation mark, two asterisks, the text, two asterisks, a closing quotation mark, and a bold section divider that opens and closes its own span. **Two automated normalisation passes were run in the writing session and both stripped closing pairs, which is what inverted the form: on delivery the batch carried 279 speech paragraphs with no closing pair of asterisks against 0 with one, and Chapters 101–110 deliver 207 with one against 7 without.** All 312 affected paragraphs — 279 speech paragraphs and 33 bold dividers, plus one paragraph in Chapter 150 that had lost its quotation marks altogether — are now in the house form and every one of the ten files has an even asterisk count. **No prose was reworded; only quotation marks and asterisks moved. This is Batch 0004's lesson for the third time in three batches, and the addition to the rule is that the form is countable and must be checked before delivery: a figure that cannot be reproduced by the next writer is a figure that will be handed forward as validated and will not be.**
2. **Fifty-one connective openers were rewritten into other shapes.** The including-bold *And* figure went from twenty-nine to **zero** against a target of under eleven, and the *The* figure from nineteen to **four**, which is Batch 0004's figure. **The chapters are the same length they were before the pass, which is the test that the rewriting was not deletion.**
3. **Chapter 144 was 5,491 words and is 4,620.** Cut twice, by 415 and by 456, and not a third time. **The reason is recorded in the delivery record and not left as a number that quietly exceeds Batch 0004's ceiling: it carries three complete scenes and cutting further would have removed a beat rather than trimmed a sentence.**
4. **The protagonist was absent from three chapters on delivery and the writing session's own measurement did not check for it.** He was named in seven of ten; **he is now named in ten of ten, with three beats written in 146, 148 and 149.** The viewpoint-presence check is in the baseline and was run on the files. **This is the second consecutive batch in which a state-file assertion would have been false and the measurement caught it.**
5. **Five recurring formula paragraphs were found on the duplication check and all five were rewritten**, and the check's third exclusion — that the house's recurring sixth-bell divider formula is not a duplicated paragraph — is now part of the method and was validated against Batch 0004, where it turns a raw two into a recorded zero. **The review phase established that this batch's own reported zero did not follow from the exclusion it was stated with: on that exclusion the measure returns three groups, all of them the clerk's daily record of the pot, the jars and the fill, and the board's entries read out, and each of the nine instances carries that day's own fact after the shared opening. The figure reaches zero only under a broader and unstated exclusion that drops every speech paragraph. Both numbers are now in the craft baseline with the exclusion that produces each.**
6. **Four meta and date faults were corrected against the week clock:** one narration *in this book* in Chapter 146 cut entirely; seven licensed instances in mouths reduced to *this clerk's book* or *this ledger*, leaving three; **the crew's column's last move corrected from the second day of last month to the second day of the twenty-sixth week in two chapters**; and Chapter 150's date for the eighth reason corrected from the second day of the twenty-seventh week to the first day of the twenty-eighth week, together with a typographical error in the same sentence, *twenty-eventh*. **Two further meta instances were cut in the review phase — *this whole volume* in Chapter 147's narration, now *this whole business*, and *the last week of a volume* in Chapter 150's count, now *in the last week of a month* — and two further date contradictions were corrected against the week clock: Chapter 141's *the second day of last month* for the count, now *the second day of the twenty-sixth week* against Chapter 150's own figure, and Chapter 150's *the fourth day of this month* for Marek Venn's *I am not a post*, now *the fourth day of last week*, which is Chapter 144's Thursday.**
7. **Two stray closing quotation marks on bold dividers were found by the file-level evenness check and removed** — one in Chapter 144 and one in Chapter 149 — and neither was found by reading.

Nine classes of defect in the prose are repaired, three errors in this batch's own review record are corrected, and one figure that did not reproduce has been restated. No plot, outline, chapter, cast, calendar or ending was changed.**

4. **Meta language is now genuinely zero**, and the two date figures that contradicted a pinned date in the same batch are corrected. See repair 6 above.
5. **Chapter 147's one garbled sentence** — *Through in twelves and then the rest went the movement* — now reads *Through in twelves and then the rest went, and the movement went on.*
6. **Three errors in the review record are corrected** in `reviews/volume-03/batch-0005.md` and in the delivery record: the board is walked in **141, 143, 147 and 150** and not in 148, which states the board *was not walked*; **Pell Roke is in two chapters of this batch**, named in 143 among the three who could not be asked and reading the first column aloud in 150, and the clause saying he is in no chapter belongs to **Wen Pask**, who is in all ten; and the calendar bullet's arithmetic no longer juxtaposes a base of 117.25 with a day list summing to 28 — the figures are 117.25 + 165 = 282.25, where 165 is 137 + 28.

**Four findings are recorded and deliberately not repaired, because repairing them would mean changing a closed batch or inventing a beat.**

- **The markup defect is inherited by two closed batches of this volume.** Counted on the delivered files, speech paragraphs that open and close their own quotation run 205 closed against 129 open in Chapters 101–110, 220 against 112 in 111–120, 195 against 224 in 121–130, and 155 against 214 in 131–140. **Volume 03 Batches 0003 and 0004 are closed and independently reviewed, and roughly 440 speech paragraphs across them will render with literal asterisks. This batch was repaired and the two closed ones were not, and that is a decision for the controller or the next review phase, not for a writer phase.**

The gender is corrected; the event is not, because no such asking happens in any chapter of this batch. **Owed to the next writer, with the repair: re-anchor the sentence to the Thursday-afternoon exchange that does happen, which is the sixth clause read aloud in a room and the clerk refusing to read the day's arithmetic to a man who is carrying it out of the building.**
