# Volume 04, Batch 0001 — delivered, Chapters 151–160

**Ten chapters in `chapters/volume-04/`, close third person on Marek Venn, no viewpoint shift anywhere in the batch, and the protagonist named in ten of ten with interior life in ten of ten.** The batch's delivery record is at the head of `state/batch-summary.md`; this section records only what a later phase must not contradict.

**`outline/volume-04.md` exists and was written in the same phase that wrote this batch.** It is a forward plan for Chapters 151–200, *Nine Roads, One Throat*, and it is the only thing Volume 04 may be written against. Its ten commitments from `outline/series.md`, its four departures, its batch map, its guardrails and its inherited canon are all in that file and are not restated here except where the delivery has moved them.

## What the batch established, in canon

- **The market form is back on the board at the gate four days up the middle passage, with a seal number on it that is not the number it had before, and nobody put it up.** A road hand brought the fact down and did not look at a cart for anybody. **A sheet comes back on a board by a schedule, and the boundary's own instrument against that is a man from a surface federation who said in a room in the twenty-ninth week that a regime is not a threat, it is a schedule, and that a thing which is scheduled is not a thing that is refused.**
- **A guild load's paper is in the building: seven lines, two of them for a name and for the person responsible for the load, and the word in it for not doing the carrying is *attended*.** Five of the seven were argued out loud before anything was marked. **The boundary will not fill in the two, and the cart is not coming up the middle passage, and nobody in this building has sent anybody or anything.** A carrier came up on foot with the paper and did not know what the office wanted of him if nobody filled it in and said so in a room.
- **A fifth document from a body the charter does not name is in this batch's record: a printed Compact schedule with a column headed for the person who will be present and three rooms under it.** It was struck in nine seconds from three steps up, with the heading and the three rooms, and no reason was given. **A third room was left standing and a carrier explained in a room what a schedule is for: it says the third room is one somebody is coming to on a day, and nobody has put anybody's name on it because there is not anybody to put.**
- **The volume's central discovery, delivered in a room: a store is a room, and a room has a keeper, and a keeper can be asked in a room with the terms out loud, and a keeper can say no.** Ormer Hatch, forty-nine, thirty-one years, survey camp, keeps a store of eleven years, said no to the timber and said *bring your keeper*, and came down the middle passage on the second morning running with a slate of his own. **The price is not money, because there is no money in this building, and it is two things: no name of his on any paper of this boundary's, and the whole of his list read out in a room with him in it including the lines that are nearly out — and a third thing he asked for and was not refused on the day, which is that a guild's fourth paragraph be named in that room as the thing it is, and which Bel Ordry deferred to a morning when there is nothing on the table, on the stated reason that a man with eleven years of beech would otherwise be the thing being persuaded.**
- **A store's list of fourteen lines has no date on it, and the reason is a schoolteacher's shape of a count given in her own mouth without knowing she was giving it: a list with a date on it is a moment pretending to be a day.** The list was read twice and compared, the ninth line is a dash and was read twice at the keeper's request, and **the list and what came down the passage agree, line by line, and that is the first time in thirty-one weeks that a document in this building and a fact in a room have been the same thing.**
- **A brace is defined in a room, out of a survey's four sentences, and this Hearthhold has one of the four things it needs.** Joinwood, timber, stone, cable or another tested support: it has stone. A counter-bearing: it has half of one. Time to let the load settle: it has none and cannot buy any and cannot beg any. A bearing mark: it has one it cannot read. **Its counter-bearing cannot be taken at the low end of the corridor, because a brace that reacts at the lowest point in a building is a brace that puts a person there, and the third of the three conditions on the blank review page says that nobody is to be sent anywhere to make it true, and the clerk read that page out of her own book before the man had finished saying it.** So the reaction goes on the party wall the schoolroom leans on, and **the survey camp's finding that the wall is a bad repair on a sound wall is what makes the brace possible, and the same sheet in the same hand says that a sound sector gets no crew put in it again, and Jo Verrick said in a room that those are the same sentence and that she is tired of that page.**
- **The mark is not his and is not chalk.** Four marks and one groove in the lintel above the open school corner's mouth, one of the four being two strokes, read three ways this month by three people — a schoolteacher, a mason, and a carpenter's mason's opinion which he says is worth nothing and gives anyway. **The four are damaged and the groove is not, and the carpenter's whole professional claim is that the one undamaged mark on a wall is the one that was cut to be read, and the brace's limit did not come out of that stone.** **The limit will be a condition written by the person the brace can hurt, in her own hand, with no number and no day on it, and it is falsifiable and it will be met.**
- **The joinwood is the school door's own.** Two wedges at the school-door head and two beech lengths out of the school store, given by the woman who keeps that door, who said in the same breath that **a door with no wedge is a door that has to be watched, and the answer is a person, and there is not a person available, and the page where a person would go is blank with three conditions on it and the third of them says that nobody is to be sent anywhere to make it true.** She said she has better answers and has looked and has not found one. **The school door has no wedge and nothing in this batch puts one back, and the brace those two wedges are waiting for is not built.**
- **Nera Oduya asked Marek Venn for a work, in the crew's own practice, with the terms out loud, with a person named who can be told no, and with the three she was not going to ask named with the reason for each before she asked him anything.** The work is to go and look at the air at the low end of the corridor, from above, not from inside it. **She said the cost out loud before anybody could say it after her: the asking puts a standing on him, and a standing is the first half of a post, and she asked for the word *standing* in the clerk's book and not the word *help*.** He said yes, and said that the reason he will go is not that she is the authority and he is not, and that he wants to go. **The clerk put his hours in the boundary's column and not the crew's, and gave the reason out loud, and it is the same reason as in the twenty-eighth week — a man is not an hour — and the second reason is new: she is not the crew and has never once asked the five of them for anything, and this is what the boundary's column is for.**
- **The third volume question was answered by his own mouth and resolved nothing:** he is going to go and look at the air on Wednesday with a lamp in his left hand, and after that he does not know, and the clerk entered the first half and not the second half and entered that she had had a fortnight of wanting to enter the second.
- **Nera Oduya's condition is not met and she said so in a room, and she set a second condition, and she said it out loud twice, and nobody asked her in a room.** The reason for saying it twice is the boundary's own: the first is a sentence and the second is a fact, and a sentence can be lifted off a page. The condition is **that she will not take it back while it is being watched.** The reason for it is hers and she did not hand it over.
- **A route-holder's post is in a carrier's hand with Iven Tallo's name in the second line, in a stiff cover with a proper seal and no date on it.** A bond, a wage in coin, hours entered against a named route in a register kept by an office, and a boy back on the roll with a number on it and not *the apprentice of* anything. **He neither refused it nor accepted it, and gave the reason: a refusal given before a thing has been understood is a thing a man says to look clean, and he has watched a man do it in this building, and it was him, in the twenty-second week, about the sill.** He asked for the entry to say the date he refuses is not today.
- **The hole in the guild's offer is not the guild's.** A clerk read the document against itself and found that the post is in this Hearthhold, and this boundary's charter says in terms that no holder of a route here is to be entered by the office against any work here, and the guild knows it. **The guild's answer is a sentence said in a room by a man who keeps a page: the post is at a camp four and a half days up a road that took the halfpenny sheet, that camp has had timber since the sheet came out, and a camp with timber can shut a route when a clerk at a counter says so and has not had to yet.** The woman who keeps the road said the other half, which is that it is a hand out of a gap in a clause wearing a bond and a wage, and a person in a bad month is going to hold the wage and not look at the hand, and that the person it will find is a boy on a bench, and a boy's roll number is a route.
- **A carrier wrote a not-refusal on the outside of a stiff cover with no name on it, and said he would hand it back to the same man in the same room, and that if anybody asks him up the road what he carried he will say he carried a piece of paper and a thing that was not a refusal.** He is the first person in this batch to work out how not to become an office without being asked a single question about it.
- **A physician asked for a mark on the party wall and asked for the clerk to read it and not herself**, on the stated reason that a physician who takes her own readings is a physician who decides when she stopped believing them. **She named the person in the brace and refused to name a child, because a child would be the easy way to stop the work and would be a lie with a name in it, and the person she named is the woman who keeps that room.** She gave the number when asked for it — four tons, or thereabouts — and made the clerk write the words *or thereabouts* next to the four tons, and said the number is not an argument, it is an instrument she has to carry into a room every morning and read out loud.
- **A condition was written by the woman who keeps the schoolroom, in her own hand, with no number and no day on it, and it is about the brace and not about her room:** the brace stands while the two of them still agree that the wall can take it; the first of them to stop agreeing takes the brace out; neither has to give a reason to the other first; the second to find out is the one who acts. **She said the cost of it out loud — that it is nearly free, and that a condition which costs nothing is a condition a person in a bad month will decide is not worth saying, and that she taught that sentence to a room herself — and that if she is the one who takes the brace out then nine children are going to think the woman who keeps their room is frightened, and they will be right and she will be wrong, and she is not going to be able to stand in that doorway and explain the difference.** **It is not met and the brace is not up.**
- **The pot went from ten days to nine.** It is at nine and has not gone up since the fifth day of the nineteenth week and has now gone down. **The cook said it out loud in a room, gave the reason, and said that a dead man's share has been going back into that pot since the fourth day of the twenty-fifth week on purpose and is not going to be done for a brace.** Jo Verrick says the seam is at four threads and was eight in the nineteenth week and has not been measured in between, and there is no number for it and the clerk has entered that she is not going to be the one who makes one.
- **The first figure anybody in this building has taken at the waist on purpose in thirty-one weeks was given in a room by a woman nobody asked: two inches and a bit of movement in a party wall over about an hour.** **The three people who decided on purpose never to measure that fill gave their reason in the twenty-seventh week and their reason is not withdrawn and the figure is here anyway.** It is in a clerk's book and not on a page, because the plan has no row for that wall and the refusal of a row for the low end of the corridor stands and was not re-argued in this batch.
- **The board is seventeen entries: eleven nulls, one claim, one mark, one row, a plan, a condition and a store; nine in the ordinary column and eight in the column with nothing over the top of it.** The store is the first thing on that board that is not in this building and it goes in the unheaded column on a courier's rule arriving in a place it was not built for. **Tams Quill gave the ninth reason for refusing to head that column and it is the first of the nine that is not about him: a heading is how a room finds out what the person in it is for, and there are rooms in this building that have never been asked that.** He refused a tenth and said he would say the week got away from him. **He is in the batch's closing image as the only person in this building whom the clerk has never once asked, and the clerk entered that she had not known that was true.**
- **Volume 04's question is asked out loud in a room in four words and not answered: who owns a wall.** Asked by Ormer Hatch, who said before he asked it that he was not asking it as a complaint, that the not-being-on the plan did not feel like a gift, and that he has about a week of store left and two days to find out an answer he cannot find out. **Four people tried and none of them did.** **A woman three steps up said she does not have half of it and said she would give it if she had, and asked for that to be entered so that a person in a year does not think there was a woman in that room who knew and would not say — and this varies the third volume's pattern and is the reason the volume's question is not answered by the air engineer.** **A man said he knows the answer for two of the four walls in that building and refused twice to say it out loud, and gave the reason: saying it in a room is making a claim, and he is not going to be the first man in this building to find a loophole in a thing thirty people agreed to.** **A clerk was asked to put two questions next to each other for the third time in a month and refused for the third time and entered the three refusals in one sentence with the two questions.** The man from the store said that was all right, and that his answer to how a thing gets looked after is *by somebody who is standing near it who can be asked*, and asked for it read back to him.

## Numbers a later batch must not re-derive

- **The week runs Monday to Sunday. 151–155 the thirtieth week, 156–160 the thirty-first.** Each chapter sits on the matching day of its week. **The corridor is shut on the first, second and fourth days and open on the third, fifth and sixth, and the seventh day is not a crossing day; the school runs on the three open days.** So in Batch 0001 the corridor is **shut in 151, 152, 154, 156, 157 and 159** and **open in 153, 155, 158 and 160**, and the school ran in those same four, being the **twenty-third, twenty-fourth, twenty-fifth and twenty-sixth mornings, all four in the room at the kitchen-line end.**
- **The school corner is open and is not used, and no chapter in this batch put the school back in it, and no school day was restored and no closure was removed.**
- **Wen Pask's count is 86 in Chapter 151 and 95 in Chapter 160, one a day, on the locked base of twenty-three on the fifth day of the seventeenth week, and all ten are on the page in the right chapter.** It is his own count, kept by a clerk, in the column with nothing over the top of it and in nothing else, it is not a register, it dates nothing, and it may not be confused, merged or remarked upon as a coincidence with the day-number register. **It is at ninety-five, it is not going to be ninety-six, and the clerk has said that out loud in six weeks running and nobody has thanked her in six weeks running.**
- **No day number is attached to any in-batch event and the day-number register's highest value remains the forty-sixth day.** The only date on any object is the date in the top corner of the plan. **Nothing in this batch is dated at all: not the market form, not the carrier's paper, not the Compact schedule, not the store's list, not the guild's post.** The store's list carries no date **on purpose**, and the reason is on the page in a schoolteacher's words.
- **The spoken measure of elapsed weeks is a separate register**, is not re-derived, is not corrected and is not used to date anything. **From the thirtieth week onward *thirty* is the week clock itself and is not available as drift.** Counts that track the week clock are re-derivable and monotonic in this batch: the review page at the low end has been blank for **thirty-one weeks**, the plan has been transcribing the anteroom's count for **thirty-one weeks**, the clerk has been this boundary's clerk for **thirty-one weeks**, and the anteroom frame's packing went in on the third day of the eighteenth week and the frame is **a finger and three-quarters** out of true.
- **No forward count of days or weeks on a courier.** The road is four days up the middle passage to the middle gate and forty days on from the top of it to a guild file, **the second gate's distance is stated nowhere in this batch**, and **a store four days up that passage is four days up it and no other figure is attached to it.** A notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time **is neither repeated nor corrected**; this batch's instance of it is a sheet that came back on a board by a schedule.
- **Crew hours: sixty-six and a half, up three from sixty-three and a half, on the third day of the thirtieth week**, on a named asking made in a room with the terms out loud and Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **and the three who could not be asked named with the reason for each before the asking.** The reasons are a third set and are not the reasons of Volume 03's third asking: **Leena Orr, because she is the person who will have to be asked whether the schoolroom's wall can take a push; Pell Roke, because he reads numbers and a measurement a person has read aloud and nobody has written down is a figure in the column with nothing over the top of it; Tams Quill, because if he is also the hands then the man who records what a thing turned out to be is the man who found out.** The work was **two hours of Iven Tallo's and one hour of Marek Venn's, and the carpenter named the split himself before he was asked.**
- **Boundary hours: a hundred and seventeen and a quarter, plus a hundred and ninety-three, = three hundred and ten and a quarter.** The list adds **by the day the work was done**: **three, two, four, three, two in the thirtieth week; three, four, two, three, two in the thirty-first**, summing to twenty-eight. **Running figures with the day's increment and the total are read out in five chapters — 151, 153, 155, 158 and 160 — and are entered and not read out in 152, 154, 156, 157 and 159, each with a reason in a clerk's hand that is specific to that morning.** The base is the constant one hundred and seventeen and a quarter, the total is monotonic, both columns reconcile, **and the reconciliation counter is re-derived once, at the start of this batch, from twelve weeks in the twenty-ninth week: it is thirteen in the thirtieth week and fourteen in the thirty-first, and it is not re-derived again inside the batch.**
- **Wedges: seven sound and one dead stick at the start of the batch, and the two at the school-door head are now in a brace that is not built.** Two in the school corner's door, three at the waist with the third up a quarter of an inch and a bit and not touched, one in the basket. **The school door has none. No wedge was bought and none was moved back.**
- **The pot is at nine days, having been at ten since the fifth day of the nineteenth week and never gone up.** **The jars are two a day, entered separately and never added to the pot, with one on the second day of the thirtieth week.** **The seam is at four threads at a first bell and Jo Verrick says it was eight in the nineteenth week and has not been measured in between, and there is no number for it.**
- **The water at the waist went off the fill on the second day of the thirtieth week and has not been on it since. No chapter in this batch says it came back or came up again, and nobody in this building has said why, and Jo Verrick has said in a room that she is not going to guess at it.**
- **The brass survey rule has now said nothing for longer than twenty-one weeks in the thirtieth week and twenty-two in the thirty-first, on the origin at the ninth week that `outline/volume-04.md` fixes and says it fixes.** The wrapped plate on the same shelf is **thirty weeks in the thirtieth week and thirty-one in the thirty-first** and is the consistent register. **Any later phase that quotes Chapter 150's sixteen must say that it is quoting a closed chapter and not the register.**
- **The right hand's fine control is not recovered. The left hand did not close after the holding in the twenty-eighth week and has not closed since, and a carpenter cut eleven pieces of beech with it in Chapter 158.** The Reader reading is not repeatable and was not used, the Chapter 99 claim's condition is unmet, the Marker is spent and its mark is off the wall, **and no power stage advanced in this batch, no route change as a stage, no binding, no relay, no brace built, no panel of any kind, and no mark cut in the stone anywhere in this building.**

## Repairs applied in Batch 0001's own writing session

**This batch was measured against the files after every structural edit, and the measurements changed the prose eight times. The findings are recorded here because the figures in `state/batch-summary.md` are the files' and not the session's belief about them.**

1. **Markup was wrong twice and both defects were in the files, not in the reading.** A speech paragraph in Chapter 151 had a bold span that closed mid-paragraph and reopened after a sentence of narration, and **a merge of two speeches in Chapter 160 dropped a bold marker and produced four doubled quotation marks and three paragraphs with an odd bold count.** Both were found by a file-level evenness check and not by reading, **and the third of them was introduced by a repair of a repair.** The lesson is Batch 0003's and Batch 0004's for the third time in three batches: **a repair made by paragraph index will break the form, and the files must be re-measured from disk after any structural edit.** All ten files are now even on asterisks and on quotation marks, every paragraph has an even quotation count and an even bold count, there is no run of three or more asterisks, and there is no doubled quotation mark.
2. **Sixty-three connective openers were rewritten into other shapes, in two passes.** In the writing session fifty-one were rewritten: the including-bold *And* figure came out of the first pass at **thirteen** and fell to **four**; *The* was **eighteen** and fell to **seven**; *Nobody* was **fifteen** and fell to **six**. **A review-fix pass then added fifteen narration paragraphs, twelve of which began *The* or *Nobody*, which pushed those two figures back to eighteen and eleven, and twelve openers were rewritten a second time into other shapes.** As corrected, including bold: *The* **9**, *Nobody* **8**, *And* **5**, *She* 12, *He* 11, forty-five together; excluding bold: *The* 7, *Nobody* 7, *And* 4, *She* 12, *He* 11, forty-one together. **The chapters are within ninety words of their length before the second pass, which is the test that the rewriting was not deletion.**
3. **The divider count was recorded as falling from a first pass of eighty-nine to sixty-three, and that figure cannot be reproduced under any definition this file states, so it is corrected and the claim behind it is withdrawn.** Measured on the delivered files there are **66 fully-bold paragraphs, of which 38 are under three hundred characters**, which is the natural reading of a section divider. The old number was a first-pass figure carried into the record as though it were a measurement of the delivery, and the claim that it fell without a beat being cut is not verifiable from the files. **The rule this establishes is that a divider figure is worthless without its definition and its exclusions in the same sentence, which is the same rule the duplication figure was breaking two items below.**
4. **Two duplicated-paragraph groups were found and both are now repaired, and the group this item described was misidentified.** It was recorded as *the school-morning paragraph*, and it is not: **it is the third of the three reasons for not asking somebody, in Dalla Sen's mouth in Chapter 153 and Nera Oduya's in Chapter 156, and the sentence the two chapters shared was the description of Tams Quill's right hand.** That sentence was rewritten in 156 in the review-fix pass. A count read-out paragraph shared by 158 and 160 had already been rewritten in the writing session. **The batch's duplicated non-bold content paragraph count is now zero, and the exclusion is stated in the same sentence as the figure: fully-bold divider paragraphs are excluded, and measured without that exclusion there are two groups, both of them the sixth-bell house formula, in 154/156/157/159 and in 155/158/160.** Volume 03's own record noted that the recurring sixth-bell divider formula is a house repetition and is not a duplicated paragraph; **the same reasoning is now applied in writing and not only in measurement, and the previous version of this item reported the headline figure without its exclusion, which is the practice item 8 tells later phases to stop.**
5. **The protagonist was absent from one chapter on first measure and the check caught it.** He was named in nine of ten and Chapter 155 had none. **A beat was written into 155 and two more into 154 and 159, the latter two for Renn Vale, who was also absent from them.** All ten now carry him with interior life, and **the viewpoint-presence check that Volume 03's fourth batch added to the baseline was run on the files and not asserted, for the first time in three batches.**
6. **One meta leak was written and cut:** *Then the room tried, and the trying is the rest of the chapter.* A scan of the ten files returns **zero** instances of *chapter*, *volume*, *this batch* or *the reader* in narration. **One narration use of *in this book* was cut from Chapter 158**, where four men carried the beech down a passage *who are not named in this book*, and the surviving licensed uses are all in a mouth or in the clerk's own entry.
7. **Two chapters exceeded the soft ceiling of four thousand words before a review-fix pass and three exceed it now, and the per-chapter figures this item carried were wrong and are corrected here. It said Chapter 159 at 4,035 and Chapter 160 at 4,169; the delivered files were Chapter 159 at 4,169 and Chapter 160 at 4,131, and the range 2,837 to 4,169 and the total 35,694 in the same item were correct, so only the attribution was wrong and the cut arithmetic that went with it, by thirty-nine and one hundred and eighteen words, is unverifiable as written. The batch as corrected stands at 2,895 to 4,294 and 36,973 in all, with 159 at 4,294 and 160 at 4,187 over the ceiling and 156 at 3,975 now under it.** The reason is that Chapter 160 carries the volume's question, four attempts at an answer, a clerk's third refusal, a sixth-bell read and a closing image, and Chapter 159 carries three complete scenes and a condition, and Chapter 156 carries two askings in full with the terms of each. **The first pass used the *And* and *The* figures as its levers instead of deletion; the review-fix pass used the sentence structure as its lever and traded about 1,400 words of run-together prose for 1,279 words of physical staging.**
8. **The craft method did not reproduce Volume 03 Batch 0005's recorded paragraph figures and that is a finding, not a defect in this batch.** Run against the delivered files of Chapters 141–150 the method returns **200 non-dialogue paragraphs against a recorded 235, 105 not bold-opened against a recorded 142, 95 bold section-divider openers against a recorded 93**, and opener figures of 3 / 3 / 4 / 4 / 4 including bold against a recorded 4 / 4 / 0 / 3 / 4. **The figures that reproduce are the ones that carry information and the ones that do not are the paragraph count and the divider count. A later phase must validate against **the delivered files of this batch, `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0151.md` through `chapter-0160.md`**, and not against Batch 0004's or Batch 0005's, state its exclusions with its figure, and must not carry any superseded paragraph figure from this batch or from Batch 0005 forward as though it had been measured. **Every paragraph and divider figure in items 2, 3 and 4 above was itself superseded once by the review-fix pass, which is the proof that a carried-forward figure decays.** The corrected baseline is: **741 body paragraphs, 214 non-dialogue, 674 not bold-opened, 66 fully-bold of which 38 are under three hundred characters, openers including bold *The* 9 / *Nobody* 8 / *And* 5 / *She* 12 / *He* 11, duplicated non-bold content paragraphs zero with the fully-bold exclusion stated, quoted words 61 to 76 per cent by chapter and 69.4 average, mean sentence 31.1 words and longest 97.** **Narrative share and sentence length were not measured at all before the fix pass, and their absence from this list is the finding: a chapter can pass every check in this section and still read as the transcript of a meeting.**
9. **The batch card was corrected after delivery, and the reason recorded in the card and in the review was itself wrong and has been corrected a second time.** `outline/batches/volume-04-batch-0001.md` placed Pell Roke in Chapters 157 and 160; the prose places him in 153, 156 and 158, with the store's figures read aloud by him in 158, which is where the card wanted him. **The first correction note went on to say that the apprentice is named in a room in 157 without being in the room, and neither *Pell* nor *Roke* appears in Chapter 157 at all** — what 157 has is an apprentice's number on a roll and a boy on a bench at the top of nine steps, unnamed, which is Renn Vale's argument and is stronger for it. **The note is corrected in the card file and in the review to what the files support.** The guardrail it protected — no chapter puts Talla Roke and Pell Roke in the same room — held in all ten chapters and was re-measured after the fix pass. **She is in 151, 152, 155, 157 and 160; he is in 153, 156 and 158.**

## What Batch 0001 leaves for Batch 0002

1. **The Bracer, and the whole of the bible's four requirements, and the whole of the four costs.** **Chapter 160's closing image has six cut pieces of beech on a bench, a school door with no wedge in it, and a condition on the brace that is not met.** The counter-bearing is chosen and forbidden from being anything else. The mark is damaged and has not said anybody its limit. **There are no pegs and no bronze and no iron, and a carpenter has said a wooden pin in green beech will split it in a year.** A physician has asked a clerk to read a wall every morning for a fortnight. **The condition is not met and Batch 0002 must meet it and admit it in a room before anything is stood on.**
2. **The school door has no wedge, and the answer is a person, and there is not one available, and the page where a person would go is blank.** This is Batch 0002's cost to solve and it may not be solved by a row on the plan and it may not be solved by a post.
3. **The pot is at nine days, the seam is going quiet, and nothing fixes it in this batch.** Four households at a second gate have nothing. **A cook has said a dead man's share is not going back into that pot for a brace, and a seam is the boundary's own drinking water, and neither of those is a thing a plan fixes.**
4. **Iven Tallo has a post in a carrier's hand with his name in the second line and has said the date he refuses is not today, and the refusal is Batch 0002's or a later batch's and not Batch 0002's to be forced.**
5. **A carrier is walking four days of road with a thing that is not a refusal, and the thing on the outside of a stiff cover has no name on it, and the carrier said he would hand it back in the same room.**
6. **A clerk has refused three times in a month to put two questions next to each other and a man has refused twice in a room to say which two walls he would let a brace push on, and the batch says those are the same argument from opposite ends.** Batch 0002 should not repeat either refusal and should cost the man something for the one he made.
7. **A store four days up the middle passage is going to be emptied of its fir on the Monday of Batch 0002's second week by a man with three of his own, and the beech stays, and the terms stand, and the list has no date on it and can be read on any morning he is asked.**
8. **The schedule with a column headed for the person who will be present exists and is a fact this boundary has to work with, and the third room was left standing and nobody in this building knows which one it is.**
9. **The board is at seventeen entries and the column with nothing over the top of it is unheaded for the ninth batch and he has refused a tenth reason and said he would say the week got away from me.**
10. **The question on the page is *who owns a wall*, asked in four words by a man who keeps a store, and nobody answered it, and it is answered in a later volume or not at all.**

Independent reviews of Volume 03 Batches 0003 and 0004 are also owed, because the files that exist for those two batches disclaim independence in their own first lines and an external review does not retrospectively make a self-review independent. `reviews/volume-04/batch-0001.md` exists and is a self-review written inside the writer's own commit, and nothing in this repository may describe Volume 04 Batch 0001 as independently reviewed.**

# Volume 04, Batch 0002 — delivered, Chapters 161–170

**Ten chapters in `chapters/volume-04/`, close third person on Marek Venn, no viewpoint shift anywhere in the batch, and the protagonist named with interior life in ten of ten.** The batch's delivery record is at the head of `state/batch-summary.md`; this section records only what a later phase must not contradict.

## What the batch established, in canon

- **The Bracer stage is delivered.** A brace is a physical support joined to a bearing mark, built by a team of five with **four hands and one cutter**, out of a school's own beech, and **joined to a mark by cutting the wood to the stone and not the stone to the wood, so that no mark was cut in the stone anywhere in this building.** Its head is a splay cut coarse by a man whose left hand does not close, a wider face than a fine cut, carrying four tons. Its joint is tied with the crew's **spent nine-metre line** and is not pegged, on the carpenter's reasoning that he would not put a pin in this brace that he would have to argue about in a year, and that a spent line tells you first. **All four of the bible's requirements are on the page and none is soft: a tested support; a counter-bearing on the party wall, with the low end forbidden and the reason read out of a clerk's book; time to let the load settle, which is four days in seven of which two were spent; and a mark.** **All four of the bible's costs are on the page: material, and the material came out of the school; a new failure point named in a room before anything was stood under it; people can be hurt while he is protecting them, with Mero Senn's rule as the instrument; and a coercive brace is brittle, which is a power-system rule and not a metaphor.**
- **The brace does not increase the anteroom's capacity.** **Ten including one litter for no more than two hours, unchanged**, said out loud in a room by the woman who cooks, and a brace that makes a room safe by making it hold more people was named in that room as the failure.
- **A joint is not a pin.** Four ways of making two pieces agree, and the one this building can afford is a shape that stands up on its own and can be taken apart by a person with a knife and nothing else. **The four things this building does not have are iron, bronze, a kiln and a second pair of hands, and the carpenter puts the one about people last and says he has never once put it last before.**
- **The shim is the joint that matters.** A beech shim a finger wide and four inches long, carrying load on its long edges in a hollow worn in nine-hundred-year-old stone. **The carpenter says its edges will crush in about two years, and that when they crush the head settles and the frame goes a twelfth of an inch out of true again, and that nobody standing in that anteroom is going to feel a twelfth of an inch for a long time, and that a twelfth of an inch is the whole of what Chapter 168 measured this week, so the shim coming out is the frame going back to where it was and not past it, and that the person who will know is a term in a clerk's book, and a term in a clerk's book is a person who has not been born yet.**
- **A fifth asking in thirty-three weeks**, in a room, with the terms out loud, Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, and **the three who could not be asked named with a fourth set of reasons and two of the three are not the names used in the fourth asking**: Leena Orr, because she reads things that are already built; Jo Verrick, because the day the brace goes in is the day the wall she reads has a push coming out of it; and **Pell Roke, because the work is holding and the clerk is not going to ask him to watch instead.** **Four and a half hours — two of Iven Tallo's, two of Marek Venn's, half of Tams Quill's — and the crew's column is seventy-one.**
- **The terms of the fifth asking have six sentences and a split.** The work is not repairing the frame, not fixing the door, not opening anything and not moving anything, and the anteroom's count does not change; the joint is tied and not pegged; **the four sentences of the fourth asking stand**; **a work that stops is a work that was stopped in a room by a person who said so**; every person whose hands are on the brace agrees out loud in a room to what they are holding and what stops it, and the one who does not agree does not hold; and a man asked for the fifth sentence to be made into a term and then said he did not want it.
- **The four terms of the fourth asking — you are not to open anything, you are not to move anything, you take no wedge and no bar, and you do not go near the waist's third wedge — were read out three times against the original in Chapter 170 and all three were the same. They were not struck out, because a strike is a lie, and they were not left, because a term kept in the letter and broken in the fact and left on the page is a term an office four days up a road can pick up and read as this boundary's practice. The finding entered is that they bound a work and not a building, and a building outlasts the terms of a work.**
- **Two people said no to holding the brace and nobody was forced.** **Tams Quill, because the page at the low end has been blank for thirty-two weeks and it is blank because a person who is willing is not a person who is standing there, and he asked for the reason to be entered before anybody was kind to him about it, and said he would be good at it.** **Renn Vale, because she is one of the two people who can take the thing out, and a person who can take a thing out cannot be one of the hands that put it in, because a room will look for the person whose hand was on it, and if that person is the person allowed to take it out then the room has learned the wrong lesson and it will have learned it from her.** The price of not forcing them was a day of delay and a name in a clerk's book, and Dalla Sen said in a room that nobody was going to be made to hold it, by her or by a term or by a pot at nine.
- **Every person whose hands are on the brace said out loud, in a room, what they are holding and what stops it.** Iven Tallo holds the head end and what stops it is a shim that will crush in about two years. Mikka Hale holds a corner at chest height and what stops it is a term and two women, and if it starts to go she lets go and steps back. **Bel Ordry holds the end that goes in and what stops it is the word, and the half against that is that a word is not a wall, and that this morning he discovered the thing he has been protecting is the word and not the wood.** Marek Venn cut it and said what stops it is the four, and that he is the person least able to see the shelter and has said so out loud twice.
- **The brace's failure point is named *the place where it comes out*, by a physician, in a clerk's book, before anything was stood under it. It is a phrase and not a term, and it is not on a stone, and it is not the ninth hearth stone's bed because he had not looked at it.**
- **The condition on the brace was met and admitted in a room on the second day of the thirty-third week**, out loud, by the two people it names, with Mero Senn's written refusal to certify standing next to it and with **three things said by the woman who keeps the room in the space where a reason goes**: that she has never liked the condition and is not pretending otherwise; that nine children will think she is frightened and they will be right and she will be wrong; and that she is glad the wall read nothing and is saying so out loud because the condition is nearly free and this is the one thing she can make it cost. **The clerk entered that the finding is not safe and that nobody in that room is entitled to read the word met as the word fine.** The condition is in force and its second clause was used in Chapter 169.
- **The condition's second clause was used and it worked.** The woman who keeps the room found out at the second bell on a shut day, on her own, with nobody sent, and said all three clauses of her own condition and said the brace was to come out, and nobody argued with her, and **four people took a piece of beech out of that wall in eleven minutes.** A physician would not put his own fingers in the gap because he has spent eleven days asking this room to read a wall and not themselves, and refused to name the man who built it. **Renn Vale refused to ask the man who built it and asked the woman it can hurt instead, and that is the first time in thirty-three weeks this building has got the right person to ask in the right order.**
- **The brace went back in a foot and a half lower**, because the bad repair in that wall is at a height and the push came out at the worst of it, and the carpenter moved the foot down and put a second length under it. **A beech wedge went under the ninth hearth stone's bed, driven by a carpenter in four taps, which is not a repair and not a brace and not a mark and is the only thing in that anteroom that costs nothing and is honest.** The frame is a finger and two-thirds out of true, down from a finger and three-quarters, and **that figure has only been the same twice four minutes apart, and the clerk entered that it is not a number anybody should put in a column.**
- **A carpenter was asked to sign the record of the thing he built and said no**, and gave the reason that his name is in the second line of a stiff cover four and a half days up a road and he has not decided about that one, and asked for it to be entered as the reason and not as modesty. **The line at the bottom of that paper stays empty and the clerk is going to leave it on the page anyway, because a page with a space on it and a page with nothing on it are two different instruments.**
- **Bel Ordry is suspicious of the man with the store, out loud, in a room, on a reason, and arranged by a clerk.** The reason: forty-one pieces of beech, eleven years, nothing in this building can pay him for it and nothing in this building can be found by it, and a store's keeper who has been given a favour by a place he is not in has less room to say no the second time. **The half against it is on the page, and the rule he stated for it is that a man who has said a thing out loud that argues against his own suspicion is the only kind of suspicion this building has ever had. He also said the arrangement was dirty and that he would have said it with the man standing in the room.**
- **Nera Oduya asked for a second work and asked for one**, in the practice, with the terms out loud, Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, and the three she is not asking named with the reason for each. The work is whether the brace changes the air and what the limit is, with no number and no day on it. **She is wrong in public before anybody finds it and says so herself: a frame that has been moving and a frame that has been held do not leak the same, and the corridor is the only thing that moves air between the anteroom and that schoolroom when the mouth is shut, and she did not put those four things together in a month of looking at that end of the building. The half against her own answer is on the page too: the wall stopped on a Wednesday, a Wednesday is a day nine children are in there, and she is not going to say nine children are not a load because she would like the wall to have stopped for a reason she can live with.** **She set a limit: the air in that room stays what it is now, and if it does not, the brace comes out before the air is argued about. She said she is not going to be one of the two women who wrote the condition on the brace, and she said the hard part, which is that being the only person who may turn that wheel is what an authority is and there is no part of it anybody should find comfortable.** Her condition is not met, her second condition stands, nobody asked her, and she did not say her theory.
- **The working consequence of the volume's sixth act of trust is delivered and it is not a scene between them.** **A man who keeps a page noticed out loud that the standing is the first thing in thirty-three weeks that has put itself in a column without anybody's permission, said the half against it, said he is not going to write the line, and the man on the step said he had had a standing for a week and did not notice it and had been proud of it, and the clerk entered the want and said it does not count for anything.** Their closest moment in the batch is a working moment in front of other people: the brace across the head of the door, the two inches and a bit she has been watching for a fortnight, and the fact that she is the person the room believes about the air and Marek Venn is the person the room no longer believes about the wall.
- **A room's rating is a word said to a page, and the word is *door*, and a man who keeps a page has asked in a room whether the word is still about the same thing now that a brace is going across the head of the door the word is about.** The objection is on the page. **It was not answered, and the word was said twice anyway and the clerk repeated it, and the count is ten including one litter.** The objection and the answer are in the same clerk's book. **And a carpenter said out loud that a person does not go out through a word, and nobody answered him, and his question is on the page.**
- **The school door at the far end of nine steps has no wedge in it and is not going to get one back.** **Five sound wedges have become two.** **The answer to a door that has to be watched is a person, the person is the woman who keeps it, she is one person, and the page where a person's hours would go is blank and is not going to be used, and nobody was sent anywhere.**
- **Talla Roke asked what a person in this building is supposed to do when a piece of beech lets go, and gave the answer: it will have to be a person who is not the man who built it, because if the only person who understands that piece of beech is the man who cut it then in ten years it is a piece of wood and a story, and a story is not a thing somebody can stand next to.** In Chapter 170 she said the thing nobody had said about this boundary's own terms: a brace has been opened, a brace has been moved, two wedges have gone out of a door, and every office that has ever written a paragraph like that works because nobody can point at the day it stopped being true. **She is not asking this boundary to be the guild and the difference is not the content, it is that this boundary can be asked in a room by a person who is standing in it.**
- **A cook said the arithmetic out loud and would not say the word.** Five people working for two days on a thing nobody asked them to be paid for in a pot means a pot at nine is going to be eight, and the only reason it is not eight is a seam that gave two jars instead of one. **She said she is not going to say a brace is being paid for in that seam, and the clerk entered the two next to each other with nothing between them and did not write the word beside either.**
- **The board is eighteen entries** — eleven nulls, one claim, one mark, one row, a plan, a condition, a store and **a brace**; **nine in the ordinary column and nine in the column with nothing over the top of it.** **The brace was entered by the man who reads the board, in the unheaded column, and the reason is that the word over that column would be *keeper* and there is no such word in this building and there is not going to be one.** The column is unheaded for the eleventh consecutive batch. **Tams Quill gave the tenth reason in Chapter 164 and it is the second of the ten that is not about him: he does not know what this building is for, and he is not going to print a blank where the answer goes, because a blank under a heading is a hole with a lid on it and a man in a bad month is going to fall into it.** **A week later he gave no eleventh reason at all and said the tenth cost him something he has not worked out, and that a man who reads numbers is not going to guess at one, and that this is the first time in eleven batches that he has had nothing and did not manufacture something. That is entered as a change of kind and not as a reason.**
- **Volume 04's question is still on the page and was not answered in this batch.** *Who owns a wall*, asked out loud in four words a fortnight ago by a man who keeps a store, and a courier said in Chapter 170 that the difference between this boundary and a guild notice is not the content but that this boundary can be asked in a room by a person who is standing in it, and that is the closest anybody has come to it and it is not an answer.

## Numbers a later batch must not re-derive

- **The week runs Monday to Sunday. 161–165 the thirty-second week, 166–170 the thirty-third.** Each chapter sits on the matching day of its week. **The corridor is shut on the first, second and fourth days and open on the third, fifth and sixth, and the seventh day is not a crossing day; the school runs on the three open days.** So in Batch 0002 the corridor is **shut in 161, 162, 164, 166, 167 and 169** and **open in 163, 165, 168 and 170**, and the **school ran in those same four, being the twenty-seventh, twenty-eighth, twenty-ninth and thirtieth mornings, all four in the room at the kitchen-line end.**
- **The school corner is open and is not used, and no chapter in this batch put the school back in it, and no school day was restored and no closure was removed.** The fire in that room has now not been lit for eleven weeks and the cook has been asked about it a seventh, an eighth and a ninth time in this batch and refused each time.
- **Wen Pask's count is 96 in Chapter 161 and 105 in Chapter 170, one a day, and all ten are on the page in the right chapter.** It is his own count, kept by a clerk, in the column with nothing over the top of it and in nothing else, it is not a register, it dates nothing, and it may not be confused, merged or remarked upon as a coincidence with the day-number register. **It is at one hundred and five, it is not going to be one hundred and six, and the clerk has said that out loud in fourteen weeks running and nobody has thanked her.** The count reached one hundred and it was announced on the Thursday before, on purpose, so that nobody would be surprised, and no mark was put beside it.
- **No day number is attached to any in-batch event and the day-number register's highest value remains the forty-sixth day.** The only date on any object is the date in the top corner of the plan. **Nothing in this batch is dated at all: not the record of the brace, not the terms, not the failure point, not the store's list.**
- **The spoken measure of elapsed weeks is a separate register**, is not re-derived, is not corrected and is not used to date anything. **From the thirtieth week onward *thirty* is the week clock itself and is not available as drift.** Counts that track the week clock are re-derivable and monotonic: **the review page at the low end has been blank for thirty-two weeks in the thirty-second week and thirty-three in the thirty-third; the plan has been transcribing the anteroom's count for the same span; the clerk has been this boundary's clerk for the same span; and the anteroom frame's packing went in on the third day of the eighteenth week and the frame is a finger and two-thirds out of true.**
- **No forward count of days or weeks on a courier.** The road is four days up the middle passage to the middle gate and forty days on from the top of it to a guild file, **the second gate's distance is stated nowhere in this batch**, and a store four days up that passage is four days up it and no other figure is attached to it. **A notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time is neither repeated nor corrected.**
- **Crew hours: seventy-one, up four and a half from sixty-six and a half, on the second day of the thirty-second week**, on a named asking in a room with the terms out loud and Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **and the three who could not be asked named with a fourth set of reasons and two of the three are not the names used in the fourth asking.** The crew have now been asked five times in thirty-three weeks and the reasons have not been the same reasons twice.
- **Boundary hours: a hundred and seventeen and a quarter, plus two hundred and twenty-one, = three hundred and thirty-eight and a quarter.** The list adds **by the day the work was done**: **four, two, three, two, three in the thirty-second week; two, three, four, two, three in the thirty-third**, summing to twenty-eight. **Running figures with the day's increment and the total are read out in six chapters — 161, 163, 165, 167, 169 and 170 — and are entered and not read out in 162, 164, 166 and 168, each with a reason in a clerk's hand, and no two of the four reasons is the same reason.** The base is the constant one hundred and seventeen and a quarter, the total is monotonic, both columns reconcile, **and the reconciliation counter is carried at fifteen weeks in the thirty-second week and sixteen in the thirty-third, and is not re-derived inside the batch.**
- **Wedges: five sound and one dead stick, and the dead stick has been missing since the twenty-sixth week.** Two in the brace, one under the ninth hearth stone's bed, one in the school corner's door, one in the basket. **The school door has none.** **Nobody touched the third wedge at the waist**, which is still up a quarter of an inch and a bit, and the terms of both the fourth and the fifth asking say nobody goes near it.
- **The pot is at nine days and it is being held up by a seam.** The seam gave two on Wednesday, one on Friday, one on Tuesday and two on Friday. **Jo Verrick says four threads and was eight in the nineteenth week and has not measured it in between, and the clerk has said in four weeks running that she is not going to be the one who makes a number for how fast that is going.** A cook said out loud that a pot at nine is going to be eight and that the only reason it is not is a seam. **Nothing in this batch fixes the pot and nobody pretends otherwise.**
- **The water at the waist has not been mentioned in this batch and no chapter says it came back or came up again.** Nobody went near the third wedge.
- **The brass survey rule has said nothing for twenty-three weeks in the thirty-second week and twenty-four in the thirty-third, on the origin at the ninth week that `outline/volume-04.md` fixes and says it fixes.** The wrapped plate on the same shelf is **thirty-two weeks in the thirty-second week and thirty-three in the thirty-third** and is the consistent register. **Any later phase that quotes Chapter 150's sixteen must say that it is quoting a closed chapter and not the register.**
- **The right hand's fine control is not recovered. The left hand did not close after the holding in the twenty-eighth week and has not closed since, and it cut a splay and a shim in this batch.** The Reader reading is not repeatable and was not used, the Chapter 99 claim's condition is unmet, the Marker is spent and its mark is still off the wall, **and no power stage beyond the Bracer advanced in this batch, no route change, no binding, no relay, no second bearing mark, no panel of any kind, and no mark cut in the stone anywhere in this building.**

## Repairs applied in a review-fix phase, after Batch 0002's own review

**A reviewer read the delivered files of Chapters 161–170 and returned ten findings. All ten are closed. The prose was repaired in place, sentence by sentence; no chapter was rewritten, no beat was moved, and nothing in `outline/volume-04.md` was moved except one figure, corrected and marked. The record of the repairs is here because the numbers in `state/batch-summary.md`, in `reviews/volume-04/batch-0002.md` and in `workspace/volume-04/batch-0003/PROMPT.md` all derive from the files, and a later phase must be able to see which of them were measured and which were believed.**

1. **The frame's arithmetic was wrong, and the error had been copied into four other files.** Chapter 168 said the frame *was a finger and three-quarters and is a finger and two-thirds* and then called that **a third of a finger back**. One and three-quarters inches is twenty-one twelfths and one and two-thirds is twenty, so the movement is **a twelfth of an inch and not a third of a finger**, and the chapter now says a twelfth of an inch in all four places it says it. **The same physical quantity was projected three ways: the shim's crushing was said to put the frame an *eighth* of an inch out of true in Chapters 164, 165 and 168, which is neither the measured movement nor anything else in the book.** All three are now **a twelfth of an inch**, which produces the better fact and not the worse one: **when the shim crushes, the head settles and the frame comes back to one and three-quarters, so the carpenter's two-year limit is a return and not a decay.** The figure was also wrong in `state/current.md`, in `state/batch-summary.md`, in `state/continuity.md`, in `reviews/volume-04/batch-0002.md` and in the Batch 0003 prompt, and all five now agree with the prose.
2. **Mero Senn's tenure was off by six weeks, and the wrong figure was in four chapters of the open volume.** He arrived on the second day of the twenty-fifth week, at Chapter 127, and Chapter 168 is the third day of the thirty-third week, so he had been in the building **eight weeks and two days** and not eleven days. The cause is identified: **Chapter 169 uses *eleven days* correctly, for a habit of his own — he has spent eleven days refusing to read his own readings — and the tenure figure was copied off the habit figure.** Chapters 166, 167 and 168 are corrected to **eight weeks, eight weeks and a day, and eight weeks and two days**, and Chapter 159 in the previous batch is corrected to **six weeks and two days** and **six weeks**. **The two *eleven days* in Chapter 169 and the one in Chapter 160 are correct and stand: they are a habit and a count of his own walls, and neither dates anything.** The same wrong figure survives in **Volume 03, Chapter 131, where it is a sixth day against a second day of the twenty-fifth week and so cannot be right; Volume 03 is closed, its prose is canon, and it has not been touched. It is logged here so that no later phase builds on it.**
3. **The wedges' week was wrong in Chapter 169 by one.** It said the two sound wedges *had come out of a school door three weeks ago*, which from a Thursday of the thirty-third week is the thirtieth. **Chapters 168 and 170 both place the removal on the Wednesday of the week before last**, which is the thirty-first, and 169 now says the same.
4. **The clerk's wedge entry in Chapter 170 stated a stock that does not fall.** It read *five sound wedges on the second day of the thirty-second week are two on the fifth day of the thirty-third*, which reads as a fall from five to two and is not what happened: **there are still five sound wedges**, two in the brace, one under the ninth hearth stone's bed, one in the school corner's door and one in the basket, and what the week spent was their freedom and not their number.
