# Batch 0005's movement, recorded at the end of Chapters 141–150

*This section is the Batch 0005 record and supersedes nothing above it; the Batch 0004 record is left standing because it is what the twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh weeks did. Volume 03 ends here.*

### Marek Venn

- **Named in ten of ten chapters, with interior life in ten of ten — and this was seven on delivery.** The batch was contracted to close third person on him throughout. **The writing session's own review measured paragraphs, openers, markup, staging and length and had not measured viewpoint presence, which is the second consecutive time that has happened, and the review in Batch 0004 added the check and this batch's session did not run it until the measurement did.** Three beats were written rather than three chapters rewritten: **in 146 he is named twice in the movement, once as a man who is not in that anteroom and is under a corridor floor at the other end of the building, and once as a man who got himself up onto a corridor floor and could not stand up in a corridor for a while; in 148 he is named in the closing image, on the anteroom step in a coat he has not taken off since Friday, with nobody sitting near him; in 149 he is named in the closing image, sitting through the whole of it and saying nothing, because on the second day of that week he said out loud in a room that he cannot go down there again.** **A viewpoint-presence check is part of the craft baseline and was run on the delivered files.**
- **Board: sixteen entries — eleven nulls, one claim, one mark, one row, a plan and a condition; nine in the ordinary column and seven in the column with nothing over the top of it.** The mark's entry has not been taken off the board, the claim's condition has not been met, the plan is not his entry, and the condition is not his entry either: the clerk entered it and it is the limit an air engineer stated.
- **Body, and this batch's cost.** The right hand has not closed since the nineteenth week. **The left hand closed this morning about a lamp — meaning it closed on Friday the fifth day of the twenty-eighth week and has not shut since — and there is a mark on the inside of his forearm from the frame, and his knee does not bend past about half, and he has not slept since Friday, and he said in a room that he cannot go down there again, that he does not know why, and that he is not going to find out, and that a man who says *I could probably do it again* in a room in a month is the man who recommended that a room be shut in the twenty-fourth week.**
- **What he said that is new and load-bearing, in order.** That a plan of rooms is a list of places and a network is several rooms each able to be emptied into the next, and that the first thing missing from one is not a design and it is a pair of hands and a crew that is not on a rota; that the network ends at a door and always will while the refusal of a row stands; that a word is not a way out and he said so by saying the word himself and the clerk repeating it and the door not opening; that **he is not the one who decides when a holding stops being safe, and he said that in a speech on Thursday and a woman turned a wheel on Tuesday and that is what it looks like when it is not a speech;** and that he is not going to be thanked, because gratitude is a way of saying *thank you for not making me be something*.
- **Immediate choice: the leaving is unchanged and unscheduled, and it was raised by somebody else for the first time in the volume and was not answered.** Dalla Sen asked him in a room, at the seventh bell of the fifth day of the twenty-ninth week, what he is going to do when the weather turns, **and he did not answer, and she did not ask him twice, and she entered it as a question and not as a finding and entered that she was not going to put a reason in the space where one would go.** That is the hand-over to Volume 04.

### Leena Orr

- **Position:** the lower level, this side of the waist, and her good arm through a doorway. **She is one of the three named in Chapter 143 as not askable, and the reason is a new one and it is not her shoulder: she is the person who is going to have to be asked, in a room, whether a person can stand at the low end of that corridor, and a woman who is going to have to answer that question is not a pair of hands in the network in the same week.** Dalla Sen put it in Renn Vale's words and said she was doing that.
- **Her beats.** In Chapter 144 she said the half of the refusal of a row that is against the people who wanted it and gave the half that is against her own position, and asked that it be entered in the book whether anybody wanted it or not: **the blank page and the refusal of the row are the same decision.** ***a list is not a location* was not used again, and that is now three batches held.**

### Iven Tallo

- **Asked for four hours' work in a room with the terms out loud and named the split himself** — two hours of his and two of Marek Venn's — and said out loud that he wanted the split in the clerk's hand because if it fell to him alone the kitchen line would carry it.
- **Struck the word *brace* out of the back of a day-board in a carpenter's own words**, because a brace is a support joined to a mark, there is no mark in it, the mark on the anteroom frame is off the wall and is not going back on, and a thing called temporary is a thing a man in a bad month is allowed to stop maintaining. **He was asked about the frame and the joint and answered about the joint, which is dressed stone on dressed stone on a stone bed and is a drain frame and not a bearing.**
- **He is not a defector, not a martyr, not a saint, not redeemed and not a signatory of anything, and nothing in this batch made him any of those four things.**

### Pell Roke

- **His work in this batch is reading numbers aloud, and it is all of his work.** He read **all sixteen numbers in the plan's first column in one breath, including the four new ones, which are the same number four times, and said nothing about any of them.** He read the second column and said sixteen conditions with no number and no day, and that the tenth is a condition that says the strip under the ninth hearth stone is still holding. He read the third column and said fifteen lines filled and one empty and that he is not going to say which, because the man who keeps it has said in a room that he is not going to say. **And he read the fourth column and said there was nothing in it.**
- **He was named as one of the three who could not be asked, with a new reason: he is fourteen, and the reason is not his age, and the reason is that a count taken by the man who reads numbers is a count nobody can argue with, and this boundary has spent four weeks being frightened of exactly that.**
- **He did not go down the steps, into the corridor, or over the waist, in any chapter he appears in, and nobody asked him to.** His sister was in the building for the whole batch and did not go up to him, **he is in two chapters of it and she is in neither of those two, and no chapter in this batch has the two of them in the same room**, and nobody in the building made anything of it.

### Tams Quill

- **The right hand is still open, flat, and still not a working hand, and nobody let it be.** He never took a bar, a chisel, a lever or a packing, and he did not go near the waist's third wedge, which the terms of the asking forbade.
- **The crew's column moved by four hours on a named asking**, from fifty-nine and a half to sixty-three and a half, **and he gave the eighth reason for refusing to head the column with nothing over the top of it, and it is the worst of the eight, and it is not about a word: a heading is a place to keep the person who works under it.** Eleven of the fifteen entries on that board are nulls, which are readings that found nothing, and under a heading they become eleven findings, **and a finding is a thing a person is responsible for, so the day this column has a heading on it is the day somebody in this building can be called in front of a clerk and asked what they found and what they did not find and why they did not write it down.** He also said that a man who has eight reasons and gives the seventh is not being careful, he is being lazy, and that the day it costs somebody is the day a heading is a thing you can be judged by.
- **He was named as one of the three who could not be asked, with a new reason: he is the person who reads the board, and the board is where a thing that has been done gets entered, and if he also walks the network then the same man is the hands, the witness and the record, and there is nobody left who can stand in a room and say that the record is not the man.**
- **He entered the sixteenth entry on the board and said the reason why a condition goes in the unheaded column, which is that a condition with a heading over it is a condition somebody can be held to, and this one has a person who can stop it, and those are the same shape and the same danger, and the difference between them is a piece of chalk.** He named no day and gave no reason for not naming one, and refused to give a ninth reason, and said the base under both columns was not going to be re-derived in the last week of anything.
- **The board is walked in four chapters of this batch — 141, 143, 147 and 150 — and is not walked in the other six, and a reason is entered in a clerk's hand in each of the six.** In 148, which is one of the six, he gave the best of them himself: a woman from another office has been in the anteroom for four hours and has not asked for the document once, and if he had walked the board in front of her she would have had it, and he is not going to be the man who puts a thing in a stranger's hands that she has not asked for.

### Nera Oduya

- **Position:** the valve, the second step, the anteroom table, the air gate, the school corner's mouth. **She came down as far as the second step twice and did not come further, and she struck two rooms out of two documents in nine seconds and gave no reason on either occasion and was not asked on either occasion.**
- **Authority: technical authority over airflow, air testing, and safe operation of the air gate, unchanged, independent, never folded into a resident's consent.** She has now refused to certify the stair's air for twenty-nine weeks and has **opened the school corner's mouth as a vent for two hours without certifying it**, and said out loud in a room that nobody is to write down after this that the mouth is fine.
- **The third of Volume 03's five acts of trust is spent, and it is the one Batch 0003 set up and Batch 0004 deliberately held.** **She stops checking his arithmetic out loud, a clerk notices out loud in a room with a stranger in it, and she gives an answer about the work and not about him:** on the third day of the twenty-fourth week his figure was the only figure in that room with nothing to agree with, and there are two handholds on that page now, one a man's and one a room's, **and a schoolteacher's hand in a column cannot be adjusted by anybody who finds it inconvenient, so if she made him say how he knows in front of a room that has a room in it she would be telling the room that the man is the thing that can be doubted and the room is not.** Nobody thanked her. Renn Vale had something in her mouth and did not say it, and the clerk entered that and entered that she did not know why. **It is not a recognition scene and there is no scene between them in this batch.**
- **In the climax she moves people, she holds the air, and she invokes her own authority over the air gate, which she has never done in this book, and it is a professional act and not a favour to him.** She said out loud, before anybody could say it after her, that she was not doing it for a man, **and that the reason she did not consult anybody is that the authority is hers and the minute was hers, and if she had asked, a room would have told her about a man in a channel and she would have had to weigh a man against a floor, and she is not going to do that in a room with eleven people in it.**
- **She stopped a holding whose limit had not been met, and she said the two halves in that order**, and the second half is that a person in a channel cannot be reached and cannot be told anything and cannot be known to be in one, and a holding whose only condition is on the other side of the floor from the man is not a holding.
- **Her theory was not said.** She said in Chapter 150 that she has half of the volume's question, that half of what she knows is about a room and what was asked is about a road, and that her condition is not met, and that anybody who thinks a good month is going to meet it should look at what this boundary did in a bad one. **Nobody asked her.**
- **She is wrong in public once, in Chapter 148**, when she says she would like a row on that page for her four pages and then declines to ask for it. **She is not leaving in this volume, no chapter stages her going, and the question of her going is not raised.**
- **Relationship:** no intimacy, no recognition scene, no acceleration, and no scene whose only content is the two of them. **Their closest moment in this batch is a working moment in front of a stranger in which she is right about a page and he has to take it, and their second is a professional act she performs in front of eleven people for a floor and not for him, and he is under a channel at the time and cannot hear any of it.**

### The Hearthhold boundary maintainers

- **Renn Vale:** keeper of the shore, the road and the lead terms. **She found a hole in her own condition — a room used three days in seven has its condition checked three mornings in seven — and said so before anybody found it, and answered it with four sentences a week in an empty room and said out loud that it is stupid and cheap and the only version that does not put a day of that school on a ledger.** She **wrote a change to a corridor she keeps, in her own hand, with a condition and no number and no day on it, on a day the arrangement shuts it, and said the reason for the yes in the same breath as the yes**; the clerk put it against the original and compared the two. She wrote four conditions for four rooms in four hands and **put the word *waits* into her own** for the fifth person at a waist. **She refused a correction to a title in a field book and entered the refusal, and said the third and best thing is available and she is not going to ask for it, because a woman who has spent four weeks being a handle does not get to choose the shape of the handle.** She **said her own name out loud in a room as the person who may stop the network, and it went in a clerk's book in a coat and not on the page, and she said a person named in a room is not a post.** And **she said the volume's last argument about a man who holds things, against her own practice: a word is not a way out, a person is, she has been signing a rule that says a person does not count for twenty-nine weeks, and she is not taking the word out of a room's terms because nine people in this building have been told that saying it made them safe.**
- **Dalla Sen:** **noticed out loud that the air engineer had stopped making a man say how he knows, said she was noticing it, and refused to say the words because a stranger was in the room**; entered that the title stays wrong as a decision; entered that nobody sent him as two entries and not as one, **and then entered that the difference between the two halves of that entry was the smallest thing in her book and that she was entering it as a difference and would not be asked whether it was a large one**; entered a man's hours in the boundary's column and gave the reason out loud; entered that a page is still blank and that the two facts sit next to each other on purpose with nothing between them; **entered the sixteenth thing on the board herself**; entered the Compact clauses answered, refused and agreed; wrote *a week is not a month* twice so that the second one is the one a person reads; **asked a man in a room what he is going to do when the weather turns, and entered that he did not answer and that she did not ask him twice**; and kept writing a dead man's count every day and said out loud in four weeks running that she is going to keep writing it, and that a woman from another office read it and did not say a kind thing about it, and that she was glad.
- **Jo Verrick:** went down onto the flags at the frame with a lamp in her hand and two women either side of her, and **a man got himself up out of the channel and two people took his weight and did not carry him.** She is the woman whose lamp test is a standing term and who says the strip is holding and that a fortnight of a hole not getting worse is not a repair.
- **Mikka Hale:** **wrote the same number four times and not four numbers, for the fifth time, and said out loud that she has not counted anybody five times and that saying it a fifth time is a way of not saying it.** She said the fire in the corner of that room has not been lit for nine weeks and asked to be asked about it a fifth time and refused a fifth time. **She said that a network with four numbers in it is a queue with a signpost on it**, and that a page saying ten is a building saying *up to here* and a page saying a number is a building saying *this many*, and that she would rather be argued with than held to. **And she said the thing about the dead man's share of the pot: she has been putting it back into the pot since the fourth day of the twenty-fifth week and did it on purpose and told nobody, and that is the reason the pot is at ten and not at eleven.** The pot is at ten days and has not gone up since the fifth day of the nineteenth week.
- **Ilsa Norr (nine children and herself):** **agreed to say a sentence to an empty room four mornings a week and put the cost of it in the book in her own words, as a preference and not as a noble position.** She said the network is four rooms and a child on a step. She **said she is not going to be the person who asks for a man to be put in a channel, because she closed a room with eleven people in it on the advice of a competent man and the room forgave nobody and blamed nobody and it cost a girl of nine her foot.** She told the sixth-bell read that the last one out of her room was a woman of sixty-eight and not one of the nine, and that the room was empty when that woman said it was. She told a surface federation that she has a count, that she is not going to say what it was, and **that the shape of it is the whole of her trade: a count of that kind is only true of a moment, and the moment is the only thing about a room that is worth a number.** She wrote a third column and said it was still hers and that the condition above her had got harder since she wrote it and that she was glad of it.
- **Bel Ordry:** thirty-five, keeper of the boundary's public maintenance plan, the sixth signatory of the charter. **He turned his own sentence of the twenty-sixth week the other way round and said so, and entered that he noticed he was saying it the other way round.** He refused a number on the common landing so that the stair would not get one by being put in a box. He asked the physician a question nobody had asked him. He asked for a correction to a title and was refused one. **He answered three clauses of a regime out loud, refused the fourth, and said the sixth is correct and that it is the reason he has been right about one thing in twenty-nine weeks.** He still says a plan in a coat is not a system and that he is the only person who has to say it. His half hinge is his own and is in a bag. **He has still not raised his leaving and nobody has asked.**
- **The woman from the wash rooms:** **not named, not asked, not rostered, not sent for.** A room was struck out of a clerk's list of rooms in nine seconds in Chapter 142 and a room was struck out of a printed schedule in nine seconds in Chapter 149, **and no reason was given on either occasion and she was not asked on either occasion and the space where a reason would go is empty on both.** The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, nobody was sent, and the page is still blank at the end of the volume.
- **Wen Pask: age twenty-two. Paid, kept, eighty-five days and eighty-five nights at the end of Volume 03, and dead.** His count is at eighty-five and is not going to be eighty-six and the clerk has said so out loud in a room in four weeks running. **He is not a martyr, not a lesson and not an argument in this batch. His bundle is in an anteroom and cannot leave this building because this boundary will not fill in two lines on somebody else's form, and that is a fact and not a speech about him, and nobody in the batch used him as an argument.**
- **Mero Senn: age forty-five.** Asked five times in three weeks whether a plan with a number in it is acceptable and gave the same answer five times, **and was then asked a different question — is there a version of this where nobody is in that channel — and said no, and said he was not going to make the search sound like a principle.** He refused to let a thing that went well be read as a good thing, on the day it went well. **He put his name against a refusal in a clerk's book, which is the first thing he has put anywhere in twenty-nine weeks**, and said that is not the physician's modesty, and gave the reason: a cut in a floor made with stone and no bar, a sill packed in stone in clay that is the only thing holding that floor up, clay that shrinks as it dries, a strip of crate board and two flags, **and that arguable is worth more than safe in a building like this and he is not going to be the man who says it is worth more than safe anywhere else.** He fixes nothing, softens nobody, is not a saint and is not a rebuke, and he was wrong in public in Batch 0004 and is not consoled.
- **Orla Kern: age nine.** The fourth of Ilsa Norr's nine. **In the room on all four school mornings of this batch and sitting down, on the anteroom step during the movement with a strip of crate board round her foot, and named once in the volume's last chapter.** Her bone is where a physician put it, it has moved, and a physician has refused in writing to certify the room she is taught in.
- **Talla Roke: age twenty-two.** **In the building for the whole batch, on her own terms, with Bevin Tace, Osha Kell and Merrit Amm, and not a rescue.** She brought the market day and the fact that a man from this Hearthhold was turned back at a gate because he would not give a name, **and the cook said out loud that the bundle has been in the anteroom since the fourth day of the twenty-fifth week.** She set the test — ordinary residents, no order, nobody at the front — **and it passed, and thirty-one people went up a market road and her three and she were four people out of thirty-five.** She said nobody is being sent and that she is not sending anybody and that her three are not being sent. She said her mark on a paper means the road is not a guild's, **and that a woman at a counter took a form off a board because a mark cannot be entered in a register, and that the office conceded nothing in a word, and that the sheet will be back in a month by a clerk who does not know about Tuesday, and that she is telling them so that nobody in this building writes it down as a victory.** She asked the volume's question out loud twice, in Chapter 140 and again in Chapter 150 in the shape the withdrawal created, and it was not answered either time. **She did not go up to her brother. He is named in two chapters of this batch and she is in neither of them, and no chapter in this batch puts the two of them in the same room.**
- **Hollis Ashe: forty-one, sixteen years, Stonelight Compact route inspection.** Her four pages were read out, decided upon, and **used**: the boundary made its own page public by reading it out in a room with her in it, under her own first and third clauses, and said out loud that it was doing that on purpose. She said on the fourth day of the twenty-eighth week that she has been trying to write a page that could be shown for four weeks and could not, and that a woman on a landing wrote the reason she could not, and that she is going to put it in her own book in the woman's words and is not going to use her name. **In Chapter 149 she said out loud, against her own office, that the instrument which made this boundary arguable is hers and that she knew the price of it when she wrote it, and that she is still glad she wrote it, and that she would rather be used than hidden and would rather be used by a boundary that has decided the price itself.** Not an antagonist, not defeated, not consoled.
- **Pettin Rahl: fifty-two, twenty-six years, Stonelight Compact, continuity.** Came up the passage with six pages he did not write and said so before he sat down, and read the fifth clause out loud: a room whose condition is not being checked may be entered, and the person who keeps it cannot refuse, and their refusal is not a ground. **He is right, at length, in a room where nobody argued with him: a number in a column that nobody has counted is a number that has to be believed, and his belief in this boundary is worth nothing, because a competent and tired man in a cell on a Tuesday will look at the first column and see a building with a number in it.** He read the count out of the clerk's book and did not say a kind thing about it. He said a regime is not a threat and that a regime is a schedule and that a thing which is scheduled is not a thing that is refused. **Not a villain, not defeated, not consoled.**
- **A Quiet Hands cell:** at least two and probably three. **Unchanged and uncaught.** Nothing in this batch recruited anybody, nothing turned their reason into a riddle or a voice, and their argument was not restated. **The One-Seat protocol and Cassian Rook remain the destination and Volume 03 does not name the One-Seat.**

### The stair, the plans, the plate, and the evidence

The stair is **restricted, corded, and in service on its near side only**, with two timber shores on the common landing, the newer one packed and **not wedged**, and a lip that is still **not measured by the people who own it**. **The common landing carries no number in the plan's first column, on Bel Ordry's stated reason, and the stair is not in the charter, the plan or the second sheet.** The four treads behind the rail are dry, and nobody has been on them and nobody will be. The eighth term is not touched, the ninth line is *none*, the ninth room has no row on the plan and is not in the charter and is not on the second sheet, **and no mark has been cut in its stone or in any other stone in this building.** The far wall of the throat is eleven feet down and has still never been seen. **The board on surfaces now holds sixteen entries, of which eleven are nulls, one is a claim whose condition has not been met, one is a mark, one is a row on a page, one is a plan, and one is a condition.**

**The plan on butcher's paper is one document in four parts in a coat, it does not leave the building, and it has sixteen rows.** The first column is a permission and has never held a count of anybody; the second column has no number and no day on any of the sixteen; the third column has **fifteen lines filled and one empty that the man who keeps it has said in a room he is not going to name**; the fourth column is empty and unheaded with its reason in two hands and a modal struck out of one of them. **Four of the sixteen rows are the network, and the first column took the same number four times and not four numbers.** The tenth row carries a proposal in his hand, an objection written above it in hers, her countersignature under it, a correction under both, **and a second condition written in the keeper's own hand in the twenty-eighth week: the same sentence is to be said out loud in a room with the room empty, four mornings a week.** **And the page was read out loud in a room to a person from another office, with no copy given, and a person who may stop it was named in that room and not on the page.**

**The plan on a dowel is a nine-row maintenance schedule in a locked school store and did not leave the store and was not unrolled in this batch.** **The resemblance between the dowel, the plan, the bench line, the mouth, the four treads, the air engineer's theory and the plate is a set of separate facts and nobody joined them in a room in this batch, and this batch's biggest temptation was the blank page and the refused row, and the chapter left it alone and then said out loud, in a clerk's own hand, that the difference between the two halves of her own restraint was the smallest thing in her book.**

**The wrapped empty-seat plate** lies in a knotted bundle of work cloth on the shelf above the anteroom bench, unexplained, unidentified, unused, unclaimed, and **unopened**. **The brass survey rule** is in the pocket of the coat on the anteroom's hook, **has said nothing for longer than sixteen weeks**, was not put on a table in this batch, and nobody looked at it.

## Relationship and power guardrails, end of Volume 03

- No harem structure and no instant romance. Nera remains an independent air engineer and a civic adult. **No intimacy, no recognition scene, and no acceleration between Marek Venn and Nera Oduya in this batch, and no scene between them alone.** **All five of Volume 03's acts of trust are now spent and recorded.** **The batch's is the third: she stops checking his arithmetic out loud, somebody notices, and she gives an answer about the work and not about him.**
- **The power stage did not advance and no panel of any kind appears in this batch.** No bearing mark, no route change as a stage, no binding, no relay, no brace, and no repeatable reading. **The right hand's fine control is not recovered, the left hand did not close after the holding, the brass rule is silent, the Reader claim's condition is still unmet, and no mark was cut in the stone anywhere in this building.**
- The five Room Checks and the declared-occupancy discipline remain the growth framework. **The anteroom's rating is unchanged for the ninth volume running, and the fifth of its five terms has been broken since the middle of the twenty-sixth week, and the room was worked over its number for two hours on two mornings of this batch, and a clerk entered it every time, and its second way out is a word that a man said in it in Chapter 147 and that opened nothing.**
- The working practice — the person who will keep a room writes the change to it — **produced four room-keepers writing four conditions for four rooms; a corridor's terms written by the woman who keeps it; a limit stated by the only person who may stop it; a schoolteacher's third column; a cook's four numbers; a courier's rule in a clerk's book in her own words; a woman with a rule striking a room out of a document in nine seconds; a physician's name against a refusal in a clerk's book; and a man entered in advance as not a post, in a clerk's book, twice.** **And it produced the volume's sharpest limit: a person who may stop the network is named in a room and not on a page, and a document with no name on it cannot tell a stranger who to write to, and the boundary has decided that it would rather be used than hidden.**
- **The crew end Volume 03 as five people who are not a debt, who are not on the rota, whose column is sixty-three and a half and moved by four on a named asking in a room with the terms out loud and the three who could not be asked named with the reason for each before the asking, a boundary with a charter whose hole is one institution deeper and is now being used against the boundary, a plan in a coat with sixteen rows and no name on it that has been read aloud to a stranger and is public, a packed sill and a propped hearth stone and a girl of nine on a step, a grate off a channel and a page that is still blank, a dead man of twenty-two whose count is at eighty-five and is not going to stop, a bundle that cannot leave the building, a cell that is not caught, six pages of a regime going up a passage, a form off a board at a counter, and a person under a lip.**

# Batch 0001's movement — Volume 04, Chapters 151–160

*This section is the Volume 04 Batch 0001 record and supersedes nothing above it; the Batch 0005 record is left standing because it is what closed Volume 03. Volume 04 is open and this is its first batch.*

## Marek Venn

- **Named in ten of ten chapters, with interior life in ten of ten — and this was nine on first measure.** The viewpoint-presence check that Volume 03's fourth batch added to the craft baseline was run on the delivered files rather than asserted, **and it found him absent from Chapter 155**, and a beat was written into that chapter and two more into 154 and 159, the latter two for Renn Vale, who was also absent from them. **This is the third consecutive batch in which a state-file assertion of viewpoint presence would have been false and the measurement caught it, and the check is now in the habit rather than in the prompt.**
- **Body, and this batch's cost.** The right hand has not closed since the nineteenth week. **The left hand has not closed since he held a channel in the twenty-eighth week, and a carpenter cut eleven pieces of beech with it on the third day of the thirty-first week.** The mark on the inside of his forearm stands, the knee does not bend past about half, and he has said in a room that he cannot go down there again, that he does not know why, and that he is not going to find out. **The load echo in the body is unaddressed in this batch and he did not use it and it is not on the board.**
- **Board: seventeen entries — eleven nulls, one claim, one mark, one row, a plan, a condition and a store; nine in the ordinary column and eight in the column with nothing over the top of it.** The mark's entry has not been taken off the board, the claim's condition is unmet, and **the plan, the condition and the store are none of them his entry.**
- **What he said that is new and load-bearing, in order.** That the answer to a clerk's question about the weather turning is a piece of paper on a cart and that he does not like it; **that the price of a refusal is a sill and a wall in lime that is not being built, and that a refusal he has not cost anything yet is a preference, and that Dalla Sen entered that as the first time anybody in this building has written down the price of a refusal before paying it**; that a plan of rooms is a store, and that the whole of a store's worth of beech and a four days' passage and two men refusing to carry a name is not a design; **that the limit on a brace will not be a figure of his in a room, because the mark is damaged and he cannot read it, and that the limit will be a condition written by the person the brace can hurt**; that the third asking's terms are the practice and that the only new one is that nobody's name goes into the store's book; **that he is not the man who decides this, and that the two available actions are filling in two lines and not doing so, and that both of them cost a schoolroom**; and **that he knows the answer to who owns a wall for two of the four walls in this building and refused twice to say it out loud, because saying it in a room is making a claim, and he is not going to be the first man in this building to find a loophole in a thing thirty people agreed to.**
- **The private book.** It is on the page once and is referred to twice: he wrote a figure to a millimetre in the twenty-seventh week and gave it to a woman and not to a room, and **in this batch he says that the book has two walls in it, that they are two walls he has been inside in the last eleven days, and that that is the whole of his qualification and he is not saying it in a room where a man he has met twice is writing it in a book.** The clerk entered that in his own words and all of it, including the two refusals and the fact that the second no was faster than the first.
- **Immediate choice: the leaving is unchanged and unscheduled, and it was raised by somebody else for the first time in this volume and is still not answered.** Dalla Sen asked him in a room at the seventh bell of the fifth day of the twenty-ninth week what he was going to do when the weather turns, and he did not answer, and she did not ask him twice, and she entered it as a question and not as a finding. **In Chapter 156 he answered the first half of it in his own mouth — he is going to go and look at the air at the low end of the corridor on Wednesday with a lamp in his left hand — and did not answer the second half, and the clerk entered the first half and not the second, and entered that she had had a fortnight of wanting to enter the second.** **He is not a post and no page is going to get his name on it, and this batch did not move that and did not soften it.**

## Leena Orr

- **Position:** the lower level, this side of the waist, and her good arm through a doorway. **She is one of the three named in Chapter 153 as not askable, and the reason is a third one and it is not her shoulder: she is the person who is going to have to be asked, in a room, whether the schoolroom's wall can take a push, and a woman who is going to have to answer that question is not a pair of hands in the same room on the same morning.**
- **Not present in the room in any chapter of this batch and not used.** ***a list is not a location* was not used again, and that is now four batches held.**

## Iven Tallo

- **Asked for two hours of a piece of work in a room with the terms out loud, named the split himself before he was asked, and gave the reason for going first: a carpenter looking at a pile of beech is a different thing from an engineer looking at a pile of beech, and a carpenter's opinion in a room where the engineer is standing is the one a room weighs.** Dalla Sen entered the distinction because it is real and not because it was kind. **His two hours and one of Marek Venn's moved the crew's column from sixty-three and a half to sixty-six and a half.**
- **He gave back half of a sentence he wrote himself in the twenty-eighth week and said he had been right about the word and wrong about one of the reasons.** The word was *brace* and the reason was that a brace is a support joined to a mark, and there is not one mark in this building that is not off a wall. **The half he took back is that there is a mark — four marks and a groove in the lintel over the school corner's mouth — and nobody has got it.** He said a carpenter's mark is offered for a plan and is refused, and that a wooden pin in green beech will split in a year and he would not put one in that he would have to argue about in a year.
- **A route-holder's post is in a carrier's hand with his name in the second line, in a stiff cover with a proper seal and no date, in coin, with a boy back on the roll, at a camp four and a half days up a road that took the halfpenny sheet. He neither refused it nor accepted it and gave the reason: a refusal given before a thing has been understood is a thing a man says to look clean, and it was him, in the twenty-second week, about the sill.** He asked for the entry to say the date he refuses is not today, and said nine words about a girl of nine when the reason for the offer was laid out in a room.
- **He cut eleven pieces of a school's own beech on a trestle with a hand that has not closed since the twenty-second week, and put the offcuts in a heap instead of a basket, and the clerk entered that a basket is a thing a person is asked to keep and that she was not going to put that beside anything.**
- **He is not a defector, not a martyr, not a saint, not redeemed and not a signatory of anything, and nothing in this batch made him any of those four things.**

## Pell Roke

- **His work in this batch is reading numbers aloud, and it is all of his work. He read the fourteen lines of a store's inventory in an anteroom, and the numbers in it are not counts of anything, and the ninth line is a dash, and he said the dash is a thing a man does not promise and he was not going to argue with the man about it because he reads numbers and that is the end of what he does.** Nothing in the room filled in after it.
- **Named as one of the three who could not be asked, with a new reason: a measurement a person reads aloud and nobody has written down is a figure in the column with nothing over the top of it, and this boundary has spent a month being frightened of exactly that.** A clerk said the age is the reason everybody expects and it is not the age.
- **He did not go down the steps, into the corridor, or over the waist, in any chapter he appears in, and nobody asked him to.** **No chapter in this batch puts him in the same room as Talla Roke, and the batch card that placed them together was corrected to the delivery.**

## Tams Quill

- **The right hand is still open, flat, and still not a working hand, and nobody let it be.** He never took a bar, a chisel, a lever or a packing, and he did not go near the waist's third wedge.
- **The crew's column moved by three hours on a named asking**, and he gave no reason for it because a clerk gave it better in a room and said so.
- **He gave the ninth reason for refusing to head the column with nothing over the top of it, and it is the first of the nine that is not about him: a heading is how a room finds out what the person in it is for, and there are rooms in this building that have never been asked what the person in them is for — the anteroom, the landing, the corridor, a store four days up a road, and this one.** He also said that a heading is a reason somebody could send for, and the clerk entered that she was not going to let three of his reasons accumulate into a policy without somebody saying so in a room, and that he is not giving a tenth and would say the week got away from me.
- **He entered the seventeenth entry on the board himself — a store — in the column with nothing over the top of it**, and the reason is a courier's rule that was written about a road and turned out to be true about a board: **a board that only holds things in one building cannot be read by a person in another one.** He said it is the first thing on that board that is not in this Hearthhold.
- **The board is walked in four chapters of this batch — 151, 154, 158 and 160 — and not in the other six**, and in no chapter is it walked by the clerk and the count on the same day for the same reason. **He is in the batch's closing image as the only person in this building whom the clerk has never once asked, and the clerk entered that she had not known that was true and was not going to start now.**

## Nera Oduya

- **Position:** the valve, the second step, the anteroom table, the school's edge. **She came to the second step in two chapters and did not come further, and she struck a column and three rooms out of a printed schedule in nine seconds without coming down, and gave no reason, and was not asked, and it was the eighth time.**
- **Authority: technical authority over airflow, air testing and safe operation of the air gate, unchanged, independent, never folded into a resident's consent.** She has refused to certify the stair's air for thirty-one weeks and has still published no rate.
- **The sixth of Volume 04's acts of trust, and it is the inverse of the third: she asks him for a work.** In a room, with the terms out loud, in the crew's own practice, with Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, and with the three she is not going to ask named with the reason for each before she asks him anything. **The work is to go and look at the air at the low end of the corridor, from above, not from inside it, and to come back and say in a room what it is and not to tell her first.** **She said the cost out loud before anybody could say it after her: the asking puts a standing on him, and a standing is the first half of a post, and she asked for the word *standing* in the clerk's book and not the word *help*, because it is not help and she has heard it called help twice this month by people who meant something else.**
- **She is wrong in public once in this batch and is not consoled:** she is the one who says the air at that end is not being pushed by water any more, and a room finds out the arithmetic of that and the nine children, and she refuses to be the somebody who says it.
- **Her condition is not met and she says so in a room.** Keeping itself and being asked to open a road while something is going wrong four days up a passage are not the same sentence, and the one where the second half happens is the one that kills somebody. **She has set a second condition — that she will not take it back while it is being watched — and said it out loud twice, and the reason for saying it twice is the boundary's own: the first is a sentence and the second is a fact. She told a room not to ask her what it is about and nobody asked.** The theory was not said. The name from the twelfth week is still not asked.
- **In Chapter 160 she is the only person in the book who does not have half of the volume's question and she says so, and says she would give it if she had, and asks for that to be entered so that a person in a year does not think there was a woman in that room who knew and would not say.** **This varies the pattern of Volume 03, where she had half of it and did not give it, and it is the reason the question is not answered by her in this batch.**
- **She is not leaving in this volume, no chapter stages her going, and the question of her going is not raised.** **Relationship: no intimacy, no recognition scene, no acceleration, and no scene whose only content is the two of them.** Their closest moment in this batch is a professional act in a room — she asks, he says yes, a clerk says which column it goes in and why.

## The Hearthhold boundary maintainers

- **Renn Vale:** keeper of the shore, the road and the lead terms. **She gave the joinwood — two wedges at the school-door head and two beech lengths out of the school store — and said the half against it in the same breath, and the half against it is the volume's argument in one sentence: a door with no wedge is a door that has to be watched, the answer is a person, there is not a person available, and the page where a person would go is blank with three conditions on it.** She said she has better answers and has looked and has not found one. **She said the sentence that makes the guild's post into what it is: a hand out of a gap in a clause wearing a bond and a wage, and a person in a bad month is going to hold the wage and not look at the hand, and the person it will find is a boy on a bench, and a boy's roll number is a route.** **She said in Chapter 154 that she is going to have to decide something about a wall in this building and has not practised it.** She is the person who shuts the waist, opens it four at a time in the pump's window, and named the space a child on a step; she is the person who can be told no.
- **Dalla Sen:** repair ledger, route record, work-bell relay, cost witness. **She named the three who could not be asked before she asked anybody and said the reasons were a third set; argued five of seven lines out loud before a mark was made; read a document against itself and found that the hole in the guild's offer was not the guild's; decided which column a man's hours go in, in a room, and gave the reason out loud twice; entered that she had been putting other things in that column for a month without knowing what it was; entered the pot going to nine days and the seam going quiet and that she is not going to be the one who makes a number for it; entered the first figure taken at the waist on purpose in thirty-one weeks, and the three old reasons for never taking one, and that the plan has no row for that wall; asked for a physician's mark to be read by her and not by the physician; said the sixth-bell read is a working practice and not a funeral; said she was glad that a man with a tally and a man with a slate had not said a kind thing about it; refused for the third time in a month to put two questions next to each other and entered the three refusals in one sentence with both questions; and said she had had a fortnight of wanting to enter the second half of an entry and had not.** She did not walk the board in six chapters of this batch and gave a reason in her own hand in each.
- **Jo Verrick:** trial pump maintainer, five paid cleanings and an estimate of ONE, still refusing to write zero. **She found the water off the fill and refused to guess at it, and said the air is not being pushed and therefore the nine are, and would not be the somebody who says it.** She is the woman who said both halves of a surveyor's finding in one breath and that they are the same sentence. **She gave a figure nobody asked her for — two inches and a bit in an hour — and said what it means and what it does not mean, and the chalk line and the string on that wall are hers to read every morning.** She says the seam is at four threads and was eight in the nineteenth week and has not been measured in between.
- **Mikka Hale:** kitchen, clinic return watch, pump frame, meals, the water, the second hand of the plan, the author of the charter. **The fire in the corner of the schoolroom has not been lit for ten weeks and she asked to be asked a sixth time and refused a sixth time in one sentence, and asked for the children to be cold in the record in the same place as the refusal.** **She said the pot out loud: it is nine days, the seam is going quiet, and a dead man's share has been going back into that pot since the fourth day of the twenty-fifth week on purpose and is not going to be done for a brace, and the half against that is that she does not know whether a dead man's ration is a thing a house can afford or a thing a house has to pretend it can afford.** **And she gave the reason a store's list has no date on it, in her own mouth, and did not know she was giving it, and the clerk entered it in her words: a count of that kind is only true of a moment, and a list with a date on it is a moment pretending to be a day.**
- **Ilsa Norr (nine children and herself):** **the person who keeps the room and the person who keeps the wall the brace pushes on.** She asked for the number a brace will push with before she wrote her condition, and said she would rather be argued with than talked out of it by a small number. **She wrote a condition with no number and no day on it that is about the brace and not about her room: it stands while she and a physician still agree that the wall can take it, the first to stop agreeing takes it out, neither gives a reason to the other first, and the second to find out is the one who acts.** She put the cost of it in the book as a preference and not as a noble position: it is nearly free, and a condition that costs nothing is a condition a person in a bad month will decide is not worth saying, and if she is the one who takes the brace out then nine children are going to think the woman who keeps their room is frightened, and they will be right and she will be wrong.
- **Bel Ordry:** thirty-five, keeper of the boundary's public maintenance plan, the sixth signatory of the charter. **He said the two available actions out loud in a room and said the half against each, and refused to name a guild's fourth paragraph on a Friday morning to persuade a man with eleven years of beech to part with it, and set a price and a day and said he would not haggle on the parchment.** He said a page in a coat is not a system and that he is the only person who has to say it, for the thirty-first week running. **In Chapter 160 he answered who owns a wall by saying he owns nothing and the page owns nothing, and then said the half against his own answer.** His half hinge is his own and is in a bag. He has still not raised his leaving and nobody has asked.
- **The woman from the wash rooms:** **not named, not asked, not rostered, not sent for.** A printed Compact schedule with a column headed for the person who will be present and three rooms under it was struck through in nine seconds from three steps up, before anybody had asked, and the reason was not given, and nobody asked, and the space where a reason would go is empty. **That is the eighth striking-out in this book and the sixth with no reason at all.** The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, nobody was sent, and the page at the low end is blank.
- **Wen Pask: age twenty-two. Paid, kept, ninety-five days and ninety-five nights at the end of Volume 04 Batch 0001, and dead.** His count is at ninety-five, is not going to be ninety-six, and the clerk has said so out loud in a room in six weeks running and nobody has thanked her in six weeks running. **He is not a martyr, not a lesson and not an argument in this batch. His count was read at a sixth bell in all ten chapters and was not made into a scene about grief, because the reading is a working practice and not a funeral.** **His bundle is in the anteroom and a courier named it out loud in a room for the first time in the book, and said it is not hers to make into a speech.** The half hinge is Bel Ordry's and is not his.
- **Mero Senn: age forty-five.** Rescue physician and trauma surgeon, twenty-two years. **Asked for a mark on a wall and asked for the clerk to read it and not himself, and said the reason: a physician who takes her own readings is a physician who decides when she stopped believing them.** He named the person in the brace and refused to name a child, because a child would be the easy way to stop the work and would be a lie with a name in it; **the person he named is the woman who keeps that room, given as a description and not a name, on the ground that a description in a clerk's book is not a handle and he has read four documents this month that think otherwise.** Asked for the number he gave four tons, or thereabouts, and made the clerk write the words *or thereabouts* next to the four tons, and said the number is not an argument. He does not fix anything, softens nobody, is not a saint and is not a rebuke, and he is right.
- **Orla Kern: age nine.** The fourth of Ilsa Norr's nine. **In the room on all four school mornings of this batch and sitting down.** Her bone is where a physician put it, it has moved, and a physician has refused in writing to certify the room she is taught in.
- **Talla Roke: age twenty-two.** **In the building in five chapters of this batch — 151, 152, 155, 156, 157, 160 — on her own terms, and not a rescue.** **She named the bundle out loud in a room and said it is not hers to make into a speech; she said a form and a load are the same instrument; she asked what an unstruck room on a schedule says and a carrier answered her in a room; she said the half against giving a thing a person and not a carrier — a favour with a keeper, and a keeper who is owed a favour has less room to say no the second time — and then the half against her own half; and she said the only person in the building who knows who owns a wall is a man who has never been the keeper of one.** Her rule is in a clerk's book in her own words and **it arrived in this batch in a place it was not built for, as the reason a store goes in the column with nothing over the top of a board.** **No chapter in this batch puts her brother in the same room as her.**
- **Ormer Hatch: age forty-nine. New in this batch.** Survey camp, thirty-one years, keeper of a store of eleven years. **He said no to the timber and said *bring your keeper*. He came four days down the middle passage with nothing in his hands in order to be asked, and said he had not been asked in eleven years and did not know until a carpenter asked him the wrong question that he still wanted to be.** He named a guild's fourth paragraph as the thing it is. He asked who owns a wall out loud in a room and was not answered and said that was all right, and gave his answer to how a thing gets looked after, and asked for it read back to him. **He is not an antagonist, not a saint, not a teacher and not a lesson, and he is a person with a store that is going to be emptied of its fir on the Monday of Batch 0002's second week.**
- **A carrier:** a second one this batch, unnamed, who came up on foot because the cart is not coming, read the outside of a paper before handing it over, established the shape of his own patience in a clerk's book before handing anything over, and **wrote a not-refusal on the outside of a stiff cover with no name on it and said he would hand it back to the same man in the same room and that if anybody asks him up the road what he carried he will say he carried a piece of paper and a thing that was not a refusal.** **He is the first person in this batch to work out how not to become an office without being asked a single question about it.**
- **A road hand:** still unnamed, twice in this batch, with a wooden tally. **She brought the fact that the market form is back on a board and the fact that there is a cart at a gate, refused twice to look at a cart for anybody, said her tally is oak and a tally is not paper, and asked for the clerk's book to record that she has been on that road for two years and nobody has ever asked her for her name once, and that she wanted the asking recorded before the not-asking.** She is not an antagonist and may return.
- **A Quiet Hands cell:** at least two and probably three. **Unchanged and uncaught. Nothing in this batch recruited anybody, turned their reason into a riddle or a voice, or restated it, and the one new fact beside them is that a document with a column headed for the person who will be present exists in this building's record and a third room on it was left standing, and nobody joined that to a cell's argument.** **The grate at the low end is still off, there is still no second grate, two flags and a length of the crew's own spent line are over the channel, and the page that says somebody stands there is blank.** **The One-Seat protocol and Cassian Rook remain the destination per `outline/ending.md`, and Volume 04 does not name the One-Seat and does not have Cassian Rook in it.**
- **Harlan Merrow, Nell Ferrin and Hollis Ashe did not appear** in this batch and nothing in it contradicts them. **Pettin Rahl did not appear**, and the schedule he said was a regime's instrument is in the building. **Dael Harrow is not named.**

## The stair, the plans, the plate, and the evidence

The stair is **restricted, corded, and in service on its near side only**, with two timber shores on a common landing, **a lip that is still not measured by the people who own it**, and a common landing that **carries no number on any page in this building** and is named once in the batch's closing image. **The four treads behind the rail are dry, nobody has been on them, and no chapter of this batch staged them or went near them.** The eighth term is not touched, the ninth line is *none*, the ninth room has no row on the plan and is not in the charter and is not on the second sheet, **and no mark has been cut in its stone or in any other stone in this building.** The far wall of the throat is eleven feet down and has still never been seen.

**The plan on butcher's paper is one document in four parts in a coat, it does not leave this building, and it has sixteen rows.** The first column is a permission and has never held a count of anybody. The second column has a condition with no number and no day on each of the sixteen. The third column is **fifteen lines filled and one empty that the keeper will not name.** The fourth column is **empty and unheaded with its reason in two hands and a modal struck out of one of them.** **The tenth row's second column now carries a condition that is about a brace and not about a room, with two people in it, and the clerk read it out against what was said and compared the two and they were the same.** **The plan has no row for the party wall the brace pushes on, because that wall is not a room anybody is going to be in, and the refusal of a row for the low end of the corridor stands and was not re-argued in this batch.** The plan was not read out to a stranger in this batch and no paper left the building except a carrier's own not-refusal on the outside of a stiff cover.

**The plan on a dowel is a nine-row maintenance schedule in a locked school store and did not leave the store and was not unrolled.** **The resemblance between the dowel, the plan, the bench line, the mouth, the four treads, the air engineer's theory and the plate is a set of separate facts and nobody joined them in a room in this batch, and this batch's biggest temptation was the store's list, which agrees with what came down the passage, and the chapter left it alone.**

**The wrapped empty-seat plate** lies in a knotted bundle of work cloth on the shelf above the anteroom bench, unexplained, unidentified, unused, unclaimed, and **unopened for thirty-one weeks**. **The brass survey rule** is in the pocket of the coat on the anteroom's hook, **has said nothing for longer than twenty-two weeks on the ninth-week origin that `outline/volume-04.md` fixes and says it fixes**, and was not put on a table in this batch.

## Relationship and power guardrails, end of Volume 04 Batch 0001

- No harem structure and no instant romance. Nera remains an independent air engineer and a civic adult. **No intimacy, no recognition scene, no acceleration between Marek Venn and Nera Oduya in this batch, and no scene between them alone.** **One act of trust is delivered and it is the sixth, and it is legible in what she did and not in a scene between them: she asked him for a work, in the crew's own practice, and said the cost out loud.** The series does not begin their romance until Volume 05.
- **The power stage did not advance and no panel of any kind appears in this batch.** No bearing mark, no route change as a stage, no binding, no relay, **no brace built**, and no repeatable reading. **A brace is defined in a room in Chapter 154 out of a survey's four sentences and is designed, costed, argued and not started.** The right hand's fine control is not recovered, the left hand has not closed since the holding, the brass rule is silent, the Reader claim's condition is unmet, the mark is off the wall, and no mark was cut in the stone.
- The five Room Checks and the declared-occupancy discipline remain the growth framework. **The anteroom's rating is unchanged, its fifth of five terms has been broken since the middle of the twenty-sixth week, and its second way out is a word that a woman on a landing has said in a room is not a way out and has not taken out of a room's terms.**
- The working practice — the person who will keep a room writes the change to it — **produced, in this batch, a condition on a brace written by the woman who keeps the wall the brace can hurt, with two people in it and no number and no day on it; a store's list read twice and compared by a man who keeps it and a clerk who does not; a market form's sheet read against itself by a clerk who found the hole in it and that the hole was not the guild's; five of seven lines of a carrier's paper argued out loud before a mark was made; a column and three rooms struck out of a printed schedule in nine seconds; and a brace's joinwood given by the person who keeps the door, with the cost of the giving said in the same breath.** **And the batch's addition, which is the volume's civic discovery: a store is a room, a room has a keeper, and a keeper can be asked with the terms out loud and can say no.**
- **The crew end Volume 04's first batch as five people who are not a debt, not on the rota, whose column is sixty-six and a half and moved by three on a named asking in a room with the terms out loud and the three who could not be asked named with a third set of reasons, a boundary with a charter whose hole is one document wider and a new kind of document, a plan in a coat with sixteen rows and a condition in the tenth that is about a brace and not about a room, six cut pieces of a school's own beech on a bench and a school door with no wedge in it, a store four days up a road with a keeper who can say no, a party wall measured at two inches and a bit and not on a page, a pot at nine days and a seam going quiet, a route-holder's post in a carrier's hand with a carpenter's name in the second line and a not-refusal on the outside of it, a board with seventeen entries and eight under a column with nothing over the top of it, a dead man of twenty-two whose count is at ninety-five, and a person under a lip.**
