# Batch 0002's movement — Volume 04, Chapters 161–170

*This section is the Volume 04 Batch 0002 record and supersedes nothing above it. Volume 04 is open and this is its second batch.*

## Marek Venn

- **Named in ten of ten chapters, with interior life in ten of ten — and this was seven on first measure.** The viewpoint-presence check that Batch 0001 added to the craft baseline was run on the delivered files rather than asserted, **and it found him at the threshold in three chapters, 163, 167 and 170, and an interior beat was written into each of the three.** This is the fourth consecutive batch in which a state-file assertion of viewpoint presence would have been false and the measurement caught it.
- **Body, and this batch's cost.** The right hand has not closed since the nineteenth week. **The left hand has not closed since the holding in the twenty-eighth week, and it cut a splayed head for the brace and a beech shim a finger wide in this batch, both coarse, and the carpenter said the coarse cut is a wider face and the wider face is carrying four tons and called that arithmetic and not a compliment.** The mark on the inside of his forearm stands, **and in Chapter 169 he is one of the four who took the brace out of the wall and he took the end that went in with his forearm under it and his right hand doing nothing at all.**
- **Board: eighteen entries — eleven nulls, one claim, one mark, one row, a plan, a condition, a store and a brace; nine in the ordinary column and nine in the column with nothing over the top of it.** **The mark's entry has not been taken off the board, the claim's condition is unmet, and the plan, the condition, the store and the brace are none of them his entry.**
- **What he said that is new and load-bearing, in order.** **That a joint is not a pin and that a joint with no pin in it has to be a shape that stands up on its own**; that a spent line does not snap but goes slack and keeps going slack and tells you first, and that a spent line in a joint is a joint that will come apart in a bad month and he would rather it came apart in a bad month than a good one; **that time in this building is four days in seven and is not a thing a person can be given out of kindness**; that if this brace is standing in ten years then the five of them are not, and he did not want to agree to that because the only people who can object are people who will be gone; **that he had had a standing for a week and had not noticed it and had been proud of it in a way he had not admitted to anybody including himself, and that a man who keeps a page has now noticed it and is not going to put it in a column**; **that he refused in nine seconds to put his name on a plan and nobody has asked him for anything since except three hours of looking at air, and that this morning he agreed to six sentences in a room with a chalk and no signature at the bottom of them, and that agreeing is not signing and the difference costs something**; that what stops a brace is the four, and that he is the person least able to see the shelter and has said so out loud twice; **and that a room's rating is a word said to a page, that the word is *door*, and that a piece of beech over its head has not changed what it is for** — except that a man has now asked whether the word is still about the same thing, and that question was not answered and he was the man who said the word.
- **The private book.** It is on the page three times in this batch. **He is named as one of the three who could not be asked with the reason that he is the person the clerk put a figure against, and he did not ask to be removed from it.** In Chapter 167 **a figure is in the book and the two people talking about a wall were a physician and a schoolteacher and he said nothing at all about it**, and the clerk entered that as a change and not as a loss. In Chapter 170 **he walked the length of the party wall with the book open on his forearm, both sides, for the fourth time in thirty-four weeks, and wrote nothing, and found that one of the two walls in the book had been taken out of a wall by the person it was hurting, and that neither of them was his to put back.**
- **Immediate choice: the leaving is unchanged and unscheduled and was not raised in this batch and was not answered.** He is not a post and no page is going to get his name on it, and in this batch he agreed to six sentences in a room and found out that the agreement is not a signature and is not nothing either. **He now has a standing, and a man who keeps a page has said out loud that he is not going to write it in a column, and he said in a room that he had been proud of it for a week.**

## Leena Orr

- **Position:** the lower level, this side of the waist, and her good arm through a doorway. **She is named in Chapter 162 as one of the three who could not be asked, and the reason is a fourth one and it is not her shoulder: she is the only person in this building whose whole trade is reading a thing that is already built, and this work is a thing that is not built yet, and the clerk is not going to spend the one person who checks her work on the inside of the work.** She is in no other chapter of this batch and was not used. ***a list is not a location* was not used again, and that is now five batches held.**

## Iven Tallo

- **Asked for two hours of a piece of work in a room with the terms out loud, and two of the four and a half hours are his.** He asked for the split to be named before somebody named it, as he has done at every asking.
- **He laid out what a joint is and gave four ways of making two pieces agree and then said the one this building can afford: a shape that stands up on its own, which can be taken apart by a person with a knife and nothing else, and that this is the reason he wants to build it this way and he is not going to be asked for it twice.** He put the one about people last in the list of four things this building has not got, and said he has been here thirty-three weeks and has never once put the people last.
- **He found the answer to the length problem and it was not more wood: the head is cut on a splay, which is longer and wider, and he said the wide face is carrying four tons and that is arithmetic and not a compliment to the hand.** He cut a splayed head and a beech shim a finger wide and four inches long, **and he did not put the shim in the heap of offcuts, and he said the reason: the heap is what is left over and this is not what is left over.** He said the shim carries load on its two long edges and will crush at its corners in about two years, and that when it crushes the head settles and the frame goes a twelfth of an inch out of true again — which is the whole of what the brace won, so the shim coming out returns the frame to a finger and three-quarters and not past it — and nobody standing in that anteroom is going to feel a twelfth of an inch for a long time. *Corrected in a review-fix phase: this read *an eighth of an inch*, which was a third value for the same physical quantity.* **He said he can tell you what the shim is made of and cannot tell you when it dies, and that anybody who tells you when a thing like this dies is selling you the certainty and not the thing.**
- **He is asked to sign the record of the thing he built and says no**, and gives the reason that his name is in the second line of a stiff cover four and a half days up a road and he has not decided about that one, **and asks for it to be entered as the reason and not as modesty, and the line at the bottom of that paper stays empty.**
- **He is not redeemed, not a defector, not a martyr, not a saint and not a signatory of anything, and nothing in this batch made him any of those five things.** The batch did not use his hand against him and did not use it for him.

## Pell Roke

- **His work in this batch is reading numbers aloud, and it is all of his work, and he is in three chapters and unnamed in two of them.** **He is named in Chapter 162 as one of the three who could not be asked, with the fourth set of reasons: the work is holding, four people hold and one cuts, and a boy of fourteen on a crutch is not going to be one of the four that hold, and the clerk is not going to be the one who asks him to watch instead.** He asked for his hours to be named before anybody named them and took half an hour of the four and a half.
- **He read nine figures off a slate in Chapter 166, having been told what they were first, and said the numbers are a wall and not a count, and that he was going to read what the book says and not what the wall says, because a book is what a person reads out.** He is on the bottom step and comes up as far as the anteroom floor and no further.
- **He does not go down the steps, into the corridor, or over the waist, in any chapter he appears in, and nobody asked him to. No chapter in this batch puts him in the same room as Talla Roke.**

## Tams Quill

- **The right hand is still open, flat, and still not a working hand, and nobody let it be.** He never took a bar, a chisel, a lever or a packing, **and he did not go near the waist's third wedge.**
- **The crew's column moved by four and a half on a named asking and he took half an hour of it and asked for the split to be named before anybody named it**, and he did not thank the clerk and the clerk entered that he had not and that she had not expected him to.
- **He said no to holding the brace, and gave the reason that the page at the low end says somebody stands there and has been blank for thirty-two weeks, and that it is blank because a person who is willing is not a person who is standing there, and he asked for that to be entered before anybody in the room tried to be kind to him about it, and he said he would be good at it and asked for that to be entered too.** The clerk entered the refusal, the reason, the cost, and the fact that the price of a brace without a complete crew was a day of delay and a name in her book and that the name was his and he gave it to her on purpose.
- **He gave the tenth reason for refusing to head the column with nothing over the top of it, and it is the second of the ten that is not about him: I do not know what this building is for, and I am not going to print a blank where the answer goes, because a blank under a heading is a hole with a lid on it, and a man in a bad month is going to fall into it, and the ones who fell into a lid were never the brave ones, they were the tired ones.** He ended by saying that if the day comes when the reason costs somebody something then it is a piece of chalk.
- **A week later he entered the eighteenth board entry himself — a brace — in the column with nothing over the top of it**, and the reason is that **the word over that column would be *keeper*, and there is no such word in this building, and the four people who held it on Wednesday are not going to be standing here in ten years.** He put the chalk down and left it there, which he has not done in thirty-three weeks.
- **And he gave no eleventh reason at all, and said so, and said that the tenth cost him something he has not worked out, and that a man who spends his life reading numbers is not going to stand in a room and guess at one, and that this is the first time in eleven batches that he has had nothing and did not manufacture something, and he would like a person in a year to know that.** The clerk entered it and did not ask him for anything.
- The column is unheaded for the eleventh consecutive batch. **The board is walked in four chapters of this batch — 161, 164, 167 and 170 — and not in the other six, with a reason in a clerk's hand in each of the six**, and in no chapter is it walked by the clerk and the count on the same day for the same reason.

## Nera Oduya

- **Position:** the second step, the third step, the anteroom table, the school's edge, and once in the room. **She came down off the step in a working morning for the first time since the twenty-seventh week, to ask for a work.**
- **Authority: technical authority over airflow, air testing and safe operation of the air gate, unchanged, independent, never folded into a resident's consent.** She has refused to certify the stair's air for thirty-three weeks and has still published no rate.
- **She asked for a second work and asked for one**, in the crew's own practice, with the terms out loud, with Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, and with the three she is not going to ask named with the reason for each before she asked anybody anything. The work is: does the brace change the air in that room and in the anteroom, and if it does what is the limit, with no number and no day on it. **The three she named were Mikka Hale, because a person who is holding the thing cannot be asked whether the thing ought to be there; Jo Verrick, because she reads that wall at a first bell and the air and the wall are two ends of the same question this week; and Iven Tallo, because she has to ask him questions and is not asking him for a work, and if those two things get confused in this building she will stop asking anybody anything.**
- **She is wrong in public once in this batch and is not consoled, and she says so herself before anybody can get to it.** A frame that has been moving and a frame that has been held do not leak the same, and the corridor is the only thing that moves air between the anteroom and that schoolroom when the mouth is shut, and the pump runs twenty-six strokes and the crossing is four minutes, **and she did not put those four things together in a month of looking at that end of the building.** The half against her own answer is on the page too: the wall stopped on a Wednesday, a Wednesday is a day nine children are in there, and **she is not going to stand in a room and say nine children are not a load because she would like the wall to have stopped for a reason she can live with.** The clerk entered both halves in her words and entered that the clerk has not consoled her and is not going to, and that she would have consoled her last week and noticed herself nearly doing it this week and stopped.
- **She set a limit with no number and no day on it: the air in that room stays what it is now, and if it does not, then the brace comes out before the air is argued about. She said she is not going to be one of the two women who wrote the condition on the brace, because she is not one of the two people it can hurt and will not be able to see what they see.** And she said the hard part out loud: she has been the only person who may turn that wheel for thirty-three weeks and has never once been asked, and she is not going to be grateful about it afterwards, and being right about the air and being the only person in the room who is right is what an authority is, and there is no part of it anybody here should find comfortable.
- **Her condition is not met and her second condition stands and nobody asked her in a room.** The theory was not said. The name from the twelfth week is still not asked.
- **The volume's sixth act of trust is spent and is neither repeated nor inverted in this batch, and no seventh act is taken.** **The working consequence of it is delivered and it is not a scene between them: a man who keeps a page noticed out loud that the standing is the first thing in thirty-three weeks that has put itself in a column without anybody's permission, said the half against it, and said he is not going to write the line.** She is not leaving, no chapter stages her going, and the question of her going is not raised. No intimacy, no recognition scene, no acceleration, and no scene whose only content is the two of them.

## The Hearthhold boundary maintainers

- **Renn Vale:** **asked to be asked and said no**, and the reason is the volume's whole argument in one sentence: **she is one of the two people who can take the thing out, and a person who can take a thing out cannot be one of the hands that put it in, because a room will look for the person whose hand was on it, and if that person is the person allowed to take it out then the room has learned the wrong lesson and it will have learned it from her.** She said she said in a room a month ago that a person named in a room is not a post, that she meant it, and that she has been waiting thirty-three weeks for a chance to find out whether she meant it about herself. **She made the clerk read the fourth asking's terms again and ask which of them she was standing behind, and said a boundary that is not one of the five can do what it likes with its own wedges and can write terms for five other people that forbid it and then do the thing itself, and that this is not a contradiction, this is a door.** She added the sixth sentence to the terms: a work that stops is a work that was stopped in a room by a person who said so. **She said the brace's evacuation plan is four rooms and a door and a word and that the last part of that is not a plan.** She raised the objection that a word can change what it is about and asked for it as an objection and not as a discovery. **And in Chapter 169 she refused to ask the man who built the brace and asked the woman it could hurt instead, and said the reason is that a person who keeps a room is the person who is allowed to be wrong in public about that room, and that a man on a step and a physician in a doorway are both people who are professionally not wrong.** She said a door with no wedge in it is a door that has to be watched and the answer is one person and the page where a person would go is blank and is not going to be used.
- **Dalla Sen: is in ten of ten chapters and asked the crew for a fifth time**, with the terms out loud, Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **and the three who could not be asked named with a fourth set of reasons, and she gave the reason for the change: a person who hears the same name come up five weeks running stops hearing the reason.** **She read the terms out three times, added a sixth sentence she had written at the second bell and read as she wrote it, and entered that the last clerk who numbered the readings got it right and she would rather get it right than be the one who said so.** **She entered the seam and the pot next to each other with nothing between them and refused to write the word brace beside either.** **She entered the count at one hundred without a mark beside it, and told the room on Thursday so that nobody would be surprised, and said that a clerk who is disappointed that nobody thanks her is a clerk who has begun to want something, and entered that she had noticed and was not going to do anything about it.** **She stood at a wall and gave the room away for four minutes and entered that she did.** **She entered, on the last day of a week in which something went right, that this boundary's record says a man in this building recommended shutting a room in the twenty-fourth week, and that a clerk who enters that only in a bad week is managing a record.** She refused to let four terms be struck out and refused to let them be left, and entered the finding that they bound a work and not a building. She did not walk the board in six chapters of this batch and gave a reason in her own hand in each of the six.
- **Jo Verrick:** **reads the party wall and the anteroom frame at the first bell every morning now, and reads the frame before she says anything about it.** She gave the four days in seven that are this building's time and said a day in this building is not a day, a day is about four threads of water in a lime joint, and nobody has measured it since the nineteenth week, and she is not going to be the one who puts a number on how fast that is going. **She took the first reading of a frame that has come back a twelfth of an inch in thirty-three weeks, and said what it means and what it does not mean, and said the second one louder, to the cook.** *Corrected in a review-fix phase: this read *a third of a finger*, which is not the movement Chapter 168 measured.* **She said the anteroom's count out loud, unchanged, on the morning the frame improved.** She says the seam is at four threads and was eight in the nineteenth week and has not been measured in between, and refused to guess at the water going off the fill and said the string on the wall is not a bearing mark.
- **Mikka Hale:** kitchen, clinic return watch, pump frame, the water, the second hand of the plan, the author of the charter. **The fire in the corner of the schoolroom has now not been lit for eleven weeks and she asked to be asked about it a seventh, an eighth and a ninth time in this batch and refused each time, and asked for the children to be cold in the record in the same place as the refusal each time.** **She said the pot's arithmetic out loud in a room — five people working for two days on a thing nobody asked them to be paid for in a pot means a pot at nine is going to be eight, and the only reason it is not eight is a seam — and said she is not going to say a brace is being paid for in that seam and the clerk entered the two next to each other and did not write the word beside either.** **She said yes to holding a corner of the brace and said the half against it first**, and asked a room to notice that the sentence about not putting a dead man's share into the pot and the sentence about holding a piece of wood for a brace are about the same thing, and that she noticed it first.
- **Ilsa Norr (nine children and herself):** **the person who keeps the room and the person the brace pushes on.** **She wrote the condition a fortnight ago and said she had never liked it and has not come round to it.** **She found out by herself, on a shut morning, on her own, with nobody sent, by kneeling at the ninth hearth stone the way she does on shut days, and the bed is a third of an inch higher than it was on Friday morning and the stone and the flags and the board have not moved.** **She said she wanted the brace out and the clerk made her say all three clauses of her own condition and not have them filled in for her, and she said the first of us to stop agreeing takes it out, that neither of us has to give a reason to the other one first, that the second of us to find out is the one who acts, and that she is not going to give anybody a reason now and is not going to be asked for one.** **She made the condition cost the one thing it could cost: she said out loud that she is glad the wall read nothing, and that she is one of the two people whose agreement holds that thing up and is therefore the last person in this building who should be glad about a wall, and that she is glad and is not going to stop being glad.** She is in the room for every part of it. Nobody made her a counter-support and nobody stopped her from being one.
- **Bel Ordry:** thirty-five, keeper of the boundary's public maintenance plan, the sixth signatory of the charter. **He noticed out loud that the air engineer's standing is the first thing in thirty-three weeks that has put itself in a column without anybody's permission, and said the half against it, and said he is not going to write the line and is not going to be argued into it by a room.** **He is the fourth of the four hands and what stops the thing he is holding is the word, and the half against that is that a word is not a wall and that this morning he discovered the thing he has been protecting is the word and not the wood.** **He raised the objection nobody had raised — that a word can change what it is about — and it was not answered, and the word was said twice anyway.** **He said his knee out loud for the first time in thirty-three weeks and asked for it to be entered separately from the morning it happened on, because this morning is a different fact, and finished the last third of a crouch on his hands and did not ask for help and nobody offered.** He is **suspicious of the man with the store, out loud, on a reason, arranged by a clerk**, and said the arrangement was dirty and that he would have said it with the man standing in the room, and gave the half of the suspicion that argues against it. His half hinge is his own and is in a bag. He has still not raised his leaving and nobody has asked.
- **The woman from the wash rooms:** **not named, not asked, not rostered, not sent for.** **No legal instrument of any kind was produced in this batch and nothing was struck out, so the count of striking-outs in this book is unchanged at eight, and the ninth was not made.** The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, nobody was sent, and the page at the low end is blank and has been for thirty-two weeks. **This batch is the one in which the blank page was used twice without being filled: once as the reason a man who is willing is not a man who is standing there, and once as the reason a page cannot be used to put a person's hours on a door.**
- **Wen Pask: age twenty-two. Paid, kept, one hundred and five days and one hundred and five nights into a count at the end of Volume 04 Batch 0002, and dead.** **His count is at one hundred and five, is not going to be one hundred and six, and the clerk has said that out loud in fourteen weeks running and nobody has thanked her.** **The count reached one hundred and it was announced on the Thursday before, on purpose, so that nobody would be surprised, and no mark was put beside it, and a clerk who is disappointed that nobody thanks her is a clerk who has begun to want something, which she entered and said she was not going to do anything about.** **He is not a martyr, not a lesson and not an argument in this batch. His count was read at a sixth bell in all ten chapters and was not made into a scene about grief, because the reading is a working practice and not a funeral, and on the day it was a hundred the clerk said she did not have to work at her face and entered that.**
- **Mero Senn: age forty-five.** Rescue physician and trauma surgeon, twenty-two years. **He asked for the brace's failure point to be named out loud before a person was stood under it, and gave it the name *the place where it comes out*, and refused to give a room a name for a thing he had not looked at, and said he wanted a person who is going to be here in ten years to have heard the name of it from somebody who was frightened of it.** He said a wall can stop for a week or stop for good and there is no instrument in this building that tells the two apart. **He would not put his own fingers in a gap in a floor to find out whether he had been right, because he has spent eleven days asking this room to read a wall and not themselves — and that eleven days is a habit of his and not his tenure, which was wrongly given as eleven days in Chapters 166, 167 and 168 and is corrected to eight weeks, eight weeks and a day, and eight weeks and two days, from his arrival on the second day of the twenty-fifth week — and refused to name the man who built the brace, because nominating the builder to check the builder is not the same as asking him and he is frightened of his own hands and is not going to do it.** He put his refusal to certify on the table because nobody asked him to and said the refusal has not changed and the reason for it has. He does not fix anything, softens nobody, is not a saint and is not a rebuke, and he is right three times in this batch.
- **Orla Kern: age nine.** The fourth of Ilsa Norr's nine. **In the room on all four school mornings of this batch and sitting down**, and she is the girl on the fourth step of the anteroom in Chapter 163, and she is the one who stopped in the doorway in Chapter 168 and looked up at the brace and went on down the nine steps. **In Chapter 163 she asked a carpenter two questions about wood and was told a rule about safety by a man who keeps nothing, and the clerk entered the rule and not the child and did not call it a good question, because a good question is a thing a person gets praised for and nobody in that room praised her and she had not asked to be.** Her bone is where a physician put it, it has moved, and a physician has refused in writing to certify the room she is taught in.
- **Talla Roke: age twenty-two.** **In the building in two chapters of this batch — 163 and 170 — on her own terms, and not a rescue.** She said she is not here about a boy in both. **She asked what a person in this building is supposed to do when a piece of beech lets go, and gave the answer: it will have to be a person who is not the man who built it, because if the only person who understands that piece of beech is the man who cut it then in ten years it is a piece of wood and a story, and a story is not a thing somebody can stand next to.** **In Chapter 170 she said the thing nobody has said about this boundary's own terms** — a brace has been opened, a brace has been moved, two wedges have gone out of a door, and every office that has ever written a paragraph like that works because nobody can point at the day it stopped being true — and that she is not asking this boundary to be the guild, and that the difference is not the content, it is that this boundary can be asked in a room by a person who is standing in it. **No chapter in this batch puts her brother in the same room as her.** She is in 163 and 170; he is named in 162 and 166 and unnamed on a step in 161, 162 and 163.
- **Ormer Hatch: age forty-nine.** Survey camp, keeper of a store of eleven years. **He went up the middle passage at the first bell on the first day of the thirty-third week with three of his own and the fir from the store, and the beech stays, and the terms stand, and he asked for nothing on his way out and nobody in this building asked him anything before he went.** The beech is in a brace over a door. **A man who keeps a page is now suspicious of him out loud, on a reason, arranged by a clerk, and said the half that argues against it.** He is not an antagonist, not a saint, not a teacher and not a lesson, and the volume's question he asked in the last batch is on the page and unanswered.
- **A road hand:** still unnamed, in this batch in one line, and she did not come in. **A man at the back of the room said a hundred is a round number and a round number is a thing people put on a page, and the clerk entered that she is not going to put a mark beside it.** She is not an antagonist and may return.
- **A Quiet Hands cell:** at least two and probably three. **Unchanged and uncaught. Nothing in this batch recruited anybody, turned their reason into a riddle or a voice, or restated it.** The grate at the low end is still off, there is still no second grate, two flags and a length of the crew's own spent line are over the channel, **and this batch is the batch in which a man who reads the board gave the reason that the page is blank — a person who is willing is not a person who is standing there — and nobody joined that to a cell's argument about a line with a space in it.** The One-Seat protocol and Cassian Rook remain the destination per `outline/ending.md`, and Volume 04 does not name the One-Seat and does not have Cassian Rook in it.
- **Harlan Merrow, Nell Ferrin, Hollis Ashe, Pettin Rahl, Sabra Kest and Wenna Dray did not appear** in this batch and nothing in it contradicts them. **Dael Harrow is not named. Oren Sill is not named. Sefu Aran is on a road and did not come back in this batch and his return is Batch 0003's.**

## The stair, the plans, the plate, and the evidence

The stair is **restricted, corded, and in service on its near side only**, with two timber shores on a common landing, **a lip that is still not measured by the people who own it**, and a common landing that **carries no number on any page in this building** and is named once in the batch's closing image. **The four treads behind the rail are dry, nobody has been on them, and no chapter of this batch staged them or went near them.** The eighth term is not touched, the ninth line is *none*, the ninth room has no row on the plan and is not in the charter and is not on the second sheet, **and no mark has been cut in its stone or in any other stone in this building, and the clerk enters that fact four times in this batch and once of them deliberately beside the ninth striking-out of a schedule.** The far wall of the throat is eleven feet down and has still never been seen.

**The plan on butcher's paper is one document in four parts in a coat, it does not leave this building, and it has sixteen rows.** The first column is a permission and has never held a count of anybody. The second column has a condition with no number and no day on each of the sixteen, **and the tenth row's carries a condition about a brace, and that condition was met in Chapter 167 and is in force.** The third column is **fifteen lines filled and one empty that the keeper will not name.** The fourth column is **empty and unheaded with its reason in two hands and a modal struck out of one of them, and the clerk entered in Chapter 167 that nothing that happened that morning changes it.** **The plan has no row for the party wall the brace pushes on, because that wall is not a room anybody is going to be in, and the refusal of a row for the low end of the corridor stands and was not re-argued in this batch, and nine readings of that wall and a figure for a bed under a hearth stone are in a clerk's book and not on a page.**

**The plan on a dowel is a nine-row maintenance schedule in a locked school store and did not leave the store and was not unrolled.** The resemblance between the dowel, the plan, the bench line, the mouth, the four treads, the air engineer's theory and the plate is a set of separate facts and **nobody joined them in a room in this batch**, and this batch's biggest temptation was the wall's two nothings, which fall either side of a Wednesday on which the school ran.

**The wrapped empty-seat plate** lies in a knotted bundle of work cloth on the shelf above the anteroom bench, unexplained, unidentified, unused, unclaimed, and **unopened for thirty-three weeks**. **The brass survey rule** is in the pocket of the coat on the anteroom's hook, **has said nothing for twenty-four weeks on the ninth-week origin that `outline/volume-04.md` fixes**, and was not put on a table in this batch.

## Relationship and power guardrails, end of Volume 04 Batch 0002

- No harem structure and no instant romance. Nera remains an independent air engineer and a civic adult. **No intimacy, no recognition scene, no acceleration between Marek Venn and Nera Oduya in this batch, and no scene between them alone.** **The volume's sixth act of trust is spent and is neither repeated nor inverted here, and no seventh act is taken.** Their closest moment in this batch is a working moment in front of other people: the brace across the head of the door, the two inches and a bit she has been watching for a fortnight, and the fact that she is the person the room believes about the air and he is the person the room no longer believes about the wall. **The working consequence of the standing is delivered and it is not between them: a man who keeps a page noticed it out loud in a room and refused to write it in a column, and the man on the step said he had been proud of it for a week and did not know.**
- **The power stage advanced to the Bracer and stopped there.** A brace is a physical support joined to a bearing mark, **built by a team of five with four hands and one cutter, out of a school's own beech, joined to a mark by fitting wood to stone so that no mark was cut, with a new failure point named in a room before anything was stood under it, a condition met and admitted in a room before anybody was stood under it, and four costs all on the page.** **The brace does not increase the anteroom's capacity and did not.** No route change, no binding, no relay, no second bearing mark, no repeatable reading, **and no panel of any kind.** The right hand's fine control is not recovered, the left hand does not close, the brass rule is silent for twenty-four weeks, the Reader claim's condition is unmet, the mark is off the wall, and no mark was cut in the stone.
- The five Room Checks and the declared-occupancy discipline remain the growth framework. **The anteroom's rating is unchanged at ten including one litter for no more than two hours, its fifth of six terms has been broken since the middle of the twenty-sixth week, and its second way out is a word that a woman on a landing has said in a room is not a way out and that a carpenter said in a room this batch a person does not go out through, and that nobody answered. Corrected in a review-fix phase after Batch 0003: this read *fifth of five terms*, and the rating stood on six from the sixth term added on a landing in this batch, which Chapters 171–173 name as the fifth of six and as a term of six.**
- The working practice — the person who will keep a room writes the change to it — **produced, in this batch: a fifth asking in a room with the terms out loud; a condition on a brace read out by a second person and compared, on the day it was met; four terms read out three times against the original and compared and found the same; a survey's four sentences read out and compared against the book; a failure point named and read back and compared; an air work asked in the practice by the person with the authority; a school door's condition given by the person who keeps it with the half against it in the same breath; a record of a thing built with a line for a name at the bottom and the name not put there; and a term written by a clerk, compared, extended by a room rather than by the clerk, and entered.** And the batch's civic addition, on the fourth asking's terms: **a term this boundary wrote itself cannot be kept and cannot be struck out and cannot be left, and the finding is that it bound a work and not a building, and a building outlasts the terms of a work.**
- **The crew end Volume 04's second batch as five people who are not a debt, not on the rota, whose column is seventy-one and moved by four and a half on a named asking in a room with the terms out loud and the three who could not be asked named with a fourth set of reasons, a boundary with a brace standing over its busiest room with a condition met and a named failure point and a shim with a two-year life, a school door with no wedge in it and two sound wedges left in the building, a wall with nine readings and a bed that is a third of an inch higher, a pot at nine days held up by a seam, a route-holder's post in a carrier's hand four and a half days up a road and a second name refused on a piece of paper in this building, a board with eighteen entries and nine under a column with nothing over the top of it, a dead man of twenty-two whose count is at one hundred and five, and a person under a lip.**

# Volume 03 Batch 0001 — what the batch did to these threads

**This is delivery, not planning.** Chapters 101–110, the twentieth and twenty-first weeks.

- **OT-83 — the keeper of the page — DISCHARGED IN PART, and this was the month.** Bel Ordry **asked to be suspicious of in a month and nobody had been suspicious of him**, and this was the month, and the batch did it. **Dalla Sen demanded his coat in front of nine people at the fifth bell, counted the four parts, made him say which was which without looking, and entered that the fourth column is empty with its reason in two hands and that he did not volunteer which third-column line is empty and she did not ask him in front of the room.** Then she entered the other two sentences, in that order: **the clerk thinks what he wrote on Friday was very good, and the clerk has no way to check it and has not looked for one.** **He was also told to his face what he is, by a man with no standing to tell him and who is right** — *a man who can be found is a man who can be checked, and a man who cannot be found is a man who has to be trusted* — and he did not defend it and did not take it back. **He also refused, out loud, to put his ring on the sheet going up a road, and gave the reason: a ring on a sheet is a mark on a sheet, and a mark on a sheet is a thing a person can be found by, and he is not going to be the first one to break it in a bad week.** The thread is not closed. **A page in a coat is not a system, that is a man, and the man is on a road** — that is the batch's last line, and it is owed a resolution in a later volume and not in this one.
- **OT-84 — the four households at the second gate — WORSENED, and this is the volume's engine.** They still have nothing. **Their water-lock is now closed for a survey by a competent office, on a clearance, correctly, with a man in a hut behind the door and the water at a counter in front of it, and the fourth house does not walk.** The keeper is on a road with the true sentence in his coat. **The boundary sent a copy of the two sentences as paper, refused to pretend it could do more, sent nobody, and entered that a piece of paper in a courier's hand is not the keeping of a promise.** The cook's cost line is on the page in her own hand and is the longest line in the clerk's hand in twenty-one weeks. **The promise is Batch 0002's, in the twenty-second week, in person, at a counter, with the true answer, which is not good, and no other batch may keep it.**
- **OT-87 — a notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time — STANDING, and it was put to work without being restated.** **A notice came up the passage from the second gate with no date on it and with a clerk's mark on the form and not a name, and it used the word *attended* — a word this boundary reads four hundred times a day and has never once read the way it was written there.** The batch did not repeat the standing discovery and did not correct it. **It is still out of our sight, and it now has an instance.**
- **OT-88 — the air valve, the spring, the theory, and the name from the twelfth week — ALL THREE STANDING, and the condition was approached and not met.** **Nera Oduya did not say her theory, in a room, at the sixth bell of the fifth day, and said one professional sentence that is not it.** She asked the clerk to enter that **the fourth thing bound to *when this boundary is keeping itself* was approached in a room and was not met, and that she was in the room.** She was **asked for a piece of work and not an opinion** — write down what the second column is for — and did it in four minutes when it should have taken nine, and said she had a great deal more to say and that nobody asked for the rest of it, **and nobody asked for the rest of it and the clerk entered that nobody in that room is going to.** **The valve's answer is still owed in the spring, in a room, with her in it. The name from the twelfth week is still not asked and no room may ask.**
- **OT-90 — every document in this Hearthhold has a place to put everything except a person — ADVANCED, not answered.** **The first column is a count with no name in it, and Chapter 110 finds that it has been transcribing a *permitted occupancy* rather than an actual one: the anteroom's ten has been its allowed number since the fifteenth week, and the ten came off a nine-hundred-year-old dowel in a locked school store that nobody in this building has ever had read out to it.** Leena Orr's *a list is not a location* earned it. **And a room with nine children in it has no row at all, so it is a room nobody has promised anything to.** That is a development of the thread and **not an answer to it**, and **nobody in a room joined the first column to the dowel's provenance, the charter, the mouth, the four treads, the theory, or the plate.**
- **OT-91 — discharged in full and not reopened. The consequence delivered.** **The crew's column did not move in Batch 0001, and the reason was stated in a room twice — by Renn Vale on the second day and by Tams Quill on the first day of the following week: it is a quantity of asking and nobody has asked.** **Marek Venn offered it twice and was refused twice, and the second refusal was worse than the first.**
- **OT-92 — the stair inside one named work, and the eighth term not in agreement — STANDING, price not withdrawn.** **The stair is not in any work in Volume 03 Batch 0001 and is not in the charter. It was mentioned once, in Chapter 105, in one sentence, by the boundary, as *not a route and not in anything*, and the inspector wrote it down, and Nera Oduya added that four treads on the far side have nobody on them and nobody is going to and that she has refused to certify the shaft's air.** No batch may bring the stair into the water-carrying or into the charter.
- **OT-93 — the ninth line and the four treads — STANDING, both refusals intact, no mark cut in the stone.** Nobody went down the four treads. **The batch did add four marks and a groove on the lintel above the shut school corner's mouth: damaged, read two different ways by two people, answering nothing, and the clerk entered that no mark has been cut in that stone by anybody in that room and underlined it, which she does not do.** The resemblance between the dowel and the plan is now explicit in the prose — the anteroom's ten is the highest on the dowel — **and it is refused as a resolution. Nobody joined it up.**
- **OT-94 — the school — ESCALATED, and this is now the volume's central physical stake.** **The school corner's floor is wet and the water is the boundary's own drinking water, traced to a stone taken out of a course and put back in lime.** The school has been moved to the worst room in the building on the far side of a fill. **One of the three open days is lost in Chapter 108 against a closure added on a day the arrangement had open, nothing is paid back, and the clerk put the two facts side by side with a reason beside them and nothing between them, on purpose. Ilsa Norr was not told which of the two is the independent one and has not asked.** **A later batch may not restore a school day without restoring a closure, and may not tell Ilsa Norr which of the two is independent.**
- **OT-95 — the wash-room condition — STANDING, unsoftened, and the sheet protects her twice.** **Chapter 102 comes within a stated distance of naming the wash rooms as a candidate room and Renn Vale stops it in the shape she stopped a party in the eleventh week; the refusal is entered in four lines with no name against it and nothing struck out of it. The floor was not approached, nobody was sent, and nobody was asked.** **Chapter 107: the covers were struck out of the new second sheet in nine seconds, before anybody had explained it, and the air engineer said the reason out loud — nobody has asked her, not once, not in twenty weeks — and nobody in that room could produce one sentence in which anybody ever had.**
- **OT-96 — the one thing he cannot do twice — SPOKEN TWICE, FOUR DAYS APART, AND STILL NOT SPENT.** **In Chapter 101 Marek Venn says it in the school corner on the first day of the twentieth week**, after the ordinary fix has been refused in front of the room: *I have said in this building that anybody who comes and asks me to read a boundary is going to be told no, and I meant it, and I have run out of ordinary answers four days earlier than I thought, and the only thing I have left is that, and I am not going to use it on a floor.* **Dalla Sen enters that she did not understand it and is not going to guess in a book what it means**, and Renn Vale notes that it is the fourth time this building has written down a person not understanding something and the first time it has been the clerk. **In Chapter 109 he refuses the Marker out loud in a room and says there is exactly one thing left that is not a reading, and the clerk enters that she did not understand the second half of it.** The two are not the same statement: Chapter 101 is about the seam in the haunch and ends in the sentence *I am not going to use it on a floor*, and Chapter 109 is about the anteroom frame four days later with the ordinary means named and exhausted. **The Reader condition is still unmet, the brass survey rule has still said nothing for twelve weeks, and neither sentence may be read as a promise that Batch 0002 will spend it. Chapter 112's Marker is owed and it must arrive as an ordinary piece of work that costs, not as the thing this thread has been saving.**
- **The charter's hole — MADE VISIBLE AND NOT FIXED.** **Clause four is a right against one office. A Stonelight Compact inspector came into the building on a permit that does not cover her, and the boundary had to write a procedure for a body it had never written one for, and the third column of the plan left the building in a clerk's hand in exchange for her promise not to report a refusal.** The four sentences are on an anteroom table where anybody in the building can read them. **They were used once inside the boundary and were misread in the reading, and the clause that was dropped was the one about what a thing is and not what it is for, and the clerk entered that next to the anteroom's rating and the word *door*, because they are the same sentence.** **The hole is worse than the outline planned, in the way the outline hoped for.**
- **The market route as the volume's toll gate — OPENED, not answered.** **A competent guild office closed a structure on a clearance and the first toll on the closed door was not money: it was a form, and the form was a procedure, and the procedure is how a door becomes a toll gate — the Chapter 100 sentence arriving as a fact on a piece of paper with a clerk's mark on it.** Batch 0002 onward.
- **The Quiet Hands cell — NOT TOUCHED.** Discovered in Batch 0003, after a sabotage, with their fear legible and their dead dead in the same chapter. **Rung three on the antagonist ladder, not a new final enemy: the One-Seat protocol and Cassian Rook remain the destination, per `outline/ending.md`.**
- **The anteroom frame — now a thing with no ordinary means left, said out loud in a room.** The frame is unchanged: a finger and a bit out of true, shored, **holding and not fixed**, with the word *door* and the clerk's repetition as its rating. **Chapter 109 names the exhaustion — no timber, no mortar of the right kind, six sound wedges and two dead sticks, a right hand that will not close — and Marek Venn refuses the one operation that is left, in a room, and Dalla Sen writes down that she did not understand the second half of it.** **This is the Marker stage's setup and it is now written, and Chapter 112 can be written without inventing a frame.**

# Volume 03 Batch 0002 — what the batch did to these threads

**This is delivery, not planning.** Chapters 111–120, the twenty-second and twenty-third weeks.

- **OT-83 — the keeper of the page — STANDING, and advanced rather than answered.** **Bel Ordry was asked in a room, with the terms out loud, and a person named who could be told no, what the four marks and the groove on the lintel are** — and was not asked to read them, and gave one craft thing about the groove and then a sentence about the next fifty years. **He also said the batch's hardest institutional sentence out loud: he has had two bodies come to this boundary that the four sentences do not name, one of them said before she left that she would write a procedure of her own, and he is not going to write a second procedure in a fortnight for a second body, because a document that gets amended every time it is inconvenient is the guild's counter-draft with better manners.** **And the four sentences came out of the coat and were read out loud in Chapter 119 with a woman from another office standing at the end of them, and a rule on a page is portable and it is out of your hands the moment you write it.** The thread is not closed. The man is still a man, and a page in a coat is still not a system, and **the fourth column of the plan is still empty and a boy of fourteen read it out loud in a room in Chapter 115 and said there was nothing in it.**
- **OT-84 — the four households at the second gate — KEPT, IN PERSON, AND NOT FIXED.** **The promise is discharged. Sefu Aran said the two true sentences to their faces at a counter, at four doors, because nothing at that gate can summon anybody, on the first of the month and not one day before.** **The answer is true and it is not good and it fixed nothing.** The fourth household, Marda Skell, sixty-one, who does not walk, asked *will it be open again* and was told *I do not know*, and said *then you came a long way to tell us a thing we had already worked out*, and he said *yes*. **The water-lock is still closed for a survey that nobody will say how long will take, and Wenna Dray told him that nobody is going to be cruel about it, nobody is going to hurry, and at the end of it the water is still a step away and down a slope, exactly as it was before anybody surveyed it — and that nobody did anything wrong.** **Marda Skell also told him his own second sentence has already gone further down the road than he knew, on a route that is not his and not a guild's, and refused to say who told her, and he did not ask.** The thread is discharged as a promise and open as a debt, and **nobody in this building knows when the keeper arrives and the room has decided not to write down how long he has been gone.**
- **OT-87 — a notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time — STANDING, and it was put to work twice without being restated.** **The market route's form has no date on it and the clerk says so in a room and draws no lesson from it. The archive's answer came back undated. Bel Ordry refused in a room to put a figure on how long the answer would take.** **One bounded new instance: a Compact form has a line for the date observed, and the inspector says she is required to fill it, would fill it, and that it is the only lie on the form.** It is out of our sight and it now has two ordinary instances.
- **OT-88 — the air valve, the spring, the theory, and the name from the twelfth week — ALL FOUR STANDING, and the condition was approached again and not met.** **The air valve is owed in the spring, in a room, with her in it. The theory was not said in Chapter 116** — she said four words, *a room is being maintained as a bench*, and **stopped on purpose**, and asked the clerk to enter that the fourth thing bound to *when this boundary is keeping itself* was approached in a room and was not met, and that she was in the room, and that nobody asked her anything. **Marek Venn had the question in his mouth and put it down.** The name from the twelfth week is still not asked and no room may ask.
- **OT-90 — every document in this Hearthhold has a place to put everything except a person — ADVANCED, and the sentence has been proved both ways.** Batch 0001 found that the first column records a permission. **Batch 0002 read all four columns out loud in a room in Chapter 115, and the third was eight of nine filled and one empty and the fourth was empty, and a boy of fourteen said *there is nothing in it*.** So the document now has a column that a person can read as nothing, in a room, out loud. **And in the other direction: the mark was placed on a stone and it is the first thing in this building in twenty-two weeks that is not a document at all, it is a claim on a surface, and a road hand saw it in four seconds and wrote it in a field book, and the record of it cannot be recalled.** That is a development of the thread and **not an answer to it**, and the batch says the two things are not the same shape and does not join them.
- **OT-91 — discharged in full and not reopened. The consequence delivered.** **The crew's column moved for the first time since the fifth day of the nineteenth week**, from fifty-two and a half to fifty-three and a half, by one hour, on an asking made in a room by Dalla Sen with the terms out loud and Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no. **The reason is on the page in a clerk's hand as well as in Renn Vale's, and the count declined to give it because a clerk gave it better.** **The column has not moved since and nobody has asked for anything else.**
- **OT-92 — the stair inside one named work, and the eighth term not in agreement — STANDING, price not withdrawn.** The stair is not in any work in Volume 03 Batch 0002 and is not in the charter. **The guild's survey covered this boundary's sector and its finding did not put the stair on a list, and nobody in the room asked about the stair, and the boundary did not raise it.** No batch may bring the stair into the water-carrying or into the charter.
- **OT-93 — the ninth line and the four treads — STANDING, both refusals intact, no mark cut in the stone.** **Nobody went down the four treads. Nobody cut a mark in the stone anywhere in this building, and the batch says so in Chapter 112, and the mark that exists is chalk and gland grease on a dressed jamb and it is stopped.** The four marks and the groove were read in Chapter 112 and asked about in Chapter 113 and **in Chapter 115 the room stood open and nobody looked up at them.**
- **OT-94 — the school — ESCALATED AGAIN, and this time in the opposite direction.** **The school corner's floor is dry, the condition is met, the room is open, and the school is not in it.** Renn Vale opened it anyway so that no condition of hers is left on a page looking met while it is not. **The reason is on the page: the reason the floor is dry is a thing two women can take off a wall, and when the mark comes off that head will start going out again and the joint will start feeding that floor again.** Ilsa Norr's cost is in her own words and is not consoled, and the closure, the opening and the un-restored school day are on the page together with a reason beside them and nothing between them. **No school day is restored, no closure is removed, and nobody has told Ilsa Norr which of the two facts is independent.** **The school still has no row on the plan, and the survey's finding about that room is that its floor is a use, and nobody joined the two.**
- **OT-95 — the wash-room condition — STANDING, unsoftened, and the protection is now three times.** **In Chapter 119 a Compact form came into the room with the wash rooms written on a line headed for rooms and fittings in the structure under inspection, and Nera Oduya read it upside down from three steps on her way past, said one word, and struck it out in nine seconds, and did not give the reason a third time** — and when Bel Ordry asked her why, she looked at him and he put his hand down. **The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, and nobody was sent.**
- **OT-96 — the one thing he cannot do twice — SPENT, PROPERLY, ON THE ONE THING IT WAS SAVED FOR.** **The refusal in Chapter 109 is answered in Chapter 112, and it is answered by the thing itself and not by an explanation.** He spent the fortnight mostly deciding not to, and did it on the second day of the twenty-second week, out of the anteroom's outer service door frame, because the ordinary means were named and exhausted and because nine children are on the far side of a fill and a school corner's floor is wet and the wall that feeds it is the wall the frame is in. **It has a visible mark, a stated limit, a burning hand, a load echo, a condition agreed by the woman who keeps the room, and a second person who can stop it. It saves nobody. It was stopped on the third day of the twenty-third week, before the volume's climax, in a room, by the person who wrote the condition, and the man who put it on was not allowed to take it off.** **The Reader claim's condition is still unmet, the brass rule is still silent, and the right hand's fine control is not recovered.**
- **The charter's hole — ONE INSTITUTION WIDER, AND NOT FIXED.** The charter names the Cartwright office. **Three bodies have now come to this boundary that the four sentences do not name: the Compact inspection line, the guild survey camp, and the market gate.** The boundary has four instruments, one procedure, has used that procedure for a body it does not name, and has refused to write one for a third. **And the batch found the two halves of the cost: a mark that is off the wall is still in a field book, and a rule that is on a page is read in four seconds by a stranger who is standing in the room.**
- **The market route as the volume's toll gate — ANSWERED ONCE, AND NOT ANSWERED FOR THE WORLD.** **The first form exists, seven lines, two of them for a name, and the word in it for not doing it is *attended*.** Five of seven lines were objected to in a room and nothing was marked until it had been argued. **The boundary's answer went out on a market day in two sentences with no name and no signature, and the clerk said the charter's part out loud first, because a market day is not a delivery.** **The form is still on a board at a gate and the first toll is still a name, and the volume's question about a route being a public good across jurisdictions is not answered by a two-sentence reply to one form.**
- **The Quiet Hands cell — NOT TOUCHED.** Discovered in Batch 0003, after a sabotage, with their fear legible and their dead dead in the same chapter. **Rung three on the antagonist ladder, not a new final enemy: the One-Seat protocol and Cassian Rook remain the destination, per `outline/ending.md`.**
- **The anteroom frame — spent, and back where it was.** The frame held from the second day of the twenty-second week to the third day of the twenty-third, the school corner's floor dried, and then the condition was met, the mark was taken off with a cloth, and **the head is a finger and a bit out of true again and the second way out of that room is a word said to a page, and a person could be found in four seconds and a description of him is in a book four days up a road.** **This is the position Volume 03's midpoint reversal is scheduled to exploit, and it is on the page, and the clerk who would have put the four facts side by side had the chalk in her hand at the seventh bell of Chapter 118 and did not do it, and has never given a reason.**
- **New, and not planned: the guild's survey is right, and being right is a cost.** **The sector is stable. The waist's three moves are seasonal and not a fault. The school corner's floor is a use. And a sound sector gets no crew put in it again, and the man who found that out said it out loud and put the good fact and the bad fact in the same sheet on purpose.** **This is the volume's cheapest answer arriving from outside the building, and nobody in the boundary has noticed that a document which says everything is fine is a document that stops anybody coming back, and the chapter ends with a man understanding it four days too late and nobody in the room saying a word.**
- **New, and not planned: a title is worse than a name.** **A field book four days up the middle passage carries *the person who keeps the anteroom's terms*, and a title is a post, and a post can be asked for by a body that has never met the person who holds it.** Renn Vale's answer is that there is nothing here to be sent for, and that she would rather be named and refused than titled and found, and that she does not know which of the two she would survive. **A later batch may raise the road that comes looking and may not resolve it cheaply.**
- **New, and not planned: a room nobody is in does not need a second way out.** **Said once, in a room, in Chapter 111, by Renn Vale, and entered once by the clerk, and the entry says *do not let anybody in here find that out before the rest of us has*.** It is the volume's thesis in one sentence and it is the cheapest thing this building knows how to do, and a later batch may use it and may not soften it.

# Volume 03 Batch 0003 — what the batch did to these threads

**This is delivery, not planning.** Chapters 121–130, the twenty-fourth and twenty-fifth weeks.

- **OT-83 — the keeper of a page — ADVANCED, and the shape of him is now on a page.** **Bel Ordry refused to write a second procedure for a second institution and said the reason out loud again, and then he argued in a room for writing a row on this boundary's own plan about a room with a child in it, and he said in the same breath that a document about a room travels and a name on a route is a name forty days away, and the room did it anyway in the open, with the reason out loud before the page was opened.** He read out a man's own book in a room and said where it was from first. **He began a sentence about second ways out in Chapter 123 and Renn Vale made him stop, and nobody in this book ever finishes it.** He says that a room does not get to check the number a man has put in it, and refuses to let anybody build a system out of it tonight. The thread is not closed. **A page in a coat is now a page with ten rows, one of which is a room with nine children in it.**
- **OT-84 — the four households at the second gate — STANDING, and a physician has been at them.** **The promise remains discharged and the water-lock remains closed for a survey nobody says how long will take.** **Mero Senn was at the second gate, on the other end of the same road, and came down it with a bag and a strap**, and the fourth house that only carries is the reason he says he could not turn round at a counter. Nothing in the batch fixed anything and nothing in the batch pretended to.
- **OT-87 — *a notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time* — STANDING, and it was put to work without being restated.** **A reply sheet came up the middle passage with a line for a name or a description sufficient to identify and a short line for an answer, and the boundary answered it in a room, in words, and sent no paper back down the road.** The market route's form has no date. The two sheets of cheap paper found in the channel have **no date on them and no name on them**, and one of their five lines is that a document everybody can fill in is worth more than a document nobody can.
- **OT-88 — the air valve, the spring, the theory, and the name from the twelfth week — ALL FOUR STANDING, and the condition was not met.** **Nera Oduya opposed Marek Venn in public in Chapter 123, was right about the air, and said out loud that she knew who was going to lose and that it was not she.** She said that a room with one door shut is a box with nine people in it, that a number said out loud twice in a room is not a check, and that she will not be able to open that door and is saying so in advance so that it is on the page before anybody needs it. **The theory was not said. Her condition is not met. Nobody asked her in a room.** She put herself into a condition without being asked, for the second time in this book, and asked for it to be entered. The valve's answer is still owed in the spring, in a room, with her in it. The name from the twelfth week is still not asked and no room may ask.
- **OT-90 — every document in this Hearthhold has a place to put everything except a person — ADVANCED, and proved in the other direction.** Batch 0001 found the first column records a permission. **Batch 0003 wrote a tenth row on that plan, in the cook's hand, with a ten in the first column that nobody counted, and the cook said out loud in a room that she chose it and why and that it makes her the worst person in the room.** **A boy of fourteen read it aloud and said ten, and the room it describes held eleven, and nobody joined the two numbers.** And **two forms from two offices, both with a line for a person, one of them filled in with a title, are the whole of a cell's argument, and a cell of at least two people was in this building in the dark and levered a grate off a channel and left a piece of paper under a flag.** That is a development of the thread and **not an answer to it**, and the batch does not join the plan to the sheets to the field book to the title.
- **OT-91 — discharged in full and not reopened. The consequence delivered again.** **The crew's column moved by three hours on a named asking made in a room with the terms out loud, with the three who could not be asked named and the reason for each.** A carpenter named the split of the work and a man agreed to it. **A piece of the crew's spent frayed line went to a hole at the low end in Chapter 130 and is not an hour and does not move the column, and the man who gave it said he was asked.**
- **OT-92 — the stair inside one work, and the eighth term not in agreement — STANDING, price not withdrawn.** **The stair is not in any work in Volume 03 Batch 0003 and is not in the charter, and nobody in this batch asked about it, and the boundary did not raise it.** No batch may bring the stair into the water-carrying or into the charter.
- **OT-93 — the ninth line and the four treads — STANDING, both refusals intact, no mark cut in the stone.** **Nobody went down the four treads and nobody cut a mark in the stone anywhere in this building.** **The Quiet Hands' second sheet lists two rooms with nothing at all in front of them, and the clerk enters that they are on it and says she is not going to say whose rooms they are and is not going to be asked, and the rooms were not staged and nobody went near them.**
- **OT-94 — the school — WORSENED TWICE IN ONE WEEK, and both costs are entered in a schoolteacher's words.** **The school ran on the third and fifth days of the twenty-fourth week and the third day of the twenty-fifth week and did not run on the fifth day of the twenty-fifth week, and the reason was a man dead in a channel at the low end, and the loss is not paid back.** The open day lost in Chapter 108 is still lost, **so two open days have gone since the school was moved, in two different weeks, for two different reasons, and Ilsa Norr has still not been told which of the two facts is independent and has not asked.** **The room the school is in had no row on the plan until the third day of the twenty-fifth week and now has a ten in it that is a permission and not a count of anybody, and one of its nine hearth stones is propped on a strip of crate board, and one of its nine children has a broken foot.** She said out loud that she taught in it with a hole in the floor under a stone, knowing, and would again, and put both of those on the same line.
- **OT-95 — the wash-room condition — STANDING, unsoftened, and the protection is now four times.** **A Compact reply sheet came up the passage with a printed line on the back of it headed for structures in the boundary whose condition is kept by a person, and three rooms under it, one of them the wash rooms, and Nera Oduya struck the heading and the three entries in nine seconds without coming down the steps, gave no reason, and was not asked.** **The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, and nobody was sent.** Her two sentences on the review page are read out of the page by the clerk in Chapter 129 and she is not in the room and is not used and the page stays blank.
- **OT-96 — the one thing he cannot do twice — SPENT, PROPERLY, AND THIS IS WHAT IT COST.** **The refusal in Chapter 101 and the refusal in Chapter 109 are answered in Chapters 123 to 127.** He recommended that a room with nine children in it be shut, and he was right, and the room holds, and the corridor's low end is saved, and a girl of nine came out of it on the Monday with a foot that cannot take weight. **His first public failure is read out in a room, in his own words, with the number in it, out of a book of his own that nobody else has read, and a physician is in the room, and the boundary does not forgive him and does not blame him.** He says in his own book, and out loud in a room, that a number said out loud twice in a room is not a check but a way of making a room agree with a man, and that being right about every wall in a building is how a man stops being able to be argued with about a floor, and that **five walls is a number he chose and not a number he counted, and that he is not going to be given a condition for saying a number out loud.** **The Reader claim's condition is still unmet, the brass rule is still silent, the right hand's fine control is not recovered, and the mark is off the wall.**
- **The charter's hole — ONE INSTITUTION DEEPER AS WELL AS WIDER, AND NOT FIXED.** Clause four names the Cartwright office. **Four bodies have now come to this boundary that the four sentences do not name: the Compact inspection line, the guild survey camp, the market gate, and the Quiet Hands.** **A reply sheet came up the middle passage with a line for a name or a description sufficient to identify, and a short line for an answer, and the boundary wrote no second procedure, sent no paper, and answered it in a room in nine words: *there is no such person here*.** And on the back of it, a printed line headed for structures whose condition is kept by a person had **three rooms under it, and somebody four days up the passage has put a keeper against a row on a page that has never left this building, and the clerk entered that and declined to write the rest of the sentence.**
- **The market route as the volume's toll gate — ADVANCED, and the first toll is now a title.** **The market form's line for *the person responsible for the load* and the Compact form's line for *the person who keeps it* are the two lines a cell read, and the cell's argument is that a line with a space in it is a post being cut and that a title is not a name.** **The volume's question about a route being a public good across jurisdictions is not answered by two sentences to a form and is not answered here.**
- **The Quiet Hands cell — DISCOVERED, after a sabotage, and it is exactly what the outline scheduled.** **They are at least two and probably three; the boundary does not know, does not invent, and does not catch them.** They came in on their own, in the dark, and levered a grate off a stone frame at the low end of the corridor with something the width of a dead stick, and weighted a sheet of paper with the same dead stick, and left it under a flag in the channel. **Their reason is legible and three people in the room say out loud that they understand it, and nobody is recruited, and Mero Senn says that a reason can be legible and a person can still be dead.** **The only sentence on their sheets that was not invented is a sentence about a hole, and that is entered in a room and left there.** **One death is available in this volume and it is spent, named, counted, and not anonymous: Wen Pask, twenty-two.**
- **OT-15 — Mero Senn — DISCHARGED, and he is not a rescue and not a saint.** **He appears in Chapter 127, the day after the count, having come down the last of the middle passage from the second gate, and he was not in the room when the door was opened and nobody sent for him.** He is owed since Volume 01 and he is here. **His rule is the volume's instrument and four people in this building have been doing his work for twenty-five weeks without knowing it, and a schoolteacher said it in a corridor the day before he arrived and did not know whose it was.** He sets the foot, says the set is correct and bad and both are true, is wrong in public about the room and says so first, fixes nothing, softens nobody, and says the good half of a document he had not read. **He may return. He is competent, bounded, forty-five, and he is not a rebuke.**
- **The anteroom frame — unchanged, and it is the reason the reversal is legible.** **The mark is off the wall, the head is a finger and a bit out of true, the packing is still clay, and the second way out of the busiest room in this building is a word said in a room and repeated by the clerk and not said to a door.** **And on the fifth day of the twenty-fourth week eleven people said a word in a corridor and it opened nothing, and on the first day of the twenty-fifth week the clerk said it at a shut door into an empty room and repeated it and there was nobody there to hear it, and the rule could not be kept and was not kept.** The frame was not a post in this batch's argument and was not measured in this batch.
- **New, and not planned: the boundary's own working practice proved what it is worth.** **Renn Vale said out loud, in a room, that the rule that the person who writes a change to a room is the one who keeps it, and is not to blame for it, is worth exactly this: that she is not the one a doctor looks at.** And the boundary forgave nobody and blamed nobody, and the cost went to a schoolteacher, a cook, a woman with a rule, and a child of nine. **The rule held and it cost the people it was written to protect, and a later batch may not argue with that and may not undo it.**
- **New, and not planned: a permit, a permit's office, and a title have become the same shape.** **A reply sheet wants a name or a description sufficient to identify. A field book carries a title. A market form carries a person responsible for the load. Three documents from three bodies, one of them not from a guild, and all three have a space in them for a person, and the cell's whole argument is that the spaces are a post being cut.** **None of the three is a page from this building's own plan, and the plan has not left the building, and nobody joined the four.**
- **New, and not planned: a count that will not stop.** **The clerk has said out loud, in a room, that a man's count in the column with nothing over the top of it is at sixty-five and is not going to be sixty-six, and that she is going to keep writing it, and that a number which stops on the day a man is found is a record of when the boundary noticed him.** **A later batch may not make the count a register, may not make it date anything, and may not stop it.**
