# Volume 03 Batch 0004 — what the batch did to these threads

**This is delivery, not planning.** Chapters 131–140, the twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh weeks.

- **OT-83 — the keeper of a page — ADVANCED TWICE, and once out loud.** **Bel Ordry extended this boundary's own public plan by two rows, argued in a room that he was aware what he was proposing, said that a document about a room travels and that a name on a route is a name forty days away, and asked for the row anyway, with the reason out loud before the page was opened.** He then wrote the second of two new rows' third column and stood up. **He asked for a row for the place where a man is dead and the room refused it, and he asked in front of the room to be refused there rather than discovered in a month.** And **Dalla Sen doubted him out loud, with a reason, and told him afterwards that she had arranged it: he said he wants the plan for the day the boundary is not looked after by anybody standing in it, and said which of his two answers was older, and the wrong one was the older one.** He refuses to sign his own plan, because a signed instrument is a thing a person four days up the passage can hold up, and he said that out loud. The thread is not closed. **A page in a coat now has twelve rows, and two of them are places rather than rooms, and it is the fifteenth entry on a board in a column with nothing over the top of it.**
- **OT-84 — the four households at the second gate — STANDING, and the water-lock is still shut.** Nothing in this batch fixed anything. **The keeper's true sentence is referred to in the closing image of Chapter 140 and no figure is attached to the gate.** Mero Senn is still in the building and was at that gate before this batch and has not gone back.
- **OT-87 — *a notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time* — STANDING, and put to work once without being restated.** **The market route's form has no date on it and now functions as a pass, and nobody wrote a rule and there is no order and no notice and nothing with a date on it, which is the property of this building arriving as a fact rather than as a discovery.** A second document exists with a line for a person in it, written by an office that does not cover this boundary. **No paper went down the road in this batch and no date was put on anything.**
- **OT-88 — the air valve, the spring, the theory, and the name from the twelfth week — ALL FOUR STANDING, and the condition was approached once and not met.** **Nera Oduya said in a room that she has had half of it since the fourth day of the eleventh week, did not say it, said that half of what she knows is about a room and what Talla Roke asked is about a road, and that her condition is not met and that a plan with twelve rows in it and a river at the waist is not the thing that meets it.** **Nobody asked her. The clerk entered that the two questions are adjacent and not the same, that she was asked to put them next to each other and would not, and that they are next to each other in the book by accident.** **She also said that the anteroom's fifth condition has been broken for a fortnight, and the clerk entered that she knew on the day it stopped being true and did not write it down.** She asked for his figures to be read against an original four times in ten chapters and **never once asked him how he knows**, and nobody has noticed. The valve's answer is still owed in the spring, in a room, with her in it. **Her theory was not said and her name is still not asked.**
- **OT-90 — every document in this Hearthhold has a place to put everything except a person — ADVANCED, and the batch's answer is an argument rather than a fix.** **The plan's first column still records a permission and has never recorded a count. The cook wrote a second permission and said out loud that she did not count anybody for the second time either, and said she was the worst person in this room twice over. A boy of fourteen read twelve numbers out loud and said nothing about any of them.** A name was argued onto the page and refused, a carpenter's mark was offered and refused, and a third column was kept because a third column is a person writing what they do and a name in a column is a person being written about. **And nobody in the building joined the eleven and the ten, and the clerk entered the not-joining as a decision with a reason in it.** That is a development of the thread and **not an answer to it.**
- **OT-91 — discharged in full and not reopened, and the consequence is now two named askings.** **The crew's column moved by three on the second day of the twenty-sixth week, on a named asking in a room with the terms out loud, Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, and the three who could not be asked named with the reason for each before the asking: Leena Orr, Pell Roke and Tams Quill.** A carpenter named the split of the work and asked to be put on the other side of a door he would not pack, and asked for his refusal from two weeks earlier to stand afterwards, and it stands. **The crew have now been asked twice in twenty-seven weeks.**
- **OT-92 — the stair inside one named work, and the eighth term not in agreement — STANDING, price not withdrawn.** The stair is not in any work in Volume 03 Batch 0004, is not in the charter, and was not in the water-carrying. **It is named once, in Chapter 140, as one of the three things that are not a way out: a stair to a landing with two timber shores on it and a slab over eleven feet that is packed and not held, and a person under it, and a post under that has never been built.** Nobody put a foot on it.
- **OT-93 — the ninth line and the four treads — STANDING, both refusals intact, no mark cut in the stone.** **Nobody went down the four treads and it is said in Chapter 140 that nobody did, and no mark was cut in the stone anywhere in this building.** **The school corner's mouth is open, has been since the fifth day of the twenty-second week, is not used and is not going to be used, and two people stood in its doorway at a first bell and read the four marks and the groove on the lintel above it two different ways and it answered neither of them.** The two rooms with nothing in front of them on the Quiet Hands' second sheet were not staged and nobody went near them.
- **OT-94 — the school — RUN ON ALL FOUR OPEN DAYS IN THIS BATCH, and the losses were not paid back and two new facts landed on it.** **The school ran in the room at the kitchen-line end on the third and fifth days of the twenty-sixth week and the third and fifth days of the twenty-seventh, sixteen to eighteen mornings in all, and the school corner stayed open and unused throughout.** The tenth row of the plan gained a stronger condition in the second column, **written by the woman who keeps the room, checked every morning the room is used, with the nine coming out without waiting for a physician if the answer is no twice.** The ninth hearth stone is still propped two flags off its bed on a strip of crate board and the strip is holding, and a fortnight of a hole not getting worse is not a repair. **Orla Kern is in the room and sits, and her bone has moved and two people have not said in a room that it has not moved.** The open days lost in Chapter 108 and Chapter 130 are still lost. **Ilsa Norr has still not been told which of the facts is independent and has not asked, and in this batch she said that a building like this one is not a thing people live in, it is a thing they are in.**
- **OT-95 — the wash-room condition — STANDING, unsoftened, and the protection is now five times and the reason is gone.** **A heading on this boundary's own evacuation sheet, and the line under it, was struck through in nine seconds from three steps up, before anybody had asked, and the reason was not given at all for the first time in twenty-six weeks.** The clerk entered the time, the absence, and that there is no reason in the space where a reason would go, because a page with a reason on it is a page somebody can read back to her. **The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, and nobody was sent.** Her two sentences on the review page are read out of the page in Chapter 140 as one of five reasons a hole is a place a person can be killed, and she is not in the room, is not used, is not asked, and the page is still blank.
- **OT-96 — the one thing he cannot do twice — SPENT, AND THE BILL IS STILL COMING DUE.** **He recommended a room be shut, he was right, and a girl of nine came out of it with a foot. In this batch he recommended the row for a hole be written and was refused, and then he sat on the other side of his own refusal all week and said out loud on the fifth day of the twenty-seventh week that the refusal was right and the refusal is why there was nobody standing at that hole.** He said the ordinary fact that a room nobody is watching finds out about itself from a stranger. He repeated a limit he had no reading for and said so: *I have got a number of people and a door and a sentence an air engineer said, and I am not going to dress that up as something I felt in a wall.* **He said the sentence this batch is built on and then took half of it back in the same breath**, which is the first time in the volume he has entered his own argument against himself in a room. **The Reader claim's condition is still unmet, the brass rule is still silent, the right hand's fine control is not recovered, and the mark is off the wall.**
- **The charter's hole — ONE INSTITUTION WIDER AGAIN, IN FRONT OF WITNESSES, AND NOT FIXED.** **Two people from the Stonelight Compact came up the middle passage together and sat through clause four being read out against the original, and neither of them is the office clause four names.** One of them has written a four-page procedure that assumes this boundary wants to be looked at and has said out loud in a room that she could not write a procedure for a boundary that does not, **because there is nothing in one.** The other has said out loud, in a room, that his office will want a regime for a boundary that keeps a permitted occupancy nobody has counted, **and that a regime is not a threat, and he wanted that said by him before anybody else said it there.** **The boundary's answer was that the plan does not leave this building, that the charter does not leave it, and that there is no procedure for either of them and none was written.** One of the two called that a bad answer and said it was the correct one. **Nothing was sent down the road.**
- **The market route as the volume's toll gate — ADVANCED, and the first toll is now a pass and the boundary has decided not to pay it.** **A clerk at a gate on that road has begun to require the form's two lines of anybody who wants to go along the road with more than they carry, and there is no order and no notice and nothing with a date on it.** Talla Roke's rule is in a clerk's book in her own words, entered on purpose so that nobody can take it off her by saying she made it up. **The boundary's stated answer is that it will not fill the form in, that the road is therefore not a public route, and that forty-one people are not going anywhere.** The volume's question about a route being a public good across jurisdictions is not answered by that and is not answered here.
- **The Quiet Hands cell — UNCHANGED, and nothing in this batch touched it.** They are at least two and probably three; the boundary does not know, does not invent, and does not catch them, and **nothing in this batch recruited anybody, nothing turned their reason into a riddle or a voice, and their argument was not restated, rebutted or agreed with.** The one new fact beside them is a sentence of a woman with a rule about why three people have never measured the fill at the waist, and it is a different argument, and the clerk entered it beside theirs. **The low end of the corridor has a plan with no row for it, a review page blank for twenty-seven weeks, a grate that is off, and a length of the crew's own spent line over the hole, and nobody has stood there since a man of twenty-two was found.**
- **OT-15 — Mero Senn — FURTHER SPENT, and still not a rescue, a saint or a rebuke.** **He was asked in a room whether a plan with a number in it was acceptable and did not answer it with a feeling, and said so in advance, and gave the same answer three times in four days and once in front of two strangers.** He refused to sign a number and said he would sign a condition. **He said the half of the refusal of a row that is against the people who want the row, and said the refusal is the reason nobody was watching that hole, and refused to be argued out of either half.** He said that a condition that has never been lifted is a sentence, and that this boundary had a page of sentences for twenty-seven weeks and shut a room with eleven people in it while every sentence on it was true. He said that a page with four columns and no signature moved about forty people through a building in fifty minutes and that he cannot tell you whether that is the best thing this Hearthhold has done or the reason one of them is not here in a year. **He was wrong in public about the anteroom and was not consoled, and he is in the building, and he has not been asked a fourth question and does not want one until somebody asks him a different one.**
- **The anteroom frame — unchanged, and its rating is broken on one of its five conditions.** **A finger and a bit out of true, shored, packed in stone and clay, the mark off the wall, and the second way out is a word.** Its terms were read out against the original in a room on the fourth day of the twenty-seventh week, and **the fifth condition — the air engineer or the elected keeper able to stop it — has not been true since the middle of last month, because the keeper is four days up a road, and a clerk entered that she knew on the day it stopped being true and did not write it down.** The anteroom went over its number on that Thursday and the word could not be said by anybody in it.
- **New, and not planned: the boundary's own instruments now disagree with each other in public, and it entered the disagreement rather than resolving it.** **A plan with no signature moved forty people and has no name against any of the twelve rows. A page with a refused row explains why a man of twenty-two died. A word is a second way out of a room that is full. A condition on a room was lifted on a child's foot and is now a harder condition than the one it replaced. Five people refused to sign anything and one person put her hand under a man's on a single row with her objection written above it. Every one of those is correct and they do not add up to a system, and the batch does not pretend they do.**
- **The Ninefold Charter — NAMED BY THE OUTLINE, ABSENT FROM EVERY CHAPTER, AND NOW SEPARATED FROM THIS BOUNDARY'S OWN CHARTER.** `outline/volume-03.md` commits Chapters 148 and 149 to **the Ninefold Charter losing exclusive access to the market route.** The name has not appeared in a delivered chapter, and no state file said what it was, so a later writer would have had to guess whether it and the boundary's own charter — seven signatures, an office's number, eight clauses, clause four against the Cartwright office — were one instrument. **They are two.** The Ninefold Charter is the guild cartel of `bible/terminology.md`, inside the Cartwright Guilds, which controls recognized clearance seals and route insurance; the boundary's own charter is a local instrument that puts **no holder against any route at all**, and therefore cannot be the thing that loses exclusivity. **The market form and the board at the gate have never been attributed to any body; naming the guild side of that road in Chapter 149 is available and is not a change of plot, and the chapter resolves either way.** This is not a new final enemy: Cassian Rook and the One-Seat protocol remain the destination.
- **A viewpoint-presence check is now a tracked quality, because it was not one.** This batch's writing session reviewed itself for paragraphs, openers, markup, staging and length and asserted in a state file that the protagonist was in all ten chapters; **a review run outside that session found him named in seven.** The check costs one command and is now part of the craft baseline, and the rule it enforces is that a batch contracted to one viewpoint must show that viewpoint in every chapter of the batch and must not certify otherwise without measuring it.
- **New, and not planned: a refusal of consent has been given a duration that is not a date.** **A condition on a room lasts as long as the person who is able to say no is able to say it.** That is the answer this batch produced to the question the volume's escalation has been carrying, and it is not a number and it is not on a page anybody can carry, and a schoolteacher said in the same week that a building like this one is not a thing people live in.

# Volume 03 Batch 0005 — what the batch did to these threads

**This is delivery, not planning.** Chapters 141–150, the twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth weeks, and the batch that closes the volume.

- **OT-83 — the keeper of the page — STANDING, and turned over.** Bel Ordry said in Chapter 148 **the thing he said in the twenty-sixth week, the other way round**: he would rather a federation want to look at this boundary than be able to take it, and the answer to that is that a page can be read to a room and not taken out of it, **and that this is in the third sentence of a procedure written by a woman from another office, which he had been reading for a fortnight as a thing about her office and is a thing about his.** He refused a number on the common landing because the stair is not in the charter, the plan or the second sheet and he will not get a number onto it by putting a box round it. He asked for a correction to a title in a field book and was refused one and entered the refusal in his own hand. **He still says a plan in a coat is not a system and that he is the only one who has to say it, and the thread is not closed, and the man is still a man.**
- **OT-84 — the four households at the second gate — UNCHANGED, and named once with no figure.** Their water-lock is still shut for a survey of a sill, a bed and a wedge of hardwood that nobody has said how long will take. **The second gate's distance is stated nowhere in this batch and no figure is attached to it in any state file this batch wrote.** The debt is neither fixed nor abandoned and the volume does not pretend otherwise.
- **OT-87 — a notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time — STANDING, and neither repeated nor corrected.** The four pages, the six pages, the reply sheet and the market form all arrived with no date on them, and the market form's withdrawal at a counter happened because of what a mark is and not because of when anything was sent. **A sheet comes back on a board in a month by a clerk who does not know about Tuesday, and a courier wrote *a week is not a month* twice in a clerk's book so that the second one is the one a person reads.**
- **OT-88 — the air valve, the spring, the theory, and the name from the twelfth week — THE VALVE ADVANCED, THE THEORY APPROACHED AGAIN AND NOT MET.** The air gate was turned for the first time in twenty-nine weeks, on her own authority, in front of eleven people, and she said out loud before anybody could say it after her that she was not doing it for a man. **The mouth in the school corner, which she has refused to certify for twenty-nine weeks, was opened as a vent for two hours and is still not certified, and she said out loud in a room that nobody is to write down after this that the mouth is fine.** The theory was not said. She said in Chapter 150 that she has half of the volume's question and gave the same three sentences and did not give it, that half of what she knows is about a room and what was asked is about a road, **and that her condition is not met and that anybody who thinks a good month is going to meet it should look at what this boundary did in a bad one, which was write a page, refuse three rows, and let a woman strike a line out of it in nine seconds without giving a reason.** The name from the twelfth week is still not asked and no room may ask. **The valve's answer is still owed in the spring, in a room, with her in it, and Volume 03 has closed without it.**
- **OT-90 — every document in this Hearthhold has a place to put everything except a person — ADVANCED, and the volume's answer is delivered.** The first column is a permission and has never held a count of anybody, and it now has sixteen rows. **A plan became public and stayed unnamed, a person who may stop it was named in a room and not on a page, a physician put his name against a refusal in a clerk's book, and a title in a field book was left wrong on purpose.** That is a development of the thread and not an answer to it, **and nobody in a room joined the first column to the dowel's provenance, the charter, the mouth, the four treads, the air engineer's theory or the plate.**
- **OT-91 — discharged in full and not reopened. The consequence delivered a third time.** The crew's column moved by four on a named asking in a room with the terms out loud and Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **and the three who could not be asked were named with the reason for each before the asking, and the reasons are not the reasons of Batch 0004**: Leena Orr, because she is the person who will have to answer whether a person can stand at the low end; Pell Roke, because he is fourteen and because a count taken by the man who reads numbers is a count nobody can argue with; Tams Quill, because if he also walks the network then the same man is the hands, the witness and the record. **The crew have now been asked three times in twenty-nine weeks. A man's two and a half days at the low end were entered in the boundary's column and not the crew's, and the clerk gave the reason out loud, and a spent line is not an hour and never was.**
- **OT-92 — the stair inside one named work, and the eighth term not in agreement — STANDING, price not withdrawn.** The stair is not in any work in Volume 03 Batch 0005 and is not in the charter and is not in the plan. **The common landing carries no number in the first column, and the reason it does not is that the stair is not in any of the three documents this boundary keeps, and Bel Ordry said so in a room rather than let a box put it on one.**
- **OT-93 — the ninth line and the four treads — STANDING, both refusals intact, no mark cut in the stone.** Nobody went down the four treads. **No mark was cut in the stone anywhere in this building, and the four marks and the groove on the lintel above the open school corner's mouth are named once in the volume's last chapter as four damaged marks and one undamaged groove, read two ways, answering nothing, with one of the four being two strokes.**
- **OT-94 — the school — ANSWERED IN ITS MOST ORDINARY FORM, and the lost days are still lost.** The school ran on the third, fifth and twenty-second days of this batch's two weeks — four mornings, the nineteenth to the twenty-second — **in the room at the kitchen-line end, over a propped stone, with a girl of nine sitting down, and the fire in that room not lit for nine weeks.** **A condition on that room was found by the woman who wrote it to have a hole in it — a room used three days in seven has its condition checked three mornings in seven — and the answer was four sentences a week in an empty room, and the schoolteacher agreed to it and put the cost in the book as a preference and not as a noble position.** No school day was restored and no closure was removed: **the corridor was opened on two days the arrangement shuts it, by a woman's own written term, and the school does not run on those two days and lost nothing.** The two lost open days of Chapters 108 and 130 are still lost and were not paid back. **The school corner is open and is not used and no chapter of this batch put the school back in it.**
- **OT-95 — the wash-room condition — STANDING, unsoftened, and the protection is now seven.** A room was struck out of a clerk's list of rooms in nine seconds in Chapter 142 and a room was struck out of a printed schedule in nine seconds in Chapter 149. **No reason was given on either occasion and she was not asked on either occasion, and the space where a reason would go is empty on both.** The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, nobody was sent, and the page is still blank at the end of the volume.
- **OT-96 — the one thing he cannot do twice — SPENT, PROPERLY, AND NOT SPENT AGAIN.** The Reader reading was not used and the Chapter 99 claim's condition is still unmet. **The Marker was not used and the mark is off the wall and a carpenter said in a room that he would not put it back.** What the volume spent instead was ordinary civil engineering: a lamp, a left hand, a channel with silt in it, and two flags and a length of the crew's own spent line over a hole. **And the cost of it is permanent: his left hand did not close after the holding, there is a mark on the inside of his forearm, his knee does not bend past about half, and he said in a room that he cannot go down there again and does not know why and is not going to find out.**
- **The charter's hole — ONE INSTITUTION DEEPER AND NOT FIXED, and it is now being used against the boundary.** Clause four names the Cartwright office and four bodies have now come to this boundary that the four sentences do not name. **The boundary has decided to use one of them: the plan was read out in a room to a person from another office with no copy given, under that office's own first and third clauses, and the boundary said out loud that it is doing this on purpose and that it knows the price.** A federation's route inspector said out loud, against her own office, that the instrument which made this boundary arguable is hers and that she knew the price when she wrote it. **Six pages of a regime have gone up the passage with a clause in them that says a room whose condition is not being checked may be entered and the person who keeps it cannot refuse, and the sixth clause is correct and the boundary said so.** The hole is not fixed and it is not fixable by this volume, and Volume 04 inherits it in a worse shape than Volume 02 left it.
- **The market route as the volume's toll gate — ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS A DOCUMENT THAT DEFEATED ITSELF.** A boundary that will not fill in two lines on somebody else's form has its own people unable to leave, and a bundle has been in an anteroom since the fourth day of the twenty-fifth week because of it. **Then a courier's rule passed its own test — thirty-one people went up a market road as ordinary residents with nobody at the front of it — and a form came off a board at a counter because a mark cannot be entered in an insurance register, and the Ninefold Charter is named for the first time in this book and it is a guild cartel and not this boundary's charter.** Nobody was defeated, the board is still standing, the seal is still on the road, and **a competent person at the same counter expects the sheet to be back in a month.** The volume's question about a route being a public good across jurisdictions is asked out loud twice, in Chapter 140 and again in Chapter 150 in the shape the withdrawal created, and is not answered either time.
- **The Quiet Hands cell — NOT TOUCHED.** At least two and probably three, uncaught, unrecruited, and nothing in this batch turned their reason into a riddle or a voice. **The only new fact beside them is that the grate at the low end of that corridor is still off and there is still no second one, and a man went into the channel under where it was and came out of it, and a clerk entered that nobody sent him and that the difference between that and the man of twenty-two was the smallest thing in her book.** Rung three on the antagonist ladder and not a new final enemy: the One-Seat protocol and Cassian Rook remain the destination per `outline/ending.md`, and Volume 03 does not name the One-Seat.
- **The anteroom frame — spent, and back where it was, and its second way out has been named for what it is.** The frame is a finger and a bit out of true, shored, packed in stone and clay, holding and not fixed, **and the mark is off the wall and has been since the twenty-third week and a carpenter said in a room that he would not put it back.** Its second way out is a word. **In Chapter 147 a man said that word in that anteroom, and the clerk repeated it, and it opened nothing, and he opened the door, and the woman who keeps the room's terms then said out loud, against her own practice, that a word is not a way out and a person is — and did not take the word out of the terms of a room, because nine people in this building have been told that saying it made them safe.** The fifth of the five terms has been broken since the middle of the twenty-sixth week and the room was worked over its number for two hours on two mornings, and the clerk entered it every time.
- **New in this batch, and not planned: the boundary has a public instrument, and the first thing anybody outside it did with it was use it against the boundary's own comfort.** A Compact procedure that said a page could be shown in a room and not taken out of it has become the way this boundary's own plan is made public. **That is a document doing the opposite of what it was written for, and the woman who wrote it said so in the room, and Volume 04 inherits a federation that has learned to use its own procedures and a boundary that has decided to be used rather than hidden.**
- **New in this batch, and not planned: a room was made unusable on any day of the week by a condition on a different room.** A network of four rooms and a door exists and can only be used on a day when nobody is watching the one place in this building that has killed a person, **and the fix for that was a man in a channel for two and a half days, and the fix was stopped by a person who was not asked to stop it and did not stop it for the limit.** The vocabulary a later volume needs — a word for a second way out that is not a way out, and a page that says somebody stands somewhere and has been blank for twenty-nine weeks — is on the page and is not resolved.

## Volume 03 closed, and what is owed next

**Volume 03 is delivered in full at Chapter 150. `outline/volume-04.md` does not exist and is owed to the outline phase, and `workspace/volume-03/CLOSE.md` is the single next phase. There is no Volume 03 Batch 0006, because Volume 03 is fifty chapters and it closes.**

### Carried into Volume 04 as open engineering and record questions, three of them raised by Batch 0005's review phase

- **The brass survey rule's silence has no agreed starting week.** It has "said nothing" for ten weeks in Chapter 100, twelve in Chapter 110, fifteen in Chapter 140 and sixteen in Chapter 150, which puts its origin at the ninth, twelfth and thirteenth weeks. **The drift is inherited from Chapter 140, a closed and reviewed batch, so it was left uncorrected rather than half-corrected, and the wrapped plate on the same shelf is the consistent register to measure it against: twenty-seven weeks in Chapter 140, twenty-nine in Chapter 150.** The outline phase should fix the origin and say which figure it is fixing.
- **Chapter 149's closing recap reports a Thursday-afternoon asking at the low end of the corridor that no chapter contains.** The person in it is correctly a woman; the event is not in the prose. **Owed a repair that re-anchors the sentence to the exchange that does happen in that room on that day**, and it is owed before the line is quoted anywhere downstream.
- **Five review files are still owed to the reviewer's phase and are not the outline phase's to write:** `reviews/volume-02/batch-0003.md`, `batch-0004.md` and `batch-0005.md`, and independent reviews of Volume 03 Batch 0003 and Batch 0004. **Batch 0005's independent review has been run and closed; that does not reduce the count, because it was never one of the five.**

# Volume 04 Batch 0001 — what the batch did to these threads

**This is delivery, not planning.** Chapters 151–160, the thirtieth and thirty-first weeks, and the first batch of the first volume after Volume 03 closed.

- **OT-83 — the keeper of a page — STANDING, and turned again.** Bel Ordry put his hand flat on the date in the top corner of his own plan in Chapter 160 and said, in answer to a four-word question from a man with a store, that he does not own the page and nobody in this building owns it, and that the page does not own a wall either. **He still says a page in a coat is not a system and that he is the only person who has to say it, for the thirty-first week running, and he said in this batch that he is not going to stop now that a man has come four days to ask him a question he cannot answer.** **And he said the half of the answer that was against his own answer, which is the thread's real content: a thing nobody owns is a thing that gets maintained by whoever happens to be standing near it, and that is not the same as keeping it, and the difference has cost this building a wall in lime for a fortnight, a pair of wedges out of a school door and a woman who is going to have to watch a door.** He also refused to name a guild's fourth paragraph in a room on a Friday morning to persuade a man with eleven years of beech to part with it, and set a price and a day. The thread is not closed. The man is still a man.
- **OT-84 — the four households at a second gate — UNCHANGED, and the pot moved instead.** Their water-lock is still shut for a survey of a sill, a bed and a wedge of hardwood that nobody has said how long will take, **and no figure is attached to that gate in this batch and no chapter of this batch went near it.** **What moved is the boundary's own side of the ledger: the pot went from ten days to nine on the fourth day of the thirty-first week, and a seam that gave eight threads in the nineteenth week gives four and has not been measured in between, and a cook said out loud in a room that a dead man's share has been going back into that pot since the fourth day of the twenty-fifth week on purpose and is not going to be done for a brace.** The debt is neither fixed nor abandoned and this batch made it cheaper to look at and no less sharp.
- **OT-87 — a notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time — STANDING, and it arrived as a fact rather than a discovery.** **Nothing in this batch is dated at all: not the market form, not the carrier's paper, not the Compact schedule, not the store's list, not the guild's post.** **The form is back on a board four days up the middle passage with a seal number on it that is not the number it had before, and nobody put it up, and it came back by a schedule.** The standing discovery was not restated and not corrected. A road hand brought the fact down and **refused, twice in this batch, to look at a cart for anybody**, and a carrier established the shape of his own patience in a clerk's book before he handed a paper over. **The batch's new instance of the standing rule is that a sheet comes back on a board by somebody else's calendar, and that is the same rule wearing a different hat.**
- **OT-88 — the air valve, the spring, the theory, and the name from the twelfth week — ALL FOUR STANDING, and the condition was approached hard and is still not met.** **The sixth of the volume's acts of trust is spent and it is the inverse of the third: the air engineer asked the engineer for a work, in the crew's own practice, in a room, with the terms out loud, with the three she is not going to ask named with the reason for each before she asks him anything.** The work is to go and look at the air at the low end of the corridor, from above, not from inside it. **She said the cost out loud before anybody could say it after her: the asking puts a standing on him, and a standing is the first half of a post, and she asked for the word *standing* in the clerk's book and not the word *help*.** She is asked for a piece of work and not consulted for a decision. **Her condition is not met and she says so in a room, and she says that keeping itself and being asked to open a road while something is going wrong four days up a passage are not the same sentence, and she has set a second condition — that she will not take it back while it is being watched — and said it out loud twice so that the second is a fact and not a sentence, and she told a room not to ask her what it is about. Nobody asked.** The valve's answer is still owed in the spring, in a room, with her in it, and the spring is now nearer than it was. The theory was not said. The name from the twelfth week is still not asked and no room may ask.
- **OT-90 — every document in this Hearthhold has a place to put everything except a person — ADVANCED, and the batch's answer is a person keeping a room that is not in this building.** **A store's list of fourteen lines was read out twice and compared, and it carries no date on it, and the reason is a schoolteacher's shape of a count: a list with a date on it is a moment pretending to be a day.** **The list and what came down the passage agreed, line by line, and that is the first time in thirty-one weeks that a document in this building and a fact in a room have been the same thing.** A board gained its **first entry that is not in this building**, in the column with nothing over the top of it, on a courier's rule that was written about a road and turned out to be true about a board. **And two people refused in the same batch to put a fact and a fact next to each other — a man refused twice to say which two walls he would let a brace push on, and a clerk refused three times in a month to join two questions — and the chapter said out loud that those are the same argument from opposite ends.** That is a development of the thread and **not an answer to it**, and the thread's actual answer is still owed and is the volume's own: who owns a wall, asked in four words in Chapter 160 and not answered.
- **OT-91 — discharged in full and not reopened. The consequence delivered a fourth time.** The crew's column moved by three on a named asking in a room with the terms out loud and Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, **and the three who could not be asked were named with the reason for each before the asking, and the reasons are a third set**: Leena Orr, because she is the person who will have to be asked whether the schoolroom's wall can take a push; Pell Roke, because he reads numbers and a measurement a person has read aloud and nobody has written down is a figure in the column with nothing over the top of it; Tams Quill, because if he is also the hands then the man who records what a thing turned out to be is the man who found out. Two hours of a carpenter's and one of an engineer's, **and the carpenter named the split himself before he was asked and gave the reason, which is that a carpenter looking at a pile of beech is a different thing from an engineer looking at a pile of beech.** **The crew have now been asked four times in thirty-one weeks and the reasons have not been the same reasons twice.**
- **OT-92 — the stair inside one named work, and the eighth term not in agreement — STANDING, price not withdrawn.** The stair is not in any work in Volume 04 Batch 0001 and is not in the charter. **The common landing carries no number on any page in this building, the landing is named once in the batch's closing image, and the stair is not in the charter, or the plan, or the second sheet, and no chapter of this batch put a number on it by putting a box round it.** Nobody put a foot on it.
- **OT-93 — the ninth line and the four treads — STANDING, both refusals intact, no mark cut in the stone.** Nobody went down the four treads. **No mark was cut in the stone anywhere in this building, and the four marks and the groove on the lintel above the open school corner's mouth are read three ways by three people in this batch, one of the four being two strokes, the four damaged and the groove undamaged, and the one professional claim made about that stone — that the only undamaged mark on a wall is the one that was cut to be read — is made by a carpenter who says a mason's opinion is worth nothing and gives it anyway.** **The mark is the brace's bearing mark and it has not said anybody its limit, and the batch is explicit that the limit cannot come out of it.** Nobody was sent near the low end and nobody was asked.
- **OT-94 — the school — RUN ON ALL FOUR OPEN DAYS IN THIS BATCH, and the losses are still lost and two new costs have landed on it.** **The school ran in the room at the kitchen-line end on the third and fifth days of the thirtieth week and the third and fifth days of the thirty-first — four mornings, the twenty-third to the twenty-sixth.** The school corner stayed open and unused throughout and no chapter of this batch put the school back in it. **The fire in the corner of that room has now not been lit for ten weeks, and the cook asked to be asked about it for the sixth time this month and refused a sixth time in one sentence, and asked for the children to be cold in the record in the same place as the refusal.** **The joinwood for a brace was taken out of that school — two wedges at the school-door head and two beech lengths out of the school store — and the school door now has no wedge in it, and the woman who gave them said in a room that a door with no wedge is a door that has to be watched, and that the answer is a person, and that there is not a person available, and that the page where a person would go is blank with three conditions on it.** **And the reaction of that brace is to go on the wall the schoolroom leans on, and the woman who keeps that room wrote a condition about the brace and not about her room, and it is not met.** The two open days lost in Chapter 108 and Chapter 130 of Volume 03 are still lost. Ilsa Norr has still not been told which of the facts is independent.
- **OT-95 — the wash-room condition — STANDING, unsoftened, and the protection is now eight.** **A printed Compact schedule with a column headed for the person who will be present and three rooms under it was struck through in nine seconds from three steps up, before anybody had asked, and the reason was not given, and nobody asked.** The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, nobody was sent, **and the clerk entered that there is no reason in the space where a reason would go, and entered for the eighth time that a page with a reason on it is a page somebody can read back to her.** The page at the low end is blank and has been for thirty-one weeks.
- **OT-96 — the one thing he cannot do twice — SPENT, PROPERLY, AND NOT SPENT AGAIN.** **No power stage advanced in this batch and the correct amount of System in it is no panel of any kind.** The Reader reading was not used and the Chapter 99 claim's condition is unmet. **The Marker was not used, the mark is off the wall, and a carpenter said again in this batch that he would not put one back and gave the mason's reason why the only mark in this building is a damaged one in a lintel.** What the volume spent instead was ordinary carpentry and stonework: a chalk line and a piece of string, two wedges, two beech lengths, a trestle, a survey's four sentences and a woman's folding rule. **And what he said in a room, unasked, is that the limit on a brace will not be a figure of his in a room, because the mark is damaged and he cannot read it, and that the limit will be a condition written by the person the brace can hurt.** The right hand's fine control is not recovered, the left hand has not closed since the holding, and a carpenter cut eleven pieces of beech with it this week.
- **The charter's hole — ONE DOCUMENT WIDER AGAIN, AND A NEW KIND OF DOCUMENT, AND NOT FIXED.** Clause four names the Cartwright office. **In this batch a fifth body sent a document that the four sentences do not name, and it was not a procedure and not a reply sheet: it was a printed schedule, a calendar, with a column headed for the person who will be present and three rooms under it.** **A carrier established the shape of his own patience in a clerk's book before handing over a sixth document, which was a route-holder's post in a stiff cover with a proper seal on it and a name in the second line.** The boundary struck the schedule's heading and its three rooms out in nine seconds and gave no reason, and **did not answer the post at all, and did not refuse it.** **The boundary's own decision on both is recorded in a room: it has four instruments and one procedure, it has used that procedure for a body it does not name, and it will not write a second one, and a man who is offered a post with his name in it inside this Hearthhold is not going to be given the twenty minutes he would need to refuse it properly this month.** **The hole is not fixed and Volume 04 inherits it in a worse shape than Volume 03 left it, and the new shape is worse because the two new documents are the two that do not need anybody to agree to them.**
- **The market route as the volume's toll gate — ADVANCED, AND THE TOLL WENT THE OTHER WAY.** **The form is back on the board with a different seal number and nobody put it up, and the road is unchanged, and the board is still standing, and the seal is still on the road.** **A guild's own load's paper is now in this anteroom with seven lines and two of them for a person, and the boundary refused those two in a room and five of the seven were argued out loud before anything was marked.** **The volume's question about a route being a public good across jurisdictions is not answered, and the batch's new fact beside it is that a courier said in a room in the twenty-ninth week that a route is not free either — a thing given by a person and not carried by a person is a favour with a keeper, and a keeper who is owed a favour has less room to say no the second time.**
- **The Quiet Hands cell — NOT TOUCHED.** At least two and probably three, uncaught, unrecruited, and **nothing in this batch recruited anybody, turned their reason into a riddle or a voice, or restated it.** The only new fact beside them is that **a document with a column headed for the person who will be present exists and is a fact this boundary has to work with, and a third room on it was left standing and a carrier explained in a room what a schedule is for**, and nobody in this building joined that to a cell's argument about a line with a space in it. **The grate at the low end of the corridor is still off, there is still no second grate, two flags and a length of the crew's own spent line are still over the channel, and the page that says somebody stands there is still blank.**
- **OT-15 — Mero Senn — FURTHER SPENT, and he is the instrument again and not a rescue.** He asked for a mark on a wall and **asked for the clerk to read it and not himself**, and gave the reason for the first: a filled ground bears differently than a drained one, and a wall that has had water standing against the bottom of it has been standing in its own wet, and when the wet goes it finds out what it weighs, and it finds that out by moving, in the direction it was already leaning. **He named the person in the brace and refused to name a child, because a child would be the easy way to stop the work and would be a lie with a name in it.** He was asked for the number and gave it — four tons, or thereabouts — **and made the clerk write the words *or thereabouts* next to the four tons, and said the number is not an argument, it is an instrument he has to carry into a room every morning and read out loud.** He did not fix anything and softened nobody and is not a saint and is not a rebuke, and he is right.
- **The anteroom frame — unchanged, and now it is the thing a brace goes across.** **It is a finger and three-quarters out of true, packed in stone and clay, holding and not fixed, with the mark off the wall and a carpenter in the room who would not put it back, and it was measured once in this batch by a woman with a folding rule who said she had not measured it for thirty-one weeks and was not going to be asked.** Its rating still depends on a word said to a room and repeated by the clerk. **Its fifth term, the air engineer or the elected keeper able to stop it, has been broken since the middle of the twenty-sixth week, and the elected keeper is on a road, and the anteroom's second way out is a word that a woman on a landing has said in a room is not a way out and has not taken out of a room's terms.**
- **New in this batch, and not planned: the volume's civic discovery is about a pile of timber.** **A store is a room, and a room has a keeper, and a keeper can be asked in a room with the terms out loud, and a keeper can say no, and a man who has kept a store for eleven years and has never once been asked came four days down a passage with nothing in his hands in order to be asked.** **That is the same working practice this boundary has been running on five people for thirty weeks, pointed at material instead of at people, and it is the volume's argument and it is also the ending's argument, one volume early, about a heap of beech.**
- **New in this batch, and not planned: a refusal made in a room is a cost, and the cost has a name and a shape.** A man said the price of a refusal is a sill and a wall in lime that is not being built, and a woman said the price of a gift is a favour with a keeper, and a cook said the price of a dead man's ration is a pot that is at nine days, and **a carpenter was given a post with a boy's roll number on it and said the two people it will find are the woman on the landing and the boy on the bench, and a person in a bad month is going to hold the wage and not look at the hand.** **None of the four is a speech. All four are in a clerk's book in the speaker's own words.**
- **New in this batch, and not planned: the first figure anybody in this building has taken at the waist on purpose in thirty-one weeks was given by a woman nobody asked, and the three reasons for never taking one are not withdrawn, and the figure is here anyway.** **Two inches and a bit, in a clerk's book and not on a page, because the plan has no row for that wall and the refusal of a row for the low end of the corridor stands.** The clerk entered the number, the three old reasons, and the fact that the plan has no row there, as **three findings and not one conclusion.**
- **New in this batch, and not planned: the volume's question is four words long and it is about material, not about roads.** **Who owns a wall. Asked out loud in a room by a man who keeps a store, and answered by nobody, and the four people who tried are on the page: a man who keeps a page, a courier, an air engineer who does not have half of it and says so, and a man who knows the answer for two of the four walls in this building and refused twice to say it out loud because saying it in a room is making a claim.** The volume's next-volume question, *can a route be a public good when the people who use it live on different sides of the law*, was asked twice in Volume 03 and is not answered here, and **the clerk has now refused three times in a month to put the two questions next to each other on purpose, and the third refusal is entered in one sentence with both questions and with her reason, which is that a clerk who joins them early makes the finding hers and not theirs.**

# Volume 04 Batch 0002 — what the batch did to these threads

**This is delivery, not planning.** Chapters 161–170, the thirty-second and thirty-third weeks, and the batch that carries the Bracer stage.

- **OT-83 — the keeper of a page — STANDING, and turned twice more.** **Bel Ordry raised in a room that a word can change what it is about**, which is the thread's real content in a new shape: the anteroom's rating is restored when the word *door* is said and the clerk repeats it, a brace is going across the head of the door the word is about, and in six weeks a room that says the word is going to hear the brace in it and not only the door. **He asked for it as an objection and not as a discovery, because he knows which of the two the clerk is writing, and the room did not answer it, and the word was said twice anyway and the objection and the answer are in the same book.** He is also **the fourth of the four hands and what stops the thing he is holding is the word**, and the half against that is that a word is not a wall and that this morning he discovered the thing he has been protecting is the word and not the wood. He said his knee out loud for the first time in thirty-three weeks and asked for it to be entered separately from the morning it happened on, because this morning is a different fact. He still says a page in a coat is not a system and that he is the only person who has to say it, for the thirty-third week running. **And he is now suspicious of the man with the store, out loud, on a reason, arranged by a clerk, and he said the arrangement was dirty and that he would have said it with the man standing in the room.** The thread is not closed. The man is still a man.
- **OT-84 — the four households at a second gate — UNCHANGED, and the pot moved instead.** Their water-lock is still shut for a survey of a sill, a bed and a wedge of hardwood that nobody has said how long will take, **and no figure is attached to that gate in this batch and no chapter of this batch went near it.** What moved is this boundary's own side of the ledger: **the pot is at nine days and is being held up by a seam, and a cook said out loud in a room that five people working for two days on a thing nobody asked them to be paid for in a pot means a pot at nine is going to be eight, and that she is not going to say a brace is being paid for in that seam, and the clerk entered the two next to each other with nothing between them and did not write the word beside either.** The debt is neither fixed nor abandoned and this batch made it cheaper to look at and no less sharp.
- **OT-87 — a notice with no date on it cannot be answered in time — STANDING, and this batch's instance is a term with no day on it.** **Nothing in this batch is dated at all: not the record of the brace, not the terms, not the failure point, not the store's list, and the two lines left blank on a sheet of a clerk's own carry no date.** The standing discovery was not restated and not corrected. **What the batch adds is the other half of the same rule on this boundary's own paper: four terms were written on the second day of the thirtieth week to govern a work, and a week later the same boundary had to decide in a room what to do with a term it wrote itself and cannot now keep, and the answer was that the terms bound a work and not a building, and that a building outlasts the terms of a work.** A notice with no date cannot be answered in time, and a term with no day on it cannot be kept, and both facts are on the page in the same week.
- **OT-88 — the air valve, the spring, the theory, and the name from the twelfth week — ALL FOUR STANDING, and the condition was not approached.** **Nera Oduya asked for a second work in this batch, in the practice, with the terms out loud, and with the three she is not going to ask named with the reason for each — which is the second time she has run a practice she spent thirty weeks taking off other people and never once offering.** She asked whether the brace changes the air and what the limit is. **She was wrong in public, before anybody could be kind to her about it, and said so herself, and was not consoled, and the clerk entered that she would have consoled her last week and noticed herself nearly doing it this week and stopped.** She set a limit with no number and no day on it and said she is not going to be one of the two women who wrote the condition on the brace, and said the hard part out loud: she has been the only person who may turn that wheel for thirty-three weeks, she has never once been asked, she is not going to be grateful about it afterwards, and being right about the air and being the only one who is right is what an authority is and there is no part of it anybody here should find comfortable. **Her condition is not met and her second condition stands and nobody asked her in a room.** The valve's answer is still owed in the spring, in a room, with her in it. The theory was not said. The name from the twelfth week is still not asked and no room may ask.
- **OT-90 — every document in this Hearthhold has a place to put everything except a person — ADVANCED, and the batch's answer is a term with no day on it and a phrase with no mark on it.** **Six terms were written in a room, read out three times, compared against an original by a second person, and the sixth of them was added on a landing by a woman who keeps a corridor and who is not the clerk.** **A failure point was named *the place where it comes out* and it is a phrase and not a term and it is in a book and not on a stone, and a clerk entered the reason: a phrase can be said out loud in a room by anybody and a term can only be read by the person who wrote it.** **And the batch's sharpest instance: four terms this boundary wrote for itself, read three times against the original and found the same, could not be struck out because a strike is a lie and could not be left because a term kept in the letter and broken in the fact and left on the page is a term an office four days up a road can pick up and read as this boundary's practice, and the answer was that they bound a work and not a building.** That is the thread's answer in a document and it is not an answer to who owns a wall.
- **OT-91 — discharged in full and not reopened. The consequence delivered a fifth time, and the price of not forcing anybody was paid.** **The crew's column moved by four and a half on a named asking in a room with the terms out loud and Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no, and the three who could not be asked were named with a fourth set of reasons, and two of the three are not the names used in the fourth asking: Leena Orr, because she reads things that are already built; Jo Verrick, because the day the brace goes in is the day the wall she reads has a push coming out of it; and Pell Roke, because the work is holding and the clerk is not going to ask him to watch instead.** **Two hours of a carpenter's, two of an engineer's and half an hour of the man who reads the board, and he asked for the split to be named before anybody named it.** **The crew have now been asked five times in thirty-three weeks and the reasons have not been the same reasons twice.**
- **OT-92 — the stair inside one named work, and the eighth term not in agreement — STANDING, price not withdrawn.** The stair is not in any work in Volume 04 Batch 0002 and is not in the charter. **Nobody went near the four treads, the common landing carries no number on any page in this building, and a person is still under a lip, packed and not held, with two timber shores above it and a post that has never been built.** The eighth term stands. Nobody put a foot on it.
- **OT-93 — the ninth line and the four treads — STANDING, both refusals intact, no mark cut in the stone, and this batch is the batch that made that matter.** **The brace is joined to its mark by cutting the wood to the stone and not the stone to the wood, and a carpenter said he would take a tool out of anybody's hand who went up to that lintel with one, and the clerk entered that no mark has been cut in the stone at the ninth room or at the school corner's mouth or anywhere else in this building, four times, and put that fact beside the ninth striking-out of a schedule on purpose and would not say why.** **The four marks and the groove answer nothing, three people read them three ways, and the brace's limit did not come out of them: the limit is a condition, and a shim with a two-year life, and a term in a clerk's book.**
- **OT-94 — the school — RUN ON ALL FOUR OPEN DAYS IN THIS BATCH, and the losses are still lost and the new costs have landed.** The school ran in the room at the kitchen-line end on the third and fifth days of the thirty-second week and the third and fifth days of the thirty-third — four mornings, the twenty-seventh to the thirtieth. The school corner stayed open and unused throughout and no chapter of this batch put the school back in it. **The fire in the corner of that room has now not been lit for eleven weeks, and the cook asked to be asked about it a seventh, an eighth and a ninth time in this batch and refused each time, and asked for the children to be cold in the record in the same place as the refusal each time.** **Nine children were taught for the twenty-ninth morning with a brace of their own school's beech going into the wall they lean on, and they came out the ordinary way, and the last one of them stopped in a doorway and looked up at it and went on down the nine steps.** **And a bed under the ninth hearth stone is a third of an inch higher than it was on Friday morning, a fifth sound wedge went under it, and a beech shim a finger wide in a nine-hundred-year-old hollow carries four tons a foot and a half above it.** The two open days lost in Chapter 108 and Chapter 130 of Volume 03 are still lost. Ilsa Norr has still not been told which of the facts is independent.
- **OT-95 — the wash-room condition — STANDING, unsoftened, and the protection is unchanged at eight.** **No legal instrument of any kind was produced in this batch.** Nothing was struck out. The floor was not approached, nobody went near it, nobody was sent, **and the page at the low end is blank and has been for thirty-two weeks, and this batch is the one in which the blank page was used twice without being filled: once as the reason a man who is willing is not a man who is standing there, and once as the reason a page cannot be used to put a person's hours on a door.**
- **OT-96 — the one thing he cannot do twice — SPENT, PROPERLY, AND NOT SPENT AGAIN.** **The Bracer stage is delivered and it is a stage and not a cure, and it cost four hands, a day, a condition, a named failure point, a day of delay, a bed under a hearth stone and a man's knee on a floor.** **No System panel of any kind appears in this batch and the correct amount of System in it is none.** The Reader reading was not used and the Chapter 99 claim's condition is unmet. **The Marker was not used, the mark is off the wall, and a carpenter said again in this batch that he would not put one back.** What the volume spent instead was ordinary carpentry and stonework: a splay cut by hand, a shim cut from the end of a length and not put in the heap, a spent line round a joint, two wedges, a chalk line and a string, and a folding rule. **The right hand's fine control is not recovered, the left hand does not close, and a carpenter cut a splay and a shim with it and said the wide face is carrying four tons and that this is arithmetic and not a compliment.**
- **The charter's hole — UNCHANGED, AND NOT WIDENED IN THIS BATCH.** No document arrived from any body the charter does not name. **The one instrument this batch produced is this boundary's own: six terms, read three times, compared, and entered, and a sheet of a clerk's own with three findings on it and a line at the bottom left empty on purpose.** **And the batch's civic finding is about that instrument and not about anybody else's: a term this boundary wrote for itself is a term an office four days up a road can pick up and read as this boundary's practice, and the difference between a term and a practice is that a term has a day on it and a practice does not, and this boundary has just discovered the price of writing one without.**
- **The market route as the volume's toll gate — UNCHANGED, and one new fact beside it.** The form is still on a board four days up the middle passage with a new seal number on it. **What is new is Talla Roke's sentence in Chapter 170, which is the closest anybody in this volume has come to the volume's question and is not an answer: the difference between this boundary and a guild notice is not the content, it is that this boundary can be asked in a room by a person who is standing in it.**
- **The Quiet Hands cell — NOT TOUCHED.** At least two and probably three, uncaught, unrecruited, and **nothing in this batch recruited anybody, turned their reason into a riddle or a voice, or restated it.** The grate at the low end is still off, there is still no second grate, two flags and a length of spent line are still over the channel, and the page that says somebody stands there is still blank, and this batch is the batch in which a man who reads the board gave the reason that page is blank — a person who is willing is not a person who is standing there — **and nobody joined that to a cell's argument about a line with a space in it.**
- **OT-15 — Mero Senn — FURTHER SPENT, and he is the instrument and not a rescue, and he is right three times in this batch.** **He asked for the brace's failure point to be named out loud before a person was stood under it, and gave it a name that is a phrase and not a term and refused to give a room a name for a thing he had not looked at.** He said a wall can stop for a week or stop for good and there is no instrument in this building that tells the two apart. **He would not put his own fingers in a gap in a floor to find out whether he had been right, because he has spent eleven days asking this room to read a wall and not themselves, and refused to name the man who built it, because nominating the builder to check the builder is not the same as asking him and he is frightened of his own hands.** He put his refusal to certify on the table because nobody asked him to and said the refusal has not changed and the reason for it has. He does not fix anything, softens nobody, is not a saint and is not a rebuke.
- **The anteroom frame — changed, and the change is a fact and not a story.** **It is a finger and two-thirds out of true, down from a finger and three-quarters by a twelfth of an inch, and that is the first better number anybody in this building has had off that frame in thirty-three weeks, taken in Chapter 168, and Chapter 170 took the same one twice four minutes apart and the clerk entered that a number which has only been the same twice four minutes apart is not a number anybody should put in a column, and Jo Verrick took it before she said anything about it and said what it does not mean louder than what it means.** **The twelfth of an inch is the same quantity as the shim's projected failure, so the shim coming out returns the frame to a finger and three-quarters and does not carry it past that, and the carpenter's two-year limit is a return and not a decay.** **Its rating still depends on a word said to a room and repeated by the clerk, and the word is now in question, and the count is ten including one litter and did not change, and its second way out is a word, and a carpenter said out loud in this batch that a person does not go out through a word, and nobody answered him.** **Its fifth term, the air engineer or the elected keeper able to stop it, is still broken since the middle of the twenty-sixth week, and the elected keeper is on a road, and nothing in this batch touched it.**
- **New in this batch, and not planned: a brace is a support and a support is a thing somebody is going to have to keep, and that is the volume's question on a wall, and it is now the eighteenth entry on a board.** It went in the column with nothing over the top of it, entered by the man who reads the board, and the reason he gave is that **the word over that column would be *keeper*, and there is no such word in this building, and there is not going to be one, and the four people who held it on Wednesday are not going to be standing here in ten years.** That is the batch's plainest statement of what the volume is about and it is a board entry and not a speech.
- **New in this batch, and not planned: nobody was sent to look, and the person who looked was the person the brace could hurt, and a man who kept a book of his own figures did not say them.** A woman went into her own room on a shut morning because that is what she does on shut mornings, and knelt at a hearth stone, and found a third of an inch, and said the three clauses of a condition she had written a fortnight ago, and four people took a piece of wood out of a wall in eleven minutes. **A physician would not touch the gap and refused to nominate the man who built it. A woman on a landing refused to ask the man who built it and asked the woman it could hurt. And the man with a figure in a private book stood in a room and did not say the figure, and the clerk entered that the two people talking about a wall were a physician and a schoolteacher, and that this is a change and not a loss, and he said nothing about it at all.**
- **New in this batch, and not planned: a shim is a joint with a date in it that nobody has.** A carpenter cut a piece of beech a finger wide and four inches long, set it where three people could see it, and said its long edges will crush in about two years, and when they crush the head settles and the frame goes a twelfth of an inch out of true again, which is the whole of what the brace won, and nobody standing in that anteroom is going to feel a twelfth of an inch for a long time. **And then he said the sentence that is the whole of the batch's cost: you take it out and put a new shim in, and you know it has to be done because you wrote a shim in the terms, and you do not know it has to be done because the frame moved, and the carpenter does not know, and the engineer who cut it first is dead or gone or sixty, and the person who knows is a term in a clerk's book, and a term in a clerk's book is a person who has not been born yet.**
