# Volume 04 Batch 0004 — what the batch did to these threads

**Delivery, Chapters 176–180, thirty-fourth (Thu–Sun) and thirty-fifth (Mon) weeks.**

**Repaired after an independent review; no thread's state changed and one thread's timeline is corrected.** The five chapters were revised in place — epigraph and recap blocks removed, the request-to-speak ritual broken, the clerk's recitations carried in narration. **No thread below was spent, advanced, rolled back or re-queued by that repair.** The one item a later phase must take from the repaired text and not from the delivered text is the faultform's clock: **the lime let go in the night before the first bell, Jo Verrick reads the wall at the first bell, and the air engineer comes down the four steps at the fourth bell with the word she will not say twice.** The delivered chapter's epigraph said the third bell and was wrong. **Chapter 180's sixth-bell figures are also now on the page, so the running figures below are readable in the book.**

- **Falsified survey — DELIVERED AS A NOUN, NOT A FIGURE.** Guild cleared-risk map of a district arrives by road hand; every figure certified and true; the sheet's own legend says the office certifies permissions and does not count; the clerk enters *falsified* against her own instinct and enters the objection to her own entry. *Independent* found to mean independent of the rooms. Two of six district rooms name ours and both figures are a ten, the same as our own first column for the same two rooms, entered as an agreement.
- **Exposure — QUEUED, NOT MADE.** Both documents on one table, columns the same way up, one chalk line under both, nothing written under it, a comparison entered as owed by somebody who is not a keeper, a clerk or a man with a page, in a room with no stranger's seal in it. **A woman says that room does not exist yet.** The sentence that ends it is 197's and is not said.
- **Boundary's own first column — RECOGNISED AS A CLEARANCE FIGURE.** Bel Ordry: ours is a permitted occupancy, a clearance figure is a permitted occupancy, they are the same kind of number, ours has been one for thirty-four weeks, it was written that way on purpose, the purpose was correct, and a correct purpose is not a defence and does not get entered as one. **The Volume 03 guardrail that the first column may never be joined to the number of people in that room is held in 176 and 177.**
- **Sabotage-by-correct-form — DELIVERED, ABOUT A DIFFERENT ROAD.** A new board at the middle gate, a form, both of the two lines filled in correctly, in the clerk's hand from the twenty-ninth week, a real seal, an ordinary day. Nobody refused anything. Ordinary ground is now a working road with a named person responsible for a load, and a survey party is a load. **The alternative is closed and no chapter dates the event to the market day.**
- **Faultform — PRESENT IN THE PARTY WALL, NOT KILLED, NOT JOINED TO ANYTHING.** A lime repair came away along bad work meeting sound stone; air four times in a sentence and a count; eleven readings read against the original and the wall is not one of them; the shape is a closing and the subject is unknown; nobody cut, tooled, measured, or put a hand or a tape in it; nobody went through; not a route change as a stage; **not joined to the dowel, the charter, the mouth, the four treads, the ninth room, the low end, the theory, the twelfth-week name or the plate.** One word said once by the air engineer and refused a second time; not a finding, not named.
- **The load reason — ON THE PAGE.** The void is the only thing in that wall doing anything with the force coming through that wall, and the force comes through whether the void is there or not; a bar in the gap is a removal, not a repair. A carpenter's disbelief is given as his trade and not as a virtue.
- **Marek's want — NAMED TWICE.** He wanted the sheet to be a lie so that he could be the man who caught it; he asked the wrong clerk the wrong question; he drew a hole for three days so that he would have something to be wrong about. **His hole is drawn and not cut, and the survey that would have made the void a room is closed.**
- **Cassian Rook — FIRST DIRECT INTERVENTION, BY SHEET AND BY SHORE.** Named, office named, his rule quoted from his own unnumbered sentence, **not in the room**; six people, six shores, nineteen minutes, a count this boundary may not compete with, timber charged to the district, and no word said against him. **The cost is entered as a cost: the first post this boundary has ever had, in somebody else's handwriting, not asked for, with the half against it entered too.** The boundary did not refuse. **The One-Seat and Morrowlight are not named; he survives and stays boundable.**
- **Nera — CONDITION RAISED BY HERSELF, UNMET, UNASKED; GOING RAISED BY ANOTHER, UNANSWERED.** *I will not certify a building that has said no to nothing*, said in a working morning, and this boundary has said no to nothing, and she does not trust herself with her own sentence this month. Nobody consoled, nobody asked. Bel Ordry raised the going and said it is not leaving; **one word, no reason, nobody asked for one, and nobody asked whether she is going anywhere.** First condition unmet, theory unsaid, twelfth-week name unasked, not leaving, no seventh act.
- **Renn Vale's sixth day — OWED FROM 175, GIVEN IN 178.** The second way out is a word, and a word is a way out of a room and not out of a building, known since the first week and not said out loud on purpose; entered that she let a man find it out in a room because it was kinder at a kitchen table. **Not a door.** The carpenter's word-question and the keeper's first-week refusal both stand unanswered and un-re-argued.
- **Held, not touched:** brace, shim and the twelfth-of-an-inch return; school door at the far end of nine steps unwedged, blank page unused, unsent; low end blank, unapproached, unsent, unnamed, no row; ninth room and four treads unwalked, no mark cut; Oren Sill and Dael Harrow unnamed; Talla Roke and Pell Roke both absent from all five chapters; wash woman unnamed, unasked, unrostered, unsent, no instrument produced; **the board at eighteen, 9 + 9, unheaded column's ordinal deliberately not restated, a map refused and a Warden's count refused as two different nineteenth entries;** pot nine to eight with seam one on Friday and two on Sunday and four households nothing with no figure; capacity ten including one litter unchanged and said with strangers in the room.

# Volume 04 Batch 0005 — what the batch did to these threads

**Delivery, Chapters 181–185, all five of the thirty-fifth week, second day to sixth day.**

- **Guild defector's crew — ARRIVED, NOT CONVERTED, NOT FORGIVEN.** Six came up the middle passage on foot on a shut Tuesday, five who carry and one who does not. **Nella Bray, a clerk at a counter at the middle gate, is one of them, is not a hero, does not want to be one, and is doing her job**; she gave this boundary her name after six weeks in which only her hand was known here. **Emrys Callow**, forty-one, shoring, nine years, gave up a cleared-risk post-holder's bond. They came for their own reasons, in their own words, and the volume's own outline clause — *people who have decided a thing is wrong* — is delivered without a conversion and without a pardon.
- **The trust problem — TWO REASONS, BOTH TRUE, NOT THE SAME REASON.** **Theirs:** a number. A clerk who has never been sent a figure of what is in a building rather than what it is permitted, and who would not have noticed the difference until Bel Ordry called his own page the worst in the district. **Ours:** a name on a line. Their post-holder is in both lines of the form that made ordinary ground a working road, and the clerk who filled it in correctly is standing in the room. **Bel Ordry declined to defend his own page in front of the stranger who said it.**
- **The public concession — PROPOSED BY THE PERSON WITH THE AUTHORITY, ENTERED, NOT ADOPTED.** Nera Oduya proposed keeping the schedule's day and putting her name in the column headed for the person who will be present. **It was correct. It is the only name this boundary has put in any column in thirty-five weeks and somebody else can read it.** The half against came from the clerk at the counter: not answering is an answer, and the sentence that goes in somebody else's book will be true.
- **The refusal available — USED, AND IT IS NOT A REFUSAL.** **This boundary has not refused a schedule. It has declined to answer one, and the clerk refused to write the word *refused*, on Pettin Rahl's standing sentence, and entered that she knew what Bel Ordry had said about a visitor's sentence and used it anyway.** Bel Ordry said out loud that he wrote that sentence into this book thirty-five weeks ago and that it is one step from a policy handed to the room.
- **The schedule's day — CAME AND WENT.** A fifth day, yesterday, the corridor open, nine children in a room that is not shut, a man expected, and he did not come. **Nobody in this building knows what an office does about that and the clerk is not pleased.** Unresolved.
- **The faultform's link — NOW WATCHED, AND NOT BY MAREK.** **The watcher is stoppable by two people — Ilsa Norr and the physician — and by a room, in that order. A courier has said out loud that she is not counting the room, and why.** Six terms between the two crews, written by the clerk and read back by a foreman who found nothing to change. **The fifth names a kind of person: not the man who built anything on that wall, not the man who found it, and can be told to stop by a person in a room. The name is left empty on purpose and the reason is entered.** The answer to a carpenter's question that stood unanswered for two weeks is in the book and it is **Renn Vale's seventh thing**, stoppable by Ilsa Norr, the physician, and a room. **The link is unwatched until Saturday morning, unmeasured, unnamed, untouched, and nobody went through it.**
- **The two facts from the party wall — THE JOIN HAS TWO FACES, AND ONE OF THE SIX SHORES IS NOT CARRYING.** A finger on the anteroom side, two on the kitchen-line side, same join, and Jo Verrick has been reporting one of them for a week. **Five and a half shores where the district's book says six, the district's figure neither corrected nor contradicted, and a true fact about a piece of timber going up the middle passage on somebody else's day.** **CORRECTED IN THE REVIEW-FIX PHASE: the span from the shores going up on Monday to the third shore coming out on Friday is four days and is four days everywhere. It was delivered as nine days in five places and had been promoted into two state files. A later phase must not write nine and must not re-derive it.**
- **The comparison — QUEUED, NOT MADE.** Untouched by this batch. **The sentence that ends it belongs to 197 and was not said.**
- **The school — RAN ON ALL THREE OPEN DAYS.** Thirty-third, thirty-fourth, thirty-fifth mornings, kitchen-line room, nowhere else; did not run on the two shut days and lost nothing; **the nine were in that room on the schedule's day on purpose, because a keeper who empties a room of nine children because of a sheet has let the sheet pick the day.** The room was emptied once at the second bell on the Warden's number and filled at the fourth bell by its keeper. **The school corner is open and unused; no school day restored, no closure removed.**
- **Held and not touched:** brace, shim and the twelfth-of-an-inch return; school door at the far end of nine steps unwedged, blank page unused, unsent; **low end blank, unapproached, unsent, unnamed, no row, named three times as a term in the crews' terms and in Dalla Sen's own unprompted entry;** ninth room and four treads unwalked, no mark cut in the stone anywhere; Oren Sill and Dael Harrow unnamed; **Pell Roke in none of the five chapters and Talla Roke in 185 only, never in the same room;** wash woman unnamed, unasked, unrostered, unsent, no instrument produced; **the board at eighteen, 9 + 9, a third refusal of a nineteenth with a third and new reason, the unheaded column's batch ordinal deliberately not restated;** pot eight to seven with the seam giving one on the Thursday; four households nothing and no figure; capacity ten including one litter unchanged and said in four of five chapters.
- **Untouched by anyone:** the air engineer's first and second conditions, her theory, her twelfth-week name, the valve, the spring, and her going — **which was not raised in this batch at all, and that is a choice and not an oversight.** Iven Tallo's post, the second line, the stiff cover; the carpenter's word-question; the four words about who owns a wall; the wrapped plate; the brass rule; the market form; the nine-second strike; the clerk's comparison; the low end's third condition.

## Volume 04 Batch 0002 — what was delivered

**The batch's spine, as delivered:** a joint is not a pin, and the one this building can afford is a shape a person with a knife can take apart; **the four things this Hearthhold does not have are iron, bronze, a kiln and a second pair of hands, and the carpenter puts the people last and says he has never once done that before**; a brace is joined to a mark by cutting the wood to the stone and not the stone to the wood, so that no mark was cut in this building, and the joint is a beech shim a finger wide in a hollow worn nine hundred years ago, and the carpenter says its edges crush in about two years and the person who will know is a term in a clerk's book; **the time is four days in seven and two of the four are the first week of the batch, and nobody can beg for it because there is nothing to beg with**; **a fifth asking with the terms out loud and a fourth set of reasons, and two of the three who could not be asked are not the names used last time, and the crew's column moved to seventy-one**; **two people said no to holding the brace and nobody was forced, and the reason one of them gave is that a person who is willing is not a person who is standing there, and the reason the other gave is that a person who can take a thing out cannot be one of the hands that put it in**; a cook said yes and said the half against it first; a carpenter was asked to sign the record of the thing he built and said no; **a man who keeps a page is suspicious of the man with the store, out loud, on a reason, and said the half that argues against it, and said a clerk arranged the timing and that it was a dirty thing to have arranged**; **the air engineer asked for a second work, was wrong in public before anybody could be kind to her about it, and set a limit with no number and no day on it**; a physician named the failure point *the place where it comes out* before anything was stood under it; **the condition was met and admitted in a room by the two people it names, with a written refusal to certify standing next to it, and the woman who keeps the room said three things in the space where a reason goes**; **a room's rating is a word said to a page, and a man asked in a room whether the word is still about the same thing, and the room did not answer, and the word was said twice anyway**; **the brace went in with nine children taught on the other side of the wall, and the frame came into true by a twelfth of an inch, and the anteroom's count did not change**; **it came out in eleven minutes because the woman who keeps the room knelt at the ninth hearth stone on a shut morning and found its bed a third of an inch higher, and nobody was sent to look**; **it went back in a foot and a half lower, and a fifth sound wedge went under a hearth stone, and four terms this building wrote for itself were read three times against the original and found the same, and they were not struck out and not left, and the finding is that they bound a work and not a building**; the count is at one hundred and five; the pot is at nine days; a board has eighteen entries.

1. **A brace is standing over the head of the anteroom's outer service door, a foot and a half lower than it was on Wednesday, with a beech shim in a nine-hundred-year-old hollow that will crush at its edges in about two years, a tied joint and not a pegged one, and no mark cut in the stone anywhere in this building.**
2. **The brace does not increase the anteroom's capacity. Ten including one litter for no more than two hours, unchanged, said out loud in a room, and a brace that makes a room safe by making it hold more people was named in that room as the failure.**
3. **All four of the bible's requirements are on the page and none is soft, and all four of the bible's costs are on the page and none is soft, and a coercive brace was handled as a power-system rule and not a metaphor: every person whose hands are on it agreed out loud, in a room, to what they are holding and what stops it, and two of them said no and nobody was forced.**
4. **A condition with no number and no day on it was met and admitted in a room, out loud, by the two people it names, before anybody was stood under the brace, and its second clause was then used and it worked: the woman who keeps the room found out and said the brace was to come out and nobody argued with her.**
5. **A failure point is named *the place where it comes out*, in a clerk's book, by a physician, before anything was stood under it, and it is a phrase and not a term and it is not on a stone and it is not the ninth hearth stone's bed because he had not looked at it.**
6. **The school door has no wedge in it and there are two sound wedges left in this building, and the answer to a door that has to be watched is one person, and the page where a person's hours would go is blank and was not used and nobody was sent.**
7. **A wall has nine readings, eight of them a quarter of an inch and two of them nothing, and a bed under the ninth hearth stone is a third of an inch higher than it was on Friday morning, and a clerk read both figures out in a room and said she is not going to write what caused either of them.**
8. **The pot is at nine days and is being held up by a seam, and a cook said the arithmetic out loud and would not say the word, and four households at a second gate have nothing.**
9. **A man with a post in a carrier's hand four and a half days up a road has neither refused it nor accepted it, and a carpenter was asked to sign a second thing in this building and refused, and the line at the bottom of that paper stays empty.**
10. **A store four days up the middle passage whose fir went up the road, whose beech is in a brace, whose list has no date on it, and which a man who keeps a page is now suspicious of out loud on a reason and a half-reason.**
11. **A board at eighteen entries with nine of them under a column with nothing over the top of it, and a man who reads it gave a tenth reason this batch, cost himself something doing it, and then said he had nothing and manufactured nothing.**
12. **A condition met, a failure point named, a sixth term added on a landing, and four terms of an earlier asking read three times and found the same and entered as having bound a work and not a building.**
13. **And the question is still on the page: who owns a wall, asked out loud in four words a fortnight ago, not answered, and this batch's closest approach to an answer is a courier's sentence about the difference between this boundary and a guild notice.**

## Volume 04 Batch 0003 — what was delivered (Chapters 171–175)

**Added in the review-fix phase, because this file's body was still Batch 0002's hand-off while its head said Batch 0003 was delivered. The Batch 0002 section above is left as it was written and is a record of that batch.**

**The batch's spine, as delivered:** an elected keeper walks back into a room that kept itself for seven weeks and says two clauses, and the anteroom's fifth term becomes true again on the day he walks in, and a clerk enters that a term was false for seven weeks as a finding about a room and not about a man, beside the standing refusal to write down how long the man has been gone; **a room is asked what a boundary owes a man who comes back and four answers are given and none of them is an answer, and the man declines the question back as a post given by the people who did the work**; **a printed schedule comes down the passage with a column headed for the person who will be present, with its covering already struck by somebody else, and this boundary strikes nothing out of it and reads it against the second column of its own plan instead, and a pump maintainer says out loud that they are not the same instrument because the printed one is filled in by somebody who is not going to be there**; **the third room on that sheet is named out loud as the room nine children are taught in, and nobody wrote a name in the column, and the room got no row, and the plan has sixteen rows and does not get a seventeenth**; **the air engineer argues that keeping a brace, a store, a road and a keeper is not the same sentence as being asked to open a road while something is going wrong four days up a passage, sets a second condition — *I will not certify a building that has said no to nothing* — says it twice, and is wrong out loud before anybody can be kind to her about having certified the air of a room she has not stood in on a morning nine children were in it, and nobody consoles her and nobody asks her**; **a physician asks out loud whether it is a good idea that the terms written for a pair of hands have been extended to a piece of wood, and gives the half against his own question himself, and there is no easy answer**; **a man who cut the splay says *I do not know* and puts three facts under it for the first time in thirty-four weeks without being asked twice**; **a man who reads the board is asked whether a returning keeper goes on it, gives the eleventh reason of his life, and the board stays at eighteen and the number can be asked without anybody being sent for**; and **the clerk reads the keeper's two Saturday clauses back to him word for word on Wednesday and asks whether they are what he said, which is the practice, and he confirms both.**

1. **Sefu Aran is in the building, returned, not a rescue and not a takeover.** Two clauses said Saturday and confirmed Wednesday; **his absence was never counted, his whereabouts were never asked, and no chapter puts a figure on it**; he was offered the school door and refused it before he was asked; he read only his own term out of the book and declined the carpenter's word-question as first-week decisiveness.
2. **The anteroom's rating is ten including one litter for no more than two hours and did not change, and its fifth term of six was false for seven weeks and is true again from the day he walked in.** A clerk entered the seven weeks as a finding about a room; a man who keeps the plan said aloud that a room which can be stopped does not get asked whether its own words are true, because you do not audit a handle you are holding; and the air engineer and the elected keeper answered that question in the first person because neither of them has to be in the anteroom at seven in the morning, and that no room was going to pretend it was a near thing.
3. **A schedule with a column headed for the person who will be present came down the middle passage and nothing was struck out of it here.** The covering was struck before it reached this room, by somebody, and the clerk entered that and entered that she will find out nothing and ask nothing. The sheet was read against the plan's own second column — sixteen conditions with no number and no day on any of them, all sixteen filled, written by the people who keep the rooms.
4. **The third room on the sheet is the room at the kitchen-line end, and it is a room nine children are taught in, and it was named as a fact in a room and not as a revelation.** No name was written in the column and the carrier, who reads a column four hundred times a year in his ordinary work, decided not to write one word in it.
5. **The plan did not get a seventeenth row, and a physician said out loud that a person is not safer for being written down twice and that he will not be the man who says the sheet is wrong, because the sheet has put a space where a person could go.**
6. **The air engineer's second condition is set, said twice, and unasked: *I will not certify a building that has said no to nothing*, because a boundary that has said no to nothing has not been shown to be able to say it.** Her first condition is not withdrawn and is not met. Her twelfth-week name is still unasked and her theory is still unstated and she is not leaving and nobody is going.
7. **A wall has ten readings, eight of them a quarter of an inch and two of them nothing, and a bed under the ninth hearth stone's bed is a third of an inch higher than it was, and a clerk entered both and will not write what caused either.** Nobody joined the two nothings to a Wednesday on which the school ran.
8. **The pot is at nine days and going to eight and is being held up by a seam at four threads, down from eight in the nineteenth week and not measured in between, and four households at a second gate have nothing and no figure is attached to that gate by anybody.**
9. **A board at eighteen entries with nine of them under a column with nothing over the top of it, and the word over that column would be *keeper*, and there is a keeper in this building and the word still does not go on.** A man who reads it was asked whether a returning keeper goes on it and gave the eleventh reason of his life: a person on a board is a thing on a board. The crew's column is seventy-one and did not move all week, and there was no sixth asking, because a room had four things come into it in four days and not one of them is a work anybody can be asked five people for.
10. **The brace stands, the school door at the far end of nine steps does not, and the page where a person's hours would go is blank with three conditions on it and the third of them says that nobody is to be sent anywhere to make it true.** Three of the five sound wedges are spoken for and two are not.
11. **A physician asked out loud whether the terms that governed a pair of hands should govern a piece of wood, and gave the half against his own question, and a man who cut the splay said he did not know and put three facts under it.**
12. **The clerk read out the day's figures on Wednesday for the first time in two days, having not read them on Tuesday because a printed sheet was open on that table with a column on it headed for a person, and read the count at one hundred and ten, and walked the board at eighteen for the last time that week.**
13. **And nothing was resolved: not the brace's watching, not the shim, not the school door, not the low end, not the ninth room, not the four treads, not the brass rule, not the plate, not the market form, not the post in the stiff cover, and not the four words on the page.** The question *who owns a wall* is still on a page in a clerk's book in a man's own hand, asked and not answered.


## Volume 04 Batch 0004 — what was delivered (Chapters 176–180)

**Added in the writer's own session, so that this file's head and its body agree. The Batch 0002 and Batch 0003 sections above are left as they were written and are records of those batches.**

### The same batch after its review-fix pass

**The five chapters were revised in place after an independent review and every plot fact below stands. What changed is how the chapters are built, and the next writer needs to know it in order not to rebuild the defect.**

- **The epigraph and recap blocks are gone from all five chapters.** Forty-three fully-bold paragraphs that gave away each turn before the scene started and restated it beat for beat afterwards. **The only bold left in Chapters 176–180 is a person speaking.** Narration is not bold anywhere in the batch. **Chapters 171–175 still carry 36 of these blocks; that is already-delivered Batch 0003 prose, untouched, and the divergence is recorded rather than hidden.**
- **The request-to-speak tag is dead as a device.** Fifty-two spoken paragraphs opened by demanding speech — *Say the covering*, *Say the half against*, *Say it back to me* — and twenty-six clerk recitations opened *Entered, in his words, and entered that*. **The formulaic tag is gone: what survives is two bare *Say* imperatives in two different mouths — Dalla Sen on the shape in 179, Bel Ordry on what is owed in 180 — plus the physician's *So say the name* in 178, which is his catchphrase. One clerk recitation survives in five chapters, because it is a finding and not bookkeeping.** The half against itself is canon and is in all five chapters; **what was retired is asking for it in the same four words.** A room now asks in about twenty shapes, and several answers arrive with nobody having asked.
- **Quoted share is back inside the range the series started in: 53.6, 46.9, 58.6, 53.7, 50.1 per chapter and 52.8 for the batch**, against Volume 01's 25–40% and Volume 03's late 60–75%. The clerk's bookkeeping is carried in narration by default, which is what took the quoted share down and what took the ritual out.
- **The 4000-word ceiling is retired.** It was never in `AGENTS.md`, `NOVEL_SPEC.md`, `outline/volume-04.md` or the bible; it first appears in Batch 0003's own review record and in the Batch 0004 and 0005 prompts; and 179 and 180 were delivered at 4303 and 4142 and cut to land at 3999 and 3997. **Lengths are now reported as measurements. The chapters are 3200, 3499, 3052, 3511 and 3582 words, and they were deliberately not padded back out.**
- **Chapter 179's timeline is corrected and the corrected version is the only one to inherit.** The deleted epigraph said the lime repair came away at the third bell; the scene had Jo Verrick finding the gap at the first bell. **The prose now says the lime let go in the night, Jo reads the wall at the first bell, Sefu listens, Iven names the join, and the air engineer comes down the four steps at the fourth bell with the word she will not say twice.** `state/chapter-summaries.md` is corrected to match and marks the correction.
- **Chapter 180's sixth-bell figures are on the page.** The chapter said the clerk read the total out loud and never said what it was, so the batch's closing **+1 / 243 / 360.25** lived only in the state layer. Both figures are now readable in the book, and the batch's arithmetic reconciles chapter by chapter from the prose alone.
- **Two of the five turns are still triggered by a delivery** — a courier in 176, a repair letting go in 179 — because both are canon. What changed is that 176 now opens three days into Marek's private hunt for a lie and takes the leaf as an interruption, and 179 opens on Jo's thumb coming out of the string wrong. **The rule this produced for the next batch: at least three of 181–185 must turn on somebody deciding something, and a document may arrive but may not be the cause.**

**The full record, with every measurement and its method, is `reviews/volume-04/batch-0004.md` and the head of `state/batch-summary.md`.**

**The batch's spine, as delivered:** a waxed leaf comes down the middle passage in a road hand's grip with a whole district on it and the word *independent* at the top of it, and its own legend says that no surveyor of its office has entered any room shown, that every figure is the last certified permitted occupancy of that room, and that **this office certifies permissions and this office does not count**; **every figure on it is true and no surveyor lied, and a clerk enters the word *falsified* against her own professional instinct and enters the objection to her own entry in her own hand, and says the honest sentence is the one that does the damage**; **the word independent is found, an hour and a half late, to mean independent of the rooms and not of the office**; **the page in the coat comes out of the coat onto a table beside the stranger's paper for the first time in thirty-four weeks, the two documents are read against each other row by row, two of six district rooms match and four have nothing on the other side, and this boundary's own first column turns out to be the same kind of number as a clearance figure and has been one for thirty-four weeks, written that way on purpose, the purpose correct, and a correct purpose is not a defence and does not get entered as one**; **a man who keeps a page asks a room out loud whether a page in a coat with no name on it is better than a printed one and cannot answer it and gives the reason with a clause in it about himself**; **a man states his design, a second way out that is a hole, low through the party wall, and a surveyor arrives at needing to be allowed in**; **a carrier comes down the middle passage with the fact that a new board has been nailed over an old one at the middle gate, four days up, with a form on it and both of its two lines filled in correctly, in the hand of the clerk who took this boundary's form off its board in the twenty-ninth week, so that the ground ordinary residents cross becomes a working road with a named person responsible for a load and a survey party is a person carrying a load, and nobody refused anything and nothing is untrue**; **a man says out loud that he asked the wrong clerk the wrong question and that what he wanted was to be the man who found out; a physician puts the man himself in the plan as the named injured person; a woman on a landing gives the answer she promised for the sixth day of a week and it is a sentence and not a door, that a word is a way out of a room and not out of a building, and enters that she let him spend two days finding it out in a room because it was kinder at a kitchen table**; **on a shut seventh day with nine children therefore not in the building, a lime repair comes away along the line where bad work meets sound stone in the party wall, and air comes out of a gap about two fingers wide four times in the time it takes to say a sentence and stops for a count, and the eleven wall readings are read against the original and against the clerk's book and all eleven are the same and this morning is not one of them**; **the room named the shape of what the void is doing, a closing, and could not say what it was closing about, and said both out loud, and a keeper said the sound is a decision being made with nobody in the room to make it and refused to guess, and an air engineer said the word once and refused to say it twice and entered that it is not a finding and this room is not going to give it a name**; **a woman who keeps a room said the room is not to be used and said nothing whatever about the room being shut, and a woman who keeps a corridor gave her the difference, and the keeper wrote one line in the third column in her own hand and it is the only thing anybody wrote in a document in this batch**; **the faultform is not killed, and the reason is on the page in the engineer's own mouth — the void is the only thing in that wall doing anything with the force coming through that wall, and the force is coming through that wall whether the void is there or not, so a bar in the gap is a removal and not a repair — and a carpenter gave his disbelief as the reason he would not put a bar in there and asked for it to be entered as his trade and not as a virtue, and nobody went through the link and nobody put a tool, a hand or a tape into it**; **Cassian Rook intervened for the first time and it is a sheet under a seal and six people and six timber shores, and he is not in the room, and the work takes nineteen minutes, and the shore goes on the common landing side because that is the only place a floor is at the right height, and the count goes into a district book that this boundary may not compete with, and the cost is entered as a cost including the half against the entry, and the boundary did not refuse, and no word was said against him**; **a woman raised her own condition in a working morning, unasked, and said this boundary has said no to nothing and that she does not trust herself with her own sentence this month, and a man with a page raised the going by other people and said it is not leaving, and she said one word and gave no reason and nobody asked her**; **the two documents went side by side on the anteroom table under a chalk line with nothing written under it, a comparison is entered as owed, and a woman said the room which can hear it does not exist yet**; **a board of eighteen refused a Warden's count as a nineteenth entry in one sentence about who makes a number, gave no reason for the unheaded column in any of the five chapters, and the column's batch ordinal is not restated anywhere**.

1. **A guild cleared-risk map of a district's occupied rooms is in this building and every figure on it is true.** It calls itself independent and is independent of the rooms. It carries a cleared-risk wax head at both corners and a clerk's name at the bottom, **Aubrey Tace, engager of clearances, ninth district**, and a seal number.
2. **The exposure is QUEUED and not made.** The map and this boundary's sixteen-row page lie side by side on the anteroom table with their columns the same way up under one chalk line, with nothing written under the line. A comparison is entered as owed by somebody who is not a keeper, a clerk or a man with a page, in a room that has not had a stranger's seal in it this week. **Renn Vale says out loud that the room which can hear that comparison does not exist yet, and gives the half against waiting herself.** The sentence that ends the comparison belongs to Chapter 197 and is not said.
3. **The dowel/plan collision is now a fact about a district with wax on it, and this boundary's own first column is one of its figures.** Two of six district rooms name rooms here and both figures are a ten, the same figure as the first column for the same two rooms. **No chapter joins that figure to the number of people in that room, and the guardrail from Volume 03 holds in 176 and 177.**
4. **A form at the middle gate has both of its two lines filled in correctly, in the clerk's hand from the twenty-ninth week, and nobody refused anything.** The ground between the end of the middle passage and the middle gate is now a working road with a named person responsible for a load. **A person with a survey lamp, a line and a note-book is a person carrying a load.**
5. **Marek's alternative is closed and his hole is not cut.** He wanted a survey of a void; a survey needs to be allowed in; a room nobody has surveyed cannot have a row; a room with no row has no keeper and no condition. **He said out loud, twice, that what he wanted was to be the man who found out, and he said he had drawn the hole for three days so that he would have something to be wrong about.** The drawing is on the anteroom table and was not burned and not folded away.
6. **A service void is open in the party wall, about two fingers, along the line where bad work meets sound stone, and it is doing a closing whose subject nobody in this building can say.** Nobody cut it and there is no tool mark in the join. **The eleven wall readings are the same and the wall is not one of them. It is not killed, not tooled, not measured, not put a hand in, and not put a tool in, and nobody has gone through it.** It is not a route change as a stage.
7. **The room at the kitchen-line end is not to be used and is not shut, and the difference between the two was given out loud by the woman who keeps the corridor and written in the third column in the keeper's own hand.** The school ran once in this batch, on Friday, for the thirty-second morning, in that room, and the nine were out of it on Saturday and Sunday and Monday.
8. **A Warden-General's instruction has been obeyed, and it saved the nine and cost the boundary its page.** Three numbered things and one unnumbered sentence in Rook's own hand. Six people, six shores from the middle gate's standing stores, nineteen minutes, a count in a district book, **no competing figure permitted from this boundary**, timber charged to the district. **Rook is not in the room, is not an antagonist, is not a final enemy, the One-Seat is not named, and he survives and stays boundable.** Sefu Aran stood at the top of the nine steps through the count and did not open his mouth.
9. **The anteroom's rating is ten including one litter for no more than two hours, was said on Monday with six strangers in the room, and did not change.** Its fifth term of six is true and both the people it names were in the room.
10. **The air engineer's second condition is unmet, unasked, and was raised by her; the going was raised by a man with a page and is unanswered.** *I will not certify a building that has said no to nothing*, said in a working morning, with her own doubt entered in her own order. Nobody consoled her. She is not leaving, no chapter stages it, and her theory, her twelfth-week name, the valve and the spring are untouched.
11. **Renn Vale's sixth-day answer, owed from 175, is given in 178: a word is a way out of a room and not out of a building.** The carpenter's word-question and the keeper's refusal to answer it as first-week decisiveness both stand unanswered and un-re-argued.
12. **A board of eighteen, 9 + 9, walked twice, refused a nineteenth twice for two different stated reasons, unheaded throughout, no ordinal restated, and the number askable without anybody being sent for.** The pot is at eight days, the seam gave one and two, and four households at a second gate have nothing with no figure attached to that gate.
13. **And nothing was resolved: not the void, not the faultform, not the comparison, not the Warden's count, not the brace's watching, not the shim, not the school door, not the low end, not the ninth room, not the four treads, not the brass rule, not the plate, not the market form, not the post in the stiff cover, not the carpenter's word-question, and not the four words about who owns a wall.** The volume's one serious injury remains unspent and available.

## Volume 04 Batch 0005 — what was delivered (Chapters 181–185)

**All five days of the thirty-fifth week after Monday. The first half of the volume's escalation, delivered; the batch's climax at 188–190 and the reverse of the schedule at 192 are not delivered and were not started.**

1. **A guild defector's crew came up the middle passage on foot, and they are not converted and not forgiven.** Six people, five of them carrying. **Nella Bray, a clerk at a counter at the middle gate four days up the middle passage, is one of them, gave this building her name after six weeks in which only her hand was known here, is not a hero, does not want to be one, and is doing her job.** **Emrys Callow**, forty-one, shoring, nine years, held a cleared-risk post-holder's bond in this district until he put it in a hand and did not go back for it. They will not carry for a man whose name is on two lines of a form; the five of them were on neither line; and when a load came down wrong in the thirty-first week of last year the figure in the district book was a man who was not standing in the passage. They came for that and for a keeper who can say no, and they have taken no work they were not asked for and are owed none.
2. **The trust problem is the plot and both reasons are true and they are not the same reason.** **Theirs is a number**: a clerk who has never been sent a figure of what is in a building rather than what it is permitted, who would not have noticed the difference until a man kept a page on a table beside a stranger's paper and said out loud that ours was the worst in the district. **Ours is a name on a line**: their post-holder is in both lines of the form that made ordinary ground a working road, and the clerk who filled it in correctly was standing in the room. **Bel Ordry declined to defend his own page and said the reason first.** Callow has no answer to the objection that a crew with nothing to do and no pay will take the next work that comes, and he asked for that to be entered.
3. **The Compact's schedule turned a safe decision into a public concession, and the concession was proposed by the person with the authority over the air and was correct.** Nera Oduya offered to keep the schedule's day, to put her name in the column headed for the person who will be present, to have the third room empty, and to let the sheet go back down the passage with a mark on it that says this boundary attended. **Her reason was the sentence she wrote a fortnight ago — she will not certify a building that has said no to nothing — and this boundary has said three yeses and no no, and she was not waiting to be asked.** The concession is entered as proposed and not adopted and it is the only name this boundary has put in any column in thirty-five weeks and somebody else can read it. **The half against came from the clerk at the counter: not answering a schedule is an answer, and the sentence that goes in somebody else's book will be that this boundary was scheduled and did not attend, and that sentence will be true.**
4. **And the refusal available turned out not to be a refusal, and that is the institutional act of the batch.** On Pettin Rahl's standing sentence — *a regime is not a threat. It is a schedule. And a thing which is scheduled is not a thing which is refused* — **the clerk refused to write the word *refused*, because a boundary that refuses a schedule has conceded that the schedule is the instrument. This boundary has not refused a schedule. It has declined to answer one, and only one of those two acts is a thing an office can act on. She entered that she knew what Bel Ordry had said about a visitor's sentence and used it anyway.** Bel Ordry said out loud that he put that sentence in this building's book thirty-five weeks ago, that it is the best sentence anybody has brought into this room, and that a room with a good sentence in its book from outside is one step away from having a policy handed to it, and that he wrote the step down.
5. **The schedule's day came and went. Yesterday was a fifth day, the corridor was open, nine children were in a room that is not shut, a man was expected, and he did not come.** Nobody in this building knows what an office does on a Saturday when a boundary does not attend. The clerk entered what a counter does on a Saturday as a fact about counters and not a finding, and entered that she is not pleased about it, because a boundary that is pleased about a day nothing happened on is a boundary that has begun to want days nothing happens. **Unresolved, and Batch 0006 must not resolve it without its own chapter.**
6. **The Warden's first numbered thing was obeyed on the next open morning, at the second bell, and a keeper turned an obedience into a decision at the third bell.** The room at the kitchen-line end was emptied last one first, the four rooms were held as one space, and the clerk entered the compliance with the hour and not with the day. **The nine went back in at the fourth bell because Ilsa Norr decided, out loud, that a thing which can be emptied twice in ten days by two documents is a thing that is being emptied, and that the woman who empties it is in neither document.** Her half against is in the space where a reason goes. **The room is used and is not shut, and the difference is still the one the woman who keeps the corridor gave in Chapter 179.** The keeper wrote the only line in any document in this batch, in the third column, in her own hand, and read it back against her own mouth.
7. **The school ran on all three open days, for the thirty-third, thirty-fourth and thirty-fifth mornings, in the room at the kitchen-line end and nowhere else, and did not run on the two shut days and lost nothing. The nine were in that room on the schedule's day on purpose.** The school corner is open and is not used; no school day was restored and no closure was removed. **On the fifth day of the week a piece of timber came out of the party wall while nine children were in the room on the other side of it, and the room knew it and did it anyway.**
8. **Two facts from the party wall changed the arithmetic, and neither of them is the void.** Jo Verrick went round to the far side of the wall for the first time since she came into this building and found **the same join is a finger wide on the anteroom side and two fingers on the kitchen-line side**, and she has been reporting one of them for a week as though it were the join. And the third shore had lost about a finger of its length at the head with its foot unmoved, which is a head being crushed for want of a spreader under the head of the sill — the answer Warden-Officer Karr gave out loud in this room on the first day of this week, which was right, and which nobody acted on for four days. **Leena Orr read the timber — she is the only person here whose trade is reading a thing that is already built — and said the fault is in the ground and not in the timber, and Iven Tallo's Monday sentence turned out to have named the head of that shore in the wrong half of itself.**
9. **The third shore came out in eleven minutes and the wall has five and a half where a district's book says six. The finding entered: the district's figure is not corrected by this boundary and is not contradicted by it, because those are two different acts.** Emrys Callow will carry the true fact up the middle passage himself, because the timber is the district's and the man who chose it should hear it from the crew that found it. **The clerk writes the day of the week on the message and not the date, on purpose, so that a person in a year can tell the difference between a message and a form.** Bel Ordry's half against is that the only road a fact takes into a district's book is somebody else's paper, and somebody else's paper has a day in it and a column in it. Renn Vale: send it, because a boundary that holds it back has learned to hold things back from offices, and that is the first sentence of a very short road to a room with a name over the door.
10. **Six terms between the two crews, written by the clerk and read back by a foreman who found nothing to change, and the name in the fifth is left out on purpose with the reason entered.** Five work the common landing side; the kitchen-line side is not worked and not entered; every person whose hands go on that wall says out loud what they are holding and what stops it; nobody is sent to the low end and the page there stays as it is; nobody goes through the wall and nothing goes into the line of nothing in it; **the person who watches that line is not the man who built anything on that wall and not the man who found it and can be told to stop by a person in a room**; none of it goes on the board.
11. **The watcher is Renn Vale and it is her seventh thing and it is not a post.** She will watch the line at the first bell on open days and the second on shut days and will say what she can hear out loud in a room and will not put a rule in it and will not put her hand in it and will not know what it is about and will not pretend to. **Who stops her: Ilsa Norr, the physician, and a room, in that order, and none of them has to give her a reason and she does not have to accept one.** Her reason, asked for by a stranger and not by the room: the room behind that wall is the room nine children are taught in, and there is no version of her that hears a sound in that wall and waits to be asked. Bel Ordry's objection: a woman who decides to take a seventh thing onto herself has become a post, and there is no page in this building where anybody's hours go.
12. **Talla Roke returned deliberately, in Chapter 185 only, on her own terms, and not a rescue and not a takeover. Pell Roke is in none of the five chapters and no chapter puts them in the same room.** She has got an answer on a road for two weeks and **says it is wrong**: a person who can be told to stop is a person somebody can stop, and at the moment that wall does the thing it has been doing, the two people who can stop the watcher will be on the other side of nine children — **and she is explicit that she is not counting the room, because a room is not standing anywhere at that moment.** The two are **Ilsa Norr and the physician**, and a room can also stop Renn Vale and is third in that order. **That is the sharpest sentence in the batch and it is unresolved.** Renn Vale gave the other half and refused to let a new thing be folded into the carpenter's unanswered sentence about a word.
13. **A third refusal of a nineteenth board entry, with a third and new reason, and the batch's craft rules held.** A term between two crews is not a thing in this building; it is a thing two rooms agreed about, and the day one of those rooms is not in this building any more the term is still on here with nobody left to ask. **No epigraph or recap block in any of the five chapters and the only bold is a person speaking; one bare *Say* imperative in five chapters after the repair pass, and the other three request-shaped openers as delivered were varied rather than retired wholesale; quoted share 46.4 to 58.4 with a batch mean of 53.5; lengths 3541, 3519, 4715, 4208, 4997 after the repair pass and 3463, 3400, 4382, 3839, 4705 as first delivered, with the retired 4000-word ceiling honoured by nothing.** **The figures in this item are the repaired ones and the method and the superseded figures are in `reviews/volume-04/batch-0005.md`.**
14. **And nothing was resolved: not the comparison, not the sentence that ends it, not the void, not the faultform, not the room behind the wall, not the schedule's unanswered day, not what an office does on a Saturday, not the carpenter's word-question, not the four words about who owns a wall, not the post in the stiff cover, not the air engineer's two conditions or her theory or her name or her going, not the low end, not the ninth room, not the four treads, not the market form, not the plate, not the brass rule, and not the volume's one serious injury, which remains unspent and available.**

### The same batch after its review-fix pass

**An independent review of Volume 04 Batch 0005 was run in a phase this writer did not control, and the five chapters were revised in place. Every plot fact, figure, date, guardrail, hand-off and the batch's ending stand. What changed is that two factual errors had been promoted into this file and into `state/continuity.md` and would have been inherited as canon by the next writer. The full record, with a method beside every figure and the six false claims in the batch's own review record corrected, is `reviews/volume-04/batch-0005.md` and the head of `state/batch-summary.md`.**

- **The elapsed time between the shores going up and the third shore coming out is four days, and it is four days everywhere.** The six shores went up on the first day of the thirty-fifth week, a Monday (Chapter 180), and the third shore came out on the fifth day, a Friday (Chapter 184). **The prose said *nine days* in five places across 182 and 184, and this file and `state/continuity.md` had promoted *nine days* to canon. Corrected to four days in the prose and in both state files.** A later phase must not re-derive this from the batch and must not write nine.
- **The page in the coat has been lying on the anteroom table four days in 181 and six days in 183, not nine.** It was laid beside the waxed leaf on the fifth day of the thirty-fourth week, a Friday, in Chapter 177; 181 is the second day of the thirty-fifth week and 183 is the fourth.
- **A page on the table in Chapter 182, Chapter 181's own *nine days ago*, and Chapter 182's *nine days ago* about Marek's own line about asking to be asked are all corrected.** The last one is now *on Saturday*, because the line is his, in Chapter 178, which is the sixth day of the thirty-fourth week, and the fourth day of the thirty-fifth week is four days after it.
- **Nera Oduya is twenty-eight and has never stood at a counter.** The batch's thesis paragraph had her claiming nineteen years watching an office from the other side of a counter, which is **Nella Bray's** credential and is hers alone. **Her credential is now her own and is stated in her own trade: she has been the only person who certifies the air in nine rooms of this Hearthhold since she was nineteen, and in nine years not one of those nine has ever said no to a thing anybody asked it for.** Nella Bray's nineteen years at a counter are unchanged and are hers.
- **The count is not read at the sixth bell in all five chapters.** It is read in 181, 184 and 185, and in **182 the clerk does not read the day's figures at all and says so in one line** — nine children went back through a door that morning. In 183 they are entered and not read. **This file previously said the count was read at the sixth bell in all five, which misdescribed 182; the correction is here so it is not repeated.**
- **Chapter 182's Bel Ordry now says the room is to be used again on a fifth day.** He previously said the fourth day, four lines away from himself saying he wanted the room not full on a fifth day, and the corridor is shut on the fourth day. 181's Callow now says the second day of a week and 181's narrator no longer counts seven strangers when six came up the steps.
- **Chapter 184's central decision is now motivated on the page.** Mero Senn states the bind nobody had stated: the work is only reachable on an open corridor morning, the corridor is shut two days in seven, and the choice was never between a morning with nine children next to the wall and a morning without them — it was between that morning and **no morning at all**, which is the same accident on a slower clock. Renn Vale then names the other way out and says she is not the one who emptied it, and Ilsa Norr answers it.
- **Chapter 183's concession now meets what 182 demolished.** Bel Ordry tells Nera Oduya, in the room, that the keeper said yesterday she would not empty that room, that it is in the book in her own words, and that a cheap thing standing on that is arithmetic with a lie in the bottom of it. **She answers that she is not asking her to do it, she is asking her to be in the building, and that the two are different requests and she picked the one that costs nothing.** The concession is still proposed, still correct, and still not adopted.
- **Chapter 185's courier no longer claims access to an instrument that never leaves the building.** She no longer says *that word*, which had no antecedent, and no longer says she has read Dalla Sen's book on a road. **She now says the word by name — *refused* — and says she knows it from a form and not from the clerk: the second column of the schedule was empty when it came off the press.** The argument is the same and it is sharper, and it runs on something she could actually know.
- **Two figures inside Renn Vale's mouth no longer use *this book* as a clock.** A character does not have a book. *A fifth of the weeks in this book* is now *a fifth of the weeks we have been standing in it*, and *I said no to a seventh thing in this book* is now *in this room*.
- **One duplicate the batch's own pass missed is closed.** Ilsa Norr's line in 182 about the nine hearth stones was twenty-eight identical words with her line in Chapter 179, the same woman in the same room, hidden mid-sentence. 182 now reaches the same decision from a different direction. The Renn Vale crossing-clause in 181 and the faultform's signature image in 182 and 184 are also separated, and the closing ledger paragraph, which ran in one fixed shape in four of five chapters, now runs in three shapes and two of the five chapters close on the room.
- **The batch's own review record is corrected where it was wrong.** Six of its measurable claims were false or overstated: it claimed the 90-word sentences were all narration when six remained and all six were speech; it claimed zero request-to-speak openers and two bare *Say* imperatives when four request-shaped openers were on the page; it claimed all five chapters close on the room when two closed on ledger lines; it called the meta pass clean while *this book* ran as a clock nine times; it claimed the brass paragraph was rewritten when the figures and the closing sentence were identical to Chapter 180's; and it reported a duplication zero that its own method does not return. **Those corrections are in the review record with the method beside each figure, and `workspace/volume-04/batch-0006/PROMPT.md` no longer carries the false versions as binding baseline.**
- **Two quantities a later phase must not re-derive or confuse.** **Mero Senn's *nine weeks* in 182 is not his tenure** — his tenure was corrected in Batch 0002's review-fix to eight weeks and two days as of Chapter 168, and the nine weeks in 182 is the number of weeks he has been saying one particular sentence. **Nella Bray's *nineteen years* is her only credential of that kind and belongs to no one else in this volume.**

**`workspace/volume-04/batch-0007/PROMPT.md` is the single next phase.** Volume 04 Batch 0006 delivered Chapters 186–192 and is canon. **Batch 0007 is Chapters 193–197, and it is the volume's climax batch**: two networks of rooms that do not touch, each with its own keeper and its own condition and no order on it; **Iven Tallo's choice at 196, in a room, in his own words, at the cost of the thing he wanted, unredeemed, and the refusal entered in a clerk's book in his own hand with the reason next to it**; **and at 197 the comparison, read out loud in a room, and the sentence that ends it — *every number in that is true and it is not a count, and I have been telling a room that for thirty weeks and nobody wrote it down*** — in a woman's mouth, and not before. **198–199 (two seals withdrawn at a counter, two Hollowmarks shut, the outer routes rearranging) and 200 (the question asked out loud and not answered) are not this batch and must not be started.**

**The position Batch 0007 inherits, stated once.** The escalation is finished and it finished as an arrangement rather than a reconciliation. **The two crews are not converted and not forgiven.** Six people came up the middle passage in the thirty-fifth week and five of them are a foreman's crew and one is a clerk at a counter; **Emrys Callow turned down six weeks of paid shoring at the middle gate for four days running and could not give a reason and stopped looking, and Bel Ordry, who argued for a month that a crew with nothing to do takes the next work that comes, has been told he was right about them and wrong about why, and the room does not know the answer and is not going to be told.** **Nella Bray asked in her own mouth for a figure of what is in this building and was refused by five people in five mouths — Renn Vale, Bel Ordry, Jo Verrick, Mikka Hale and Tams Quill, who said nothing — and Marek Venn had one within two or three and did not give it, and said out loud that a figure from a man with no post has a source and a source is a post.** **Callow's answer is the batch's sharpest sentence about a number: a shoring crew's trade is a count of what is behind a wall, and a wall with an unknown number behind it gets a shore that comes out in four minutes, which is a hundred times too slow for the person holding the other end.** This boundary's own reason for not distrusting them — a name on a line — has been narrowed and not answered: **the arrangement holds because neither crew's work is a load on a road, and Nella Bray said in the room that the answer is correct and narrow, and that the day one piece of timber goes out of this building on a cart the objection stops holding, and the clerk entered it on the day she said it.**

**The arrangement, and it is the batch's spine and it must not grow.** Chapter 190, said out loud in both crews' mouths and written down by nobody as a shape: **two crews, one wall, one morning, and we are not one crew.** The six terms stand for both crews. **The check crosses and the hours do not** — the person who checks the work is a person from the other crew, because a crew that checks its own work has stopped being able to find out, and it is not dishonesty, it is that a man holding a bar cannot see the end of his own timber. **The hours do not cross and do not join: two lines under no heading, and nobody adds them up, not this week, not in a month, not ever, entered as a thing we are choosing and not as a thing we have run out of ways to do.** **No name goes in a second line anywhere**, and Renn Vale named Iven Tallo's paper as the one instrument in the room with a second line in it, said nothing in the arrangement touches it, and said nobody is going to ask him about it. **Neither crew's work goes on a line with a name on it.** The order is six words said once and written down by nobody: lift, bed, carry, set, seat, and then the check. **Callow: that is not trust and I am not handing you any. That is a rule, and I have worked nine years under rules that were true.** Bel Ordry's standing objection: a boundary that cannot state a figure of its own hours on a wall will be told one, and the person who tells it will have a column, and that person will be a foreman whose name is in both lines of a form. Renn Vale's first half against it: the thing she has been defending for thirty-five weeks is a figure she could not give. **A later phase must not turn this into a merger, a post, a shared book, a heading, a name in a column, a second line with anything in it, or the two networks of rooms that do not touch, which belong to 193–197.**

**The wall, the brace and the line of nothing.** **A flag stone came out of the corner of the anteroom floor at the second bell on the fifth day and was bedded as a spreader under the head of the sill, and the anteroom has a hole in the corner of its floor for the rest of the week and for a long time after, and the nine go round it, and the rating is ten including one litter for no more than two hours and did not change.** The wall has **five and a half shores, a spreader, the sixth place empty and not filled, the iron four days up a passage, a brace of a school's own beech pushing on the same wall from the other side, a bad repair on one face only, a line of nothing a finger wide on the anteroom side and two fingers on the kitchen-line side of the same join, and a keeper's nine behind that.** **Nobody put a hand, a tool or a tape into it, nobody measured it, nobody named it, nobody killed it, nobody went through it, and Jo Verrick reads it with her thumb at the join and a string and has never once put a rule in it.** In 192 it was said out loud that the frame's twelfth of an inch and the shim's crushing are the same quantity and that it is a return and not a decay.

**The watcher, and her sentence, which is now on the page and unanswered.** Renn Vale reports nothing, four times, at the first bell on open days and the second on shut days, and the clerk has entered a figure of nothing three times and does not know what a clerk enters for that. **At the second bell on the fifth day she said out loud, in a working room, that Ilsa Norr is in the room with nine children and the physician is in the kitchen-line doorway and has not moved in an hour and a half, that those are the two of us who can stop me, that she is not counting the room, and that she is telling the room where they are because that is what she said she would do and because the person who said it to her on Saturday has not been answered.** The clerk entered it in the watcher's words and entered that the room knew and that nobody in the anteroom could do anything. **Nobody answered it. Do not answer it in Batch 0007 without its own chapter, and do not have it stop being true.**

**The reverse of the schedule, delivered, and what it was.** A fifth day came and went in the thirty-fifth week and a man did not come, and nobody in this building knows what an office does about that, and the clerk decided in 187 **not to find out**, and entered that it is the first decision in thirty-five weeks it cannot take back. **A sheet about this building is on a board four days up the middle passage with a line for the date it was observed on it, filled in, and the day on that line is a day somebody chose** — a road hand's fact, from watching a pen, and it is a fact about somebody else's form and is not available to any instrument in this building. **The reverse was not a counter-schedule.** Nella Bray gave the half against that anything the boundary does about that day is a counter-schedule, that a counter-schedule is a schedule, and that a thing which is scheduled is not a thing which is refused. The answer was that **it is not a day, it is a morning; nobody is appointed and nobody is told; a seventh day is not a crossing day, so nobody could come up the nine steps and nobody could go down them.** Eleven people looked at what they keep and said out loud what they found, a foreman read the six crews' terms from memory and five men agreed to them by their own names and none of it was written down, and **a clerk put her chalk on the anvil end out of her own reach and wrote one line with no day of the week and no date of any kind on it** — *that this boundary looked at its own rooms in a room with the people it concerns, and entered nothing* — **and said out loud why, which is that a day of the week is how a counter-schedule begins.** **Tams Quill refused a nineteenth entry for the fourth time, with a fourth reason, and it is the first refusal he has wanted to give: the reverse of that day is not going on the board, because a board is a column.** **If a later phase decides the line was the wrong call, deleting one line and one paragraph of entry removes it and nothing in the plot changes.**

**Everything else the next batch inherits, in one place.** **The sixth asking was made in 189** — four and a half hours, the terms out loud, Renn Vale named as the person who can be told no and **not used**, three who could not be asked named with new reasons (Marek Venn because he built the brace, Pell Roke because he is inside the room's own permitted occupancy every morning, Talla Roke because she is not in the building and because asking a person who is not in the room is asking a room), and the split named before anybody named it — **and the crew is at seventy-five and a half and does not move again unless a later phase asks a seventh time and says why the reason changed.** **The brace's condition was spent rather than met for the first time in six weeks, in 189, by the woman it can hurt, on her own, with the other half of it unasked because the man who built it is one of the three who could not be asked, and she said she thought about it for a day and spent it anyway.** **The fourth-asking terms were not used at all, so neither is near its cap.** Nera Oduya's first and second conditions are unmet and **unasked by anybody in seven chapters**; **her going was raised once, in 187, by Nella Bray, in a counter's shape — a building has one person in it who answers for the air, and when that person is not there the building has nobody, and a building with nobody in it about its air is a building somebody closes on a piece of paper — and it is unanswered, and Nera answered a different question.** Iven Tallo is unredeemed, his post is unresolved, **his second line is still empty and no signature has been asked of him for six weeks and a woman protected the one paper with his name on it without being asked and he said thank you and was told not to and said that not doing anything about it is going to cost him the thing he wants and he has not worked out what it is.** Sefu Aran is present, not a takeover, and has refused the one thing an elected keeper could do here. **Talla Roke is in no room in this batch and is named once, in a list of people who were not asked, in a chapter that says she is not in the building; Pell Roke is named in that same list and appears once, on his bench at the top of the nine steps, and the two are never in a room together.** The comparison is queued and not made: **the guild map and this boundary's sixteen-row page are still on the anteroom table with a chalk line under both and nothing written under the line, and Bel Ordry said in 192 that the comparison is still owed and that the room which can hear it still does not exist, and 197 is where that changes.** Pot **three days**, seam at four threads, four households at a second gate with nothing and no figure, the wall's reading a quarter of an inch and the fifteenth, the bed under the ninth hearth stone a third of an inch higher and uncaused, the low end blank and unapproached, the ninth room and the four treads unwalked, the wrapped plate unopened thirty-six weeks and the brass rule silent twenty-seven and neither in a room, and the count at one hundred and twenty-seven.

**Nothing in Batch 0007 may make the comparison before 197 or say the sentence that ends it before 197, put a name in a second line, convert or forgive either crew, put a person on the board, answer the courier's sentence, resolve the void, kill the faultform, name it, measure it, tool it, put a hand or a tool or a tape into it, or go through it, add a row for the low end of the corridor, approach the review page, cut a mark in the stone anywhere in this building, raise any room's capacity, meet Nera's first or second condition, ask her about either one, stage her going, raise a repeated signature-ask of Iven Tallo, or name the One-Seat or Morrowlight or the Quiet Hands.** The void must not be joined to the dowel, the charter, the mouth, the four treads, the ninth room, the low end, the air engineer's theory, her twelfth-week name or the plate. The wash woman, Oren Sill, Dael Harrow, the ninth room and the four treads stay exactly where they are. **Warden-Officer Ansel Karr and Cassian Rook are competent and bounded if they appear and may not be turned into anything, and Cassian Rook's office may not become an antagonist.**
